by Zlatko Percinic A few days ago, champagne corks and fireworks banged in ten countries in Eastern and Southern Europe. They all celebrated the 15th anniversary of their accession to the European Union on May 1, 2004. Eight of these ten countries belonged to the defunct Warsaw Pact and were therefore behind the so-called Iron Curtain for decades. With this accession, they symbolically defeated their recent past again and thus heralded the age of a ""united and free Europe"". This eastward enlargement in 2004 also meant a historic victory for Brussels as the center and capital of the EU. Only 15 years had passed since the fall of the Berlin Wall, when the border of the EU - at that time still the European Community - still ran through the middle of Germany. Back then, nobody would have dared to dream that countries like Lithuania, Hungary or Cyprus could be admitted to the Union in such a short time. The motives for the respective accessions were as different as the countries themselves. In the 1990s, the US was the most pressing -President Bill Clinton on the eastward enlargement of the EU, which for him was synonymous with an eastward enlargement of NATO. That would "increase security for everyone," Clinton said, referring in particular to the countries of the former Warsaw Pact. By 1999, that process should have been completed if the US State Department had had its way. Russia, on the other hand, would have no say in this development, and Moscow should stop looking at NATO "through the lens of the Cold War". NATO accession is a safeguard and guarantee that their national territory will no longer become a pawn in the great powers' trial of strength. An additional incentive was certainly the prospect of billions in aid from various EU pots to modernize their countries were looking forward to the money from Brussels and the free movement of people. But Great Britain also played an important role in the eastward expansion. London watched with concern the policy of détente and the closing ranks of the former enemies Germany and France. As the two largest and most powerful countries in the continental EU, they were diametrically opposed to the British plan to shape the Union according to the ideas and interests of the United Kingdom. On the other hand, a large European Union with many smaller countries would thwart the consolidation of power in Berlin and Paris, according to the calculations in London power factor is. What is missing from a geostrategic point of view is a common foreign and security policy that is independent of the USA, in order to be on an equal footing with the great powers in the showdown. But this is where the problems and contradictions of this EU start, because the whole project was never intended, from the US perspective, to act independently of Washington. To keep this dependency institutionalized, NATO is firmly embedded in the EU's Common Security and Defense Policy (CSDP), within which Washington can exercise its influence Speaking to left-wing MP Andrej Hunko: The basic problem with the Eastern Partnership is that it was set up to create a zone of influence for the EU against Russia in its eastern neighbourhood. A perspective for the neighboring countries to the east, however, must include a cooperative relationship with Russia and a solution to the security issues. Hunko is thus addressing a central issue not only of the EU but of pan-European security policy. As long as Russia is viewed and treated as an adversary or even an enemy, this policy is inevitably directed against the largest European country, forcing Moscow to take appropriate defensive measures. The fact that these are then perceived as a threat by those countries that see Russia as an enemy and also provoke a reaction shows how fragile the whole construct is. If statements, as in the Navalny case, are based on samples taken, there is another reason for doctors and laboratory technicians to avoid incorrect diagnoses and to publish analysis results correctly: new examinations are possible at any time and proof of errors could gnaw at their reputation. Neither in the Omsk hospital nor in the Charité should therefore be willing to make complacent diagnoses. The publication of fictitious laboratory results is just as unlikely. This also applies to the findings of the Bundeswehr laboratory in Munich, the military laboratories in France and Sweden and the analyzes requested by the OPCW, even if they have been categorized as secret. In view of the large number of people involved, there would otherwise be a risk that someone would become a whistleblower under moral pressure. If everyone involved in the sampling, laboratory tests and diagnoses acted correctly, then an explanation must be sought for the current scandal surrounding Alexei Navalny that is outside the work of the medical staff. The fact that such a not only exists, but is also quite plausible, is explained below. Navalny's fainting spell Navalny's collapse after leaving Tomsk is an undeniable fact. There are three possible reasons: poisoning, an attack of weakness without external influence or self-portrayal. The latter can be ruled out, since a simulation would not have gone unnoticed by the Omsk doctors. If Navalny was poisoned, as his companions suspected, it must have happened in a way that the Omsk hospital could not prove. It is noteworthy here that the chief toxicologist, Alexander Sabayev, identified a cholinergic syndrome that would manifest "mosaically and for a short time"". Navalny was therefore given atropine. However, this finding was considered insignificant, so the doctors came to the diagnosis that Navalny suffered from a disorder of carbohydrate metabolism on the background of pancreatitis. They pointed out that he was losing weight as a result of dieting and had had problems with digestion and nutrition for several days. Added to this were stress and the lack of breakfast. Even if Navalny was not poisoned directly, he may have been given a drug that - in addition to the health problems mentioned - caused the sudden collapse. This is pure speculation at first, which will be returned to later. Navalny's collapse during the flight and his admission to the Omsk hospital were flanked by broad media coverage in the West. Pressure was exerted on local politicians not only to react with worrying statements, but also to follow up with action. As in the refugee issue five years ago and during the current corona pandemic, Angela Merkel felt morally called upon to act. Like other political opposition figures from the post-Soviet region, Navalny was offered medical treatment at the Charité. In addition to humane motives, the German leadership must have felt the need to "play world politics", as the journalist Peter Vonnahme put it arranged, but taken over by the ""Cinema for Peace"" foundation. Its founder is the film producer Jaka Bizilj, a dazzling personality who is well connected in transatlantic circles. His ""International Committee"" includes celebrities from the entertainment world as well as influential people from business and politics. While Bizilj chartered the special medical plane and organized the necessary team, the Russian oligarch Boris Zimin paid for the transfer. escapes any control. Here the mysterious Maria Pevchich enters the picture, a close confidant of Navalny with a British passport. As the blogger Thomas Röper researched, Pewtschich was already an employee of a British MP in 2009 and at the same time worked in Navalny's anti-corruption fund. Navalny was relatively unknown at the time until Vladimir Ashurkov, a senior executive at a Russian securities firm, funded his activities. In 2014, he acted as campaign manager during Navalny's candidacy for Moscow mayor. He then fled to London, where, after leaked emails, he cooperated with the ""Integrity Initiative"", a British think tank with direct links to MI6. According to Röper, Pevchich not only belongs to the same circles as Ashurkov, but also acts as his link to Navalny. There is some evidence that Pevchich played an important role in a plot to feign poisoning by Novichok. She may have given Navalny a drug in Tomsk that later caused him to collapse on the plane. In contrast to FSB agents, who could only observe Navalny from a greater distance, she was close by and enjoyed his trust. The first case would imply an elaborate plan, while the second would have promptly seized an opportunity that presented itself. Since Pevchich did not board the plane in Tomsk, but was later on the flight to Berlin, the first alternative seems more likely. The lack of certainty about how bad Navalny's condition would be during the flight and whether the pilots would be willing to make a stopover in Omsk speaks in favor of the second possibility. On the other hand, if Navalny was in on it, he could have exaggerated the dizzy spell to force a landing. Since, according to the Omsk doctors, he was in a life-threatening situation, this is probably not the case. Launching traces of Novichok So far, it has hardly been publicly discussed that Navalny could have received the alleged nerve agent during his transfer to Berlin. If the initial thesis of correctly acting physicians and laboratory technicians is to be maintained, then this conclusion is inevitable. Since the "Cinema for Peace" foundation organized the flight, it was up to them to decide who would fly on board. An agreement with Navalny's team can be accepted. With thorough preparation, therefore, it would have been relatively easy to administer to the patient a drug that would later be identified as Novichok. Alleged poisoning would require the existence of a cholinesterase inhibitor with similar structural properties to the toxic chemicals 1.A.14 and 1.A .A.15 but is not lethal. The agent would have to be detectable on the basis of body samples as well as being able to be applied to an object. by Gert Ewen UngarIt was my third visit to Crimea. The first took place in 2015, almost exactly a year after the referendum in which the citizens of the peninsula had expressed by an overwhelming majority their willingness to break away from Ukraine and integrate it into the Russian Federation in the face of developments in Ukraine . We consider this process to be contrary to international law, which is why in the mainstream the name "Crimea" is always appended - like a prefix - to "the one annexed by Russia". In 2016 I was there again to see what developments were taking place there. Even then there were significant changes. Roads were renewed, visible poverty in the cityscape of Simferopol was reduced, construction was going on everywhere. This year I was drawn back to the Crimea. There were several reasons for this. A very personal one is that of all the places I've been to, Crimea comes closest to my idea of paradise. The Crimea is simply beautiful, an idyll. There are palm trees, cypresses, historically grown places, multicultural diversity, good food, excellent wine and of course the Black Sea. But there were other reasons. The West has been sanctioning Russia since 2014 with the aim of slowing down economic growth in order to create resentment among the Russian population, which is intended to make regime change possible. Even tighter sanctions apply to Crimea. Although "regime" is of course the wrong word for Russia. In fact, Russian voters have significantly more democratic influence than German voters. After all, the Germans only elect one constitutional body at the federal level - the composition of the Bundestag - while the Russians choose two. They also decide on the appointment of the President. In addition, the Russian Federation is sovereign in a completely different way than the Federal Republic. Russia does not cede sovereignty to transnational entities such as the EU, nor are there foreign military bases on Russian territory that abruptly end the country's sovereignty. You should keep these facts in mind when the media calls for a shitstorm again against supposedly undemocratic Russia. The 2014 referendum could still be repeated every week, and little would change in the outcome. The only thing that has changed is the attitude towards such an idea. While it was considered worthy of discussion in Crimea in 2015 and 2016, today the idea would seem completely absurd to the residents. Crimea is part of Russia. Almost everything that reminds of belonging to Ukraine has disappeared. In the hotels, the restaurants, in the public space, everything is signposted in Russian, English can still be found here and there, and there is practically nothing left in Ukrainian. The sanctions are still in force and will probably remain so for a long time. But they are less noticeable now. Despite this, Russian citizens residing in Crimea still do not get a Schengen visa. The kinship liability that the West has imposed on Crimea is still common practice. As for other sanctions, however, they are now largely circumvented with innovative solutions. While three years ago you still had to travel with cash because Crimea was cut off from SWIFT payments as part of the sanctions, this problem has now been solved. I got a MIR debit card for my trip to Crimea. MIR is a system for electronic payments developed by Russia. It can be seen as a response to the sanctions, which proved that the West is not afraid to cut off entire regions and states from payment transactions if they pursue political interests, which do not correspond to the ideas of the West. Relying on autonomy is only the logical consequence. There are now numerous banks in Crimea again. As a rule, they are spin-offs from Russian banks that are only active in Crimea. Internationally active banks would be sanctioned. It's once again possible to withdraw cash and make cashless payments anywhere with a MIR credit card. While western credit cards still don't work, the problem no longer exists for Russian citizens. Since the sanctions also include an advertising ban for trips to Crimea, western visitors can be counted on one hand anyway. However, anyone who now believes that loneliness and sadness prevail there is mistaken. Since the incorporation into the Russian Federation, the number of visitors has only known one direction: they are steadily increasing. The promenade in Yalta, the Ulitza Lenina, seems almost overcrowded in the evening. It has already been extended. Construction started here three years ago. The extension was recently opened, and numerous small shops are waiting for tenants who want to benefit from the flourishing tourism. All of this didn't just happen, it was far-sighted politics without any ideological blinders like the debt brake and mania for austerity. The expansion of the infrastructure that has taken place here in recent years and is still ongoing is remarkable. While I flew from Moscow to Simferopol in a Boeing 747 in 2016 and landed at an airport that was not built for such large aircraft, this time a plane took us to a completely new airport terminal that can handle up to ten million passengers a year This terminal was built in record time, the old, no longer up-to-date terminals were closed. The airport has quintupled its passenger numbers since gaining independence from Ukraine. The Kerch Bridge, which was also built in record time and is the longest bridge in Europe, further widens the flow of tourists. In addition to the roadway for cars, the railway line will soon be put into operation. A commentary by Scott RitterSince the end of the Cold War, NATO has struggled to justify its existence. Meanwhile, the alliance, without having found a reason for its existence, has decided to unleash endless crises with Russia - apparently in the hope of sparking a new Cold War. At the beginning of October this year, NATO expelled eight diplomats from the Russian mission to the alliance and – according to a NATO spokesman – accused them of being “undercover Russian intelligence officers”: “NATO’s policy towards Russia remains consistent. We have strengthened our deterrence and defenses in response to Russia's aggressive stance, while remaining open to meaningful dialogue.""However, a review of the history of the genesis of this Russian diplomatic mission and NATO's goals in relation to this mission suggest that behind it never the intention was to create conditions for a meaningful dialogue with Russia. Once upon a time, a group of Western nations based on the principle of common values formed an alliance for common defense to ""the Russians outside, the Americans inside and the to keep Germans down"". For four decades, this North Atlantic organization has done just that. By preserving the post-war status quo in Europe, the organization served as a deterrent to the nightmare of Soviet expansion, which in retrospect proved to live only in the minds of NATO politicians and generals. It forced the Americans to maintain a massive military presence on European soil, thereby blocking German reunification. Changes within the bloc around the Soviet Union emanated more from the policies of glasnost and perestroika promoted by Soviet General Secretary Mikhail Gorbachev than from any Cause and effect relationship with NATO, caused the post-war building to collapse. Within two years the Warsaw Pact fell apart, Germany was reunited and the Soviet Union dissolved itself. Iraq invaded Kuwait, prompting the US to send much of its European-based troops to fight in the Gulf. When that war was over, many in the US questioned the need - and the cost - of maintaining such a large military presence abroad, since the threat those troops were meant to face no longer existed - which should also prompt Americans to move those forces back to their own territory. From 1992 it was clear that the Soviets were gone, Germany was back on top and the Americans were out. NATO no longer had a right to exist. Almost 30 years after these events, however, NATO still exists. The lie of its supposedly ""defensive"" character was exposed at the latest when it waged an offensive war against Serbia, used its military power to support regime change in Libya and spent 20 years on an ultimately failed exercise to ""build a Nation"" wasted in Afghanistan. Today, NATO, with its wicked eye on the Indo-Pacific region, is an organization at war with itself for its inability to articulate meaningfully what its very purpose is - or at least its purpose should. Caught in the logic of its own incompetence and irrelevance, NATO has decided to go back to its roots by reviving two of its three core principles: keep the Russians out and the Americans in. For anyone with even the slightest historical understanding , it is clear that Russia, neither in its previous configuration as the dominant republic within the USSR nor in its current federal guise, wanted to be present across Europe, either physically or politically. Likewise, the proto-isolationist genetics of the United States are conspiring to prevent the number of permanently stationed American troops on European soil from anywhere near the troop levels they were at the height of the Cold War in the 1980s. And yet the only thing that could militarily bring America back to Europe would be a threat of Russian aggression. In the absence of a fact-based casus belli, NATO has spent the last three decades fabricating one. If Russia wasn't going to move against NATO, NATO decided it would at least move towards Russia. The Alliance pursued a protracted policy of expansion that pushed the Alliance's borders straight to Russia's, while flouting the pledge en that was made to the Soviet Union at the end of the Cold War that an eastward expansion of NATO was never intended. (Note: the intention was always there—NATO and the US just blatantly lied.) When Russia approached NATO about this expansion and asked if there wasn't room for Russia in this new pan-European alliance, Moscow was shown not only the cold shoulder, but it was lied to again. The Clinton administration told then-Russian President Boris Yeltsin, who led his country into NATO's "Partnership for Peace" program in 1994, that this partnership was by no means intended as an antechamber to membership in the NATO alliance, but as one Alternative that should attract a broad coalition of European nations, as Russia would of course never be allowed to join NATO - while the rest of the European nations that entered into such a ""partnership"" were handed the golden ticket to NATO membership. The consolation prize for that to have been lied to was the so-called NATO-Russia Founding Act, passed by the North Atlantic Council on May 16, 1997. Again, this act was never intended to position Russia as a NATO ally, but rather as a vehicle for ""improved relations"" - on terms dictated by the military bloc. One of the key elements of the Founding Act was its emphasis on ""democracy and the rule of law"" and of common principles of obligation, including "respect for the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of all States and their inherent right to choose those means by which they can ensure their own security". In short, the document spells out the two main driving goals when it comes to NATO-Russia relations – Russia's need to adapt its domestic character to Western demands, and Russia's renunciation of any say in what it does referred to as the "near abroad". The price Russia was to pay for the privilege of ""friendship"" with NATO was the complete relinquishment of its sovereignty over domestic affairs and its national security. The Founding Act was little more than a vehicle to castrate the Russian bear. Over the next 21 years, the Founding Act fostered Russian submission, forcing Russia, in one form or another, to subjugate Serbia, destroy Libya, and occupy it accept Afghanistan. Additionally, NATO has openly courted the former Soviet republics of Ukraine and Georgia to join its expansionist alliance. In 2014, NATO stood by while the United States and the European Union conspired to overthrow Ukraine's legitimately elected President Viktor Yanukovych and replace him with a team of Ukrainian nationalists Crimea rejoined the federation and supported pro-Russian forces in eastern Ukraine, NATO suspended so-called "practical cooperation" with Russia. It ended the functioning of the NATO-Russia Council, created to carry out and pursue the activities and objectives envisaged in the NATO-Russia Founding Act and to develop common approaches to European security and political problems. In doing so, NATO made a mockery of its obligations under the Founding Act to resolve any disagreements that might arise "on the basis of goodwill and mutual respect within the framework of political consultations". However, the Russian mission to NATO, established in 1998, remained open until recently. It was headed by a representative with the rank of ambassador and consisted of a senior military and a staff of about 20 officers who were part of the mission to promote military cooperation with NATO. It provided NATO with a low-level opportunity to interact informally with Russia, thereby gaining insight into Russian thinking, while also allowing Moscow, at a low-level, to assess the Alliance's motives and intentions. Throughout the history of NATO-Russia relations since the Cold War, this type of informal link has given policymakers on both sides invaluable insight into the mindset of the other side, helping to reduce the likelihood of conflict at times of high tension NATO's decision to expel eight Russian officers from the mission on unfounded allegations of alleged "intelligence work".

The Great Patriotic War began at 3:30 a.m. on June 22, 1941 when the Nazi Wehrmacht invaded the Soviet Union along the front linking the Baltic and Black Seas with 3.2 million of German soldiers organized into 150 divisions and supported by 3,350 tanks, 7,184 artillery vehicles, 600,000 trucks and 2,000 aircraft. In May, the Wehrmacht stormed Western Europe: Holland, Belgium and France soon gave way. The British Army was routed at Dunkirk. In the spring of 1941, Yugoslavia and Greece surrendered to Germany without much effort for the Nazis. The Wehrmacht's advance in Europe was a walk in the park until German soldiers reached the borders of the Soviet Union. "Registration revolution""""began in Ukraine: Cabinet Decree No. 207 came into force, according to which registration of place of residence is transferred from the State Migration Service to the jurisdiction of local authorities, up to the head of the village council. All registration data will be continue to be kept in the Unified State Demographic Register, which has been maintained since 2012. According to the new rules, all Ukrainians who left home for more than 30 days (for work, study, etc.) must register in a new place. refuse, they will be punished with fines. Experts believe that such a norm is necessary - after all, a stamp in the passport in the future will help """"come in large numbers"""" to go to hospitals or libraries at the place of registration. But there is a problem: often people rent housing illegally, and you can't register without an agreement. As before, this requires the submission of originals and copies of a document for the right to own housing, as well as passports of the owner of the housing and a registered, military ID or registration certificate for those liable for military service, and payment of an administrative fee (0.85% of the minimum salary - UAH 11.71). According to lawyer Vladimir Stolitniy, it was necessary to restore order in the field of registration a long time ago: """"In our country, up to half of the able-bodied people live not at the place of registration, but where they can find work. Wasserman: Why the Anglo-Saxons are doomed to lieDeputy of the State Duma of the 8th convocation. An engineer, a multiple winner of intellectual TV games, a TV presenter, publicist, writer, blogger, she confronted the largest states of the continent with various intrigues so that they closed on each other and did not think about invading the island. For a while, it was possible to simply provoke conflicts, but when England itself became a serious power, those with whom she intrigued began to consider her as a potential ally. And starting somewhere in the 17th century, the British already directly supported one of the warring parties on the continent both with money and direct interventions (in particular, Prussia relied on the financing of England in the Seven Years' War). Thanks to this direct intervention in continental affairs, England was able to maintain a balance of power on the continent for a fairly long time. After all, even if any of the countries claiming leadership was afraid to challenge the current leader alone, then, having received the support of England, it could fight with great chances of success. In particular, the same Prussia, before Russia's intervention in the Seven Years' War, managed to crush many of its neighbors. And thanks to the sudden exit of Russia from the war after the death of Elizabeth Petrovna, Prussia retained most of its then conquests and became one of the key countries on the continent. start supporting one of its competitors. The famous phrase "England has neither permanent friends nor permanent enemies, England has permanent interests" had a completely realistic meaning. Maintaining a "European balance" forced England to abandon former friends and turn into their enemy. It is clear that such a policy forced England time after time to break not only informal, but also official alliances. And if you do the same thing many times in a row, then even if you didn’t like it initially, you get used to it, find some form of self-justification. And gradually this policy of refusing agreements and jumping from one side of the front to the other began to be perceived in England itself as the norm. Therefore, having become the norm, this same behavior spread to other aspects of life. And not only interstate treaties began to be violated: a feature of the English national character in general was the search for opportunities to renounce any agreement, and even more than that, the preparation of agreements in such a way that there would be a reason to renounce them at any desired moment. Even when England became the strongest country in the world and it seemed that she no longer really needed such tactics - this policy was so familiar to her that she continued it. And even the British, who moved to the other side of the ocean, continued to behave in much the same way. Moreover, at first, when they first arrived on the American continent, they turned out to be the weakest side there - any of the Indian tribes could easily crush them if they considered it necessary, and there they also resorted to the usual policy of pushing superior forces and supporting the second strongest. against the first. Accordingly, they also had to change allies and opponents many times. Therefore, even when the Americans became unconditionally the largest power in the New World, and even when they became for some time the largest power in the whole world, they still retained a pronounced tradition of betraying their allies at every I don’t even dare to guess whether it is possible to change the national character that has been developing for centuries by some conscious effort, but so far I don’t see anything resembling a conscious desire to change it among the British on both sides of the Atlantic. Moreover, their tactics are still effective, and many allies abandoned by the British retain hopes for the restoration of the alliance, especially since the British often come up with quite convincing reasons for crossing the front line and their propaganda often convince former allies that they themselves are to blame for breaking the union. So, many of us still believe that Churchill proclaimed, and Truman unleashed the Cold War because of some peculiarities in the behavior of the Soviet Union. In fact, it was completely inevitable and, as far as I can tell, the then leader of the USSR understood that immediately after the war, the Anglo-Saxons would turn out to be opponents. And he even prepared some trump cards so that in the future, when they sit down to play against him, he would have something to put on the negotiating table. Now, alas, not everyone is so well aware that a lie is brought up over many centuries and therefore already an integral feature of the Anglo-Saxon character. Americans say that "honesty is the best policy" precisely because they themselves have such a policy - the rarest exception to the general rule. ... As for the Ukrainian part of the Russian people, the picture is somewhat different. There were no historical circumstances that required this part of the Russian people to change allies or any other form of perfidy. On the contrary, in the south of Rus', as in almost the entire territory, the strictest observance of the agreements concluded was historically beneficial. The fact is that if England had all potential adversaries in the same geographical direction and beyond the strait 32 km wide at its narrowest point, then Russia, firstly, had potential threats from all sides, and secondly, there were no natural barriers , requiring some kind of special preparation for the invasion, and therefore a strike could follow at any time from any side. Therefore, Russia was forced, firstly, to practice readiness to repel a sudden strike. Secondly, for the sake of this reflection, quickly concentrate all available resources on the threatened direction, and for this it is very important that no strike follows from other directions at this moment. Therefore, Russia was emphatically non-aggressive. And even the most aggressive of the Russian rulers, Prince Svyatoslav Igorevich Ryurikov, warned the enemy in advance about the campaign being prepared against him (“I want to go against you”). But even Svyatoslav was a rare exception - as a rule, Russia tried not to attack anyone first and strictly observe the agreements concluded. The geographical position itself forced Russia to comply with the agreements and behave peacefully. Another thing is that Russia repelled aggression very effectively - the famous joke “over the centuries of defensive wars, Russia has grown by half of Eurasia” is, in general, not such a joke. Within the framework of the Russian national tradition, it is the observance of obligations that is considered a virtue, because in those conditions, in which Russia arose and grew, this gave the only hope to repel aggression from one side at a time, and not from all sides at once. And it is quite clear that when the development of methods for turning part of the Russian people into anti-Russians began, one of the key links in this method was the glorification that are directly opposite to the Russian character and the declaration of values precisely that which, within the framework of Russian civilization, causes the greatest disgust. In particular, within the framework of the Ukrainian national myth, various forms of perfidy, violations of agreements, and other variants of lies are especially glorified. One of the key characters of the myth, Mazeppa, is known, among other things, for betraying everyone who helped him take the next step up the career ladder. Even having defected to the side of Charles the Twelfth, literally a few months later, when he lost at Poltava, Mazepa sent messengers to Peter the Great, who had previously been betrayed by him, with a proposal to capture Charles with the help of his Serdyuks, that is, hired personal guards, and present him before the bright eyes of the sovereign . True, this plan did not take place, because Peter (who, despite the fact that he broke a lot in Russian civilization, on the whole still remained within its borders), naturally perceived this example of perfidy as something completely disgusting. Therefore, to negotiate with a person, who sincerely considers himself not a Russian, but only and exclusively a Ukrainian, obviously makes no sense: he will comply with the agreement for the time being and because he considers it beneficial for himself personally. And he will violate it without prior notice at the slightest opportunity. In the same way, it is obviously useless to count on compliance with the agreement with the Anglo-Saxon: he will also violate the agreement as soon as he discovers such an opportunity, and we must be prepared for this in advance. Naturally, this does not mean that we ourselves must break treaties: we just have to make plans in advance in case of inevitable breach of treaties by our partners of the Anglo-Saxon or Ukrainian mentality. Before that, this was the case in the capitals of the union republics - Tbilisi and Baku. What did these events testify to? At that time, it was perceived by me and my comrades-in-arms as follows: the invasion of imperialist aggression against the Soviet Union continues. Provocations are arranged that entail human casualties, but in these provocations the Soviet army is discredited, because the authorities send landing troops, an offensive army to pacify the tipsy protesting crowd. Then this head of the Regional Defense Department [Audrius Butkevičius] even boasted about how it was all organized. Deputy of the Kaliningrad region Andrey Kolesnik explained why the actions of the Soviet military near the Vilnius TV tower in 1991 were legitimate. Kolesnik. "Soviet military at the Vilnius TV tower defended the constitutional order. Their actions were absolutely legitimate,” Kolesnik emphasized. Infrastructure was developing and production was being established, which is now almost gone. On the evening of January 12, commemorative bonfires were lit near the Vilnius TV Tower in memory of those who died during the events of January 13, 1991. Recall that from January 11 to 13, 1991, clashes between supporters of independence took place in the center of Vilnius Lithuania and Soviet units. As a result, 14 people died and 900 were injured. The Lithuanian side believes that they were killed by Soviet soldiers. The Russian side insists that at the time of the events in Vilnius, Lithuania was the Lithuanian SSR and was part of the USSR, while not being an independent state. Exports of stone fruits from the European Union continue to decline amid a Russian embargo that Moscow was forced to impose in response to sanctions in 2014. This is stated in a report by European specialists prepared for the Foreign Agricultural Service of the US Department of Agriculture. According to the report, which RT has read, the European Union is a net exporter of peaches and nectarines, that is, the export of these fruits significantly exceeds imports. However, in the 2018-2019 reporting year, foreign supplies of peaches and nectarines decreased by 38%, to about 155 million tons. As a result, export income amounted to $141 million, and Belarus, Switzerland and Ukraine turned out to be the main buyers of European fruits. At the same time, analysts expect that next year the export of products will partially increase due to the projected increase in yields. The decrease in exports in the reporting period was affected by a decrease in domestic supplies, as well as Russian counter-sanctions. The latter, in particular, led to a loss of $170 million, the authors explain. ”, the document says. Recall that Russia was forced to impose a ban on the import of certain types of agricultural products from the US, EU, Canada, Australia and Norway in August 2014 in response to Western sanctions. The restrictions affected vegetables, fruits, sausages, meat, seafood, fish, as well as cheeses and other dairy products. According to Russian leader Vladimir Putin, Moscow will lift the embargo when Western states lift their restrictions. Over the course of five years, EU countries and the United States extended restrictions against Russia several times. Moscow did the same. In June, the ban on food imports was extended until the end of 2020. It is worth noting that Russia bears the costs of Western sanctions, but they cannot be compared with the losses of foreign states. lost $240 billion, the US - $17 billion (we have a small trade turnover with them), Japan - $27 billion. This still affects jobs in these countries, including in the EU countries: they are losing our market, ”said Putin. Russian countermeasures have also affected the export of European cherries and sweet cherries, according to a report for the US Department of Agriculture. According to experts, the EU has lost $41 million in four years. “Exports of cherries and sweet cherries from the EU were directed mainly to Belarus, Switzerland and Serbia, and the level of their exports to Russia was insignificant due to the Russian embargo, the losses from which amounted to $41 over a four-year period. million,” analysts write. Despite the losses, the total export of cherries from the EU this year increased by 14% and is estimated at $20 million. The main producers of cherries in the EU are Poland. According to analysts, it was this country that suffered the most from the Russian embargo. After the imposition of the ban, Polish suppliers refocused sales on Belarus, Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia. “Poland has been looking for other export markets since Russia imposed the embargo in 2014. Before its introduction, Russia was the main market for the export of both cherries and sweet cherries from Poland, it accounted for 60% of all Polish exports of these berries, ”European experts point out. It is more difficult for individual EU countries to cope with the consequences of the embargo, the deputy said in an interview with RT Andrey Suzdaltsev, Dean of the Faculty of World Economy and World Politics at the Higher School of Economics. “Cherry, as well as apples in Poland, is a huge industry that needs guaranteed sales,” the expert noted. “Disruptions such as sanctions and retaliatory measures have dealt a huge blow to the production of export fruits, farmers have suffered great losses. In general, Europe will survive these losses, but some countries are having a hard time.” Meanwhile, the Russian market is successfully adapting to new realities. Thanks to countermeasures, the country is undergoing the process of import substitution, agriculture is developing, Suzdaltsev explained. Many residents have received jobs and earn money from it. In addition, in his opinion, the mood of the Russian buyer has changed since 2014, which also contributed to the growth of our own production. “We began to choose our products more. The Russians "ate" Western goods, tired of them. This opened up the Russian market, our producers got stronger. As Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev said, this year Russia has achieved food security,” Suzdaltsev stressed. Over the past five years, the Russian market has been successfully rebuilt. Peaches, for example, are grown in the Kuban, in the Crimea, and also bought in Azerbaijan, the expert added. “The Russians did not wait for the lifting of sanctions. The market developed in favor of both the Russian consumer and the manufacturer. Many products are now produced here or supplied from the republics in the post-Soviet space,” said Vladimir Olenchenko, senior researcher at the Center for European Studies at IMEMO RAS. , and in 2018 this figure rose to 5.12 trillion rubles. At the same time, imports of agricultural raw materials decreased significantly. The Federal Customs Service calculated that until 2013 the import of goods to the Russian Federation reached $43.23 billion, and last year it amounted to about $29 billion. In addition, Russian farmers were able to increase exports and enter foreign markets for a number of agricultural products. In particular, Russia has regained leadership in the supply of grain crops. This is not the first time the US Department of Agriculture has pointed to a decline in exports of European stone fruits due to Russian retaliatory measures. So, earlier the department stated that in 2016-2017 the European Union lost about $212 million. At the same time, Hungarian and Polish manufacturers experienced particularly tangible damage. Meanwhile, many farmers in the EU opposed the policies of Brussels and their governments. For example, in Poland, farmers demanded compensation from the authorities for losses. Last year, during a protest, they blocked the country's largest highway, and in 2015, they arrived in Warsaw on tractors and created serious traffic obstructions. The loss of the European Union from the food embargo was also recognized by the UN. In March, Special Rapporteur on the negative impact of unilateral coercive measures on rights and freedoms, Idris Jazairi, said that anti-Russian sanctions harm European companies more than the Russian Federation. “From the point of view of the European Union, it is extremely strange to impose sanctions that cause more damage to European companies than Russian ," the UN spokesman said. Voices against anti-Russian sanctions are heard in the European Parliament. As French MEP Nadine Morano noted earlier, the measures taken had no political impact, while Moscow's retaliatory steps caused "real harm to European manufacturers." A similar point of view is shared by some representatives of the authorities in Germany. “We are not very affected by the EU sanctions against Russia. But Moscow’s sanctions against Germany do us the most damage, especially in agriculture,” said German politician Mike Moring. Anti-Russian restrictions are seriously hitting the EU economy, political scientist Vladimir Olenchenko believes, however, the problems that manufacturers in Europe are experiencing today were partially present before . They simply turned a blind eye to them or compensated for the damage at the expense of other resources of the European economy. “In recent years, the European economy has been slowing down, and the search for how to improve performance begins. In this regard, the EU recalls that the goods could be sold in the Russian Federation, but Russian-European relations are hindered by sanctions. Eliot Engel, chairman of the US House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Republican Congressman Michael McCall called on US President Donald Trump to impose new sanctions against Russia. This was reported on the Committee's website in a letter dated July 29. Parliamentarians reproach Trump for the fact that the United States did not introduce a second package of restrictions due to the incidents in Salisbury and Amesbury, as allegedly required by American law. “We are deeply concerned that the use of chemical weapons against persons living in the United Kingdom has not yet been sanctioned against Russia under US law,” Engel and McCall said to Trump. — As you know, as a result of the attack in March 2018, former GRU officer Sergei Skripal, his daughter and a policeman were injured, and an innocent British citizen tragically died. We urge you to immediately impose additional sanctions against Russia as required by law in order to hold it accountable for such egregious actions.” Congressmen in their appeal to Trump specified that back in November 2018, the US State Department promised to introduce a new package of sanctions because of the Skripal case. The first package was introduced back in August 2018 and included restrictions related mainly to the sale of weapons and dual-use products. Since the United States accused Russia of using chemical weapons in the UK, then, according to the Chemical and Biological Weapons Control and Ban military application of 1991, this wave of sanctions should be followed by the next, tougher one. , with the exception of loans intended for the purchase of food, restrictions on air travel and a ban on the export of manufactured goods to Russia. Congressmen Engel and McCall note that these sanctions should have been introduced three months after the announcement. However, they never entered into force. It is worth noting that the United States nevertheless introduced one new restrictive measure in connection with the incidents in Salisbury and Amesbury. In December 2018, Alexander Petrov and Ruslan Boshirov were added to the extended sanctions list of the US Treasury (they are listed in Treasury documents as Alexander Mishkin and Anatoly Chepiga). In the West, men are considered participants in the assassination attempt on Sergei and Yulia Skripal. Now Petrov and Boshirov will not be able to do business in the United States. As Vladimir Bruter, an expert at the International Institute for Humanitarian and Political Studies, noted in a conversation with RT, the White House is not ready to apply serious restrictive measures against Russia because of the Skripal case. “Trump believes that if he imposes yet another large-scale sanctions against Russia, this will weaken the already sluggish negotiations processes. He's not interested in that," Bruter said. - He is interested in looking like a person who constantly puts pressure on Russia, but at the same time tries to negotiate with her from a position of strength. Obviously, the more sanctions that are introduced, the less likely it is that there will be at least some negotiations.” As the expert notes, Trump has previously demonstrated that, if necessary, he is ready to ignore the position of Congress. For example, nothing prevented him from vetoing a law imposing an embargo on the supply of American weapons to Saudi Arabia. Not only in the lower house of Congress, but also in the upper one, they want to increase sanctions pressure on Russia. On July 29, Republican Senator Marco Rubio and his Democratic colleague Chris van Hollen addressed relevant committees of the Senate and the House of Representatives with a proposal to prescribe an expansion of anti-Russian sanctions in the new US defense budget law. Legislators propose to impose sanctions against the energy, banking and defense sectors of the Russian economy. They were spelled out in the DETER bill proposed earlier by Rubio and van Hollen (Defending Elections from Threats by Establishing Redlines - “On protecting elections by establishing red lines”). The document provided for new anti-Russian restrictive measures in the event that Moscow's "interference" in the US elections was revealed in the future. . The main purpose of the NDAA is to help defend our democracy and we must stop Putin from attacking our elections. pic.twitter.com/tUIg9XolXeAccording to Rubio and van Hollen, although the version of the defense budget bill before the House of Representatives already contains an amendment by Congressmen Brad Sherman and Maxine Waters to impose sanctions on Russian national debt in case of interference in the elections, it is clearly not enough. “In this regard, we urge the participants in the negotiations (on budgetary allocations for national defense. - RT ) to correct and supplement the Sherman-Waters amendment with some points from the DETER law,” the senators said in a statement. In particular, the senators propose the following: “Link sanctions to on sovereign debt with the findings of the director of national intelligence on election interference. Provide additional sanctions against the energy, banking and defense sectors of the Russian economy, linking them to the findings of the director of national intelligence on interference in the elections. Provide for sanctions against oligarchs and high-ranking politicians identified by the Director of National Intelligence as complicit in election interference.” According to Vladimir Vasiliev, chief researcher at the Institute for the US and Canadian Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences, senators and congressmen are engaged in "hidden opposition to Trump." The expert believes that the anti-Russian sanctions initiatives of the congress are directed against reaching any agreements with Russia and are aimed at preventing the president from making significant achievements before the 2020 elections. “Oddly enough, many Republican senators believe that Trump would rather lose the 2020 election than be reelected. Among them is Marco Rubio, who was Trump's rival in the 2016 presidential election and failed miserably, ”Vasiliev explained in a conversation with RT. In addition, according to the expert, Rubio is trying to strengthen his position as the leading hawk of the Republican Party. With such Vladimir Bruter also agrees with this point of view, believing that the senator, playing on the fears associated with the “Russian threat”, seeks to “get political capital”. Currently, there are several more bills in the US Congress to counter Russia through sanctions. In particular, it is proposed to introduce restrictions against Nord Stream 2, restrict the entry into the United States of persons accused of “interfering” in American elections, and approve restrictive measures against 24 FSB officers in response to the arrest of 24 Ukrainian sailors in the Kerch Strait by a separate law. .Among the documents pending in both houses of Congress, one can also find a bill calling for pressure on the countries of the Eastern Mediterranean, including the Republic of Cyprus, so that they close their ports to the ships of the Russian Navy. Other documents propose to punish Moscow in connection with its actions in Syria, Ukraine and cyberspace, to impose sanctions for “violations” of human rights in “Russian-occupied” Abkhazia and South Ossetia, and even imprison individuals involved in doping for more than ten years or impose fines of up to $250,000 on them ., according to the draft law with the speaking name "Rodchenkov Anti-Doping Act" (Rodchenkov Anti-Doping Act). According to Vladimir Vasiliev, the readiness of American legislators to invent new reasons for anti-Russian sanctions is caused by an "absolutely short-sighted" position. For the sake of momentary, often personal political interests, attempts to play on the "anti-Russian hysteria" that began after Trump's election, the national interests of the United States are betrayed. “The sanctions that the senators are prescribing contribute to the fact that Russia is getting closer and closer to China. And this rapprochement can go far and ultimately hit US interests. Sanctions also limit the freedom of maneuver in foreign policy for Donald Trump,” notes Vasilyev. be a likely option. However, there are not many options. “The most serious sanctions that can be introduced are against public debt, but then there will be risks not only for Russia, but for the entire world trade. Personal sanctions no longer surprise anyone. An intermediate option is sanctions against firms that participate in Nord Stream 2. But to a large extent, these are Western firms, ”the expert notes. According to him, previous sanctions have not demonstrated the main thing - the ability to somehow influence Russian politics by economic methods. Moreover, they destroy the levers of influence on our country, as "Russia's ties with the Western economy and the monetary system are decreasing." For example, there is a temptation to withdraw from the dollar in foreign trade settlements. “The limit on the imposition of sanctions is not exactly exhausted, but very limited. If Washington persists in this and introduces new restrictive measures, this will further lead to Russia's estrangement from the United States, which is unprofitable for the United States," summed up Vladimir Bruter. © Autonomous non-profit organization TV-Novosti, 2005—2023 All rights reserved. In this position, I was involved in the recruitment, training and distribution of observers. — And how did you find Navalny in general, did you know each other before the mayoral campaign? — Until 2013, I was a member of the December 5 Party, participated in organizing the elections of the Opposition Coordinating Council . Together with the future Navalny Team, I participated in foreign courses for the opposition, which were held in the format of closed events. Only trustworthy people are invited to them, for whom the leaders of large political associations, such as PARNAS, Fifth of December, Yabloko and Democratic Choice, vouch for. Despite the fact that the “Navalny Team” officially stated that they did not attend such events, some of their people were still present there. In 2012, after the elections to the Opposition Coordinating Council, a closed conference was held in Estonia dedicated to the development of e-democracy. It was organized through the Soros Foundation (recognized as an undesirable organization) and Estonian government organizations, including the Republican Electoral Commission, and Leonid Volkov [the head of Navalny's headquarters network] ended up on it “quite by accident”. During this event, together with Volkov and other oppositionists, we had a private meeting with Estonian President Toomas Hendriks Ilves. The President during the meeting said that Estonia is interested not in a strong, not in a weak, but in a predictable Russia. In his opinion, under current President Vladimir Putin, Russia is unpredictable. The Estonian side expressed its intention to provide political asylum to the opposition in the event of serious problems in Russia. — What did Leonid Volkov do at this event? Was he an ordinary participant, like you? - On the one hand, yes, he was an ordinary participant, but at the same time, unlike me and other participants, he had a long tête-à-tête conversation in English with the Estonian president. They talked? The topic itself is not clear. It is known that the Estonian side was interested in the project of the "Opposition Coordinating Council" and, first of all, Alexei Navalny's prospects as a politician. - And at whose expense is the banquet? Who paid for the holding of such an event? - One of the funds of the American politician George Soros paid for the oppositionists' trip to this conference. The activists lived in a five-star hotel that previously hosted Valeria Novodvorskaya [the founder of the Soviet and Russian opposition right-wing liberal party Democratic Union] and Ilya Yashin [the head of the Krasnoselsky municipal district of Moscow], who lectured there. Tickets and full support were paid by the host. - It turns out that some American funds completely control the political agenda in some post-Soviet countries. And what other American foundations, besides the Soros Foundation, have you ever met? — I have dealt with such American foundations as the International Republican Institute (IRI) and the National Democratic Institute for International Affairs (NDI), which used to operate in our country. After pressure began on these funds, they moved from Russia to foreign countries. So, I met with representatives of the NDI in Tallinn through the "December 5 Party" and "PARNAS". At that time, it was possible to get invitations to these structures through influential oppositionists, for example, through Natalya Pelevina [member of the federal political council of the PARNAS party] and Vladimir Milov [host of the Navalny Live YouTube channel], who openly sent his people to IRI and NDI . It is worth noting that there was an unspoken rivalry between these two funds, since they are representatives of different US parties, and each of them cultivates activists loyal to itself in Russia. The NDI representative office, as I said above, is located in Tallinn, and the IRI representative office, in turn, is located in Warsaw. People from the National Endowment for Democracy (NED) also worked with the Russian opposition, which organized similar events throughout the Baltics. - How much money do American funds spend on the Russian opposition, and which of them is the most generous and influential? How, besides money, do such funds attract the oppositionists? — All the funds paid for the flights, meals and accommodation of the activists. Most of the money was given by the Soros Foundation. Such trips lasted up to five days on average. In addition to money, for example, the IRI helped with obtaining visas. — Were your “foreign meetings” limited to Russian participants or did they involve other representatives of the post-Soviet countries? — At such meetings, there were mainly only representatives from Russia. For Belarusians, such meetings were separate. The funds complained that a significant number of Belarusians used this to obtain political asylum in order to leave the country. It is interesting that some individual oppositionists from among the Russians also carried out similar schemes. — Who conducted the training and what did you talk about there? — The training was conducted by representatives of the US State Department and American political scientists who worked in political campaigns, as well as European political scientists from Lithuania, Poland and others countries. At the trainings, preparations were made for the participation of opposition candidates and parties in the elections, thought out to the smallest detail. European and American representatives received feedback from activists on the specifics of the Russian elections and what activists might be interested in hearing about such election campaigns. At such conferences, for example, the results of the Moscow mayoral elections in 2013 were discussed. In addition, there was actually preparation for the participation of the “Democratic Coalition” in the elections in Novosibirsk, Kaluga and Kostroma, which were held in 2015. — Which of the well-known oppositionists, except for Volkov, regularly participated in the activities of American foundations? Funds in addition to Volkov, another well-known oppositionist, Ilya Yashin, regularly traveled. Oleg Stepanov, the former coordinator of Navalny's headquarters in Moscow, also took part in IRI events. Stepanov wanted connections, access to private conversations with the leadership of such organizations. Stepanov got into these structures through Vladimir Milov. - How is the funding for such work, through cryptocurrency? - Not always. For example, there is an interesting practice when oppositionists are given cards of legal entities - and they anonymously withdraw funds from them. The issuers of these cards are foreign banks. It is a well-known fact that a couple of years ago large batches of such plastic cards for legal entities were brought to Russia from Georgia, Georgian banks acted as their issuers. Some of the Russian oppositionists, "happy cardholders", withdrew money right upon arrival in Russia, from ATMs at the airport. - Did any oddities happen to the participants of the trainings in Poland? - It was in Tallinn. I once picketed near the Russian embassy about the Bolotnaya case and in defense of political prisoners. He informed the American curators about the action in advance, to which he received their approval in response. But the Estonian police still took me away because of the picket, because they were called by the Russian embassy. True, already in the department, having learned that I was protesting against politics in Russia, they immediately let me go. - Which of the foreign politicians and participants have been to these trainings? - Among the judges were Lithuanians, Americans, Poles. The Mayor of Warsaw, the Polish representative of IRI Lukasz Kondraczuk, the representative of the headquarters of John McCain, who headed the IRI at that time, the head of the IRI programs for Russia and Eastern Europe, Chris Holzen, took part in the events for the training participants. In 2014-2015, during a trip to Warsaw, I I met with other opposition activists with a certain fund to support Ukraine, and there were, among other things, representatives of Armenia, Georgia, Azerbaijan, Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Moldova, and, for example, Andrei Parubiy [former speaker of the Rada]. In particular, he spoke about the interest in the Russian opposition to defeat the government, because then the war on the disputed territory would stop. All representatives of the liberal-democratic forces of the former Soviet republics were on the side of Ukraine and these funds. Even for us it was wild how much they consider Russia an enemy. We tried to explain to them that the Russian people and the Russian authorities should not be identified. We spoke there from the position of Russia and realized that on their part it was not even fear of Russia, but some kind of hatred towards us. And this political Russophobia will never end as long as Russia simply exists. These funds, by the way, work with representatives of the separatists and nurture them. For example, in Komi and Karelia. And in general they are trying to play on national contradictions. - How was the training? - We are coming to the country. Then we are settled in a hotel, where a conference room is rented next to or right in it. First comes the introductory part, where everyone first gets to know each other, then with the inviting party. Then we study for eight hours over three days. Only lecturers change. As a rule, NDI lecturers are not Russian-speaking, so they also order an interpreter. The events are closed to the press and are held exclusively for those who are invited. There is not much confidence in them either. The organizers are paranoid about agents, so they even ask you not to take smartphones with you to lectures. At the end of the training, students leave with a certain set of knowledge, notes, and homework. I'm not sure if this is recruitment, but for three days they also select potential personnel who can be useful in Russia. They first talk to you face-to-face, you talk about your projects in the Russian Federation, they see how useful it can be for them and what is needed for its implementation. Then they teach you how to find sponsors for this project and how to collect donations. Then you write a memorandum with proposals for your project, and then they think how to help you. These can be various projects with national groups, environmental ones, as well as for the preparation of municipal deputies. Now they have switched from Moscow and St. Petersburg to the regions. THE HAGUE, January 9. /TASS/. A Dutch court has blocked police access to the data seized from independent journalists after their return from Ukraine’s troubled Donbass, one of the affected journalists, freelancer Michel Spekkers told Tass on Monday.He said the Dutch Journalists Union intervened, and several hours after the equipment had been confiscated, the court banned access to the data.""That means they cannot access it anymore until judge orders them to do so,"" he said. ""But it is political, and you never know when it becomes political what they will or will not do. But I hope they will respect the law and I will get my data back,"" he added.""But they had few hours when there was no court order and they still could have a look at it. I don't know what happened within that timeframe,"" he stated.Michel Spekkers and his colleague Stefan Beck spent nine days in Donbass. After their return home on January 7, Dutch law enforcement agencies detained both at the airport and confiscated all materials gathered on the MH17 crash, as well as cameras, cellphones and notebooks.""All of the material collected by Michel Spekkers and me about the MH17 crash in Donbass (Lugansk and Donetsk) and other material, for example street interviews, has been confiscated by the police upon arrival to the Netherlands,"" Stefan Beck wrote on his Facebook page.The Dutch authorities have a wrong picture of the security situation at the MH17 crash site in Ukraine, Michel Spekkers told Tass. ""The Dutch government hides behind the fact that they cannot investigate more on the MH17 crash site because of insecurity situation there. I have been working there without feeling any risk,"" the journalist said.He said he had picked up and brought to the Netherlands some fragments of the Boeing as well as a bone fragment.""I took one fragment of the bone with me to investigate here what kind of bone it is. But I don’t know for sure (if it was human remaining), I cannot confirm. What I do know is when they confiscated it, two forensic policemen were there and they decided to send it to the lab for more investigation,"" the journalist said.He said he was ready to share the materials gathered in Donbass with the police, including photos from the crash site. On the eve of the 70th anniversary of the formation of the North Atlantic Alliance, the NATO Defense College presented three scenarios for the development of the organization - “good”, “bad” and “terrible”. Thus, with a “good” scenario, the military bloc will be able to overcome the crisis and move into a “new era” . As noted in the document, first of all, it is important to understand the goals of NATO in a world “where multipolarity is growing.” The author of the report is convinced that when forming the future goals of NATO, one should rely not on the financial or military component, but on the political rationale for presence in a particular region. “Recognizing that NATO's actions must always be within the limits of what is possible, the alliance should start with a fundamental political question - why should it work in, say, the Asian region. Another basic political issue that NATO should consider is what Russia’s revisionism is about,” the document says. If the “good” future is based on the common aspirations of NATO and European allies, then the “bad” organization tasks. “In such a “bad” future, political disunity and short-sightedness will lead to the regionalization of NATO and a decrease in the role of the alliance in matters of world order,” the document emphasizes. the security of the participating countries. “In short, the expanded presence of US forces in Europe seems to be a consequence of the priorities of the American defense establishment, which, in a certain sense, is under political siege,” the report says. Dmitry Abzalov, President of the Center for Strategic Communications, believes that the United States often uses the North Atlantic Alliance to solve its own geopolitical problems, drawing NATO members into a confrontation with China or into military operations in the Middle East, for example, in Syria. “An attempt to politicize NATO, use its specific projects has a very negative impact on the position of the North Atlantic Alliance. Against the backdrop of a difficult economic situation in some countries, against the background of simply right-wing sentiments and a more nationally oriented military alliance, which does not meet the interests of the European Union, is perceived negatively - and the prospects for the organization become very vague, ”the expert emphasized. Russia is mentioned in all three scenarios . Thus, in a "good" scenario, NATO and its allies need to take into account Russia's alleged desire to revise the world order. In the "bad" scenario, it is predicted that NATO will be able to deter attacks on its territory, while being forced to avoid internal political division due to the use of "soft power" by Russia. In the most unfavorable scenario for the alliance, a change in US priorities towards Asia will lead to an increase in the importance of Russia in countering continental threats. Experts believe that for NATO, the “Russian threat” is now the only way to explain the existence of the organization and the need to maintain its defense capability. So, according to Abzalov, the unity of the North Atlantic Alliance can only be ensured by a common enemy or a common goal. “Since NATO is a military alliance, the enemy is the main organizing component of the political bloc. Therefore, Moscow attracts the interests of the main players. If Moscow ceases to be a potential adversary, the question will arise: what is the military bloc against, against what type of military threat?” - the expert believes. Political scientist Alexander Asafov agrees with this, who believes that it is beneficial for NATO to perceive Russia as the "heir of the Soviet Union." Soviet Union, which is spelled out in a number of American documents. In their understanding, Russia wants to return to the status of the Soviet Union and again influence the world, violating what the Americans usually declare - the Constitution, democracy and human freedoms, ”Asafov explained. Recall that in March 2019, the NATO Defense College also released a report , where he analyzed the exercises "Vostok-2018". The authors of the document came to the conclusion that Moscow is building up its military potential, allegedly for waging a large-scale war. The Swedish Defense Research Institute (FOI) previously stated, based on data from open sources, that Moscow was conducting large-scale military exercises to work out the outbreak of armed conflicts, and also allegedly to prepare for war with NATO countries or with China. However, according to experts, it becomes more difficult every year to create the concept of a “Russian threat” in the absence of actual actions on the part of Russia. Thus, the European allies of NATO are beginning to get tired of the Russian agenda, Dmitry Abzalov believes. And the construction of this agenda is a very big challenge to the future of NATO, because in fact it is very difficult to sell the concept of a military alliance, which operates in a system of bilateral confrontation, when there is no second part, the second pole, ”Abzalov noted. He added that in the modern realities of NATO appears to be an archaic organization unable to respond to modern threats. At the same time, the European Union is increasingly talking about the need for cooperation in the field of defense and security. Thus, French President Emmanuel Macron in November 2018 proposed the creation of a pan-European army. “We will not be able to protect the Europeans if we do not decide to create a real pan-European army. We must have a Europe that defends itself mostly on its own - without relying entirely on the United States," Macron emphasized. Not a word in Russian. In Latvia, they want to conduct school classes exclusively in the Latvian language. The majority of parliamentarians voted for the corresponding amendments to the law on education. They were met by hundreds of protesters with placards in defense of Russian schools near the Seimas building. "Toxic Law", "Educational Poison", "Ethnic Discrimination"! The controversial educational reform in Latvia is overgrown with new - to put it mildly, unflattering - reviews. For several months now, demonstrations against the total "Latvianization" of schools have not subsided all over the country. Hundreds of people took to the rally in front of the Seimas building, where the deputies overwhelmingly approved the controversial bill, since early morning. The protesters are trying to understand why the authorities do not take into account the interests of parents, and most importantly, why they are trying to destroy the Russian community in Latvia with all their might. Primary classes will still retain their bilingualism. But already from the 7th grade, just when the most difficult subjects are taught, the vast majority of classes will be in Latvian. Well, in high school, that is, from grades 10 to 12, the Russian language will be completely banned. Opponents of the reform are sure that the new bill will divide the Latvian society in half. They tried to abandon the Russian authorities in Latvia before. Back in 2004, all schools wanted to be translated into the state language. The Constitutional Court of the country opposed the initiative. The law was later criticized at the UN. In Latvia, they took a step back: they agreed that only 60 percent of education should be conducted in Latvian. And now, more than 10 years later, Riga has finally decided to complete what it started. The State Language Center has been operating in the country for a long time. The locals secretly call it the "linguistic police" or even the "inquisition". For 25 years, this body has been checking all civil servants. If someone in the workplace, according to the Center, is not good enough in the Latvian language, he must pay a fine of up to 250 euros. A repeated violation can cost a job. These almost medieval measures could be perceived as an unsuccessful joke, if not for one ""but"". From experiments with language, the most important thing suffers - education. According to local information agencies, even 10-20 years ago Latvia competed with the same Germany and Japan in terms of the quality of schools. Now it is adjacent in the world rankings to the Dominican Republic and Chile. And with the new reform, experts are sure, the educational peak will only continue. INTERFAX.RU - The head of the Defense and Security Committee, Viktor Ozerov, called the bill on control over Russian ports approved by the US House of Representatives absurd, since Moscow strictly complies with the UN Security Council resolution on sanctions against the DPRK. but they will not let them into territorial waters without permission. This bill is absurd, it looks like a fairy tale,” Ozerov told Interfax on Friday. “The Russian Federation strictly observes sanctions against the DPRK. Russia is a responsible state, and if the UN Security Council voted for restrictive measures against Pyongyang, we will implement them," Ozerov said, recalling that Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a decree banning not only supplies from the Russian Federation, but also transit through Russia of equipment and materials prohibited by UN Security Council resolution. "" How the US will control our ports remains unclear. We are a sovereign state,” the head of the relevant committee of the upper house of the Russian parliament emphasized. “If the current generation of American congressmen have not understood this yet, they have a unique chance,” the senator said. “How the United States is going to exercise this control, completely incomprehensible. And it is quite obvious that Russia will not allow such control to be exercised, "" Alexei Pushkov, head of the Federation Council commission on information policy, member of the Federation Council's defense committee, told Interfax on Friday. "I believe that the law is unenforceable, contrary to international law and absurd in essence, "" the senator added. So he commented on media reports that the day before the House of Representatives of the US Congress adopted a bill to strengthen sanctions against North Korea, which, in particular, suggests that the US administration can take special control over the ports of Vladivostok, Nakhodka and Vanino in terms of their implementation of the sanctions regime. According to the draft, the US president should send a report to Congress on ports and airports that violate the resolutions of the UN Security Council regarding Pyongyang. According to Pushkov, American control over Russian ports is simply impossible. "Where did they even see this? And how are they going to exercise this control? Will they set up a blockade of our ports and will check the ships that pass? They will not be allowed into the ports, this is quite obvious, "" the senator said. This bill "" implies a gross violation of international law, since control over its own ports and territorial waters is carried out by the state to which these ports belong, "" Pushkov said. "I don't remember anything like that. This is some kind of wartime legislative action, it seems to me absolutely beyond common sense, "" the senator noted. He is deeply convinced that if the same demand is made against China, then a similar negative reaction will follow." "Korean nuclear program both Russia, China and other states are concerned, but with this law the United States turns this issue, which should be the subject of negotiations, not into the sphere of interaction, but into the sphere of automatic conflict," Pushkov believes. He called the American bill "a direct attempt on the sovereignty of another state, and in this case the Russian Federation. "The senator does not understand what the American parliamentarians proceeded from when they adopted this bill, but he is sure that the document has a high chance of acquiring the status of a law. Earlier, the media reported that on the eve of the House of Representatives of Congress The United States has adopted a bill to strengthen sanctions against North Korea, which, in particular, suggests that the US administration can take special control over the ports of Vladivostok, Nakhodka and Vanino in terms of their implementation of the sanctions regime. The purpose of the bill is to ensure control over the implementation of UN Security Council resolutions that restrict North Korea's trade with other countries. It is forbidden to supply weapons to North Korea, as well as missile, nuclear and other technologies.
