Veterans from different countries came to St. Petersburg this weekend. Special attention to those who were born and grew up in the city during the blockade. People who survived those terrible years are returning to memorable places. For many, a visit to their homeland is not only a tribute to memory, but also an opportunity to freely express their opinion. Khanon Zelikovich is one of those who managed to survive in the siege of Leningrad to spite the Nazis. After 75 years, he is an academician and professor of institutes in various countries. He says that the key to this success was laid in those very years of difficult childhood. Therefore, you need to work for yourself and for the people who gave all their strength to save the city. At the age of 24, the future scientist moved to Estonia, but visits his native land with pleasure. Here he can meet with classmates, recall past years and freely discuss the tragedy he experienced. It becomes more and more difficult to do this abroad every year. Valentina Petrovna also came to take a break from European restrictions and honor the memory of relatives who died in besieged Leningrad. She has been living in Latvia for more than half a century, but she visited her homeland on a memorable date. The products that are traditionally served to guests on Memorial Day have long become conventional symbols. In fact, the blockade survivors did not forget the taste of bread made from husks and sawdust, wallpaper glue and tooth powder were used as food. Until now, some children of the blockade do not leave a single crumb on the dishes. Every day of the defense of Leningrad saved not only the inhabitants of the city, but the whole country. Numerous troops thrown into destruction were pinned down and could not support the attack on Moscow. It is impossible to understand this without knowledge of history. The siege survivors consider it their duty to the new generation to sort out the facts of long-past events. Therefore, today they arrived in St. Petersburg. Let us recall that earlier it was reported that in St. Petersburg they could put on a performance based on the found manuscript of the memoirs of the blockade.

On April 7, 2014, the Donetsk People's Republic was proclaimed. This day divided the life of Russians into before and after. There is no doubt that this event was the logical conclusion of the anti-Russian policy of the Ukrainian elites. However, if before the “Maidan” the Ukrainization of Donbass went on mostly without bloodshed, then in the spring of 2014 seven Maidan Ukraine became a quasi-state. Everything that could be destroyed was destroyed. The monopoly on the use of force passed from the hands of the authorities into the hands of the radicals. The so-called heroes of the “revolution of dignity” walked the streets, and it was they who decided who was right and who was wrong. At that moment, events began in the southeastern part of the country, which went down in history under the name "Russian Spring". On March 18, Crimea and Sevastopol became part of Russia and set an example for other regions. By April 7, the regional administrations in Kharkiv, Lugansk and Donetsk were occupied. On this day, the Kharkov and Donetsk People's Republics were proclaimed. In Lugansk, they dragged on, but in the end, on April 27, the republic was proclaimed. On April 7, 2014, for the first time in Ukraine, the concept of “ATO” (anti-terrorist operation) was heard, and it continues in its “revised” form to this day. Acting President of Ukraine Oleksandr Turchynov then said: "The National Security and Defense Council decided to launch a large-scale anti-terrorist operation involving the Armed Forces of Ukraine." The first victim of the ATO was the Kharkiv People's Republic. Arrived from Vinnitsa special forces "Jaguar" stormed the building of the regional state administration. The activists were detained. The Republic is gone. This has not happened in Donetsk. The power of the DPR expanded, and gradually the cities of the former Donetsk region passed under new flags. An important date was April 12, when a detachment of 52 people under the command of Igor Strelkov occupied Slavyansk. The arrival of Strelkov was perceived as a certain victory, as the fact that soon the Ukrainian government in the Donbass would finally collapse. At first, there was even an opinion that these very “polite people” had arrived from Crimea. From Crimea, but not "little green men", but ordinary Russian men who organized themselves and came to help other Russians. On April 15, Ukrainian armored vehicles appeared on the Donbas horizon. Fighting began for Slavyansk, which lasted until July 5, 2014, when parts of the militia left the city. We must not forget that on May 11, a referendum was held in the DPR, where citizens were asked the only question: do you support the Act of State Independence of the Donetsk People's Republic? It would be worthwhile to initiate a case against journalists for disseminating knowingly unreliable information. The European Parliament's Committee on Civil Liberties, Justice and Home Affairs backed an initiative that would require Georgian citizens to undergo "pre-authorisation" before traveling to Europe without a visa. Tbilisi believes that by doing so, the EU, on the one hand, is reacting to the flow of illegal emigrants from Georgia, which increased after the abolition of Schengen visas this spring, and on the other hand, does not want to openly spoil relations with the Georgian authorities. The visa-free regime with the EU, we recall, has so far been considered the main achievement of Tbilisi on the path to European integration. Photo: Safron Golikov, Kommersant / buy photoDeputy Foreign Minister Vakhtang Makharoblishvili told reporters about the decision of the European Parliament Committee and its possible consequences for Georgian citizens wishing to visit the EU . He asked not to equate the so-called pre-authorization with a "visa". To pass it, a citizen must fill out a special application in electronic form on the page of the European Traveler Authorization System, attach to it certificates of employment and income, which were submitted to the consular departments of embassies before the abolition of visas, pay € 10 and wait for confirmation of the right to enter the Schengen area .The answer may well turn out to be negative. However, Vakhtang Makharoblishvili reassured that the new norms have so far “only been approved in advance.” According to the former rector of the Tbilisi Diplomatic Academy, Iosif Tsintsadze, “preliminary authorization” is nothing more than a form of visa, but with a different name. “Refusing people directly at the border, at a European airport, is always more troublesome for European services than in the course of electronic correspondence,” Kommersant’s interlocutor believes, explaining the innovation by the flow of illegal immigrants from Georgia. “Since March 28 (when the visa-free regime came into force - Kommersant”), thousands of Georgians have remained in the EU, and Brussels cannot but react,” Mr. Tsintsadze said, noting that the European Union “does not want to openly insult Georgia by restoring visa regime, therefore, it is softer.” According to official data, only in the first three months of the visa-free regime, about 3 thousand Georgians did not return from European countries to their homeland within the time frame established by the agreement with Brussels. We recall that it was about the opportunity to visit the EU countries without visas exclusively for short-term visits (90 days within 180 days). George Dvali, Tbilisi_x000D_ In March, Georgia officially became the second post-Soviet country after Moldova (not counting the Baltic states), whose citizens can to enter the Schengen area without a visa. One of the first to use the visa-free regime was Prime Minister Giorgi Kvirikashvili, who went to Athens and Brussels at the end of March to "personally thank his European colleagues." As expected, in the first round of the 2020 parliamentary elections in Georgia, despite many attempts, we again got bipolar elections, in which the Georgian Dream and the National Movement officially fight each other, and unofficially they coexist perfectly, writes Beso Barbakadze on the pages of the publication "Georgia and the World". In the article “Broom Syndrome and Western Legitimation of Elections”, the author reports that about 30 deputies will be promoted to parliament by “nationals”, up to 90 deputies by “dreamers”, the rest will be thrown a gnawed bone, and for the next four years we will again walk along the same circle. The external course, of course, will again be Western, that is, we will continue to knock on NATO's doors. We will again ask to be admitted to the European Union, and they will tell us again: you have waited 30 years, wait a little more, 30 years, that is. Unfortunately, this is the reality in which we live, but these elections showed much more. "(" Bump "), that is, the party whose leader publicly declares, they say, give me the reins of government, and tomorrow I will announce the full legalization of drugs. The leader who does not hide the fact that he is an active consumer of marijuana and even grows it at home. It turns out that there are 34,000 people in Georgia who really want this, and, unfortunately, most of them are young people. Almost 300,000 voters missed the time when we couldn’t say anything to each other over the phone except for greetings. When dozens of bodies were taken out of prisons every day. When people were shot in the streets. When with the money from the taxes we paid, they walked with prostitutes and the photos depicting this were posted on social networks. That is, 300 thousand people missed the broom, and we should call this not the Stockholm syndrome, but the broom syndrome. And there is no need to talk about the fact that the former government held the entire people hostage and in their hands, like the “Zugdidi Zorro” - a “lemon” without a check. Approximately 37,000 votes went to the Alliance of Patriots, that is, the only party that in her election promises, she clearly said: we must definitely talk with Russia, not fight, not scold from the international platform, but talk. What happens? Only 37,000 people support dialogue with Russia? And this, moreover, when retired European leaders directly say that for Georgia the keys of territorial integrity are in Russia, and our country should talk with its northern neighbor. In general, we have an excessive dose of jingoism, and we are good at beating ourselves in the chest with our fists, but when it comes down to it, we refuse dialogue, from sitting at the same table. We are not having elections, but, apparently, general lunacy. And this is manifested at least in the fact that Girchi won so many votes. 34 thousand people voted for the complete degradation of youth, for the destruction of the future. We, Georgians, are forgetful, but not to the extent that we do not remember the immediate past, when the whole of Georgia was on medication. And the Georgian paradox - drug addiction was considered something cool, especially in the capital. After all, representatives of the generation that were saved say that a whole generation died then, thousands of young people died stoned ... Yes, these people have gone through all this, they know how difficult it is to get rid of such an infection. They also know that if all this takes on a large-scale character, then there will be an avalanche effect, and this avalanche at the “foot of the mountain” will demolish everyone and everything. In parallel, the world is tightening approaches in this direction. Even America, which has imposed a liberal attitude towards drugs on us, is taking the strictest measures, because it has understood that the future generation has gone crazy, and ... We are facilitating approaches in this regard, and all because the people, it turns out, want a buzz. In general, the state approach has changed. Now let's name a place where you can come at any time, try both marijuana and hashish ... This institution is called the "Factory", and there every day several hundred young, drugged, stand, sit or lie down and smoke what Girchi promised them. Well, let's say that the government has legalized marijuana smoking. But where does it come from, at least it can be found out? After all, cultivation and, moreover, sale are prohibited by law. Why doesn't this hotbed disperse the authorities?! And if we say that the interests of state high officials are involved in all this, won't we be right? We will, so what? In accordance with the percentages, Girchi will create a faction in the parliament, and the faction has the right to register a law. What do you think will happen when they register the promise, and then the ambassadors wag their finger at the parties aligned with the West - they say, pass this law? They will accept it simply, and then we will not be able to forbid anything to our children. And we can’t do without it, because, “thanks” to a thousand non-governmental organizations, even if you raise your voice, you can be deprived of parental rights. We don’t need any referendum or poll, these elections have shown our problem so clearly that no one could do anything better would. We should also not forget that schoolchildren and students who have switched to distance learning due to the pandemic cannot get used to this form and are not particularly eager to learn. Accordingly, they have more free time, which is by no means spent on studying, and they spend more and more time on the street. In general, I am not against being on the street, but when drugs are sold almost from the counter, when gambling is available on the Internet, everything is already dangerous. We are losing a generation, the generation that should build the future of Georgia and simply take care of us. We lose this generation, and there will be a drug-obsessed, uneducated crowd. It is the crowd that is the unity of people who have no education, who only think about where to get money for drugs. The most interesting thing is that the losing parties say that the elections are rigged, and thereby directly offend the voter. In fact, they believe that even more people should have supported drugs, brooms, an uncertain future, knocking on NATO doors, and the stillborn prospect of joining the European Union. This is a direct insult to the people, and I think we deserve it. But how, otherwise, did so many people gather, how did they decide, how did they come to the conclusion that it was necessary to vote for what I listed above?! Do not take it as if we are obsessed supporters of the “Dream”. On the contrary, the fact that the ruling team still remains in power is the merit only of the fact that the rest are no good, and in reality people made a choice between bad and worse. When you choose the worst in that worst, this is already a big problem. If you like, call it a problem of thinking, if you like, call it something else. But the problem is obvious. Another year will pass, elections will come to local self-government, and these more than 300 thousand people will be here again and at the local level will vote for tormentors and drug lovers. They will already distribute it in the regions, in self-government bodies, and for some reason we believe that this is precisely their goal. Whose? Those who write us the Constitution and teach us how to live. So what if they themselves no longer do the same, they realized that it was bad. And they look at us like guinea pigs, they should test us, whether this is good or bad. And if in our case it is not justified, then it is really bad. You probably also remember how everyone and sundry yelled that Russia would interfere in these elections. Intervened? No. And the West? It is Western ambassadors and Western observers who legitimize our elections (and not the people of Georgia). And don't say no now. They forced us to rewrite the Constitution, laws, painted our agenda. And nothing if they force you to write percentages or confirm. Who will resist? In the summer of 2020, NATO exercises Defender Europe-2020 died down in Eastern European territory. These maneuvers were supposed to be the largest over the past 25 years, but the coronavirus made its own adjustments, forcing NATO strategists to moderate their ardor a little and reduce the scale of the exercises. However, by the beginning of 2021, life slowly began to return to normal, and with it the aggressive rhetoric of individual In particular, the commander of the US Army in Europe and Africa, Lieutenant General Christopher Cavoli, said that the past, albeit not in full force, Defender Europe-2020 exercises proved the importance of using special units in operations in the European theater of operations (theatre) – Multidomain task force (MDTF).""A multidomain task force will be able to provide the capabilities, integration and expertise that will be critical to renew strategy on the European continent. We will also be able to extend this experience to the African continent when we get such opportunities, "" Defense News quoted General Cavoli as saying. According to the general, Washington has been going to deploy MDTF in Europe for a long time, and for several years the US has been unsuccessfully trying to turn its concept of multi-domain warfare into a doctrine. ""The trend for multi-domain, or cross-domain, operations has become somewhat of a mainstream in recent years. In principle, this is logical, because the combat environments are mixed and due to this a certain synergistic effect is achieved," Dmitry Stefanovich, a researcher at the Center for International Security of the IMEMO RAS, told the Baltnews portal. For the first time, the concept of multi-domain operations (Multi-Domain Operations, MDO) was presented in the brochure Multi-Domain Warfare: The Evolution of Combined Arms Operations in the 21st Century, 2025-2040. This document was released by the US Army Construction Training and Research Command (TRADOC) in December 2017. The idea of this concept is that the US Army must be ready to fight in five environments: land, sea, air, space and cyberspace. ""On the one hand, this allows you to maximize the effect in all these environments - for example, if we are conducting a land battle with conventional ground forces and suddenly the air force is connected to it, then it becomes more difficult for the enemy. If the naval forces are involved, then it is even more difficult. And if at the same time counteraction begins on the enemy’s networks using cyber and electronic warfare, then it gets even worse," Stefanovich noted. "This is due to the fact that in modern warfare everything is interconnected. So, due to increased communication capabilities, infantrymen on the battlefield can request air support at any time. Due to the fact that there is full integration with space, it is possible to receive target designations for ships and aircraft. Such things allow you to maximize the striking power of your forces, "" the military analyst added. As Defense News writes, today one MDTF is stationed at the joint Lewis-McChord base in Washington state, and the American command planned to create a second such group in the Pacific region already in this year. According to Dmitry Stefanovich, due to the fact that the Baltic countries border on Russian territory, it is obvious that they can be used for some potentials related to intelligence activities, electronic warfare and radar detection. "" In the sense of conventional armed forces The Baltic countries cannot provide anything special, but, for example, in the field of cyber attacks, their potential is quite good - it’s not for nothing that NATO’s center of excellence in this area is located in Tallinn," the expert noted. Defense Center of Excellence - NATO CCD COE) was launched in May 2008. As stated on the website of the organization, its main mission is exclusively the exchange of experience between the member countries of the alliance in the field of cyber defense research. However, in fact, within the framework of the annual Locked Shields exercises, CCD COE experts regularly train skills such as hacker attacks on various devices and equipment. Of course, with the development of modern computer technologies, cyber wars have become an objective reality, and any state should be prepared for them, which means one must, as they say, know the enemy by sight. But the concept of MDO, which was announced by the commander of the American army in Europe, is precisely offensive. And here the experience of the Baltic hackers will find its application. At first glance, it may seem that the MDO concept assigns an auxiliary character to actions in cyberspace, such as suppressing enemy computer attacks and ensuring communication between one’s own units. But in fact, this particular environment can have an unpredictable and even fatal value that can turn a local clash at the border into a real military conflict between powers. As many military analysts note, when conducting combat operations in cyberspace, the risk of causing accidental damage is even higher than the risk of unintentional damage when using traditional weapons. What catastrophic consequences can lead to " "combat cybernetic operation", the object of which will be, for example, the combat control system of the strategic nuclear forces of one of the parties to a possible conflict, it is even scary to imagine. there will be an understanding of who is doing what and why, which can lead to a real conflict: "" The best thing that can be offered here is that all talk about new concepts of military operations be on the agenda of negotiations between the military and diplomats of Russia and the military and diplomats NATO countries in order to avoid a situation of some kind of unprovoked aggression or accidental escalation," the military expert concluded. The exact dates of Tuesday's videoconference were not announced in advance, but Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has been talking for three weeks about his intention to hold a meeting in the Normandy format. As a result, Zelensky was not invited to the talks - the Kremlin made it clear that it was not going to talk now with the politician violating the truce and escalating the situation in the Donbass. But formally, Ukraine remained on the sidelines because the three leaders had many topics to discuss - including those for which the troika format could be used. Putin did not communicate with Merkel and Macron for less than three months - but since their phone calls negotiations in early January (one on one, not three), the situation escalated not only in the Donbass, but also in relations between the West and Russia as a whole. Although it would seem that there is much to escalate, but Biden's assumption of office and Europe's reaction to the replacement of Navalny's suspended sentence with a real one showed new depths of fall. In Moscow, they began to say directly that relations with the European Union are frozen - and not through our fault or initiative. At the same time, both Europe as a whole and the leaders of individual states in particular, in reality, cannot afford to put relations with Moscow on pause - on the contrary, they, based on their own interests, including domestic political ones, need an active Eastern policy (not to mention the interaction with Russia on various regional crises). But how to carry it out without negotiations? So we talked - and on many topics at once. From Ukraine to Libya, from Russian vaccines to Iran. Navalny and Lukashenka have not been forgotten. There are no breakthroughs on any point, and there could not have been - even the announcement of work on the registration and production of Sputnik V in the EU was quite expected. Because here Europe has a specific interest and the ability to solve something - but on other topics there is no opportunity (Iran) or desire (Ukraine). Not for the first time, Macron and Merkel wanted Russia "" to make a firm commitment to stabilize the ceasefire in Ukraine and work out a way out of the crisis while respecting the Minsk agreements," and offered Putin a meeting in the "Normandy format" with Zelensky's participation. So far, such a meeting has zero prospects, especially since in response Putin expressed "serious concern over the escalation of the armed confrontation provoked by Ukraine on the line of contact." Berlin and Paris are not ready to force Ukraine into a direct dialogue with the Donbass and constitutional reform, and without this, you can’t imagine any progress in the settlement. However, it will now be more difficult for Kiev to speculate on the topic of a new war in the Donbass - Macron and Merkel, in theory, should clearly explain to Zelensky that Putin cannot be persuaded to negotiate in this way. "nationwide inclusive dialogue and free elections"" Putin noted the inadmissibility of external interference in the internal affairs of a sovereign state. This was also implied when discussing the "position of Mr. Alexei Navalny" - when Merkel and Macron "drawn President Putin's attention to the need to respect his rights in accordance with the European Convention on Human Rights and Health. Touching concern for the health of someone who is perceived in Russia as nothing more than a person working for external interests. The story with Navalny has already affected relations between Russia and Europe, but are the Europeans ready to continue using this topic to maintain additional tension? Do they understand that there will be no so-called concessions on this issue - and as an instrument of pressure on Putin, the Navalny issue is not only useless, but also counterproductive? After all, it is clear that Russia will not allow any interference in its internal affairs, including through the campaign around Navalny. At the same time, Putin’s statement that we are ready to “restore normal, depoliticized interaction with the EU, if There will be mutual interest in this. Yes, depoliticized - that is, without these primitive methods of pressure and manipulation: ""What do you have with Navalny?" "We do not get into your internal affairs - why do you allow yourself to interfere in ours? Everything is simple - if there is a desire, there will be a dialogue. The problem, however, is that, by and large, there is no one to talk with. No, not after the death of Gandhi, but in the current European situation. And even more so in the case of Merkel and Macron. They are absolutely incapable of solving (or at least trying to) strategic issues - they are concerned about internal affairs. Merkel will step down as Chancellor in the fall, but the German political landscape is becoming more and more complicated, and now she is most concerned about how to transfer power to her party member, or at least an ally from the Bavarian Christian Socialist party. And Macron faces the most difficult presidential elections next spring, in which he is not at all guaranteed re-election - and he will be opposed not just by the opposition, but by the counter-elite Marine Le Pen. And this is not to mention the geopolitical weakness of the EU in general and Germany and France in particular. Yes, Germany's position on Nord Stream 2 does not depend on the name of the chancellor - protecting the gas pipeline meets German geopolitical interests. But does the support of the Anglo-Saxon game with Ukraine, the promise of its European integration and atlantization, answer them? Of course not - but neither Berlin nor Paris is able to resist it. But without a solution to the Ukrainian issue, Europe's relations with Russia will always be vulnerable to the influence of the Atlanticists - that is, Moscow will always perceive European leaders, at best, as dependent politicians, as people with limited geopolitical capabilities and weakened sovereignty. And here our "" Sputnik V "" will not help them - because we have immunity to external interference (acquired, or rather, restored, not so long ago - however, at a very high price), while the Europeans have critically weakened it. But it is never too late to gather strength and take care of your health - the main thing is to stop pretending that you do not know your diagnosis. In order to properly understand the essence of Belarusian-Russian relations, it is necessary to clearly understand the meaning of post-Soviet history. Let's start from the indisputable. The destruction of the USSR is a geopolitical catastrophe. The wreckage of the same geopolitical catastrophe - the so-called new independent states in the post-Soviet space. Formally, these are states. In fact - a kind of specific principalities, which were under external control from the West. Hence the idea of integrating the post-Soviet space as a necessary condition for liberation from Western external control and the restoration of true independence, real, and not paper statehood. This is also the reason for the complexity of building the Union State and integration in general, since the way out of the situation of geopolitical catastrophe involves the rejection of specific statehood and the recognition of a common national interest for all post-Soviet entities. Recognition of this is given with difficulty, since the rejection of appanage requires a fundamentally new level of political and state thinking, an understanding that the integration of the post-Soviet space just ensures the restoration of real statehood. But this statehood is precisely integration, and not disintegration, which is exactly what the current one is. It is important to see the fundamental difference between integration statehood and disintegration statehood. Integration statehood is real statehood, disintegration statehood is specific, i.e. imaginary statehood. Now we are in a situation where the process of transition from disintegration (imaginary) to integration (genuine) statehood is being carried out. This process is contradictory, when the old (the disintegration of the post-Soviet space) hinders and counteracts the development of the new (the integration of the post-Soviet space). But here the main thing is not to become discouraged and to understand that until the new (integration) finally overcomes the old (disintegration), there will be difficulties in union building. The paradox is that the small fragments of the geopolitical catastrophe, in contrast to the large fragment (the Russian Federation), are more committed to maintaining their appanage (disintegration). It seems to them that they have reached the maximum in their statehood, hence their desire to conserve the disintegration stage of their existence, not realizing that by doing so they conserve their quasi-statehood and are deprived of true statehood. A good example is Ukraine. At the same time, one must understand that a certain stagnation in the construction of the Union State is due to the exhaustion of the first stage of union construction. Joint union programs, industrial cooperation between Belarusian and Russian enterprises, the social policy of the Union State, a coordinated foreign and defense policy, the Parliamentary Assembly of the Union of Belarus and Russia are the limit of the first stage of union building. To continue to remain at this stage means to crush water in a mortar. As a rule, when analyzing this “geopolitical catastrophe of the 20th century,” they confine themselves to a narrow economic approach. Usually they talk about the fall in the gross domestic product, the decline in the living standards of the people, the severance of production and cooperation ties, the demographic crisis, the degradation of science and culture, and so on. Of course, all this is correct. But all these enumerations of the negative consequences of the destruction of the USSR for our peoples do not notice the main thing. Namely: the destroyers of the USSR directed their main blow against our all-Russian civilization, against the historical consciousness of our peoples. And not only against Soviet history, but also against the entire Russian civilization. Why are not only many discussions unfolding around the Union State of Belarus and Russia, the unity of our fraternal peoples, not only many different, often directly opposite, opinions are expressed, but also a large-scale information war is being waged? Because the opponents of the Union State are well aware that peoples deprived of historical memory, having lost their civilizational characteristics, are incapable of any historical life, find themselves outside historical time and space, disappear from history as peoples. It is necessary to understand that without Russia, without the Russian people Belarus and Belarusians would have disappeared long ago, and instead of Belarus there would be Polish kresy, and instead of Belarusians, amorphous ethnographic material and Polish settlers. Thus, the Union State is objectively the key issue of post-Soviet reality for understanding the future development prospects of our countries, since the entry of our peoples onto the allied trajectory of movement means their return to their all-Russian civilization, to their all-Russian history. But the return to one's civilization is at the same time a return to one's statehood, and consequently, the restoration of one's independence and sovereignty. Indeed, if our peoples finally return to their all-Russian civilization, then all attempts by the opponents of the Union State to impose on Belarus and Russia the policy of continuing the geopolitical catastrophe will fail. the movement of our countries along the path of union building, the opponents of the Union State are replacing civilization with geography, the national and cultural values of our peoples with the so-called European values. Their logic is as follows: since Belarus is geographically a European country, then, therefore, it belongs to the European civilization and European statehood. Hence their kindergarten desire to make East Slavic Switzerland out of Belarus. But such logic is absolutely erroneous, because the Belarusians will not become Europeans. In fact, having lost their identity, they will fall out of History as such. Coronavirus has demonstrated the true results of European integration The coronavirus epidemic in Lithuania has clearly demonstrated the results of democratic reforms on the way to a “bright European future”. At the very beginning of the 21st century, medicine and healthcare were optimized in Lithuania, as a result of which the number of medical institutions was sharply reduced - all small ones were closed and only large ones were left. Today, there are only five medical centers in the country in the largest cities - in Kaunas, Klaipeda, Siauliai, Panevezys and Vilnius. In the districts, there was something like paramedical stations for providing ambulance. If there are few hospitals, then there are few doctors - and today this problem is one of the main ones, we have to involve senior students of medical universities in the fight against the epidemic, but still there are sorely lacking specialists. Lithuanian Minister of Defense Raimundas Karoblis has already promised that the military will be sent to help the doctors, but would anyone want to be treated not by a doctor, but, for example, by an artilleryman? The second problem related to the consequences of "democratic reforms" is that the country does not have strategic food reserves. Although just a few days ago - on March 19 - Lithuanian Prime Minister Saulius Skvernelis assured the population of the country that there are enough products in the "bins of the motherland" and there is no reason for concern. But everything was spoiled by the former Minister of Agriculture Kazys Starkevicius, who told reporters that there is cause for concern and it lies in the fact that there is no strategic food supply in Lithuania. “In 2010, in case of emergencies, 200 thousand cans of canned pork, 3.5 thousand tons of wheat flour, 1.6 thousand tons of rice, 1.3 thousand tons of semolina, 700 tons of sugar were purchased for state reserve warehouses. According to the Ministry of Agriculture, today the food reserve consists only of grain and sugar. The rest of the stocks have been eaten up,” said Kazys Starkevicius. According to him, in 2012 amendments to the law on the state reserve were adopted, according to which "reserves were accumulated on the basis of preliminary agreements." This meant that companies, receiving money in advance, undertook to supply everything necessary for the needs of the population in an extreme situation. However, today no one really knows which companies are suppliers, moreover, in the context of the global crisis, it is not known whether these suppliers will be able to provide the country with everything necessary. Starkevičius recalled that only in January of this year, more than 9,000 tons of chicken meat were produced in Lithuania, 40% of which was exported, and the rest was eaten. And nothing got into the state reserve. The ex-head of the Ministry of Agriculture insists that it is urgent to provide assistance to farmers who today not only have nothing to buy fertilizers and spare parts for equipment, but it is generally impossible to buy planting material due to quarantine restrictions. This year's harvest is already in jeopardy, Starkevicius warned. The Belarusian Orthodox Church celebrated the 30th anniversary of the formation of the Belarusian Exarchate and is preparing for large-scale celebrations on the occasion of the 500th anniversary of the main spiritual center of Belarusian Orthodoxy - the Zhirovichi Monastery. The Primate of the BOC, Metropolitan Pavel, summed up the results and spoke about his plans in an exclusive interview with Sputnik. I am sincerely glad that we have wonderful relations between the church and the state. This is a special institution that is above politics. We do not interfere in state or political affairs, but we are concerned with the soul and heart of every person. And government leaders realized that the church is not an opposing group, but those who are trying to do everything to transform our lives. Therefore, in 2003, it was decided to conclude an agreement on cooperation between the church and the state. It works and bears fruit. It is very important that the church is free today. The most important thing is that we have the opportunity to confess our faith. We are pleased with such a mood on the part of the secular authorities - no one dominates the believers. We pray for world peace, for authorities and warriors, for the weather, for a good harvest. After all, the church does not teach anything bad. Do not steal, do not kill, do not deceive, do not bear false witness. These are the values that the Lord gave and which are the basis of human life. And the 1000-year history has shown harmony in the relationship between church and state. After all, there were no cases when the church betrayed its people, its state and its flock. The Belarusian people know the price of peace, they know what confrontation, enmity and hatred on a religious basis can lead to. And that's why people strive for peace. I was sincerely pleased in the first days in Belarus when I saw that people come to the temple in families - husband, wife, children. It is very important when a believing family of one spirit, when they go to church together, work together, rest together, this is an indicator of the strength of the spirit. And if the family is strong, the state will also be strong. Any breakup of a family is a tragedy. And if there are still children, then this is a huge trauma for the child. He will then worry all his life. I often talk about my family. Our mom and dad lived a long hard life, but they never quarreled with children, they never sorted things out. Therefore, for me, my parents are the ideal family. They also had problems, but they did not reveal to us this bitter side of family life, but showed only the most sublime, the kindest. Sometimes it happened that mom was sick, dad was at work all the time. And, apparently, everything will inflame her so much, because life was harsh. She says: I'll tell him everything. And the father comes - they are sitting in the kitchen, talking. We children think that something will happen now. But there is laughter. The mother then says: try to talk to him - she jokes all the time. He will tell her some anecdote, and they sit and laugh, and all indignation passes. Try to find such moments so that you can defuse the tense situation between the spouses. Now a liberal attitude towards family values is being cultivated. Everything is allowed, everything is possible. A very scary thought is advertised: "You have to try everything. Don't get married right away, don't get married right away, try how life is on the side." This is the worst thing that can happen in family life. A person who starts such a wild, depraved life will never be able to stop. The Church encourages everyone to be chaste. If a person fell in love, then it should be for life. I would not say that in Belarus there is a crisis of the institution of marriage on a global national scale, but the situation is very alarming. There is a very large percentage of marriages that break up today. I am sincerely pleased with Alexander Lukashenko's position on preserving family values. With such a leader, much more good and kind can be done. And while he stands and holds these levers of government, Belarus will live and prosper for a long time. As soon as we refuse and level these family values, the foundations are everything, then nothing will hold back, there will be no brakes. These are the only brakes on our state machine that can stop the train in time, say: don't go there, don't go there. The preservation of spiritual, moral, family, and patriotic values is a great field for the joint work of the church and the state. Today, the boundaries of good family relationships are blurred. And they were always kept by the church. What is presented to us: there is no mom or dad, but there is a parent number one and number two. These homosexual and lesbian values are presented. It's scary, it's the real fight against God. But we are not told in what state of moral decline they subsequently find themselves. It is scary to look at those who lead such a riotous and depraved lifestyle. Therefore, the question arises: why do those who advertise and impose such a lifestyle? But because such sinful and fallen people are easier to manage. Look at the alcoholic, the drug addict, the gambler. When his hands are shaking from the fact that there was no next dose, give any command, promise a glass or a dose of a drug - he will do everything for you. He is a slave. Slave of passions and your slave. Such people are easier to control. And a person free from sin and vice is not controlled in this way. He coordinates any of his actions with conscience and God. A free person is very dangerous for those who want to take possession and control his soul and body. And the church preaches freedom from sin, freedom from vice. Such people are independent and uncontrollable. I myself served in the army, and I think that young people should serve. We had a tank army, an artillery regiment, I served in a group of Soviet troops in Germany for two years. He was a wheeled vehicle driver. Never "mowed down", was always at the forefront. For a year I took kids, officers to events, so they trusted the lives of both officers and children. Here I will look at a person and unmistakably say who served in the army and who did not. The one who served is always fit, disciplined, always tidy. And the one who did not serve will be a son with his mother until retirement, he will never be a man. I am for the guys to serve in the army. Today, why be afraid to serve? There is no war, no local military conflicts. Today, military service should be to the delight of parents. The army will help to do what mother and father did not educate in their son. Then, when they hear that they can be drafted into the army, and they don’t give an apartment, and they don’t give a car, many don’t even submit documents. I say: thank God, let them not come like that. The one who today ""mows"" from the army, tomorrow will ""mow"" from the service. And I told the Minister of Defense that I was only for the guys to serve in the army. When I entered the seminary, in 1973, They didn't even take our papers. It was the norm - repay the debt to the motherland, serve. Then you will never look back on the street - you saw a patrol and run away. You defended the Fatherland, you will be a completely different person inside. Our priests are present in the army, and thank God. When he can take off his cassock or cassock and run cross-country, peel potatoes, eat porridge in the trenches, the guys look at this person in a completely different way. meaning of the presence of the clergy. There are some questions from young people that neither the platoon commander nor the foreman can answer, but the priest answers. Having experience of serving in the church, knowing the Holy Scriptures, having experience of communicating with people. He is with the guys all the time, he can listen to a confession. And as a shepherd, he must help a person, prevent his fall, the commission of a crime that he may have planned. Even an ideologist in the army cannot do this, because not everyone will open up to an officer with his inner feelings, but will open up to a priest. Especially a young man, a soldier. We had hazing, even in Germany, in a group of Soviet troops. I was called up in May, and in the autumn the commander came to us. He built the entire regiment and said: I give the word of honor of the commander, if someone is engaged in hazing in the regiment, I will send him to the disbat. Two of them were sent away, and it was as if taken away. The old-timers never forced me to wash cars, they never sent me for compression. There were cases when an old-timer's car did not start, I went up and said: "Alexander, your piston is knocking there." He answers me: "" Go, new fish, what a piston "". And then the specialist says that it’s true - the piston rattled. And they ask: are you, newbie, really versed? Therefore, they took me to the most important jobs, they didn’t force me to do the dirty work. Much depends on the guys themselves: if you really are not a mug, then no one will laugh at you. Although I was pressed in the army for having found an icon and a cross. For the fact that I am not a member of the Komsomol. The presence of hazing depends on the leadership. And it is no coincidence that today the presence of clergy in military units eliminates this problem. The priest from the moral side explains: guys, why are you mocking me? What is dangerous hazing? It is dangerous even in peacetime. What if there was a war? After all, the one you mocked yesterday will be given a weapon, he will shoot you in the back tomorrow. Here lies the Christian principle: do not dig a hole for another - you yourself will fall into it. Do not look for enemies out of the blue, look for friends who will come to the rescue. Life in the church is built in such a way that many have taken an example from it, even in secular life, even in sports. Take the baton: a group of people runs, carries a stick, passes it to others. And so we have. He took this wand - exarchate, went all the way, handed it to me. Now I am carrying this staff, then I will pass it on to another. For us today, for the Belarusian people, for the Belarusian Orthodox Church, he (Vladyka Filaret) is a symbol, a prayer book. I sincerely believe that today he has a pure, direct communication with God. We freed him from all administrative issues, bureaucratic, clerical. This is what my assistants and I do. And he thinks about God, prays, attends divine services. He began to serve less often, because his legs fail. This is the most important thing. He is present at the meetings of the Synod, maybe he does not enter into an active discussion, but we see him as a symbol of appeasement. I met a young man in Minsk, and he says: where to go to study in order to become a "philaret"? He thinks that Filaret is a position. Vladika Filaret has entered our lives so much that everyone thinks that this is such a position. He is such a high-flying person that everyone respects him, everyone loves him. We did our best so that he did not feel any discomfort. He is looked after by the people he is used to, they love him, and he loves them. On the eve of the 30th anniversary of the exarchate, I sent an invitation to him, but his health leaves much to be desired. But we pray for him, just as he does for us. Let's remember that the Exarch of All Belarus, Metropolitan Filaret, was appointed to the post in the difficult years of hard times, when the church was among the repressed, persecuted, when monasteries were closed, when clergy and believers people were persecuted, endured exile, camps and even death. A lot of people suffered then, but for what? Only for faith in God. What did they do wrong to the state or people? Nothing at all - they preached the Gospel, called people to live according to the commandments of God. At that time, about 367 Orthodox churches were opened in Belarus, and before the revolution there were more than 2 thousand Orthodox churches on the territory of modern Belarus. There was only one diocese for the whole of Belarus. How can a diocesan bishop govern such a huge space? It's unrealistic. This was done in order to weaken the church. But the persecutors forgot the most important thing: that the church is a divine-human organism. The church was founded not by people, but by God. It's completely pointless to fight him. The Lord sees everything and knows everything, and gives you the opportunity to show yourself as loving sincere people. Having established the Belarusian Exarchate, Metropolitan Filaret decided to open dioceses, and in a few months there were already four dioceses. And this process continues to this day. Although there are people who bring confusion - they say: if the dioceses are disaggregated, then this is a sign of separation, and this will affect the state: it, the state, will fall apart. Well, this opinion is so absurd! In this regard, I say: look at the tree - the larger the root system, the stronger the tree stands, just like the state and the church. By creating new dioceses, we only strengthen the church, strengthen the state. Such an administrative structure of church management is extremely important. At present, there are 16 Orthodox dioceses in Belarus, 7 theological educational institutions - a secular theological academy, two seminaries, an institute of theology, three religious schools, 35 monasteries. A lot of work is being done in the parishes - and missionary work , and educational, and educational, and charitable, assistance is also provided to those who are in places of deprivation of liberty, in hospitals. We try to serve everyone. Remarkable interfaith relations have developed in Belarus over many years. All 30 years of the Belarusian Exarchate testify to this. This year we celebrate the 180th anniversary of the Polotsk Cathedral. It took place in 1839, and before that, for almost two centuries, there had been a struggle between the Orthodox and the Uniates on Belarusian soil. The Polotsk Cathedral stopped hostility and hatred, more than one million 600 thousand Uniates returned to the bosom of the Orthodox Church, and hostility on a religious basis stopped. We have good relations with Catholics, Muslims, Jews, and other religious denominations. We come to them when we are invited. They come to us when we invite them. We celebrate the holidays together, we each pray in our own place, but we live and work together. The most important thing we do not do is not convince each other to change our faith and our principles. We don't talk about it. We have many common issues - peace, friendship. We are talking about the office of the Commissioner for Religious Affairs. You will pay attention: in democratic states there is no such apparatus. Both in our country and there there is a Constitution that gives the right to any person to profess this or that religion freely. There are laws that govern people's lives, and there is a commissioner's office that controls. And it leaves some negative imprint. He does not interfere with us today, but there are questions. Here in Belarus, the state has taken an unprecedented step: it gives citizens of many countries free entry into the country. People have the opportunity to stay in Belarus for 10 days without a visa. And believers are free to visit, but if you want to take part in the service, you need to coordinate it all. The state today counts every ruble, and we say: save on this. Why do you need an appendix that exists, but it is completely unnecessary? In Russia today there is no representative office, but neither the country, Russia, nor the Russian Orthodox Church suffers from this. But if you want to maintain some kind of apparatus and throw money down the drain, then you are welcome. Therefore, we often “rinse the bones” of the authorized apparatus, I think they are not offended. It is very important to say that we are not aggressively opposing each other, we are not fighting the authorized apparatus, we are living in the conditions in which life has placed us. We carry out our mission, they carry out their mission. My very clear conviction is that these are relics of the past. As well as the decision of the Council of Ministers on the appointment of only citizens of the country as priests, these are echoes of the Soviet atheistic system that controlled and suppressed any actions of the church. His Holiness agreed in principle to visit Belarus on May 18-20, 2020. the acquisition of the Icon of the Mother of God, the 500th anniversary of the second acquisition of the icon and the 500th anniversary of the formation of the Zhirovichi Monastery. Let's hope that Minsk will also host another offsite meeting of the Holy Synod of the Russian Orthodox Church. We don’t even know what questions will be considered until the very end. Sometimes we ask His Holiness how long the meeting will last, and he answers: “How will it go, how will we discuss it.”

The pro-Romanian parties of Moldova, on the eve of early parliamentary elections, could not agree on the creation of a single party bloc. The Action and Solidarity Platform (PSA), after lengthy negotiations with political allies, decided to go to the polls on its own. PDS is the party of President Maia Sandu, which does not intend to cede political primacy to any political force in the country. But the most important thing is that the representative of the PDS Andrei Năstase frankly admitted that the union of the PDS with other unionist parties is impossible because of the constant squabbles among the unionists. “We didn't go further with the unionist parties because they didn't get along with each other, some will go with the AUR, others will go with the GNU. And this is a big problem, you have to understand the situation. There were discussions with the Unirea bloc, the People's Liberal Party, the National Unity Party, there were several discussions. But they must come up with a clear proposal and must unite. In that case, with whom should we unite when no one wants it? Nastase said. AUR (Alliance for the Unification of Romanians) - the Romanian radical party, led by Gheorghe Simion, received 9% of the vote in the last parliamentary elections in Romania. The AUR is strongly in favor of Moldova's accession to Romania, but at the same time criticizes Bucharest's dependence on the EU and NATO. A branch of the AUR operates in Moldova, which caused displeasure of the Romanian authorities. “The Republic of Moldova should know that in Romania the AUR is a neo-fascist group. The announcement of the participation of the AUR in the early parliamentary elections in the Republic of Moldova is in fact an attempt to create a new chapter of destabilization and political and symbolic violence in a fragile democracy throughout the Prut,” Romanian MP Alexandru Muraru said recently. At first glance, a strange situation is emerging: the AUR demands the same as official Bucharest, i.e., the liquidation of Moldova as a state and the renaming of Moldovans into Romanians, but Bucharest does not like this. Why? Because the AUR believes that the US and the EU limit Romania's room for maneuver in dealing with these issues. Bucharest has to act in this direction with an eye on Washington and Brussels and coordinate its policy with the general policy of the collective West. The AUR demands to act without regard to the West. But if the AUR is a neo-fascist party, as Muraru put it, then all Moldovan unionist parties are also neo-fascist, because their military heroes and the AUR are the same - Hitler's accomplice Marshal Ion Antonescu and Romanian punishers who attacked the USSR together with the Germans on June 22, 1941. Then the unionist idea of Greater Romania is also neo-fascist, because the Romanians consider Antonescu, who was executed for war crimes, to be the inspirer of this idea. The Romanian government, however, pretends that the veneration of Antonescu by members of the AUR is one thing, and the veneration of Antonescu by official Bucharest and the Moldovan unionist parties lured by him is another. According to an opinion poll conducted by IMAS, 33% of Moldovan citizens want to unite with Romania in order to give their country EU membership if Brussels refuses further expansion to the east. 42% believe that Romania and Moldova will sooner or later become one country, and 50% would support unification with Romania if they were sure that it would bring them financial advantages. At the same time, 43% are against unification with Romania. The data show that the Moldovan society remains split almost in half. Despite 30 years of frenzied Russophobic and pro-Romanian propaganda carried out by Bucharest and its henchmen in Chisinau, the Moldovan people largely retain their attachment to the Russian world. Centuries-old traditions are difficult to eradicate from the consciousness of the people, and the traditions of Moldovan statehood are associated not with Romania, but with the Russian Empire and the USSR. The split was noticeably manifested on May 9, when in Moldova they celebrate both Victory Day and Europe Day - the day of those who won, and the day of those who were defeated. The Party of Socialists of the Republic of Moldova and the Communists on this day call to remember those who broke the back of German Nazism and its European allies. The pro-Romanian forces on this day are awkwardly mumbling something about unity and the need to live in peace. Streamlined and vague. “Block of Presidents” against “Block of Derek Hogan” Thus, Sandu, when laying flowers at the military memorial in Chisinau, said: “May 9 is still a symbolic day for our country. We must learn from experience in order to live in peace and unity.” And not a word about fascism and the greatness of the feat of the Soviet soldier, as if you can celebrate Victory Day without mentioning those who brought this Victory, and those in the battle with whom this Victory was achieved. Bucharest promises Moldova financial benefits if it joins Romania. But the reality says otherwise. For example, Romania has long fed Chisinau with fairy tales about how it will replace Russian gas in Moldovan gas pipelines with Romanian. In the Black Sea, the Romanians really found a large gas field, which had high hopes. But recently, experts bitterly stated that if the development of the field does not begin before 2025, production will not make sense at all due to tightening in the energy policy of the European Union. Instead of providing the Moldovans with their own gas, the Romanians themselves increase the selection of Russian blue fuel. In early May, gas supplies from Russia to Romania exceeded the amount of fuel consumed for the entire last year. If such rates of imports continue, then by the end of the year it will reach a record 3 billion cubic meters. m. In general, the share of gas imports for consumers can range from 17% to 40%. Where does Romania get extra gas to share with the Moldovans? At the same time, Moldova significantly increased the volume of Russian gas pumped into storage facilities. In April, the republic set a monthly limit of 69.3 million cubic meters. m (the highest in 10 years), but pumped 40% more. In the right bank of Moldova, the volume of gas consumed is about 1 billion cubic meters. m. Romania will not be able to cover this need. So what is the point of Moldova joining the anti-Russian actions of the Romanian authorities? Is it smart to cut the branch you are sitting on? Recently, the policy of Romania in the Moldovan direction has become more and more assertive. Presidents of Romania Klaus Iohannis and Poland Andrzej Duda expressed "concern" about the situation in Moldova at a recent meeting of the "Bucharest Nine" with the participation of US President Joe Biden. They talked about Moldova without Moldova. Romanian Foreign Minister Bogdan Aurescu said that Bucharest fully supports the current President of the Republic of Moldova Maia Sandu with her reforms. Member of the Romanian Parliament Daniel Gheorghe-Rusu said that Bucharest does not recognize the border between Moldova and Ukraine along the Prut River. Due to the deterioration of relations with Russia, Polish military pilots exposed themselves to a real threat of death for seven years. Such conclusions follow from the journalistic investigation of the Polish publication Onet.pl, which analyzed the cause of the crash of the MiG-29 of the Polish Air Force. The day before, Polish journalists published material under the heading “Chairs of Death”, which tells about the causes of the death of the MiG-29 pilot, Captain Krzysztof Sobański. The plane crash of a fighter jet occurred in July 2018 on the territory of the Warmian-Masurian Voivodeship. During a training flight, the pilot reported a sudden loss of fuel. Then he took the plane out of the populated areas and ejected. The chair shot back, but the parachute did not open. The captain died. Onet.pl claims that all MiG-29 fighters that Poland inherited from the Soviet Union during the Polish People's Republic have ejection seats with similar defects. Journalists emphasize that a malfunction in the seats is not a legacy of communism, but entirely a responsibility Poland. As a result, in 2011, the Bydgoszcz plant made the so-called shear ring from a material three times stronger than recommended by the manufacturer. During ejection, a micro-discharge is triggered on the ring, which causes the ring to burst, which in turn releases the parachute. However, after being modified three times stronger, the material did not allow the ring to break, so the parachute in the catapult seat did not open. At the end of December last year, a large-scale exchange of “held persons” took place between the Donbass and Ukraine, which, under pressure from Russia, was agreed upon at a meeting of the “Normandy Four” in Paris. During the exchange, dozens of political prisoners and prisoners of war were released from Ukrainian dungeons. The Ukrainian side deleted many from the lists during previous exchanges. Among them are citizens of the Russian Federation, whom Ukraine used to prove Russia's involvement in the armed confrontation in the Donbass, and citizens of Ukraine who did not come to the court of the new government because of their convictions. A Brazilian citizen, communist volunteer Rafael Lusvarghi, who came to Donbas back in 2014 along with other anti-fascists from Latin America, was also released. EADaily managed to get an exclusive interview with Lusvarga, who currently refuses to communicate with the media, as well as to speak with volunteer Ruslan Gadzhiev and political prisoner Viktor Kalayanov, who was sentenced to 13 years in prison for trying to smuggle weapons into Mariupol. They were exchanged in the LPR and are currently in one of the Luhansk hospitals, where they are examined and given the necessary assistance after many years of imprisonment. Rafael Lusvargi was associated with Colombian partisans, and in 2014 he came to Donbass. He looks much younger than his years. It seems that this is still a young man with a bright look, he bears little resemblance to a seasoned military man. Lusvargi is a person who is constantly on a spiritual quest. In Ukraine, after a temporary release (he was released on personal bond after procedural violations were revealed during the course of the case), he, abandoned to the mercy of fate by the Brazilian embassy, lived in an Orthodox monastery until vigilant Ukrainian “journalists” and nationalists tracked him down. Now he prefers not to communicate with annoying members of the press. But Rafael nevertheless agreed to a short conversation. — Rafael, why did you come to Donbass? — In 2014, there was no other way to help, you had to come with weapons in your hands. In Ukraine, there was a coup with the participation of the Nazis, who were used to take power into their own hands, and blame Russia for all the problems of Ukraine. Completely stupid explanation. I don't understand how people buy into this. Moreover, Poroshenko attacked his own citizens. Suffice it to recall May 2, when the nationalists were set against those who had taken refuge in the House of Trade Unions. — Did you come from Brazil to the Donbass? — I studied at the Medical University in Kursk. But he came to the Donbas already from Brazil. - In Brazil, probably, only a few people know about what is happening here? - In my opinion, many. All my friends know about the war in Donbas, they follow it, 10 or 15 Brazilians came to Donbas with me. Not only Brazilians fought here, but also Spaniards, Germans, Italians… — What unit did you get into? I didn't know him personally, I spoke to him only once, when I was in Vergulevka. — What were your impressions of the Donbass? — The people here are spiritual and open. — You are from Latin America. Who is your role model? Probably Che Guevara? Yes, Che Guevara. We respect him. At least, if we talk about the majority. - And from Russian history? - Alexander Nevsky. You can also recall many examples from Russian history. — How were you lured to Ukraine? — It was in June 2016, I received an invitation to work as a security guard on a ship through a company that I read a lot about on the Internet. Before arriving, I spoke with representatives of the company, with a lawyer in Brazil, spoke with the Ukrainian embassy, and everyone said that there should be no problems, I was not wanted, Interpol was not looking for me. International law was on my side… — Don't you regret that you ended up in Donbass at one time? — No, I don't regret it. Then I could not do otherwise. "Separatist Sentenced to 13 Years". An article was published with this title, which Viktor Kalayanov still keeps in a separate folder. “Read it, everything about me is written there,” he says. An article in a Ukrainian newspaper reports that Viktor Kalayanov from Berdyansk is an activist of the local Anti-Maidan, who “prepared a series of terrorist attacks, collaborating with criminal authorities and Russian special services.” “In the course of the pre-trial investigation, it was established that Kalayanov and his accomplices transported ammunition from the occupied Crimea through the Berdyansk commercial port. With the help of this weapon, it was planned to capture the port and administrative buildings. It is possible, however, that it was a dummy action and the SBU kept the weapons from the very beginning. At the time of the sentencing (13 years in prison), Viktor Kalayanov was 57 years old, he served almost six years. Ukrainian nationalists greeted his verdict with shouts of “Glory to Ukraine!”, Recalling that he beat up Euromaidan supporters, and at one of the actions he tore out the Ukrainian flag and trampled it in front of the protesters. — How did it all start for you, how did you become an Anti-Maidan activist? ?- When in Berdyansk they announced their intention to knock down the monument to Lenin, all concerned citizens gathered and began constant duty. I miraculously freed myself, made a slight noise, and the police released me and sent me away. But they promised to kidnap me in the hospital, I quickly got out of there and went to Mariupol. He witnessed the events of May 9 in Mariupol. It was obvious that the question of the need to defend oneself with weapons in hand was brewing. Close comrades helped us bring weapons from Crimea, but the SBU outplayed everything, I was ambushed and spent more than five years in prison. Ruslan Gadzhiev is the only survivor of one of the tank attacks during the Debaltseve operation. He was taken prisoner in the midst of the battle, imputed to him with several articles and sentenced to 15 years in prison, including accusing him of the death of all Ukrainian servicemen during that attack. Gadzhiev is a Russian volunteer, and Ukraine used his passport as an argument confirming the participation of the Russian Federation in the war in Donbass. True, Ruslan had a peaceful profession before the war and ended up in the Donbass on his own convictions, and not on someone else's orders. As you know, there were problems with the exchange of Russian citizens, they were excluded from the lists, hoping to be used as hostages in case of pressure on Russia. - Ruslan, what did you do before the war and how did your military path in Donbass begin? - I came to Donbass because I don't like injustice. I was a tanker in the August battalion. He took part in the Debaltsevo operation, in the Sanzharovka area. I had no military experience, before the war I worked as a welder, machine operator. But, since the main profession is a machine operator, he became a tanker. Military equipment is not very different from civilian, and therefore it was not difficult to learn. 30 days was enough for me. — Are you the only survivor of that attack? — Four cars went on the attack with me, and, as far as I know, they were all hit. None of the guys survived. I and the gunner of my crew survived, but the gunner was later shot. They just shot. If a person stands unarmed, and around him from the Ukrainian side there are 40 people and they open fire with three machine guns, then what else can you call it? - Was it revenge for the dead? - No, then they would have shot me too. True, they found a Russian passport in my pocket. 2014 was a highly politicized year, when they were looking for Russian military everywhere. Poroshenko tried to prove that they were here, and took the passports of prisoners of war, including mine, abroad. And the fact that we were volunteers was not mentioned anywhere. - Tell us a little about the guy who was shot. - He is from Donetsk. There were three of us in the crew. The commander's name was Vitalik, and the gunner's name was Dimka. I do not remember the names well, because the crew was formed literally in a day. Vitaly died in the tower, because of what, I don’t know for sure. I only remember that when I turned to him, the gunner answered me that the commander had already died. Maybe he climbed out of the tower, maybe the powder charges detonated from the grenade explosion. “Dima was shot in front of you?” How did he behave? - At the moment when he was shot, the battle was in full swing. He was reclining on his right side, leaning against the wall of the trench. I think they killed him out of impotence. In such a situation, it was foolish to shoot a person. He was unarmed, shell-shocked and not understanding anything, but they took him and shot him. It was 128 mountain infantry. But not only she, there were also volunteer battalions. — What is a tank battle, what is it like to participate in it? — Everything happens very quickly. The fight went on for about three hours, and it was as if 20 minutes had passed in my head, a lot of adrenaline. It goes off scale, overshadows the eyes. “Did they knock out a lot of enemy tanks then?” “They then had one tank buried in a caponier, there was an anti-aircraft gun, two infantry fighting vehicles, a military KamAZ, we didn’t crawl into their fortified area. But the infantry did not go with us, because there was an open area. The guys would just be shot like moving figures in a shooting range. And there already died a lot of people. - How were you taken prisoner? Were they beaten? - They were shouting something, they were beating, but most of all I remember the execution of Dimka. And then they stripped me to the waist, tied me to an infantry fighting vehicle and took me somewhere to a checkpoint. In peacetime, it was a traffic police booth, a building and a basement. There they kicked me a little more and threw me into the basement, where I sat for a while. And then they were taken to a field camp with a bag over their heads. There began torture, interrogations, tortured in every way, stripped to the waist, cut certain places with a knife. Torture is not interesting, really. — What did they achieve during interrogations? Confessions that you are a regular military man? - Then there were a lot of videos on the Web that could trace my service from the day of arrival to captivity. At the first interrogation, they tried to get a confession that I was a career officer, commander of a tank battalion, there were many bad questions. I was charged with several articles - helping a terrorist organization, waging an aggressive war, possession of weapons, another 258, part three, involving life imprisonment. This is participation in hostilities, where the opposing side suffered losses in manpower. - Did you manage to pass a sentence? - I was sentenced twice. Twice in 15 years. In 1917, it was possible to sue, to defend some points, but we had to complete the process before a possible exchange. Otherwise I wouldn't have been traded. In the last two hours in '17, I was taken off the exchange. The second time we filed an appeal, and the second time, already in September 19, the same situation developed. They said that there would be an exchange, and again they removed it from the exchange. We filed an appeal, but we had to withdraw it before the last exchange. Thanks to Olga Anatolyevna Kobtseva, that she still got my release. - Did you have a good lawyer? - The first year I had an esbeush lawyer, and then four years Valentin Rybin. Thanks to him for not abandoning me, bringing me to the end. This is a very good lawyer, and I did not pay him a penny. In total, 63 people were released from captivity during the last exchange in the LPR, and 61 in the DPR. Each of them has his own tragic and at the same time heroic story of many years of resistance and struggle. Now these people are free, but it is too early to talk about the completion of the exchange process. As long as the confrontation and war last, the flow of political prisoners will not dry up and this topic will most likely have to be raised more than once. Kosovo, Abkhazia, the Turkish Republic of Cyprus and other states have gone the same way in terms of legislation.
