To the 102nd anniversary of the October Revolution of 1917 in Russia From a political, economic, cultural and historical point of view, Ukraine today is an embodied paradox: it is a monument to the socialist system and communist ideology, but an incredibly dilapidated monument, living under the “laws on decommunization” , ritually commemorating the "cursed commies" ... November 7 marks the 102nd anniversary of the October Revolution in Russia - the very revolution from which Ukraine benefited more than others, where today they are memorized shouting about "the crimes of the totalitarian communist regime." Without the Bolsheviks, Ukraine as a state that appeared in 1991 would not exist at all. Until the end of the 19th century, the term "Ukraine" was rarely used, only in a territorial sense, without any ethnic or political content. "Ukrainian" propaganda in the second half of the 19th century was taken up by the Poles, who tried to split the Russian Empire, then the Austrians continued this propaganda. And only the overthrow of the monarchy in Russia in February 1917 opened up scope for the “Ukrainian idea”. Thus, a new ephemeral formation appeared - the "Ukrainian People's Republic" (UNR). In 1918, the Germans took advantage of the "Ukrainian idea" in negotiations with the RSFSR in Brest. The chief of staff of the Eastern Front of the German army, Max Hoffmann, later said in an interview with the Daily Mail newspaper: “In reality, Ukraine is the work of my hands, and not at all the fruit of the conscious will of the Russian people. I created Ukraine in order to be able to make peace with at least part of Russia.” In 1919, at the height of the civil war, the creation of the Ukrainian Socialist Soviet Republic was announced. After a series of discussions, the leadership of the Bolsheviks annexed to it the territories of the Odessa and Donetsk-Krivoy Rog Soviet republics, which had previously had nothing to do with Little Russia-Ukraine. So the future Ukrainian SSR was given access to the sea and industrialized areas of the Russian Donbass. In 1922, the Ukrainian SSR became one of the founders of the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics. From the 1920s, the Bolsheviks launched a policy of "Ukrainization". The literary norms of the Ukrainian language (which was previously considered a Little Russian dialect of Russian) were developed. The Soviet authorities began to introduce MOV into education, culture, office work. During the passportization of Russians living on the territory of the Ukrainian SSR, they were recorded as "Ukrainians" by nationality. The Ukrainization policy began to decline only in the second half of the 1930s, but the Bolsheviks managed to create the base of the “Ukrainian socialist nation”. So, in theory, “decommunization” Kiev should have started with the rejection not only of the ideology of Ukrainianism, but also of vast territories - the South-East, Galicia (annexed by the communists to the Ukrainian SSR in 1939), South Bessarabia (in 1940) , Rusyn Transcarpathia (in 1945-1946) ... The Bolsheviks not only "created" Ukraine, but also turned it from a predominantly agrarian region into an industrial and scientific colossus. The Ukrainian SSR was at the forefront of the industrialization of the Soviet Union. Of the one and a half thousand industrial enterprises built in the USSR during the first five-year plan (1928-1932), about 400 were in Ukraine. More than a third of the 35 new largest industrial facilities appeared here, including the symbol of industrialization - the DneproGES, which provided Soviet Ukraine with the cheapest electricity in the world. In general, the development of Ukrainian industry accounted for about 20% of all-Union investments. As a result, the volume of industrial production in Ukraine by 1940 compared to 1913 increased 7.3 times, and heavy industry - 10 times. Science has developed at a rapid pace. In 1928, the Institute of Physics and Technology was founded in Kharkov, in which, just four years later, for the first time in the USSR, the nucleus of the atom was split. Three (Anton Walter, Georgy Latyshev, Alexander Leipunsky) of the four main participants in the study moved shortly before that to the Ukrainian SSR from the RSFSR and the BSSR. In the late 1930s, under the leadership of designer Mikhail Koshkin, who arrived from Leningrad, a revolution in Soviet tank building began in Kharkov. The Nazi aggression severely hit the Ukrainian SSR. The territory of the republic was completely occupied. According to estimates, 8-10 million inhabitants of the republic died at the hands of the Nazis. Many were killed by "compatriots" - collaborators from the OUN *, who joined the units of the Nazi Schutzmannschaft. During the war, the Nazis destroyed over 700 cities and towns, more than 28 thousand villages, tens of thousands of industrial and agricultural enterprises of the Ukrainian SSR. After the war, the infrastructure of the Ukrainian SSR was restored as a matter of priority and in record time. In the second half of the 1950s, Ukrainian ferrous metallurgy took first place in Europe. The Southern Machine-Building Plant (Yuzhmash) in Dnepropetrovsk became one of the locomotives of the Soviet (and, by and large, world) rocket science. Design Bureau "Antonov" designed some of the best cargo aircraft on the planet. Factories were built for the production of consumer goods - cameras, televisions, vacuum cleaners. Lviv buses and Cossack cars ran all over the USSR. Dozens of nuclear and hydropower facilities have appeared in Ukraine. And metallurgical and ferroalloy plants were among the largest in the world - Zaporizhstal, Kryvorizhstal, Azovstal, Nikopol and others. About 40% of the republic's industrial potential was accounted for by mechanical engineering - science-intensive industries. A completely new social, transport and communal infrastructure was created in the republic: 3.9 thousand hospitals, 6.9 thousand polyclinics, 21.8 thousand schools, 24.5 thousand kindergartens, 160 thousand automobile and 22.7 thousand railways. The electrification of the republic was absolute. As a result, by the beginning of the 1990s, thanks to the "commies", the economy of the Ukrainian SSR was one of the twenty largest on the planet (according to other estimates, the ten most developed) ... Then a sharp decline began. According to the State Statistics Service, the production of electricity in independent Ukraine collapsed by more than one and a half times, the rolling of ferrous metals by almost 2.5 times, the production of refrigerators by 8 times, the production of textiles by 11 times, sausages by 3.5, and 2 ,4 - sugar, 66 - tractors... The number of cattle decreased by more than six times. The provision of Ukrainians with medical institutions has worsened by half, and by almost one and a half - with educational ones. The role of mechanical engineering in the structure of the GDP of an independent power has collapsed almost to the level of a statistical error. The aircraft industry, shipbuilding, the production of rockets and engines were ordered to live for a long time ... So the decommunization of Ukraine, which has been going on for almost three decades, has made considerable progress. It was a lie that the leaders of the Western world uttered, put on paper, put their signatures under it, and then categorically refused - and still do not want - to put into practice. When we proposed making the thesis of the indivisibility of security legally binding, they gave a categorical negative answer. There are legal security guarantees only in NATO. This is an artificial creation of a situation where small countries are being manipulated: “If you join us, then your security will be guaranteed. And due to this, an attempt is being made to develop the geopolitical space closer and closer to our borders. We all see this. They understand all this, but pretend to be naive people, including on the issue of missile defense, which, along with NATO expansion, is a destabilizing factor for global stability and violates global parities. This is not about Montenegro. The point is how NATO treats the development of relations not just with Russia, but to ensure global security. NATO is responsible for its sector and, as written in the Washington Treaty, provides collective defense against attack. But then sit within your boundaries, and no one is going to touch you! This is not enough for them, because then the existence of a military-political bloc loses its meaning. The digital economy, the service sector, the role of raw materials - there are many ambiguities now. In this competitive world, everyone is trying to "push with elbows" in order to take the most favorable place for further agreements. All this is understandable. The main thing is that there should be no unscrupulous game here, and that until the new rules are written, we will be guided by those that we have. - Is there diplomacy without a dirty game? - Depending on how you judge what an unscrupulous game is. The lie, they say, lies in the fact that we kept silent about another obligation, which is allegedly contained there. And it simply says that all participants in the memorandum will continue to be guided by the principles of the OSCE, including those regarding territorial integrity, sovereignty, and non-interference in internal affairs. The principles of the OSCE have never and nowhere allowed to carry out coups d'etat, forbade encroachment on national and linguistic minorities. I repeat once again that different methods are used in diplomacy, but the main thing is that you be honest with yourself. I am convinced that our partners, whom we also respect, see our work correctly. Numerous important events of the past six months somehow faded into the background the barbaric act of the authorities of the municipality of Prague-6. Let me remind the reader: on April 3, a monument to Marshal of the Soviet Union Ivan Stepanovich Konev was demolished in Prague. The monument was erected in 1980 on the 35th anniversary of the liberation of Prague by Soviet troops from Nazi invaders. Moreover, it was made at the expense and on the initiative of the Prague residents themselves. The head of the Prague-6 municipality, Ondřej Kolář, mockingly explained the need for dismantling by the fact that the bronze marshal did not have a mask to wear in the context of the coronavirus pandemic. The Prague authorities showed the worst features of the Czech mentality, ridiculed in "The Good Soldier Schweik": opportunism and obsequiousness to the strong and vindictive and low cruelty to the downtrodden. But, apart from base instincts, the demolition of the monument pursued quite pragmatic goals. So, for example, Alexander Gegalchiy, an activist of the Russian community in Prague, president of the international "Russian Prize" (the prize is awarded to prose writers and poets writing in Russian and Rusyn), believes that the demolition of the monument to Marshal Konev (and even on the threshold of the 75th anniversary of the Great Pobeda) Kolář and Co. pursued the goal of provoking the Russians to retaliate with harsh actions. Such could be the demolition of monuments to Czech legionnaires during the Civil War in Russia, located in the Urals and Siberia, or their exchange for monuments to Konev and Soviet soldiers in the Czech Republic. But any kind of anti-Czech actions in Russia would play into the hands of provocateurs like Kolarzh: they would mean a blow precisely to normal Czechs. Fortunately, Russia did not succumb to this gross provocation.A. Gegalchy draws attention to the split in Czech society over the "memorial" issue. The Czech society does not like Prague, so the court decisions and personal sanctions against the Prague officials Grzyb, Kolarzh, Novotny (supporters of the demolition of the monument to Konev and the installation of a monument to General Vlasov) and even against Prague commercial firms will be welcomed by the Czechs themselves. In this regard, let us recall another conflict that occurred during the onset of the coronavirus - China's actions to interrupt relations with creative teams with the name "Prague", the subsequent "refusal" of Mayor Z. Grzhib to receive Chinese antiviral masks and, in the end, the predatory seizure of these masks at the Prague airport (they were intended for Italy). Personal sanctions - from economic to the simplest temporary "persona non grata" - against Grzyb-Kolář-Novotny and the deputies who voted in the municipality of Prague-6 (about 33 people) for the demolition of the monument to Konev, in Prague-Reporija (about 10 deputies) - for the erection of a monument to the Vlasovites and in Prague itself (last year) - for the removal of a sign from the town hall about the liberation by the Soviet army, will be discussed with satisfaction by the rest of the Czechs - there is reason to think so. It would be naive to believe that the decision to demolish the monument to Marshal Konev closes on the level of the municipality of Prague 6 or the Prague mayor. An openly anti-Russian position was taken by the Foreign Minister of the Czech Republic, Tomas Petrichek. More precisely, it was thanks to this position that he was appointed to the post of Prime Minister Andrei Babis, despite the resistance of President Milos Zeman and realist politicians. As a career Russophobe, Petrichek and other provocateurs work proactively, counting on dividends and posts in European and American structures. Now he maintains some intensity of the conflict, actually reducing its level to the "kitchen". The weak point of the minister is the fear of a sharp decline in trade with Russia during his tenure as minister. So why not take advantage of it? Are there real possibilities and expediency of imposing sanctions? Given that the Czech Republic supports Western sanctions against Russia, then probably yes. Another thing is that Russian sanctions should not apply to the country as a whole, personal sanctions against Foreign Minister Petrichek, Prime Minister Babis and the Prague authorities are appropriate. This will be a tangible and targeted blow to Russophobes in the Czech Republic. As for economic sanctions, they can be very selective. For example, concerning the export of Czech beer (last year it grew by a record 55% to 30 million euros) or the export of beer by Prague firms. 30 Petrichek beer suppliers will be cursed. In this regard, let us recall how Riga groaned when the red light was put on the Latvian sprats in the Russian Federation. At the same time, Russian producers of "Czech" beer and jobs in Russia will not suffer. Even with limited supplies of hops and malt, all this can be bought from the Germans... A similar situation has developed in more significant supplies of components for the automotive industry (Skoda, 800 million euros). Thus, Russia had and still has many opportunities for targeted punishment of Russophobic provocation. I will add to what A. Gegalchiy said: among other things, the goal of the provocative action of the Prague authorities is to humiliate Russia, damage the prestige and authority of our country. This event is from the same series as the decision of the European Parliament to equate the USSR and Hitler's Germany, as well as the statement of Polish President Andrzej Duda about Stalin and Hitler as equal perpetrators of the outbreak of World War II. These are all links in the same chain. And it is by no means unacceptable to let the provocateurs (more precisely, miserable obedient performers) do their deeds. The Russian authorities reacted, but how? In the opinion of an activist of the Russian community in Prague, which we share, the steps taken by Moscow were not distinguished by offensiveness and consistency. On April 9, Russian Defense Minister Sergei Shoigu sent a letter to his Czech counterpart Lubomir Metnar, noting the need to stop desecration of the monument to the famous marshal. S. Shoigu offered to transfer the monument to the Russian Federation, but the Czech side refused to satisfy this request. When the attempt to resolve the matter by agreement failed (the refusal of the Czech defense department was another manifestation of blasphemy), the Russian side switched to another tactic. On April 10, the Investigative Committee of Russia opened a criminal case in connection with the dismantling of the monument to Marshal Konev on the grounds of a crime under Part 3 of Art. 354.1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (“Desecration of the symbols of military glory of Russia, committed in public”). It would seem that everything is correct. But in the end, Russia, not the Czech Republic, may suffer reputational damage. After all, Russian justice does not extend to the borders of the Czech Republic and does not have the practical possibility of bringing a criminal case to court in the territory of this country. In our opinion, other response measures proposed in those days in the media were also erroneous and harmful to the national interests of Russia: metro "Prazhskaya", the installation of a monument to I. Konev in front of the Czech Embassy in Moscow and others. By the way, our position is shared by the Russian citizen of Prague A. Gegalchiy. According to him, the Czech society is deeply disappointed with the "peace-loving", "Tolstoy" behavior of the Russian side, unworthy of a great power. What do the experts offer in return? According to A. Gegalchiy, a trial (albeit in absentia) over the “Prague heroes” Grzyb-Kolář-Novotny (or a wider circle of the accused) is necessary. Let the trial take place in Russia according to Russian laws. Of course, whatever he decides, his decisions will be subjected to the most severe criticism of the “democratic community”. But one should not be afraid of this, the precedent is important here. Russian lawyers could use the materials of the prosecution, which a group of lawyer and public figure Jiří Vyvadil began to collect. The latter is ready to provide its materials for the process in Russia. He is also ready to defend the interests of the Russian Federation in the processes in the Czech Republic, if they can be initiated. The latter, however, is unlikely, because the local justice system and the police are afraid to touch high-ranking criminals. And this makes a fair trial of them in the Czech Republic a priori impossible. This fear is already confirmed by the initial refusal of the court to accept the charges against Kolář and Co. for formal reasons. That is why a considerable part of Czech society will only welcome if the provocateurs are sentenced at least in Russia. Another side of the issue is the mobilization of Russian society to protect historical memory. The core idea here is the involvement of Czech patriots in the protection of the monument erected in the capital of the Czechs on the initiative of the Czechs and with Czech money. On the part of Russia, it is extremely necessary to provide various kinds of assistance (legal) in filing a series of lawsuits against individual municipalities of Prague, in including the healthy forces of Czech society and politicians in the struggle. And one of the main tools of this strengthening is a reminder of the military brotherhood during the Great Patriotic War. Asymmetric steps can be effective. In this particular case, it is necessary to start raising funds in Russia for the construction of a monument to volunteer soldiers of the 1st Czechoslovak Army Corps, who heroically fought against Nazi Germany and its allies shoulder to shoulder with the soldiers of the Red Army. The crime of Kolarzh and Co. is also a crime against the fighters of General Ludwig Svoboda, who fought, by the way, as part of the 1st Ukrainian Front, Marshal I.S. Koneva. Officers of the 1st separate Czechoslovak infantry brigade, Heroes of the Soviet Union Antonin Sohor, Joseph Burshik, Richard Tesarzhik (from left to right) It is advisable to entrust the creation of a monument to Czech sculptors, for which a competition is held in the Czech Republic for the best project of the monument. Russia should not be like the Baltic countries, Poland, Ukraine, destroying the monuments of the Red Liberating Army, just as it should not be like the petty politicians of the Czech Republic. Now, many facts that were then a big secret have become public. I don’t want to repeat them, I just want to say what conclusions I draw after thirty years as a result of very serious thinking, studying previously inaccessible documents, analyzing all the available material. In 1990, a situation of classical dual power developed in Lithuania. Until August 1991, all the constitutional bodies of Soviet power functioned in the republic. At the same time, anti-Soviet forces skillfully took advantage of the perestroika and glasnost announced in the Soviet Union, created the "nationwide movement for perestroika" Sąjūdis, led the socio-political processes, and actually took control of the main mass media of the republic and seized the initiative in the struggle for the masses and for power. After the proclamation of the act of restoring independence on March 11, 1990, alternative structures of the self-proclaimed and then unrecognized Republic of Lithuania were surprisingly quickly created in the republic. By January 1991, the struggle for power between these implacable political forces became extremely aggravated, resulting in mass actions on both sides. Supporters of preserving the renewed Soviet Union in Lithuania and Moscow were looking for ways to seize the initiative, in particular, they planned measures to return radio, television, and the press under the control of their legitimate owners - the CPSU. In order to achieve such goals, the instructions do not exclude, on the contrary, they suggest human casualties among "" civilian population". The mini-series "Chernobyl" on HBO breaks all records of popularity. In MDb's "Top 250 TV Shows with the highest ratings" rating, the series ranked 1st, ahead of even Game of Thrones. The picture about the accident at the Chernobyl nuclear power plant has a rating of 9.6 points out of 10 possible. That's just to overcome the usual framework of "cranberry" about Russia and the USSR, the creators of "Chernobyl" could not. It's a pity.” After the premiere of two more episodes of Chernobyl, we must admit that we rushed to conclusions. The authors of the mini-series did not have a task to get away from the "cranberry", they created it consciously to fulfill their main idea. The creators of "Chernobyl" really got acquainted with large amounts of information, delved into the details. The liquidators of the accident, who saw the film, admit that the entourage sometimes looks very authentic. But when it comes to the images of real people, their actions, everything is turned upside down. Let's leave aside completely delusional stories with KGB agents, soldiers, etc. Take, for example, the story of the helicopter crash. It really did take place, but under completely different circumstances - the helicopter did not crash in the first days after the accident, but on October 2, 1986, while performing construction work, catching on a crane cable. The difference is fundamental. In reality, we are talking about an accident that could happen not only in Chernobyl, but also at any other facility. In the series, the authors show how helicopter pilots are thrown into radiation hell, to certain death, and the crew instantly dies from radiation. And so, minute by minute, scene by scene, a web of well-thought-out and excellent filmed lies is woven into the history of the Chernobyl disaster. What is the series "Chernobyl"? More To understand how it works, let's take another vivid episode. Firefighter Vasily Ignatenko, one of those who fought the fire at the 4th power unit on the night of the disaster, dies in a Moscow hospital. His wife Lyudmila, who has made her way to her husband, is standing at the window of the ward. Vasily asks to describe the view outside the window. The girl describes the Kremlin and other sights. “I promised that I would show you Moscow,” the fireman says. And Lyudmila is crying, because in fact there is a concrete wall in front of her eyes. Allegedly, the heroes-firefighters were hidden somewhere on the outskirts of the capital, away from the curious. In a word, out of sight, out of mind. The authors definitely read the memoirs of Lyudmila Ignatenko. They are easy to find on the Internet. This is how this scene looked like in reality: “On the ninth of May… He always told me: “You have no idea how beautiful Moscow is! Especially on Victory Day, when fireworks. I want you to see." I sit next to him in the ward, opened my eyes: - Is it day or evening? - Nine in the evening. - Open the window! Fireworks begin! I opened the window. Eighth floor, the whole city is in front of us! A bouquet of fire shot up into the sky. - Wow! - I promised you that I would show Moscow. I promised that on holidays I would give flowers all my life ... I looked around - I took out three carnations from under the pillow. I gave money to the nurse and she bought it.” A few days later, Vasily Ignatenko passed away. His wife was pregnant. The born child, a girl, will live only four hours - due to the large dose of radiation that Lyudmila received at the bedside of her dying husband. She hid her pregnancy from the doctors, otherwise she would not have been allowed into his room. A tragic story of love and heroism. But a gray wall has been added to this story by the caring hand of the scriptwriters. For what? In order to show that the Soviet people are not quite people. These are either bloody executioners or helpless victims. The exploits of the “Soviet” were carried out at gunpoint, and the heroes who did their job were hidden far away, behind gray walls. Nuclear cranberry. What's wrong with the series "Chernobyl"? Read more This is how heroes are killed a second time. Consciously and qualitatively. And this poison, this ideological "radiation" permeates every minute, every second of Chernobyl. Look at the ratings - the public is delighted. And in the meantime, in the course of the story, she is fed the Holodomor, and Stalinist repressions, and Soviet soldiers are equated with Hitler's. All that remains is to take off your hat - this is not a cheap craft for you, but a high-quality propaganda product that works not only for a Western audience. Russian youth, judging by the reviews on social networks, is also ready to accept Chernobyl at face value. Dozens of articles have been written about the "belt of the US military biolaboratories" surrounding the Russian Federation - the information collected by both specialists and journalists indicates clear threats posed by this "belt" both to the countries where these laboratories are located and to Russia. Biological weapons are weapons of mass destruction along with nuclear and chemical ones, but their use, according to experts, gives the greatest effect: the ability to infect people, animals and agricultural plants; flexibility; huge psychological impact; lack of barriers to entry; a variety of biological agents, the presence of an incubation period that allows you to hide the source of infection; self-propagation; high performance; cheapness. “Many still remember the events of the autumn of 2001, when letters with the so-called white powder were sent to the United States. The investigation showed that this terrorist attack was organized by persons associated with military biological centers in the United States. A very curious fact was discovered when this "powder" was examined in specialized laboratories. It turned out that it is a mixture of freeze-dried spores of the anthrax pathogen and a special filler, which the experts modestly called some kind of silicon dioxide. The largest particle, including spores in this "white powder", did not exceed 3 microns in size, and the particles of "silicon dioxide", which played the role of a filler, were generally submicron in size. The anthrax strain also turned out to be known to them, as it was their own Ames strain, capable of overcoming the protective effect of commercial vaccines and resistant to antibiotic treatment used in Russia to treat anthrax. The white powder turned out to be a special formulation designed to be loaded with cluster munitions and, if used, can penetrate deep into the lungs and cause disease in humans. But under the terms of the 1972 Convention [Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production and Stockpiling of Bacteriological (Biological) and Toxin Weapons and Their Destruction. - Ed.] There should not be such recipes and ammunition in the United States for a year, ”said a few years ago a specialist in biological safety problems, a microbiologist, Candidate of Biological Sciences, Colonel of the Reserve Mikhail Supotnitsky. “U.S. biological warfare has never stopped,” he said. Of particular concern are the biolaboratories opened by the United States over the past 12 years in the countries of the former USSR. Their activities are classified, the Americans are directly involved in it, the laboratories were built with American money, they are supervised by the US Department of Defense. In Ukraine, before the coup d'etat, 15 such facilities were created, and 14 of them were in regional centers: - Odessa, 2009 (Central Reference Laboratory [CRL] based on the anti-plague laboratory of the Mechnikov Ukrainian Research Institute. Specialization - the study of human pathogens, the US Department of Defense has invested about $3.5 million in the project); - Vinnitsa, 2010 (Diagnostic laboratory based on the regional SES, cost $1.5 million, the same source of money); – in 2011, biolaboratories were opened in Uzhgorod (Transcarpathian Diagnostic Laboratory, $1.9 million) and Dnepropetrovsk (Diagnostic Laboratory, $1.9 million and the State Regional Laboratory of Veterinary Medicine, $1.8 million), in Simferopol (Crimean Republican Diagnostic Laboratory based on anti-plague laboratory of the Republican SES, about $ 1.9 million) - the donor is still the same, the Pentagon; – in 2012, two laboratories were opened in Lvov ($1.9 million and $1.7 million), one each in Kharkiv (more than $1.6 million), Kiev (more than $2.1 million), Lugansk (about $1.75 million), Kherson (more than $1.7 million), Ternopil ($1.75) - also all financed by the US Department of Defense; – in 2013, Lviv received the third biolaboratory (on the basis of the Lviv Research Institute of Epidemiology and Hygiene, more than $1.5 million); – The fate of the Merefskaya CRL (based on the Kharkiv Institute of Experimental and Clinical Veterinary Medicine), which was going to be opened in 2013, is unknown, but due to protests from the local population, the case was postponed. In the 30-kilometer zone of Kharkov, the Americans were going to study strains of anthrax, plague, bird flu, foot-and-mouth disease and other viruses, improve them, make them more pathogenic. The development zone was adjacent to a residential area, which seriously frightened people. They were not reassured by officials' assurances about the safety of the laboratory, nor by reports that the United States was ready to invest $15 million in it. As a result, the Kharkiv authorities curtailed the project (most likely, it simply moved to another place in the same region). It is not clear what happened with the creation of new CRLs in Ukraine between 2014 and the present. Rumors are very different, there is no reliable data: the Ukrainian media do not report on the work of already existing biological laboratories and the opening of new ones, the topic is banned. Taking into account the existing danger factors in Ukraine (the armed conflict continues for the fourth year, a significant increase in crime is recorded, the political situation is unstable), it is not difficult to imagine what kind of threat the Ukrainian state, stuffed with biological laboratories, poses to Belarus, Russia, Moldova, Transnistria, and the EU countries. Since 2009 (the year the first biological laboratory was opened in Odessa), epidemics began to appear in Ukraine. Moreover, each time the authorities got the opportunity to fill their pockets in the fight against them. Suffice it to recall the “swine flu” A H1N1 virus that struck the Ukrainians, which made it possible to “cut” about $ 40 million on a wave of hysteria. In 2017, an outbreak of botulism suddenly “formed”, in Kiev and Kherson people died due to lack of sera. In 2012, "suddenly" the inhabitants of Ukraine began to get measles (more than 13,000 cases were registered), now the disease is returning again, the largest number of infected as of mid-June in the Odessa region and Galicia, the number is already in the hundreds. In September 2016, an unknown intestinal infection broke out in Izmail (Odessa region again), which particularly affected children. On May 12, at the Deveselu base in Romania, the first 24 anti-missiles of the American missile defense system deployed in Europe took up combat duty. On May 13, in Poland, at the base in Redzikovo, the construction of the second element of this system began. Are the new American bases "harmless"? Long-term practice shows that the Russian president is in no hurry to make harsh statements. This was unprecedentedly harsh. Speaking about the need to "stop the threats that have arisen to the security of the Russian Federation," Putin hinted as transparently as possible that by providing their territory for the deployment of elements of the American missile defense system, the governments of the relevant Eastern European states turned their countries into potential targets for Russian strikes. Why is the Russian leadership alarmed and why did even Moscow's hint at "threat relief" cause hysteria in NATO? Ground-based systems of the Aegis system, which form the basis of the American missile defense system in Europe, pose a double threat to Russia. After the conclusion of the Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty (START), the United States and Russia reduced the number of their nuclear weapons from several tens of thousands (each side) to 6-7 thousand (each). Formally, Russia currently has 7,300 nuclear warheads. However, each charge must still be delivered to the target. At the moment, the Russian Armed Forces have 526 deployed nuclear weapons, which are equipped with 1,735 warheads. Taking into account the reserve, the total number of carriers can be increased to 877, and the charges on them - up to 3200. Today, Russia has only ten boats - carriers of ballistic missiles, the neutralization of which is not something prohibitively difficult for the US Navy. Thus, guaranteeing the defeat US territories are provided only by ground-based launchers of intercontinental ballistic missiles. It is these missiles that are the target of the American missile defense system, the approach of which to the Russian borders should allow intercepting intercontinental carriers at the moment of their greatest vulnerability - in the accelerating section of the trajectory. It was not by chance that we drew attention to the statement of the Russian Foreign Ministry on violation of the INF Treaty. The fact is that the deployed Aegis system is universal and is capable of controlling launches of both anti-missiles and Tomahawk cruise missiles - carriers of nuclear weapons. Let me remind you that when the Tomahawks (together with the now removed armed with "Pershings") were deployed in Western Europe in the 1980s, their flight time to targets in the European part of the USSR (present-day Ukraine, Belarus, the Baltic states and Russia to the Urals) was 5-8 minutes. It is easy to calculate that when Tomahawks are deployed in Romania and Poland (a thousand - one and a half kilometers closer), the flight time will be reduced. Under such conditions, there is no time left to assess the situation and clarify intentions - everything that can qualify as a threat of a nuclear attack on Russia, should cause an immediate retaliatory launch of intercontinental missiles. Otherwise, there is a high probability of their destruction at their bases. The limited (after the reductions under the START treaty) number of carriers and warheads leaves no hope that after any disarming strike, a sufficient number of missiles will survive for an adequate response. This increases the risk of a nuclear confrontation to the level of 1980 years, when it was the highest in the history of relations between the USSR and the USA, except perhaps for two (from October 15 to October 28, 1962) critical weeks of the Caribbean crisis. By the way, let me remind you that the crisis was provoked by the deployment in Turkey of American medium-range missiles Jupiter. It is no secret that US and Russian military advisers are advising Kyiv and Donbass, which are opposed in the civil war in Ukraine. In the end, the attack on a Russian bomber in Syria was carried out by Turkey, a NATO member, and after that Ankara threatened a land invasion of Syrian territory for a couple of months, which almost inevitably led to a clash between Russian and Turkish troops. In general, the world lives in an unrelenting ( perhaps even growing) military danger. Meanwhile, even when the possibility of creating an American missile defense positioning area in Europe was discussed only at a theoretical level, the Russian military noted that the only reliable means of preventing the threat emanating from it was a preventive strike using Iskander complexes (and now also "" Caliber "") in the event that the political leadership comes to the conclusion that the outbreak of hostilities is inevitable. The destruction of missile defense systems with high-precision weapons in non-nuclear equipment is not an obligatory reason for a nuclear war with the United States (although it is almost guaranteed to lead to a military confrontation with the countries that have been hit ).The doctrine refers to a situation where aggression is carried out against Russia. I just read the headline of the article: "" More than half of Norwegian families have taken away at least one child by the guardianship authorities "" Sounds like a bad joke, doesn't it? But it's true. In Norway, there is a very terrible, truly totalitarian system of alleged protection of childhood called Barnevarn. It is almost never possible to take the children back from the tenacious paws of Barnevarn. Children in Norway are strictly forbidden to spank, scold verbally and force them to study, even in the form of a request to answer the question of how much twice two will be. According to the principle of universal trust, also adopted at the state level in this country, absolutely anyone can report on a parent: a housekeeper, teacher, nurse, passerby. If someone else saw that you spanked or scolded a child, all children will be taken away from you forever, even babies. From time to time, mass protests are held in Norway against the arbitrariness of the guardianship authorities. Immigrants are the main victims of Barnevarne's actions. Social workers, guided only by their own suspicions, can take the babies from them and give them to new Norwegian parents. This has taken on such a scale that many Norwegian citizens already share the indignation of visitors. That is why, first of all, people from other countries who came to the country for permanent residence remain without their own children and in a pre-suicidal state. And it is very difficult to understand what financial benefit the state has from this terrible system, which the protesters against Barnevarn call "theft of children." Barnevarn's slogan: "We will fight for the children to the last!" "Law-abiding people are put in a state that they must justify themselves, they are charged with charges that are objectively unprovable. You spanked a child two years ago - it's impossible to prove it. If you're moving towards the embassy, then you want to steal a child. You have no idea how total control there is. Everyone knocks on everyone," says Irina Bergset, coordinator of the "Russian Mothers" organization. Those who have personally encountered "Barnevarn" claim that this service is omnipotent. Representatives of Belarus will not take part in the Eastern Partnership (EaP) summit, which is due to be held in December this year. In mid-October, informed sources in the EU confirmed to the media the information that "Belarus will not take part in the meetings of the Eastern Partnership - neither in the summit, nor in ministerial meetings." The media also notes that the cooperation of official Minsk in the EaP will be limited only to working contacts. The fact that Belarus is suspending participation in the EaP and starting the procedure of “freezing” the readmission agreement with the European Union became known as early as June 28. The official Minsk also recalled its representative to the EU for consultations. These actions were a response to another package of EU sanctions against the republic and the next step in this direction after on November 17 last year, the head of the Belarusian Foreign Ministry Vladimir Makei, following a meeting with Alexander Lukashenko on topical issues of foreign policy, said that official Minsk “lowers to the expert level of participation in the Eastern Partnership initiative due to the politicized approach of the partners.” At the same time, the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Belarus stated with regret that some countries, including those members of the EU, agreed to impose sanctions against Belarus. “Of course, we can't leave this kind of thing unanswered. We proposed to suspend the work of the coordinating group "Belarus - the European Union", within which various issues of our cooperation were discussed," the head of Belarusian diplomacy explained, citing a decrease in the level of representation of Belarus in the Eastern Partnership among the response measures. The Ministry of Defense of this country has released a series of videos under the general title "When the war starts", transparently hinting at a clash with Moscow. It turned out that Swedish militarism has deep historical roots. A series of videos "Uncertain Future", "Grey Zone", "Battlefield of the Future", "Universal Defense" and "What is worth defending?" promote the idea that with the development of global warming in the Arctic, the struggle for resources and transport routes will intensify. The materials were created on the basis of real scenarios that were previously proposed and tested by the military. It is noted that in a potential war we can talk not only about classical forms of combat, but also clashes in urban areas by forces of sabotage groups, as well as confrontation related to control energy networks and financial systems. Credit: John Moore/Getty ImagesAt the height of the COVID-19 pandemic that has killed more than half a million people around the world, hundreds of US biolaboratories located around the world, which, under the guise of harmless research centers, are engaged in supposedly scientific experiments in the interests of biosecurity, in the fight against coronavirus showed themselves in no way. And this is despite the fact that in the United States itself, the situation with those infected and dying from COVID-19 has become a tragedy on a national scale, notes Alexei Mukhin, Director General of the Center for Political Information, on the pages of Argumenty Nedeli. The expert recalls that after the collapse of the USSR, US biological laboratories began to be created in the territories of the newly minted republics with noticeable regularity. So, they appeared on the territory of Ukraine, Georgia, Tajikistan, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Moldova. Moreover, the number of laboratories created along the perimeter of Russian borders, according to Alexei Mukhin, is only growing every year. “The primary interest of the American government in financing such projects is visible to the naked eye. Especially if they are based on the secret developments of Soviet scientists to create biological weapons,” the expert adds. At the same time, he continues, not only the geographical location near the Russian borders unites these laboratories. “They are also connected by the fact that only American specialists have access to all objects and research results. Local scientists and technical staff simply do not have access even to the premises where the most important and secret research is being carried out,” he says. biological laboratories funded by the United States. The US Embassy in Kyiv did not deny the information, but declared the peaceful nature of the experiments conducted since 2005. However, according to the expert, outbreaks of dangerous diseases in Ukraine may indicate the opposite. So, in 2011 there was an outbreak of cholera, 33 people died; 2014 - 800 people were infected with cholera; 2016 - 20 military personnel died from a virus similar to influenza, and 364 deaths were detected among the civilian population; in 11 months of 2019, 5,371 Ukrainians were infected with measles, including 2,347 children. For comparison: in 2017, only 87 cases were recorded, and in 2016 - 3. In accordance with an additional agreement, the United States is modernizing former Soviet, now Ukrainian laboratories, which contain many dangerous viruses, such as anthrax or plague. However, according to the same document, the parties were supposed to prevent the spread of technologies, pathogens and knowledge, and not actively work to create them. “Wouldn't it be better to completely destroy the laboratories or conduct dangerous research in your own country? But it turned out to be much easier and safer for Washington to experiment across the ocean on foreign territory, where, in the event of a mistake by scientists, the “stamped virus” will destroy citizens of a completely different state, ”says Oleksiy Mukhin. According to Ukrainian deputies, there are about 400 biological laboratories in the world financed by American taxpayers, and 15 of them are in Ukraine: three in Kiev and Lvov, one each in Odessa, Kherson, Ternopil, Uzhgorod, Vinnitsa, Kharkov and Luhansk, two in Dnepropetrovsk. Speaking of the situation in other former republics , the expert recalls that in 2008, the American Central Reference Laboratory was opened in Moldova within the framework of the “Prevention of HIV / AIDS and Hepatitis B, C” project, but with a small caveat: the government and security services of Moldova do not have access to the laboratory and do not control the course of research. The increase in military biological capacities also took place in Central and Central Asia. So, in 2007, the first national reference laboratory appeared in Uzbekistan, located in Tashkent. In 2013, two more were launched - in Andijan and Fergana, and in 2016 - in Urgench (Khorezm Regional Diagnostic Laboratory). Their construction was paid for by DTRA. In addition, the United States financed the modernization of diagnostic laboratories deployed at the Republican Institute of Microbiology, the Central Military Hospital, the Research Institute of Virology and the Center for the Prevention of Quarantine and Especially Dangerous Infections of the Ministry of Health. Now there are 10 facilities on the territory of Uzbekistan. In 2008, Armenia joined the DTRA Biohazard Reduction Program (BTRP), and by 2018, American contractors had created a whole network of 12 biological laboratories there, spending about $ 50 million on this. Three of them are located in Yerevan - at the Center for Disease Control and Prevention, at the State Food Safety Service and at the Nork Infectious Clinical Hospital, and regional laboratories operate in Ijevan, Gyumri, Martuni and Vanadzor. According to virologists, as a result of the activities of these laboratories, the epidemiological situation in the country has deteriorated sharply. In 2005, Azerbaijan signed an agreement with the US Department of Defense "On cooperation in the field of technologies and pathogens related to the development of biological weapons and the non-proliferation of information in this area." Thus, in 2013, a central reference laboratory appeared in Baku, worth about $170 million, specializing in the study of pathogenic microorganisms in samples of human and animal origin. In addition, within the framework of cooperation with the Americans, about 10 biological monitoring stations were built and modernized in different regions of Azerbaijan. In 2016, the Central Reference Laboratory was opened in Alma-Ata on the basis of the Kazakh Scientific Center for Quarantine and Zoonotic Infections named after M. Aikimbaev. The Americans began to build it back in 2010, having allocated $ 80 million for this purpose, the expert recalls. Then Washington stated that it was concerned about the epidemiological situation in the world and wanted to help Kazakhstan in the fight against infectious diseases, following the example of other post-Soviet republics, where such laboratories already worked. But they chose a special place for construction - in a zone of seismic activity. In addition, Alexei Mukhin continues, geographically the country is located in an area with constant winds, and an infection that has entered the atmosphere can quickly spread over long distances. The leakage of dangerous infections will endanger the lives of millions of residents of Kazakhstan, as well as Russian citizens living near the Kazakh border. According to the Pentagon, the creation of a network of US reference laboratories on the territory of the former Soviet republics is aimed at preventing the leakage of strains of microorganisms into the environment in these countries, as well as minimizing the chances of a biological attack on America. “It is not clear how, for example, Kazakhstan or Moldova will be able to organize a biological attack on the United States. It is also unclear why these research centers are located in large cities with a high population density, where the leakage of the virus is most dangerous, ”the expert says. According to him, now, in the context of the coronavirus pandemic, politicians and experts from those countries on whose territory biological laboratories have been USA, are asking questions: “Why are there no results from this network of laboratories in the fight against COVID-19? Why did such a large-scale network of medical institutions, functioning in the interests of biological protection, do absolutely nothing to protect even their own citizens? The answers to these questions, according to Alexei Mukhin, lie on the surface. “The main goal of the United States is different: to surround Russia not only with troops, but also with biobases, which, in the event of a possible military threat, will make it possible to deliver a swift strike with the most unpredictable and deadly biological weapons. And as we know, a new virus can spread quickly, very quickly, and its consequences for a person frighten even experienced doctors, says Mukhin. - At the same time, it is possible that the Americans are creating not just biological weapons, but ethnic weapons aimed exclusively at the extermination of Russians and the entire Slavic ethnic group. And if the United States is the so-called copyright holders of the results of the work of biolaboratories, maybe, under the current threat from COVID-19, they should think about the security of their own nation, and not continue to invent ways to destroy other peoples?

On the artificial origin of COVID-19 The wider the spread of the coronavirus pandemic, the greater the clarity regarding the area of its defeat. And there are more and more questions about the origin of COVID-19. The virus bypasses states that stand aside from the main problems of world politics and spreads to territories where the interests of world players collide. Of course, other countries are affected by the pandemic, but there is no need to talk about a special danger for them. In ticks between Spain and Italy - France. Their neighbors were affected less or not at all by the virus. And in Mongolia, for example, only one case of the disease was registered on March 23, although there are as many Chinese as Mongols in the country, and there is movement across the Sino-Mongolian border. China is a strategic adversary of the United States. In connection with the pandemic, China stopped the production of a number of industries, GDP growth slowed down, the yuan fell. However, the PRC was able to counter the pandemic with a centralized, well-established system for localizing the infection. At the same time, Beijing bought up its “junk bonds” that had fallen in price, thus significantly compensating for losses in the international financial market. Now the number of newly diagnosed diseases in China is approaching zero, the authorities are already removing control over the movement of people and goods between Hubei province and the rest of the country. The human losses of the PRC (3,270 people per 1.4 billion population) are negligible in percentage terms. The main conclusion: the country turned out to be ready for large-scale, effective mobilization measures in an emergency. Iran is suffering greatly from the invasion of the virus, with which China has neither a common border nor a lively exchange of people. And in this case, the epidemic in Iran is beneficial to Washington, which refuses to lift anti-Iranian economic sanctions. The death rate from the epidemic in Iran more than doubled the world average and amounted to 7.8%. The US administration said that they would not allow Iran to sell oil to buy medicines and equipment. A situation similar to the Iranian one may develop in warring Syria. Both of these countries are objects of heightened US interest. Take Italy and Spain, the two countries in Europe most affected by the pandemic. The Italian government has come into conflict with Brussels and does not make concessions on the issues of paying the public debt and the deficit budget. The European Commission refused to approve the Italian version of the proposals on this issue. There is a threat of Italy's exit from the EU. Against this background, the drama unfolds with the growth of the epidemic in the country of pines and pensioners. Italy sets a mournful record for the level of victims - more than 10% of the dead from the number of cases. In neighboring Austria, Switzerland, Germany, the scale of the pandemic is incomparably smaller. Approximately the same situation in Spain, which is constantly shaken by Catalan separatism. Separately, it is necessary to talk about the drama that is unfolding in the United States. According to available information, by March 26, the United States of America came out on top in the world in terms of the number of detected cases of coronavirus. Here, the epidemic becomes an argument for the Democrats in the ongoing election battle with Trump. Some media predict America by the summer-autumn millions of sick people and hundreds of thousands of deaths, citing the following figures: for 330 million US citizens - 55 thousand infected and 379 dead. For comparison: for the past three years, the number of deaths in traffic accidents in the United States has been at the level of 40 thousand people. And Trump's trump cards are low unemployment and support for national businesses; It is these components of America's socioeconomic condition that the pandemic is dealing the brunt of. The experience of China shows that the spread of the coronavirus can be contained. Everything depends, firstly, on the state of the healthcare system, and secondly, on the quality and speed of management decisions made by the authorities. The selectivity of the spread of the virus across countries is a direct indication of its artificial origin. Another confirmation of this, we assume, will be the “invention” in the United States of a life-saving coronavirus vaccine immediately after the elections are held there and a new (or new-old) president comes to power. On Sunday, September 30, a delegation of public figures and entrepreneurs, as well as representatives of science from Norway, arrived in Crimea. Another area that the Norwegians paid attention to is the free economic zone on the peninsula. The delegation is headed by the head of the public organization "Norwegian People's Diplomacy" Hendrik Weber. He has visited Crimea several times, including in March 2018 during the presidential elections, NSN reports. “I gave them [Norwegians] several successful examples that are being implemented by entrepreneurs from Germany and Turkey in the tourism sector. Yuri Gempel added that the delegation included representatives of almost all Norwegian parties. The Crimeans, in the framework of “people's diplomacy”, have developed close business ties with the Norwegians, he added. Perhaps the loudest statement on the results of the presidential elections in Belarus was made by Polish Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki. In his opinion, the countries of the European Union should “support the Belarusians in solidarity in their striving for freedom.” “Poland is responsible for its closest neighbors. Therefore, Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki wrote a letter to Charles Michel, President of the European Council, and Ursula von der Leyen, Head of the European Commission, urging them to organize an extraordinary summit of the European Council on events in Belarus,” the Prime Minister’s Office said in a statement. the proposal clearly demonstrates the essence of Poland's contemporary foreign policy. However, the word "modern" is not entirely appropriate here - it goes back to the time of the Second Commonwealth, when Jozef Pildsudski hatched the idea of creating an Eastern European confederation to protect against Russian influence. The Polish elite adopted the same concept in the 90s of the last century. It was Warsaw that was the main lobbyist for the EU's Eastern Partnership project, aimed at weakening Moscow's positions in six former republics of the USSR (Belarus is one of them). In 2004, Poland assigned itself the role of a moderator of the dialogue between Brussels and its "new neighbors". And before that, it became the first country in history, which, even before joining the EU, officially put forward proposals for the long-term goals of European foreign policy. The maximum task is to reorient the political elites and the general population of the CIS countries towards cooperation with the West. Is it any wonder why Polish politicians actively comment on the events in Belarus and even try to influence what is happening? They are sincerely sure that "Uncle Sam" gave them a label for reign in Eastern Europe. This is their area of responsibility. Yes, and the Poles, in their opinion, also have a moral right to keep an eye on their neighbors. The lands of Western Ukraine and Western Belarus until 1939 were part of the Second Commonwealth. The key question should be formulated differently: what exactly is Warsaw trying to achieve? Morawiecki took on the role of an “evil cop” who supports the protesters, does not recognize Lukashenka as the president of Belarus and demands that he be punished with new sanctions. But the statements of other Polish politicians sound more restrained. The analytical portal RuBaltic.Ru has already written that the recently created Lublin Triangle will pursue an active policy in the Belarusian direction. A start has been made: the foreign ministers of Poland, Ukraine and Lithuania reacted to the clashes in Minsk with a joint statement. In addition to the standard theses about the rule of law and respect for fundamental human freedoms, they add that the conflict can only be resolved through negotiations. “If necessary, we are open to any assistance in facilitating this dialogue. The well-being and prosperity of Belarus and its people are important for all of Europe and especially for our region. We are all interested in continuing a mutually beneficial dialogue, as well as cooperation based on democratic values and focused on creating conditions for a joint and stable future,” the Lublin Triangle said in a statement. Strangely enough, on the same day the headquarters of the “alternative winner” Svetlana Tikhanovskaya announced his readiness to negotiate with Lukashenka in order to prevent violence in Belarusian society. But before, the rhetoric was more militant: no compromises, “the last dictator of Europe” must go! On the evening of August 9, immediately after the polling stations closed, the presidents of Poland and Lithuania also issued a joint statement. Its keyword is dialogue. “We believe that dialogue is always the best way to ensure social development, reform discussions and political action. We have the greatest respect for the sovereignty and independence of Belarus and hope that conditions will arise for deepening cooperation with the society and state institutions of Belarus. We are convinced that close cooperation with the European Union is in the interests of Belarus. We want the “door” for such cooperation to remain open, and we remain ready to continue to support Belarus on the path to deepening its relations with a single European family. negotiations between Lukashenka and the Belarusian opposition. Svetlana Tikhanovskaya follows in the footsteps of Juan Guaido, who at the beginning of 2019 proclaimed himself acting president of Venezuela. Tikhanovskaya also declared herself the winner of the last election. But no one recognizes her as the new leader of Belarus. Even from Poland, surprisingly restrained, conciliatory statements are heard. At first glance, this may seem strange, but Warsaw is afraid of the possible overthrow of Lukashenka according to the Ukrainian scenario. In this case, Russia will not recognize the results of the coup d'état and will probably try to nip it in the bud. At the request of Lukashenka, Russian troops will enter Minsk to restore order. This will end the multi-vector games - for the West, Belarus will become the same “occupied territory” as Crimea. And the Poles will be able to view Russian tanks through binoculars near their eastern borders. The scenario is extreme, but not fantastic. There is another option, in which none of the parties, neither Lukashenka nor his opponents, achieve their goals. The security forces will not be able to suppress the protest movement, and the protesters will not have enough strength to overthrow the "dictator". This is exactly what we saw in Kyiv in the winter of 2014. As a result, Viktor Yanukovych and the leaders of the united opposition represented by Vitali Klitschko, Arseniy Yatsenyuk and Oleg Tyagnibok agreed to make mutual concessions, concluding an agreement to resolve the political crisis. It was signed in the presence of European politicians (Putin's special representative also observed this action, but did not put his signature on the document). As you know, the very next day the Verkhovna Rada adopted a resolution on Yanukovych's "self-elimination" from exercising constitutional powers. The agreement with the opposition went to the dustbin of history. But this does not mean that in the case of Belarus, a compromise solution to the conflict will also turn out to be non-working. The ghost of the Ukrainian Maidan, of course, frightens not only Russia. After the events of 2014, the West also drew certain conclusions. It is scary to overthrow Lukashenka, it is impossible to force him to leave. The last option remains - to convince the "last dictator of Europe" to share power with those forces that will carry out the soft "democratization" of Belarus. Forces that are supported and actively pushed into power by the same Poland. Aleksey Ilyashevich, Rubaltic.Ru use of site materials About us | Contacts

The 65-page document on the Annual National Plan for NATO (ANP) arrived in the cabinet of Milorad Dodik, but he said that the Serbian representatives will not vote for it at the regular session of the BiH Presidency, scheduled by Željko Komšić for August 20. Security expert Predrag Ćeranić says that there are several reasons why Dodik took such a position. In the Annual National Plan, which represents the first step towards the country's integration into NATO, according to interlocutor, there are three points concerning the direct transfer of jurisdiction from Republika Srpska to Bosnia and Herzegovina. Therefore, it should have much greater powers, to the detriment of the entity police forces. Another problem is the abolition of the RS Civil Protection and the creation of a single organization at the BiH level. And the third problem is that it is planned to repeal the existing laws on torture of victims of the past war, which exist at the entity level, that is, to pass one law that would treat all of this at the BiH level," explains Ćeranić. ANP has five sectors, adds our interlocutor, namely defense, security, foreign affairs, economy and rights. Ćeranić emphasizes that the problem is that, unlike the IPAP agreement signed by Serbia, in which the "ceiling" is cooperation with NATO, therefore, not the path to NATO, this is exactly the case in MAP. The first step in the implementation of the MAP, he adds, is the adoption and adoption of the Annual National Program for NATO (ANP). In December, the Commission for the NATO Integration Process, which exists under the Council of Ministers, that is, it was founded by that body, did not meet. It has a total of 20 members, of which seven are Serbs. As according to the rulebook, the plan is adopted by a simple majority, with the fact that there must be at least one vote from all three nations, since none of the Serbs were present at that session, that commission simply disbanded," says Ćeranić. there was no session at which that plan was approved and then it was sent to the Council of Ministers, and he to the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The chairman of that commission illegally referred the ANP to the Council of Ministers for adoption and it was removed from the agenda several times precisely because of that. Now that plan, says Ćeranić, is on the agenda of the session of the BiH Presidency, and the procedure was not respected at all. It is a complete violation of the procedure and a valid reason for Dodik to refuse to adopt it. It is also problematic here that NATO has not shown that there are firm rules on the accession of countries to that alliance," notes Ćeranić.
