The basin is a case of spontaneous renaturation in the heart of the capital. The councilor for urban planning: ''''The industrial area is contaminated''''. The Territorial Forum: '''"We do not know that any analyzes have been carried out'"'"The natural oasis of one of the most polluted urban areas in the center of Rome is in danger of dying. This is Lake Bullicante ex Snia, a basin of water born in 1992 from the excavation for a shopping center in the Prenestino – Pigneto district, in the eastern quadrant of the capital. A sort of ''miracle'' as those who live in the area often say. Among the five cases of spontaneous renaturation in Europe, together with its Brussels twin Marais Wiels, this area is rich in biodiversity. It also has great historical value: immersed in the waters are the ruins of the disused Snia Viscosa factory, an important piece of Italian industrial archaeology. Thanks to these characteristics, the lake has become a point of reference for the inhabitants of the neighborhood and for numerous associations, which organize cultural or educational events. In addition to the permanent territorial forum of the Parco delle Energie, there are also the young people of Fridays to defend it for Future. In 2021 part of the area was declared a natural monument by the Lazio Region. However, the efforts of citizens risk becoming in vain. Nicola Zingaretti, before resigning as governor, did not sign the act to extend the protections. However, the battle to protect the lake continues at the Tables with the Region and in the neighbourhood, where demonstrations and actions to raise awareness among the inhabitants continue.'"'"Regardless of the fact that for us the conditions for the adoption of the however legally the president Zingaretti could not sign the deed for the extension of the natural monument, because the opinion of the environment commissions was lacking'"'", explains the owner of the area, Ponente 1978 srl, who adds having presented numerous projects for the site, also taking into account the '''"fruition of the community'"'". '"'"From the Department of Urban Planning'"'" of the Municipality of Rome Capitale '"'"we have not had positive feedback and we are always there at the window, because these projects can only be done together and not alone '"'". In the lake area, during the summer of 2022, there was a cut of vegetation contested by the Forum. The property defends itself, claiming that a cleaning was carried out at the request of the Rome Police Headquarters. For this reason, no proceedings have been concluded'"'" against the deed, concludes Ponente 1978 srl.'"'"First of all we must distinguish the part of the lake, which is already within the perimeter of the Natural Monument and that thanks to the joint work with the Agenzia del Demanio, state property is being made, on the other hand the former industrial one, for which the request for a restoration and conservation rehabilitation permit is under investigation at the offices. - affirms the councilor for urban planning of Roma Capitale, Maurizio Veloccia - As regards possible redevelopment projects for the area, it is quite clear that these will depend on the possible extension, or otherwise, of the Natural Monument restriction as well as on a land reclamation plan which, precisely at the request of Rome, were analyzed and found to be contaminated with threshold values such as not to allow, at the moment, destinations other than production ones'"'". '"'"While we are fighting with technical opinions and scientific data in hand, to unblock the Decree for the enlargement of the Natural Monument to the remaining 40% of the former SNIA in the Region - replies the Forum - councilor Veloccia breaks the silence to take a position on the extension of environmental protection as if it did not concern Rome as the capital, but to inform us that instead an investigation is actually being carried out in its offices, the one for the Building Permit requested by Pulcini. On the indication that the soils have been polluted, one wonders with astonishment when it was possible to carry out these analyses, given that no institution has opened those gates to ascertain the environmental damage, and now to certify the presence of protected habitats. In any case, it doesn't scare us at all if some pollution value is confirmed in some areas, the fact that the rest of the factory is now a Natural Monument shows us the right choice, that of environmental restoration'"'". “The battle for Lake Bullicante ex Snia is part of our fight for climate justice. For this, we embrace the one for the enlargement of the Natural Monument”. The young people of Fridays for Future Rome, the local group of the international movement founded by the Swedish Greta Thunberg, have no doubts: the natural oasis on via Prenestina, one of the busiest in the capital, must be protected. To defend the environment on a global level it is often necessary to start from smaller realities, such as one's own city. Even "rewilding, (like what is happening at the former Snia) done well, followed and cared for for the necessary time, is a way of tackling the climate crisis", explains Emanuele Genovese, 25, who recently finished his mandate as the Capitoline referent of Fridays for Future and has followed, alongside the permanent territorial Forum of the Energy Park, the meetings with the Lazio Region. Gradually restoring an area in an urban and densely populated context like that of the Roman suburbs to nature would have enormous benefits: it mitigates the high temperatures that often make the esthete unlivable in the city, absorbs the noise of cars and public transport and offers a peaceful and relaxing refuge for all the inhabitants of the neighborhood. According to the activist, there is also one more reason to side with the Lake: integral protection is not just a "habit", it is a fundamental step in the fight for justice climate at the city level. "It crosses a procedural dimension, because it provides a precious space for the community" for sharing, comparison and democracy. In fact, the area already hosts numerous events and assemblies of the inhabitants of the neighbourhood. In the future it will be fundamental "for those participatory processes with which to build ecological reconversion together", says Genovese. The establishment of the natural monument is then a "reparative and redistributive" act towards the citizenry. "It is the reaction to those who have committed an environmental crime", by appropriating a public good, such as the aquifer that feeds the Lake Bullicante basin and have managed it for years "to the detriment of the community". Considering all this value is essential to "meet" the challenges of the climate emergency. The former Snia Bullicante lake risks dying, due to the resignation of Nicola Zingaretti. Before continuing his political career in the Chamber of Deputies, the former president of the Lazio Region did not sign the extension of the Natural Monument for the basin born on the industrial remains - "the monster" - of the disused viscose factory. Now, this precious casket of biodiversity a few steps from the traffic of Rome, is exposed "to the speculative aims that have already interested it in the past", explains Sabrina Baldacci of the Permanent Territorial Forum of the Energie Park, the assembly of territorial realities and inhabitants that since 2010 takes care of the whole area of the former Snia. This body of water of about 1 hectare originates in fact in 1992, from "an abusive deed". The employees of Antonio Pulcini, the entrepreneur at the head of the Ponente 1978 srl building company, intercepted an aquifer, digging to build the underground car park of a shopping centre. Despite attempts to channel it, the water began to flow and filled the excavation, which became a real lake. Since then there have been many promises and projects to give it back to the citizens, but also those, on the part of the private sector, to transform it, by erecting skyscrapers or making it a film set. In 2004 a part of the area was expropriated to be used as a public park, but it was returned to the Romans only ten years later, with "the so-called breach of Portonaccio", the entrance that leads from the homonymous street to the Lake. After various meetings with the Municipality and the Region, a decree signed by Zingaretti in June 2020 made the body of water a natural monument. Approximately 40% of the site was excluded from the protections, but at the end of a year of monitoring, it was expected to be extended. According to the property, however, the governor of Lazio '''"legally'"'" could not have signed ' "'"the act for the''extension of the natural monument because the opinion of the environment commissions was lacking'"'". According to the surveys of Ispra (the Higher Institute for Environmental Protection and Research), a very rare phenomenon is taking place within the perimeter of the former Snia: the spontaneous renaturation of an urban area. However, the signature for the enlargement of the Monument has not yet arrived. The Region has asked for new exams. The process – according to a letter delivered by the governor to the population – cannot be concluded due to "conflicting opinions of the various subjects in charge". However, these subjects "are not made explicit", says Baldacci, "the only one to have presented observations against the project for now is the property". While awaiting clarification, citizens live in doubt. In fact, after Zingaretti's resignation, few responses came from those directly involved in the Lazio Region, especially from the Department of the Environment and from the Presidency itself. Meanwhile, the builder, last summer, in the area still owned by him and, despite the landscape and archaeological constraints, "cut down many trees" as denounced by the Forum. Among these are also protected species such as the Aleppo pine. The police and forest rangers, called by the citizens, however were unable to intervene. Instead, the owner says that '''' a cleaning was done at the request of the Police Headquarters. For this reason, no proceedings have been concluded against the deed. According to the Forum, '''"this motivation is belied by the reading of a note itself, issued by the Porta Maggiore police station, which asked for the cleaning for safety reasons of a completely different area, the strip that separates the Energie Park from the escarpment behind the lake. What clearly emerged is that the large-scale operations for the elimination of vegetation conducted by Ponente '78 in the spring of 2021 were abusive. There was no request or authorization issued by the Superintendency and by the competent bodies to intervene with the bulldozers to remove the soil and to cut down dozens of tall trees, given the nesting period of the birds, nor to carry out activities of excavation and earthmoving, actions carried out illegally for which criminal proceedings are in progress'"'". '"'"Since the inauguration of Mayor Gualtieri - the activists always underline - that the Forum Parco delle Energie has requested a meeting with councilor Veloccia to find out the intentions of the new administration on the future of the former factory (...) for a strategic reforestation project to enhance the ecological network of the territory which should be brought to the Council for approval and which instead lies in the drawer. The councilor should also provide clarifications on the state of the art of other important procedures, the state property of the entire body of water and the investigation for environmental damage hinged on the Ministry of the Environment following the devastation of the habitats carried out by Ponente 1978 srl, the company that owns the land, on the portion of the area subject to the expansion. The Assessor in one year of activity has never granted this interlocution, just as the Council has not given an answer to Resolution of the Town Hall Council V unanimously approved on 27 October which calls for the same commitments. While we are fighting with technical opinions and scientific data in hand, to unblock the Decree for the enlargement of the Natural Monument to the remaining 40% of the former SNIA in the Region, the commissioner Veloccia breaks the silence not to take a position on the extension of the protection environmental as if it did not concern Rome, but to inform us that instead an investigation is actually being carried out in its offices, the one for the Building Permit requested by Pulcini. On the indication that the soils were polluted, one wonders with amazement when it was possible to carry out these analyses, given that no institution has opened those gates to ascertain the environmental damage, and now to certify the presence of protected habitats'"' ". Lake Bullicante ex Snia, thanks to the citizens who have been committed to protecting it for years, has also become a place of culture and awareness. In fact, in 2019 the NGO Crocevia, which has been involved in cooperation, international solidarity and nutrition and protection of biodiversity since 1958, moved its archives and media library to the Parco delle Energie. “It's about 2,000 films, a few thousand slides and printed photographs, in addition to the paper archive - explains Danilo Ricciardello of the association - A heritage also recognized by the Ministry of Culture. We wanted to keep it in a park where biodiversity is alive and lively, also given the history of the lake". Crocevia, together with the Sapienza University of Rome, often organizes film screenings, conferences and book presentations on biodiversity and peasant struggles. Getting young people and students to know the naturalistic aspect of the former Snia park and involving them in its protection is also the challenge of Giulia Olivieri, 27 years old. In his period of civil service with the association he chose to deal with environmental disclosure. “Doing it here in this place, near the lake, has an added value. – he says – It offers us a stimulating environment to understand environmental issues. Bringing school children here allows them to experience first-hand the fact that struggles are not only waged, but can also be won, if the citizens organize themselves". The former Snia park, in addition to the natural one, also contains an incredible historical heritage. In operation from 1922 to 1954, the viscose factory, from which the lake takes its name, represented a decisive element in the development of the Roman district of Prenestino Labicano. "It employed up to 3,000 workers, mostly women, and was a stronghold of anti-fascist struggles," explains Sabrina Baldacci. Under the industrial surface there is one of the best preserved anti-aircraft shelters in Italy while the ruins of the factory are protected as industrial archeology. The stories, documents and files of the workers of the former Snia Viscosa are kept in the Territorial Documentation Center Maria Baccante. Abandoned by the property after the factory was abandoned, the precious material was saved in 1995 by a group of inhabitants of the neighborhood, the same ones who had occupied the sheds and created the Ex Snia Social Center. On 3 July 2012, the Management regional authority for the cultural and landscape heritage of Lazio has recognized its value and today the Archive is visited by researchers, students, industrial history enthusiasts as well as by relatives of former male and female workers who want to reconstruct their family history, or simply by curious people who want to learn more about the city of Rome."

The confrontation with the EU pushes the government to eliminate from the maneuver the threshold within which traders could have refused to use the official pos. The obligation to accept the pos remains, regardless of the amounts. The executive has canceled the rule included in the maneuver which provided for a limit of 60 euros under which fines were not triggered for traders who did not accept electronic payments. Now he is studying forms of refreshments for operators who will have the burden of commissions. The turning point announced by Giorgia Meloni and was confirmed by Giancarlo Giorgetti in the Budget Committee, where the Minister of Economy outlined the maxi-amendment with which the budget law is modified. '"'"The government - assured Giorgetti - is open to a discussion with the Budget commission regarding a solution compatible with the legislation and the commitments undertaken by the previous government on the Pnrr'"'". This is the crux which, in the interlocution with Brussels, led to the rethinking. The executive supports - explained Giorgetti - forms of compensation for operators who will have to face a greater burden for the commissions applied to these transactions'"'". Covid has marked a watershed in Italy from which there is no go further back on electronic payments: our country, among the last in Europe, is gradually climbing back up the slope. In the first half of 2022, the growth in digital payments seen in 2021 continued, achieving a +22% thanks to the leap in contactless (+49%) and smartphones or bracelets (+139%) above the euro area average . It therefore seems that some of the usual habits are changing, linked a lot, as stated in a paper by the Bank of Italy, to the degree of computer knowledge, age and geographical position, rather than purely fiscal issues . Of course, what Italy is not lacking in is tools: cards are plentiful in customers' wallets and the diffusion of POS is even above average. Technology also opens up new spaces and closes others, the physical ones of the branches given the increasingly massive use of home banking. From ABI data, in 2021 there were 1.21 average monthly visits to the agency against 1.71 in 2008 and since then the branches have dropped by 36% to 21,650 (in 2022 the decline continued). However, the bank maintains contact with customers via the "advanced" ATMs, apps, online and the telephone. ''"'"With reference to the charges linked to transactions carried out using electronic payment instruments - Fabrizio Balassone of Bank of Italy pointed out in the hearing on the economic maneuver - it should be remembered that even cash has costs linked to security (such as those connected with theft, transport of valuables, insurance). Our estimates for 2016 indicate that, for merchants, the cost of cash as a percentage of the transaction amount is higher than that of debit and credit cards'"'". The world of commerce has reiterated that it has no preclusions to the use of cards but asks for special attention especially for some categories of merchants whose margins risk being crushed or even eliminated under the burden of electronic money. '"'"We would be in favor of a cashless world but the costs are not only passed on to the merchants'"'", affirm the representatives of Confesercenti. ''"'"We are not against the use of cards'"'", echoes Lino Stoppani, president of Fipe Confcommercio, who however underlines how, for example, for certain micropayments there is no economic convenience because often commissions and costs landlines weigh like ballast especially on small businesses'' which have little bargaining power. Italians like more and more'' to make purchases by paying with contactless. To date, in fact, in stores, 7 out of 10 digital payments are made by bringing the card, smartphone or smartwatch close to the POS. Health also passes through technologies and the national system must ensure its widest diffusion and use, to avoid healthcare at different speeds throughout the territory and guarantee all citizens the right to health guaranteed by the Constitutional Charter. This is the message launched by the 23rd national conference of the Italian Association of Clinical Engineers (AIIC) which took place in Florence from 10 to 13 May with the title 'Innovation and accessibility: the governance of health technologies as a social challenge'. The event registered 2,138 participants, 929 enrolled in training courses, 221 speakers and 37 in-depth sessions on topics such as innovation, sustainability, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, telemedicine and European regulations. The 23rd conference of the Association also coincided with the thirtieth anniversary of Aiic: the association was founded in 1993, at the dawn of the technological revolution in healthcare services. In the closing ceremony of the event, Francesco Pezzatini (AIIC vice-president), Carmelo Minniti (AIIC vice-president) and Stefano Bergamasco (president of the conference scientific committee and AIIC study center coordinator), underlined the success of the event "which made it possible to celebrate the 30 years of life of the Association looking courageously forward and trying to contribute with competence and strategic vision to the future of the NHS”. The conference in Florence was therefore an opportunity to take stock of the 30 years of Aiic which has recorded a constant increase in members: from 18 clinical engineers in 1993 to 382 in 2008 up to 1,976 in 2023.“The numbers are in constant growth - highlighted the AIIC president Umberto Nocco - and indicate an almost homogeneous geographical distribution between North, Center and South. It is also interesting to observe the professional population: the young component is increasingly relevant, while the 'female' component is becoming the majority, even if today there is absolute parity in the gender balance”. Attention to the 'social' role of innovation in healthcare was highlighted with the presentation of the Social Manifesto, launched by AIIC with Cittadinanzattiva to draw the country's attention to the challenges that need to be faced for a balanced, timely and useful system development . During the event, prizes were also awarded for the best multidisciplinary projects (Apulia and Lombardy were awarded above all) and the three Innovation 2023 prizes assigned to an intelligent treatment coordination platform based on artificial intelligence, a wearable medical device for the diagnosis and monitoring of Parkinson's and a more accurate computed tomography system. People who have evening chronotype, i.e. who prefer to stay up late and are more active in the second part of the day, have worse eating habits than people with morning chronotype, i.e. who wake up early in the morning, are more active in the first part of the day of the day and go to bed early. This is what emerges from the research on a sample of overweight people, released on the occasion of the national congress of the Italian Society of Human Nutrition underway in Florence. The study, carried out by Sofia Lotti and her research group from the University of Florence , investigated the role of chronotype on body composition, eating habits and cardiometabolic risk parameters on a sample of 51 overweight and obese subjects, recruited at the clinical nutrition unit of Aou Careggi in Florence from March to April 2023, composed of 71% women and 29% men, mean age of 50.3 ± 13.5 years. It was found that 26% of the participants had an evening chronotype, 74% morning ones. From the analysis of eating habits it emerged that subjects with evening chronotype consumed significantly more daily calories than morning ones and that the calorie distribution of meals varied according to circadian preference, with evening subjects consuming significantly more calories at lunch and dinner. Evening subjects also reported eating a diet significantly higher in carbohydrates and fat, due to higher consumption of sugary drinks, fast food and sweets. Analyzing the time of consumption of meals, it emerged that subjects with an evening chronotype tended to consume all meals later than those in the morning. '"'"In conclusion, although no significant differences emerged for body composition between the different chronotypes, the results of the study associated evening subjects with worse eating habits both in terms of dietary quality and in terms of meal timing, eating more total daily calories, fat and carbohydrates, and eating meals at later times. In addition, evening subjects reported lower blood levels of folic acid and vitamin B12'"'". PI IT00876481003 - © Copyright ANSA - "

Journey to a school in Rome where many young people, especially girls, learn the oldest stage magic to surprise and make us children again. Women and the Circus, a story of emancipation and challenge. Circus literature is full of past and present examples of how the pink universe has, with the Circus, been able to assert its artistic and expressive freedom and, in this story, the example of the Roman School of Circus is a confirmation contemporary: more and more girls want to attend it, and it's not just a Capitoline phenomenon. In this Magazine we tell the circus art 2022, some emerging protagonists and the peculiarities of the training no longer linked only to the charm of surprise and amazement but to the need to structure a scenic composition involving the spectator, large and small, in a imaginary capable of animating a story perhaps to be told to friends once one leaves the ''Chapiteau''. In the 1960s, the traditional circus began to lose popularity. The public is increasingly interested in animal rights and interested in alternative forms of entertainment. The new circus is a live performance movement which then developed in France in the 1970s and early 1980s, using the theatrical aspects of the circus to tell a story and dramatizing acrobatic acts. Among the first contemporary circus companies we remember the'"'" Cirque Bonjour'"'", '"'"Le Puits aux Images'"'" which would become the '"'"Cirque Baroque'"'", '" '"Cirque Aligre'"'", '"'" Cirque Plume '"'", '"'" Archaos. Their shows have totally changed the point of view of the public, and of the institutions on the circus world, also implementing a real training in the circus arts open to all, unlike the traditional circus where training took place within the " big families” itinerant circus. The popularity of this new way of conceiving the art of the circus was marked by one of the most famous theatrical stages in the world: the Avignon Festival which in 1995, for the first time in the history of the festival, included a circus show on its billboard: The Cri du Caméléon. This event represents an important turning point as it will offer better recognition of circus as an art and formalize this new form which, in the course of its evolution, is now called contemporary circus. One of the major characteristics of the contemporary circus is, as demonstrated by most of the current creations, that of focusing only on a single discipline (for example juggling, trapeze or wire, etc.), and of making it a complete show. The fruitful exchange with the other arts is also a feature of the contemporary circus. Indeed, dance, theatre, music, video or architecture or the arts have influenced many circus arts in recent decades. It is also common for circus performers to enlist theater directors or choreographers to help them create their shows. Called ''Clic'', the work is a reconstruction of a library bandwagon with a life of its own that goes among the people and '"'"spreads knowledge and culture in an original way - says Catia Fusciardi, director of the Roman Circus School - welcoming visitors in a magical environment suspended in time'"'". Clic is much more than a simple traveling library, it is an installation, handmade by the designer Simone Alessandrini, which transforms the place that hosts it. The guardians of the library and its knowledge are the artists of the Circus Follies company who present anecdotes and stories about the circus to the public with impromptu virtuosity of balance, juggling and clowning. The Community Library of the Scuola Romana di Circo collects, preserves, enhances and shares the most important books and documentary materials - analogue and digital - related to the history of the circus. '"'"It is an innovative model of library - Catia always explains - which organizes cultural events and promotes reading, creative pedagogy and live entertainment; a point of reference and an aggregation center for students and professionals, children and teenagers of the neighborhood, simply curious''. The Roman Circus School was born on February 1, 2006 from the need of a group of young artists to create a space in their city dedicated to the study and sharing of circus arts and street theatre. Over the years he has developed a pedagogical project that combines sports training with artistic research thanks to the contribution of many passionate professionals and gives life to the Circus Community Library. The Roman Circus School places the technique at the service of the scenic gesture, it is characterized by the attention to the acrobatic movement and the individual and authentic artistic research. From 2006 to today it has trained about 500 artists, every year there are about 30 professional students. In addition to professional training, the School organizes amateur courses for children and adults. From contemporary circus schools to the scene, the step is not so easy and discounted. An emerging example is ''"'"Il Petit Cabaret 1924'"'" born in 2015, a traveling show of various art, which is inspired by the light-hearted variety theater of the beginning of the last century, a period - defined by the circus themselves - of great hope and social and artistic emancipation. The artists who perform during the show are Italian and of international origin and offer an entertainment program to the rhythm of jazz, charleston and swing. The show is always a surprise for the public because a vast repertoire is proposed and it is different with each assembly of the big top, in circus jargon the ''Chapiteau''. '"'"Each of the spectators - says Romeo Matteo Zanaboni Dina, director of the Petit Cabaret 1924 - is a welcome guest and is snatched from reality to be led into an engaging and emotional experience. The work of art is not the product of creation, but the artist himself'"'"."

Pensions will be able to be exceptionally valorized already in the middle of this year. Also, already in August, the parental allowance will increase significantly. Sociálna poisťovňa (SP) will start keeping the insured's electronic account and will inform future pensioners about their pension forecast. This follows from the amendment to the Act on Social Insurance, which was signed by President Zuzana Čaputová. The original aim of the amendment was to adjust the right to a parental pension contribution for parents of professional soldiers and police officers. However, the members of the National Council (NR) of the Slovak Republic submitted and approved several amendments to it, which significantly changed the original wording. The parental allowance will be exceptionally increased by the approved amendment of Petra Krištúfková (We are a family) from August 1 of this year to the extent that was increased by traditional valorization from January 1, 2024. This will no longer occur subsequently. For parents who previously worked, its amount will increase to 473.30 euros. For those who did not work, to 345.20 euros. In the final vote, the proposal of Erik Tomáš (not classified) for an earlier possibility of extraordinary valorization of pensions from July 1 of this year was also passed. Until now, the valid regulations made it possible to take into account high inflation in pensions during the year up to and including January 1, 2024. Pensions will increase exceptionally if the condition is met that the cumulative month-on-month growth in consumer prices for pensioner households exceeds 5%. Selected accident benefits will also be increased exceptionally. During the traditional valuation at the beginning of next year, the relevant percentage of this year's extraordinary increase in benefits will be taken into account. The adopted amendment proposal of the deputies We are a family introduces an obligation for the Social Insurance Company to keep an electronic account of the insured, which replaces the current individual account of the insured. At the same time, it also leaves room for written communication in case the insured person prefers such a form. In order to consistently inform the insured person, SP will in the future be obliged to send the insured person information about anticipated pension claims from pension insurance and old-age pension savings, the so-called pension forecast. It will inform the insured not only about the forecast of his pension, but also about the variables on which his future pension depends. The amount of the pension is also influenced by his own decision, therefore he will be provided with various alternative forecasts, adapted to his age. Pension management companies (DSS) will be obliged to provide the SP with data on the saver's birth number and his forecast of the old-age pension from the second pillar. Compared to the original proposal, the MPs also modified the parental contribution to the pension for parents of professional soldiers and policemen. The creation of this right will require the active access of a police officer or a professional soldier, through his written declaration. The amendment also determines the substantive jurisdiction of the social security departments of the ministries and the Military Social Security Office for the action and decision-making on the parental pension, which is derived from ""active '"'" a policeman or a professional soldier whose service relationship continues. One of the changes was also passed in the amendment by the deputy Petr Kremský (OĽANO). He recommends finding more detailed information on the calculation of the amount of the unemployment benefit on the website of the Social Insurance Agency. Also when entrepreneurs and other self-employed persons (SZČO) are not compulsorily insured, they may be entitled to a benefit. "The manner in which the employment relationship was terminated (by agreement or termination) and whether it was a fixed-term or indefinite time. "If the employer's insolvency occurs in the period from July 1, 2023 to June 30 2024, the amount of the guarantee insurance benefit can reach a maximum amount of 3,912 euros. The employer is insolvent in connection with the claim for the guarantee insurance benefit if a proposal to declare bankruptcy has been submitted to the relevant court or the court has started bankruptcy proceedings without this proposal under the Bankruptcy and Restructuring Act. China's real estate sector will probably struggle with the "persistent depression" for several years. Analysts of the investment bank Goldman Sachs stated this on Monday, adding that the problems of this sector will continue to have a negative impact on the development of the Chinese economy. This was reported by the agency. The problems of the real estate sector are particularly felt in smaller cities and in the financing of private developers, analysts said. They pointed to the promise of Chinese politicians that they do not plan to use the real estate sector to support short-term economic growth, which means that China wants to limit economic dependence on this sector. "Given these facts, we estimate that the recovery in the Chinese real estate sector will take the form of the letters L,''" Goldman Sachs analysts reported. The Chinese real estate sector fell into a deep debt crisis in the past two years. The reason was the Chinese government's measures to limit the rapidly growing debt. Many developers thus did not get access to new loans, and had difficulty completing the properties under construction. and repay the original debts. In response to the collapse of the sector, the government later adopted several support measures, and the unexpected cancellation of anti-pandemic measures in December of last year also partially helped, despite this, investors' optimistic expectations regarding the Chinese real estate sector did not last long. "We are convinced that the priority the Chinese government is to manage several years of slowdown in the sector, rather than ensure a return to the original strong growth,'''' Goldman Sachs analysts said. As they added, they do not expect a repeat of the situation from 2015-2018, when the government financed a recovery program for poorer urban areas. They expect only gradual changes from Beijing to support the market, such as a further reduction in mortgage interest rates, or the relaxation of restrictions on the sale of houses in large cities.

Douglas Atkinson, a political scientist from the University of Salzburg, and his colleague, Kevin Fahey, from the University of Nottingham, analyze the war in Ukraine on The Conversation. As they write, the Russian invasion escalated in a few days into one of the biggest European military conflicts since the Second World War. According to experts, in the confusion it is difficult to decide who will win or how long the fights can last, but scientific research related to wars can help to understand the situation. Based on the literature, the path leading to wars resembles a situation called a bargaining game in game theory. Rival countries compete over issues of territory, resources, patriotism, or style of government, among other things. Since war is extremely costly, states initially try to resolve differences peacefully, but sometimes the process ends up in an armed conflict. According to experts, three factors can basically be behind the outbreak of war. One is that states do not have enough information to ensure success to know its relative probability. Another reason may be that the parties do not trust that the agreements made with the opponent will be kept. Finally, there are cases when states are unable to settle disputes - this is especially typical when ethnic, religious or ideological tensions play a role. According to this approach, war ends when the problem that triggered it is settled on the battlefield. How long the fighting lasts and what form it takes depends on the depth and type of the root cause. After the broad generalities, Atkinson and Fahey move on to the specifics, the situation in Ukraine. The researchers believe that in this case, neither side assessed their chances well. As they write, success in war is based on two main factors: the ability to fight and the willingness to bear sacrifices. In the current conflict, it was clear that the Russian army was much stronger than the Ukrainian one in terms of weaponry and numbers, but for Russia it was not it is obvious that the Ukrainian will to fight is better. At the moment, one of the big problems is that it is difficult for Ukraine to demonstrate its willingness, and Russia is probably uncertain about any relevant communication. According to experts, this can lead to an information problem that is difficult to solve, which often ends only with the surrender of one of the parties. And from this point of view, the support may be decisive. In the case of Vladimir Putin, the Russian oligarchs, the local mafia and the army are essential for survival. Although the Russian president has tried to build a financial bulwark to protect the oligarchs, Western sanctions seem to have undermined those efforts. According to researchers, the conflict is already costing the oligarchs enormously, and the costs will only increase. When enough of Putin's allies become secretly anti-war, the president must choose whether to end the fighting or risk his position. Of course, it is questionable when the turning point will come, as well as whether there are other alternatives serving common interests for Putin's alliance. In Russia, the attitude of the general population is less important. It is worth emphasizing that the costs of the war, such as inflation, economic decline and the weight of battlefield deaths, must also be borne by the Russian people. For the time being, Putin manages the tension with selective selection, control of the state media, and elections that are not free or fair. The latter means that the Russians can only oust the president through mass mobilization and revolution. In the case of Ukraine, the situation is simpler: it is a democratic country, so the willingness of the general population is an extremely important factor in the war. If the masses do not support the defense, the resistance will fall apart. Atkinson and Fahey, however, believe that the determination of the Ukrainian people so far does not indicate a quick surrender. Due to the increasingly aggressive Russian tactics, the Ukrainians will have to face increasing losses in any case. It is no coincidence that Western countries are increasing humanitarian and defense aid to Ukraine. Experts generally believe that the war could last a long time. The end of the conflict can be brought about if the Russian army succeeds in breaking Ukraine's will to fight, or if the war losses and economic problems break Russia's willingness. Researchers expect neither to happen in the coming weeks or months.

Moreover, in case of serious, deliberate negligence of the consumer, the payment service provider (e.g. bank) has no obligation to compensate. However, the bank must prove negligence or fraudulent intent through a detailed investigation. The use of a bank card or mobile bank, the provision of a PIN code or strong customer authentication alone does not prove that the transaction was initiated by the customer. , the rules governing the operating principles of the payment system apply. For this reason, there are only limited opportunities to recover money stolen by criminals through the active cooperation of the customer. Instant transfers reach the beneficiary's account in 5 seconds, so it is almost impossible to recall them. The bank may initiate this, but the money will only be returned to the remitter if the beneficiary has approved the return. The card transaction is already created when the order is authorized: its amount must be blocked on the cardholder's account, and the incoming settlement debits must be accepted and debited to the cardholder's account. These can also only be withdrawn with the consent of the beneficiary. The reason for this is that the payments typically also affect third parties. If the bank automatically revokes or cancels the transaction at the customer's request after a bank card purchase in a store or online store, the otherwise innocent merchant could be burdened with the damages resulting from the misuse. This could undermine confidence in the financial system. Therefore, according to the law, the bank does not have the possibility to unlock the amount blocked during a bank card purchase at the customer's request. According to the law, the bank is obliged to do everything in order to recover the money, but it is not guaranteed that it will be successful. In addition, you must reimburse the customer immediately, but no later than within 1 working day after the customer's notification, if you performed a payment transaction that was not approved by the latter. However, it is an exception if the bank suspects fraud for reasonable reasons in the given situation and informs the MNB of this in writing. With this notification, the bank is not exempted from the obligation to pay compensation, but only from the 1 working day deadline. It must investigate the customer's complaint and the circumstances of the disputed payment transaction. In the case of transactions demonstrably approved by the customer or due to his gross negligence or fraudulent behavior, he may be exempted from compensation. The chances of getting the money back are greatly increased if the customer files a police report immediately after reporting the case to the bank managing the account, and also provides information on the beneficiary name and account number to which the money was sent. Correcting an unapproved payment transaction in connection with a request for - come as a bank card complaint or customer complaint - the bank card, mobile bank, etc. its use (and even the provision of personal authentication data) does not in itself prove that the customer acted fraudulently or approved the payment transaction, or intentionally or seriously breached their duty of care. This can only be established by the bank after a thorough, individual examination that takes into account all the details. It was done by entering a PIN code or with strong customer authentication, does not mean that it was actually initiated by the customer. During the investigation, the bank must prove that the customer acted fraudulently, intentionally or with gross negligence. During its proof, it must pay attention to all the essential circumstances of the individual case, as well as the relevant information about the customer. and how the approval was done, whether an SMS or push message was sent and to which device, how much time passed between the initiation and the approval, whether the PIN code was tampered with, whether the transaction differed from the customer's habits, etc.) . During the investigation, the bank also pays attention to the content of the client's report, which it can also use as evidence. If, based on the available information, it can be established that the client acted fraudulently or was intentionally or grossly negligent, the bank does not have to compensate the damage . There is a high chance that the consumer will not be able to get his amount back. Most of the bank investigations that have reached the MNB state that the abuse may have taken place due to the customer's seriously careless behavior. In many cases, unfortunately, they actively contributed to the creation of disputed transactions, e.g. by entering their bank login credentials on a fake page. Others dictated the approval codes received by SMS or push message to the fraudsters over the phone, provided their bank card authentication data, or made their data available by downloading a screen-sharing application. you wanted to pay your utility bill on a website or by clicking on a phisher's e-mail link. However, you have actually given your data to unauthorized parties. In the majority of such cases, it is not possible to recover the amounts transferred. Banks do not reimburse the customer for the customer's careless behavior. In all cases, the MNB expects the bank to investigate the execution conditions of the disputed payment transaction individually, taking every detail into account. If you reject the customer's rectification request or complaint, you must justify your position in detail, describe the evidence you have collected and their evaluation, as well as the conclusions drawn from them. The bank's rejection does not necessarily mean that the money will not be returned. Knowing the bank's answer, the injured customer can initiate a consumer protection procedure at the MNB, request the procedure of the Financial Conciliation Board operating within the central bank, or go to court. With the participation of the MNB, the authorities and market players working together in the Cyber Shield initiative are actively working to reduce cyber fraud, and customers in order to strengthen your financial awareness. In 2021, 475,038 prisoners were registered in the twenty-seven member states of the European Union, which means that there were an average of 106 prisoners per 100,000 inhabitants, according to Eurostat data. They add that the proportion of prisoners increased after the decrease in 2020 - at that time there were 104 people per 100,000 inhabitants - but it is still the second lowest figure since the turn of the century. However, the picture is very varied when looking at individual countries. Going back to 2018, it can be seen that at that time Lithuania had the highest rate, more than double the current EU average: 230 prisoners per 100,000 inhabitants, while Finland, which is at the other end of the scale, only had 53. In Hungary, the rate was 166 five years ago, and then a year later it grew by one person. After that, however, we can observe a significant jump: in 2020, there were already 171 inmates per 100,000 inhabitants in 2021, and in 2021, there were 191 inmates per 100,000 inhabitants in our country, with which we jumped to first place in the EU ranking, tied with Poland. Meanwhile, Lithuania, which was at the top in 2018, slipped to fourth place (181). It is worth noting that eight of the top ten places in the list from two years ago are occupied by Central and Eastern European countries, while for example Croatia (96) and Slovenia (53) ) is also far behind, and a decrease in the ratio can also be observed in the case of Slovakia and the Czech Republic. The Eurostat article also examined the overcrowding of prisons, according to which, in 2021, there were overcrowded prison cells in eight EU member states, and excess capacity was registered in 17 countries. During the utilization rate of the prisons, the number of inmates was compared to the official capacity of the penitentiary, and then this was multiplied by 100. In the case of overcrowding, the utilization rate exceeds 100, that is, there are more inmates in the prison than could be accommodated according to the original plans. Overcrowding was observed in Cyprus (146), Romania (116), France (114), Greece and Italy (both 108), Sweden (102), Croatia and Denmark (101). The lowest prison utilization rates were in Malta (65), Estonia and Latvia (66) noted. They added that in fourteen of the twenty-five EU countries providing data in 2021, prison utilization increased compared to 2020, which was probably due to the end of measures related to the Covid epidemic. It was more difficult to maintain social distancing and isolation in prisons, which is why there were prisoners who were - temporarily - sent to house arrest due to their vulnerable condition. Our infographic shows that Poland had the most places among the EU member states, around 86 thousand, while the number of prisoners it did not exceed 75,000 in any of the examined years. In contrast, in France in 2018, there were 70,000 prisoners out of 60,000 places, i.e. around 10,000 more than there would have been enough space for. The situation was similarly bad in Italy, but by 2021 this number was halved. In 2017, however, Hungary still led the prison overcrowding statistics in the EU: there were 124 inmates for every 100 places. The government wanted to help with this with a prison construction program. In 2016, they promised that new prisons would be built in Béké, Csenger, Heves, Kemecs, Komádi, Komló, Kunmadaras and Ózd, but too high price offers were received, so the public procurements were repeatedly classified as ineffective. In the end, Attila Paár's interest in Csenger, West Hungária Bau Kft., won the construction of the prison without competition, after the National Defense and Law Enforcement Committee of the Parliament exempted the investment from public procurement, Átlátszó recently wrote. The construction will cost HUF 50 billion, although the investment was only planned for HUF 900 million a few years ago. Elsewhere, the government is expanding existing prisons, for example 2,750 new beds were created in ten penitentiary institutions with lightweight container buildings. At the same time, the number of beds in Hungary rose from 14,469 in 2018 to 18,713 last year, but the number of prisoners also increased. number, from 16,303 to 18,623. However, since the number of prisoners has increased less than the number of places, the overcrowding of five years ago has been eliminated, although there are still not many free places in Hungarian prisons. Regardless of this, the government has taken new, rather strange measures to further reduce overcrowding, and a very simple solution found by releasing prisoners from prison. At the end of April, the government decree came into force, on the basis of which the release of convicted foreign human traffickers became possible. In exchange, the Hungarian state asks human traffickers to leave Hungary within 72 hours. According to Gergely Gulyás, head of the Prime Minister's Office, the measure is necessary because it is too expensive to detain foreign convicts, and prisons are already overcrowded, which is why compensations were sentenced to prison. At the same time, the government stopped the payment of these at the beginning of 2020, saying that the prison conditions had to be re-regulated - after that the building extensions came. According to the National Correctional Command, 606 convicts were released until May 23, and another 202 human traffickers will be released. The national housing market has changed over the past decade. The resident population has decreased in the majority of settlements, including fewer people living in the big cities, while the catchment areas have become more popular, according to the analysis of ingtalan.com, which processes official census data. The real estate advertising portal compared the changes in population and house prices based on more than 720,000 apartments and houses for sale in 2,970 settlements. The official data just published are not surprising. The sustained upturn in the housing market seen in the second half of the 2010s clearly benefited the agglomeration settlements. Due to the high housing prices, many people moved out of the big cities to the lower-priced agglomeration settlements. The process was intensified by the quarantine effect associated with the coronavirus epidemic, in the framework of which some buyers turned to properties with gardens instead of city apartments, said László Balogh, the leading economic expert of ingatlan.com. He added: the holiday areas, especially around Lake Balaton and Lake Velence, can also be classified as winners of the last decade. According to ingatlan.com's analysis, in Nagytarcsa near Budapest, for example, the population increased by 67 percent in ten years, and compared to 2018, the average price per square meter rose by 122 percent to HUF 880,000. There are 32 percent more people living in Nagykovácsi, which also contributed to the fact that the average square meter prices in the settlement rose by 128 percent, so that they now exceed HUF 1 million. In Érd, the population increased by 12 percent in ten years, and the average price per square meter of residential properties increased by 131 percent compared to 2018 to nearly HUF 800,000. The settlements of the Győr catchment area can also be said to be popular. In Győrújfalu and Győrzámoly, for example, the population has grown by nearly 60 percent since 2011, and the average price of residential properties has risen by 153 and 99 percent in the last five years. The same scenario prevailed in Kozármisleny near Pécs, where real estate prices of more than 300 percent accompanied the growth of the settlement. In Ballószög, which belongs to the Kecskemét catchment area, the population increased by 29 percent, and the average price of real estate increased by 165 percent. In addition to Balaton, several settlements also achieved population growth. Among others, Balatonrendes, where the number of registered residents increased one and a half times in ten years. Compared to 2018, the square meter price of residential properties offered for sale increased by 255 percent. The population in Alsóörs and Balatonalmádi also increased by more than 10 percent, and residential properties rose in price by 222 and 280 percent in five years. they are part of the wider metropolitan agglomeration, and are also members of the Székesfehérvár catchment area. In both settlements, the population grew by more than 30 percent. Compared to 2018, the price of residential properties offered for sale in Velencé increased by 105 percent to HUF 805,000 and in Gárdony by 136 percent to HUF 771,000. László Balogh said that despite the slowdown in the real estate market, agglomeration zones can remain popular. The value of the properties there is still 20-30 percent lower than the prices of real estate in big cities. In the coming years, agglomeration homes with good technical condition and modern heating systems will be the most popular, he added. The specialist also highlighted that dynamic population growth can be observed in certain small settlements across the country. As these are without exception rural chocolate settlements, it can be expected that thanks to the support, some of the small settlements can also achieve a dynamic increase in population and housing prices in the coming years, he said. ingatlan.com expert.

He is a grown man, that is, well beyond being medically related to me, but he calls me before Easter to say he has a problem and asks for my help. We will arrange a meeting after the holiday, he is happy and says a heart-warming goodbye: "Thank you, doctor aunt!" He was my patient from the time he was a newborn until he was an adult, or more precisely, my "rare patient", as he was a strict, inquisitive, friendly little boy, then a big boy. Today, he is still strict and interested and friendly, only in the meantime he got into a serious, stressful job, there is a lot of pressure on him, it is understandable that I worry about him, and even now I just hope that he is not in serious trouble. Although he never said it, I think he was happy that I became a doctor, he enjoyed watching me work, and of course he also liked the children, especially the braver ones, including Laci - he sometimes exchanged a few words with them. The child turned back and looked at me: "It's really good for you that your dad is here with you even at work." It was really good. Many, many years later, as an adult, he knocked unexpectedly Laci; we were after dad's funeral. All he said was, “I'm sorry. I loved your father... Can I hug you?" Which meant much more to me than the usual "sincere condolences". Well, this Laci is coming to me now. It turns out that the stress remained, even increased, and some excess weight also jumped up. Plus, the grandfather had serious problems with his heart at the time, and Laci is worried, especially because his blood pressure has recently been erratic. She read everything on the Internet, she was even more scared, and she wants to clearly see and understand what is happening in her body, what risks she has to face. She grins at me: "That's exactly what you say , who came to order after surgery with a walking frame?!" My answer: "You're right, I'm not an example to follow at work, but I perform quite well in other factors." With a good feeling, I let Lacika go, who promises her long-ago doctor aunt that she will report on the developments without delay. And I am happy that sometimes I can also help my adult "children".

Born into a multi-generational Austrian military family, Otto Skorzeny became a member of the Austrian National Socialist Party organized on the German model at the age of 24 in 1932, and soon after joined the SA. He played a significant role in the implementation of the Anschluss, and later, now as a German citizen, he applied to join the Luftwaffe. After this failed, the German dictator's bodyguard unit, the Leibstandardte SS, became part of Adolf Hitler's soldiers, Rubicon.hu reports. This was a special action group, with which its commanders wanted to compete with the military defense, the Abwehr - Skorzeny carried out his daring commando operations with this special squad until April 1944. His most famous deployment was the so-called Oak Tree operation on September 12, 1943, when he freed Benito Mussolini from his captivity in the Grand-Sasso mountain following a parachute operation. Later, Skorzeny organized an operation against Stalin, Churchill and Roosevelt, who were meeting in Tehran, which was thwarted by the Soviet secret service. , then in April 1944 he tried to capture the partisan leader Tito Joszip Broz, who was staying on the island of Drvar in the Adriatic. After returning to Berlin, the commando took part in the capture of General von Stauffenberg, who had organized an assassination attempt against Hitler in July 1944. After it became clear to Nazi intelligence that Hungarian Governor Miklós Horthy was preparing to jump out of the war, Skorzeny was given the task of paralyzing the action. On October 15, 1944, the commando - as an alleged Yugoslav partisan - called Miklós Horthy Jr. to negotiate and kidnapped him. The Germans later successfully blackmailed the elderly governor with his son's life. penetrated behind allied lines and began sabotage operations. He is said to have planned the liquidation of Commander-in-Chief Eisenhower, which is why he was called "the most dangerous man in Europe". After the collapse of Nazi Germany, he then retreated to the territory of Austria, where he tried to organize guerrilla groups under the name of Werewolves, but finally surrendered to the British on May 15, 1945. Skorzeny was primarily held responsible for the things he wore in the Ardennes, since there - with the fake uniform - he violated numerous military conventions insulted. He was soon imprisoned in Darmstadt, from which he escaped in 1948 and traveled to Paris, Spain and then Argentina. The former Nazi officer took part in the founding of the neo-Nazi organization ODESSA, while during the fifties he also appeared close to Argentine President Perón and Egyptian President Nasser as a military advisor. he founded the Paladin Group – while becoming a millionaire through his services. The former commando was diagnosed with cancer in his spine in 1970, from which he initially recovered, but later he could no longer fight it and died in July 1975.

"Good afternoon, can we go to the slaughterhouse?" "It's closed, there's no one here," says the porter, coming out of his booth at the gate of the settlement on the edge of Csengele. He adds: "I don't know when they will be here again." There is no reason to doubt the man's words. The parking lot in front of the slaughterhouse is empty, there is no movement in the main building, the entrance door is closed. We walk around the building, we don't see a single person. A janitor may only be needed at the abandoned plant, because the various machines and refrigerators in there are of great value, and they must be protected. A neighbor of the lowland kosher slaughterhouse, owned by the United Hungarian Israelite Community (EMIH), a little further from the janitor's booth, says the 24 .hu, that according to his memories, there has been no production here for 3-4 months, he has not experienced trucks bringing the poultry to be slaughtered or transporting the processed kosher meat. Another neighbor reports that, according to him, the building has been opened recently only for technical maintenance or inspection, but they haven't opened chicken necks there for a long time. The Cengele kosher slaughterhouse, which previously generated billions in losses, was closed. We searched for the company on the publicly provided phone numbers, but we could not reach anyone. Quality Poultry Kft., the operator of the slaughterhouse, finally confirmed our information and our on-site experiences in a written response by saying that they decided to stop in 2022, but what the future will bring for the slaughterhouse, the management can only imagine for the time being - there is no definite direction yet. However, before explaining the company's position in detail, let's take a look at how the kosher slaughterhouse announced as a success story turned into a closed property. Six years ago, in the summer of 2017, EMIH's kosher slaughterhouse was opened in Csengel, Csongrád county, amid intense media interest. The importance of the event was also indicated by the presence of Israeli Chief Rabbi David Lau and the then Minister of Agriculture Sándor Fazekas. The government did not only play a role in the festive event: the slaughterhouse, which was established on the site of the former cannery and basically specializes in geese, costing a total of 2.8 billion, was realized thanks to a 1.75 billion loan from the state-owned Eximbank, as well as a non-refundable state grant of nearly 400 million forints. Slomó Köves did not skimp on the big words at the event. At that time, it was announced that this is the world's largest kosher goose slaughterhouse and processor. In addition, it was also said that there is a huge demand for kosher goose liver worldwide. (In our previous articles - here and here - we wrote in detail about why, compared to several EU countries, the Hungarian legal framework, which is much more permissive and does not restrict kosher slaughter, really creates a good basis for exporting kosher from Hungary to Western Europe, for example France and Belgium products. In Hungary, several companies operating kosher slaughterhouses take advantage of this favorable legal environment, we will talk about them later.) However, the business venture in Csengela, which was launched in 2017, soon began to generate serious losses. According to public reports, all this meant a total loss of more than HUF 1.2 billion for Quality Poultry, which is owned by the religious community, against which many executions have been requested in recent years. According to the latest report, the company had a loan of more than HUF 3.6 billion. In our previous article, we also wrote that EMIH made up for the billion-dollar losses "out of its own pocket". It is not known for sure whether this happened in 2020 or 2021, it can only be assumed, since in these years, in contrast to previous years, no mention was made of this in the minutes of the members' meetings uploaded to the system of the Ministry of Justice. At the same time, it can be seen from the minutes of the 2020 and 2021 members' meetings that the company's capital fell from 154 million to 87 million forints. It is hardly possible to find a single reason why the Slomó Köves project, burdened with billions in mortgages, was not successful (according to the minutes, it came from somewhere other than Eximbank We heard information from professional circles that the management of the slaughterhouse was changed several times, but we also received a version that there was not enough professional knowledge in the circles of EMIH to make the slaughterhouse a success. After the community invested 600 million euros in this business, and then put in another 1.2 billion euros to compensate for the losses, it is also possible that EMIH's management reached a point when they no longer felt that the losses could be financed. We asked Cengele the operator of the slaughterhouse, Quality Poultry, about the exact situation at the plant, why it was closed, and what their plans are. This answer was sent: Since 2020, there have been eight bird flu epidemic cycles in Hungary. In the counties of Bács-Kiskun and Csongrád, where the slaughterhouse and the majority of our goose farms operate, there was a closure for approximately 14 months out of the last 36 months, which means that the animals could not be moved between the rearing and stocking farms, and the slaughterhouse was prohibited export of slaughtered birds to Israel. (The kosher slaughterhouse in Jászberény was in a more fortunate situation, as Jászberény was in an infected area significantly fewer times.) In view of this, in November 2022, the slaughterhouse's owners decided to suspend the operation of the slaughterhouse according to the original model, until there is a systemic solution to the problem of bird flu. As written , in terms of the future of the Cengele slaughterhouse, three possible directions are currently being investigated: The latter option is interesting in light of the fact that they previously hinted that they had essentially already switched to poultry slaughter. In a 2020 interview - which we also quoted in our previous article - Sámuel Oirechman, managing director of Quality Poultry Kft., stated that during the coronavirus "we have almost completely switched to slaughtering chicken and turkey, all the more so because the demand for fattened geese and ducks due to Israeli demand, the closure of catering units and the small number of events, it has dropped dramatically." This decision can also be justified by the fact that chicken and turkey are usually cheaper than geese, which means that they can play a bigger role on weekdays. A kosher slaughterhouse can even be a good business in Hungary: the Israeli-French company based in Jászberény also focuses on kosher goose products. and a Belgian-owned company called Palmi-Top. In 2022, this company produced a profit of HUF 1.3 billion with a sales revenue of more than HUF 7 billion, compared to a profit of HUF 1.15 billion a year earlier. Kóser Baromfi Kft. from Nagykőrös is a smaller company, but last year it also closed with a profit of 46 million.

The sequel to The White Lotus may take place in Australia, but showrunner Mike White has already floated the idea of a possible prequel series, which would focus on the character played by Jennifer Coolidge, Tanya McQuoid. White took part in a film festival in Sydney, Australia, where Coolidge accompanied him, and talked about all of this there. Deadline wrote that at his press conference on Saturday, he was asked, among other things, about the hit series that will debut on HBO Max, which is currently being filmed in Thailand. The director told us that he would like to bring the fourth season to the Australian continent, because his dream is to have a season take place on every continent. At the same time, however, he did not confirm that The White Lotus will definitely continue even after the third series, saying that if they continue, they may come to Australia. But another statement of his also suggests that they are really thinking about expansions: they are planning a prequel series which it would focus on one of the most entertaining characters in the series - and one of the few who appears in both seasons - Tanya, for whom Coolidge received a Golden Globe and an Emmy Award. It could absolutely work, we've already talked about it, it's a funny idea. Jennifer could be made twenty years younger, said White.

At first, it didn't seem like a good idea at all to peel another skin from a series that, as entertaining as it was, still told a closed story. Anyway, the White Lotus was the name of the fictitious Hawaiian luxury hotel where the first season took place, so what's the point of telling a completely different story with the same title elsewhere, with different people? However, HBO not only felt that we could watch more of Mike White's satirical series, but they also had a good guess that White could transfer this tone to anywhere else - for example, to Sicily, where the second season takes place. contributed to the fact that he worked on an extremely fashionable topic: social differences and class struggle are especially appreciated nowadays, and several of the most celebrated films of our time try to show this. However, the first season of Fehér Lótusz largely successfully avoided the traps that, for example, The Living Ones or even The Triangle of Sadness fell into, and was only slightly didactic. In addition, White sketched well-hitting, lifelike characters who were very entertaining to watch suffer in the paradisiacal setting. Even though the story was a bit longer than it needed to be. However, the series became a bombshell success and made a star out of Mike White, who until then was the closest to this success as the screenwriter of Richard Linklater's film Rocksuli. Apart from that, he mainly worked on TV, but even his series Enlightened, which was rewarded with several awards, did not become as popular as The White Lotus - in fact, it was very far from it. White was also surprised by the success and the possibility of a continuation, and finally agreed to continue it as an anthology series. This is how the season ended up in Sicily, and two characters remained: Tanya (Jennifer Coolidge), who is constantly unhappy and spectacularly suffering despite her wealth, and her husband, Greg (Jon Gries), whom she met in the first season, but the latter is only present for a short time. And the others are wealthy American tourists who arrive at a luxury hotel in Taormina, and now we also get to know the members of the service staff, as well as two local girls who are looking for money. However, this season takes a completely different direction, because instead of social differences, now "sexuality dark side" came into focus, but not at all for its own sake, but with the help of many small and large dramas. While the first season was more of a satirical character drama, where the plot wasn't so important, this season's much more consciously edited story threads were tied together and separated, and many conflicts drove the plot forward. This is especially exciting in places, which can be said less about the first season. However, the structure is still similar: at the very beginning, we found out that someone(s) died among the characters, and then through seven episodes it was possible to guess who it would be. However, investigating infidelity and jealousy, White now puts his characters in a series of extremely unpleasant situations, or slowly but surely steers them towards some kind of disaster. It is already clear from the beginning that there could be trouble with the fact that the two tech bros, Cameron and Ethan, are in vain old friends from college, if they and their wives are completely different: Cameron (Theo James) is a classic alpha male, with all his confidence, and he's also cute, while Ethan (Will Sharpe) is an introverted, intelligent, classic nerd who recently he broke into the elite with his company, but with the latter he endangers his relationship with his wife, Harper (Aubrey Plaza). In contrast, the marriage of rich, white Californian dream couple Cameron and Daphne (Meghann Fahy) is perfect, at least on the surface. Then it can't end well that the sex addict Dominic Di Grasso (Michael Imperioli) is not deterred from having fun with prostitutes by the fact that his marriage is in ruins and that his awkward father (F. Murray Abraham) and his idealistic son ( Adam DiMarco) too. They are looking for their ancestors in Italy, but then the trip also thoroughly tests their relationship. Finally, here is Tanya, whom we met from the first season, accompanied by her husband, her assistant Portia (Haley Lu Richardson), who has lost her case. The hotel guests are then joined by young Lucia (Simone Tabasco) and her girlfriend Mia (Beatrice Grannò), who is preparing to become a singer, and later we meet the decadent, bored Englishman Quentin (Tom Hollander) and his group of cheerful, gay men, and the his nephew, West Ham hooligan Jack (Leo Woodall), who stands out from the rest with his flawless Essex accent. Of course, the main characters are still filthy rich, but this is no longer such an essential part of the script that it should be rubbed under our noses every five minutes, like the first in season. Even more so, because you don't have to be rich to experience the emotions that drive the season: love, desire, jealousy, disappointment, and especially lies and silences, which play an important role in all plot lines. However, all of this is presented by White in a very effective and enjoyable way, so The White Lotus is both very funny and exciting, especially since there is not a single positive or negative character in the series, and each character can be liked or even hated for something. Of course, there are degrees, it is difficult to sympathize with Cameron, for example, while seeing the misfortunes of the naive Albie Di Grasso, there is no one whose heart does not fall for him. We can even get the feeling that White actually loves these characters, he presents them so sensitively. This is also helped by the fact that his actors are also top-notch: this could be the big breakthrough for Aubrey Plaza, known mainly from indie films, he plays the frustrated, cynical character so perfectly and I really hate Harper a lot. But the producers will definitely remember the name of Will Sharpe, who played a completely different character in the Giri/Haji series that gave him his best-known role so far, while Michael Imperioli, known from Mafiozók, or especially F. Murray Abraham do not need to be introduced. White (who also directs the parts) also has a special sense of visuality, sometimes he composed regular pictorial orgies from Sicilian nature images, cityscapes or frescoes decorating buildings, which function more than simple eye-candy in a story reminiscent of such a baroque opera - especially, if we know how unhappy most of the characters are among these picturesque settings. The Italian location may have been an inspiration for White in the sense that the tone of the series sometimes recalls the frivolous Italian social satires of the sixties and seventies, and at other times it recreates Antonioni's A one of the famous scenes of the film classic adventure. However, so much tension accumulates in the last episode that it is a bit different from the other parts with its more serious tone and less humor, even though we like to laugh first and foremost on The White Lotus, even if it is not the most trivial humor in general (there is some: how could we forget the in the first part, is he constantly hitting on Grandpa Di Grasso?). But apart from that, we really have few complaints, because this season has everything that makes a series work well. Fehér Lótusz also makes sure that it is unmistakably a 2022 series, since the end of the world, so characteristic of the age, leaves its stamp on the dialogues. mood, like references such as Albie's Gen Z criticism of The Godfather. But it no longer makes us feel that we are seeing people in a privileged position here, while it is more empathetic with the other characters who do not belong to the 1 percent. It is a smart, brutally honest and terribly entertaining series, while also being infinitely humane. If everything is true, there will be one more season of The White Lotus, and now we don't even feel this is a problem at all. The White Lotus, season 2, 2022, 7 episodes, HBO Max. 24.hu: 9/10
