Alpine skier Lindsey Vonn was seriously injured in the Olympic downhill race on Sunday and was taken to the hospital by helicopter. Former Finnish alpine ski star Tanja Poutiainen-Rinne says the situation feels especially bad because Vonn had worked hard to make her comeback. Alpine skier Lindsey Vonn's thrilling comeback project came to a shocking end when the 41-year-old legend crashed out of the Olympic downhill race on Sunday. Vonn's run was cut short at about 15 seconds into a long curve. Vonn's screams of pain echoed on the slope as she was treated for a fall on the slope. She was taken to the hospital by helicopter from the scene. Former Finnish alpine star Tanja Poutiainen-Rinne was also watching the race from the home stands. “Yes, it felt bad, oh my. When I watched her performance on TV, oh my. It felt really extra bad when she had made such a great comeback and worked so hard to get to that point and then it happens like this. It's a shame for her.” According to Poutiainen-Rinte, the course looked good, as it should be in a major competition. She didn't notice anything dangerous or bad about the course or the conditions on TV. “The course was bumpy when coming into the bend, everyone went a little bit into the air. The worst thing was when her hand got caught in the gate and tore her body into a spiral and Vonn took off recklessly. Maybe it wasn't a hundred percent in the glass then, but it was a lot of speed. If she had just touched the gate and stayed on the right side of it, but this is the sum of many coincidences.” Lindsey Vonn's hand got caught in the gate. Photo: IOC / OBS / The run out was rough. Photo: Handout Vonn started the Olympic run from a risky position. She crashed out a week ago in the Crans-Montana super giant slalom and tore her anterior cruciate ligament. Poutiainen-Rinne still understands Vonn's decision to retire. "She herself said that these are her last Olympics and then her career ends. In a way, I understand that at that point you go and try. She also assured me that the knee was stable. That's the decision she made with her support team." Poutiainen-Rinne is now a physiotherapist. She says that it is quite individual how a torn anterior cruciate ligament affects her. "It is a ligament that supports the knee inside the knee, it doesn't keep the knee stable on its own, it is so thin. The most important factors are the muscles, the nerves and the coordination around the knee. There are alpine skiers who have skied with a torn anterior cruciate ligament and won Olympic medals." And how does it affect you mentally to have recently fallen badly? “It definitely has an impact. It’s not easy to leave if the previous race ended in a bad crash and the anterior cruciate ligament is gone. But she’s loaded everything she has into this winter and the Olympics. She’s been in a strong mental state. It’s all or nothing.” Vonn retired for the first time in 2019. She had suffered injuries even before her first retirement decision. Vonn had a partial knee replacement. Vonn returned to the World Cup this season with it. Vonn won the World Cup downhill race in St. Moritz in December at the age of 41, becoming the oldest World Cup race winner in the sport. “Fortunately, she breaks the mold, a 40-year-old athlete is not yet old to be at the top of the world. Of course, there are different sports and not just anyone in their forties can do it, but if they are physically fit and work towards it, then why not.” Lindsey Vonn is an athlete to watch. Photo: Leonhard Foeger But now it seems that the career of a top athlete will end in perhaps the saddest way possible: through injury. “You wouldn’t wish that on anyone. I myself was injured a year before I quit. I rehabilitated and got back into the world’s top five. I was allowed to make my own decision about continuing my career,” it wasn’t the injury that ended her career. Poutiainen-Rinne ended her career at the age of 34. “Vonnit,” or returning to the sport, has not crossed her mind since. “Physically, I could have continued, but mentally, the meter was full. I had a long and successful career. That was enough and I no longer had the motivation to be a top athlete,” came other things in life. Let's try to avoid a messy separation, Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen (KOK) hoped in diplomatic reports leaked to the media on US-European relations. The transatlantic rift can be observed in the speeches at the Munich Security Conference, which begins in Germany on Friday. In Munich, President Donald Trump's inner circle is represented by Foreign Minister Marco Rubio. The fact that Vice President J. D. Vance is not present is already a relief. A year ago, Vance was expected to give an analysis of the war in Ukraine and European defense in Munich, but he attacked European democracies instead. Among other things, Vance claimed that attempts to suppress freedom of speech - read: curb disinformation - are a greater threat to Europe than Russia and China. The Munich Security Conference has been a barometer of transatlantic relations throughout its history. Now the pressure has broken the glass. NATO is in disarray and trust in the United States is at zero, as Trump no longer seems to make a difference whether he attacks a dictator or a NATO partner. The separation is coming, or at least the United States is clearly withdrawing from NATO and Europe. Europe has made its own moves and protections. Now, the speeches of European leaders sound like a new self-confidence – or lack thereof. Still, it is difficult to break the dependence on the United States, as the country has been responsible for many very critical issues in European defense. There is no prospect of negotiations between the United States, Ukraine and Russia to end the war, although Russia seems to be genuinely negotiating this time. However, there is still reason to fear that Trump will sacrifice Ukraine. The Finnish leadership in Munich is represented by President Alexander Stubb, Valtonen and Defense Minister Antti Häkkänen (Kok). Stubb is a sought-after and fluent speaker, but the long year with Trump also figures in the president's analysis. The place in the limelight is no longer as comfortable as it used to be.

Salla Vaahersalo from Kotka noticed that a scammer was selling her holiday home in Ruka online. The exterior photos of the holiday home were real, but the photos taken inside were fake and stolen from somewhere else. The scam notice was posted on Facebook in several different groups within a short period of time. At least one person has already lost 600 euros after falling into the scammer's trap. At the end of last year, Salla Vaahersalo from Kotka received a confusing phone call: the holiday home she owned in Ruka was being rented out online in someone else's name. The scam notice included real, recognizable exterior photos of the apartment and yard, but the interior photos were fake and stolen from somewhere else. The notice had been posted on Facebook in a Ruka area group where you can offer and search for accommodation in Lapland. It looked credible: it included the names and phone numbers of the landlords, and, for example, the address of the holiday home matched. However, when you looked at the pictures more closely, you could see that they were screenshots from Vaahersalo's own ad. "It was half of our semi-detached house, one half of which we use ourselves, and the other half has been for rent and sale. Our real estate agent called and reported the scam," Vaahersalo says. Salla Vaahersalo found a rental ad for her own holiday home in Ruka in an online Facebook group. The exterior photos were real, the interior photos were stolen from somewhere else. Photo: Screenshot from Facebook Vaahersalo was incredulous, but before she could investigate the matter further, the Facebook group's administration had time to remove the ad as a result of the real estate agent's report. Vaahersalo had taken a screenshot of the ad, however. In it, a holiday home in excellent condition was being sold as a "sudden departure offer" for 600 euros per week. "That's very little in the high season. The correct price would be double that," Vaahersalo says. In January, the scammer operating under the same name struck again, and this time Vaahersalo noticed the fraud himself. There was another announcement about the holiday home on Facebook, but this time in a different group. “You start to feel quite insecure. You can’t trust anything anymore,” says Vaahersalo. What strikes her as particularly brazen and systematic is that the scammers are selling the same property that they have already been caught selling once. At least one victim of the scam has already been found. It came to light when an unknown woman called Vaahersalo’s spouse and said that she had paid 600 euros for a week’s holiday in Lapland, but had begun to suspect that she had been scammed. Salla Vaahersalo considers the scammers’ actions to be systematic and brazen. At least one family has already lost their money trying to rent her cottage. Photo: Salla Vaahersalo Archives “He asked my husband if our half of the semi-detached house was available for rent for that period, and it wasn’t. A single mother with her two sons lost her money,” Vaahersalo laments. The rental advertisement, which the victim of the scam had signed, had an address for the landlord that led to a completely different person, and the phone number was a prepaid number, the details of which were not available. “It makes you feel really bad for others when you do something like this, and it feels helpless when you can’t do anything yourself and prevent scams,” Vaahersalo says. She herself lost her money to a scammer a few years ago when she rented a house in Mallorca, Spain, for her mother’s birthday. Vaahersalo found out in advance the location of the accommodation and that the house existed. However, the rental website on which the advertisement was posted turned out to be a fake, and Vaahersalo never saw her money again. Based on her own experiences, she wouldn’t dare rent anything from private individuals. "Unfortunately. You have to be really careful with these. It's better to have a rental service in between to protect both parties." The scammer had drawn up the attached rental agreement for Salla Vaahersalo's vacation home, in which all the sections had been filled out conscientiously - but with incorrect information. Vaahersalo received the rental agreement from a real estate agent who had noticed one scam attempt. The real estate agent had blacked out the information of the scam victims from the ad. HS has covered up other private information with black bars.

Warning strike on Tuesday, February 10, in over 1,300 city halls across the country. Civil servants will not work with the public between 10:00 and 12:00. They are dissatisfied with some provisions of the reform package proposed by the Government. The warning strike will take place during the Prime Minister's meeting with the mayors who are meeting at the General Assembly of the Association of Communes in Romania. The meeting is scheduled for 10:30 at the Palace of Parliament. The strike is organized by the National Union SCOR. The protest is taking place in all city halls where this union has organizations. According to union leaders, this would involve 1,370 city halls. "The warning strike that actually involves closing the city halls to work with the public while we, the employees, will be present at work, but without accepting this interaction with the public or with other external entities," said the leader of the SCOR union in Arad county, Cantemir Dărău. Trade unionists? that some measures are unconstitutional. "There are provisions in the legislative package on local public administration that discriminatoryly concern, we say, salary cuts for smaller communes or reductions in the number of hours, half-time, in a public position that was acquired through a competition," said the leader of the SCOR union in Arad county, Cantemir Dărău. The protest action takes place while the mayors of the Association of Communes of Romania are meeting at the Palace of Parliament, where Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan is also expected to arrive. "There are some commune mayors who have a correctly calculated staff and where there will be no reductions. And we have another part of communes who, unfortunately, have hired more people than necessary and now, of course, when the calculation is correct, they will have to reduce this additional staff", the prime minister explained to Digi24. 500 mayors are participating in the mayors' meeting at the Palace of Parliament. Authors: Julia Nagy and Ciprian Boițiu

Alert, last evening, on a beach in Mamaia, after a broken drone was found on the seashore. Representatives of the Coast Guard, SRI, ISU Dobrogea, Gendarmerie and Police isolated the perimeter. The drone was lifted and taken for identification. Authorized sources do not rule out that it is a decoy drone or target simulator, without pyrotechnic charge. The alert to 112 was given on Monday evening, at 18:27. A passerby noticed on the beach, probably thrown by the waves to the shore, an object that appeared to be a drone. It was a full-scale mobilization. ISU Constanța sent teams with firefighting trucks, a ladder truck and a truck to detect explosive substances. While firefighters checked all the nooks and crannies of the restaurant by the beach, and the gendarmes surrounded the perimeter where the drone was, the SRI and Coast Guard examined the object that looked like an aircraft. On the fiberglass body, painted green, was written MO4, dash 25. The tail and body were intact. Only the end of the drone was broken. However, due to some plastic wires, it remained hanging from the rest of the aircraft. The broken part had an electronic monitoring device, a GPS, and at the top a motor and propeller. The drone was examined for more than three hours. Later, the Coast Guard reported that there were metal debris that appeared to belong to an unidentified aircraft. SRI said that the Army was communicating on the drone side. MApN has not communicated anything so far. The drone was taken by the gendarmes. The case is being investigated by the Constanta Court of Appeal.

Representatives of the Danube Delta Reserve, veterinarians and local authorities organized, at the beginning of the week, a large-scale action to check and take measures in Grindul Dranov. This is the area where environmental volunteers reported significant mortality among free horses, due to the frost, but also to the restriction of access to food and water, due to the placement of electric fences by farmers. After several horses from Grindul Dranov, a less accessible area of the Danube Delta, towards Dunavăț, were found dead or in agony, the Association for the Protection of Animals, ARCA, requested the intervention of the authorities. The goal: to save wild horses from the grind. The authorities' action began with: "Dismantling the illegally placed electric fence, in order to allow the free movement of horses across the entire area of 2,200 hectares", announced the governor of the Danube Delta Reserve, Bogdan Bulete. The approximately 10-kilometer fence, which restricted the horses' access to food and water, was dismantled by those who had placed it, to protect the cows on the moor. They were fined 12,500 lei. "The horses were on an area of 260 hectares, and the cows on 1,400 hectares," said Governor Bogdan Bulete. According to Governor Bogdan Bulete, veterinarians will conduct thorough checks. "Other sanctions will follow for those who abandoned their animals. I'm sorry to spoil the idyllic image: there are no wild horses on the Dranov moor. There are domestic horses with owners who abandoned them," Governor Bogdan Bulete also said. The only horses in the Danube Delta admitted as semi-wild are those from the Letea Forest, where around 1,000 specimens live.

Controversy in Hungary over the fate of a battery factory. The Budapest government has not closed the factory, although it is known that it has caused serious poisoning among employees. The battery factory is located in God, 25 kilometers from Budapest. It belongs to a large South Korean company. According to information revealed by the publication Telex, the factory exposed many of its employees to carcinogenic chemicals, and internal measurements revealed much more alarming results than those reported to the authorities. These aspects were recorded in a 2023 report, which accused the company of doing nothing practical to stop these poisonings. The Hungarian publication claims that although the Budapest government estimated in 2023 that the factory represented a "political risk" from a public health point of view, it still chose not to order its closure. The reason: not to scare away other potential investors. The Orban government has offered attractive tax breaks and job creation subsidies in a bid to attract Asian investors.

The High Court of Cassation and Justice is expected to make a decision on Tuesday, after several postponements, regarding the case in which former MP Dan Vîlceanu, former Minister of Investments, was sued by the General Prosecutor's Office for outrage, abusive behavior and disturbing public order and peace, after allegedly hitting and scratching his party colleague, PNL MP Florin Roman, in 2024. The case is in the preliminary chamber phase, when judges decide whether the conditions are met for the trial to begin. In May 2025, former MP Dan Vîlceanu was sued by the Prosecutor's Office attached to the High Court of Cassation and Justice for outrage, abusive behavior and disturbing public order and peace, after the altercation he had, the previous year, with PNL MP Florin Roman. "The evidence administered revealed that, on May 21, 2024, at 11:15 a.m., while he was in the plenary session of the Chamber of Deputies, in the Palace of Parliament, the defendant committed acts of violence against the injured person, a deputy in the Romanian Parliament, who was exercising the duties specific to the public office given by the constitutional mandate of deputy of Romania. Through the acts of violence, the defendant caused the injured person traumatic injuries, by hitting him with a hard body and scratching him, requiring 4-5 days of medical care for healing," specified PICCJ. At the same time, Vîlceanu is accused of having addressed offensive expressions to Roman, his actions having as a consequence, according to prosecutors, the disturbance of public order and peace. According to art. 25 of Law no. 96/2006, deputies benefit from the protection of authority during the exercise of their parliamentary mandate, being bearers of public state authority. "We note that the defendant benefits from parliamentary immunity for political opinions, an aspect regulated by the provisions of art. 20 - 22 of Law no. 96/2006 and art. 72 of the Constitution. Deputies and senators may, however, be prosecuted and sent to criminal trial for acts that are not related to the votes or political opinions expressed in the exercise of their mandate, according to art. 23 of Law no. 96/2006, but they cannot be searched, detained or arrested preventively or at home without the approval of the Chamber of which they are a member and without proceeding to hear them", the Prosecutor General's Office mentioned. Radu Miruță spoke on Digi24 about Romania's defense in the event of Russian attacks from Ukraine, close to the Romanian border. The Defense Minister says that the defense against these devices "we succeeded", but specifies that it is difficult for him to talk about a system that "covers everything". Asked about the Russian drone attacks at the mouths of the Danube and entering Romanian airspace, the Defense Minister says that he sees a constant. "It depends on the weather conditions. I mean, in the last three or four days they haven't been, because maybe because of the weather conditions. It's a very delicate matter, because the stakes of these attacks are the ports on the Danube of Ukraine, that is, 100-200 meters from the Romanian shore. We see these drones coming, usually from the Black Sea area, Snake Island. They are seen on our radars. It's a very millimeter analysis, if you estimate that they stop at the Danube port, on the right bank or come on the left bank, you no longer have the capacity to react. If you see it starting to cross the Danube, that's a second, probably even less. Depending on the type of drone that is flying and then military, there are some scenarios that we have seen working so far," said Radu Miruță. The Minister of Defense says that there is equipment on the ground that can target the drone and shoot it down if it comes into the sector where the equipment can fire. There are situations that, depending on the military analysis, the kinetics of the drone type, require the lifting of fighter jets to prevent it. So far, fighter jets have prevented it. "It was the case of those drones that were discovered, and an analysis was done. They came from Russia, someone came with them by road and picked them up from Romanian territory. There was that drone in Vaslui, there was another one, I was a minister. They discovered it in Câmpul Lung, in a forest, during a hunting trip and it was discovered that it had been there for months, that an electronic analysis was done. There are these scenarios. "We see this higher frequency, because the intensity with which Ukrainians are attacked at Danube ports is higher than at the border, I don't know, in another area of the border with other countries, the radars that we have... It's complicated, that at any altitude they can cover the entire 649.5 km length that we have of the border with Ukraine, because it's a physical matter, of relief, of wave heights, reflected militarily. The concern is to have a guard on the populated area and we move devices depending on how we observe that the part of the "Russia attacking the area in Ukraine. So far, we have succeeded. It did not happen to be an attack on a populated area in Romania," Miruță added. "Well, what I got, asking about this system, is that it is operable, but the integration into the national system still needs work. It's hard to answer you, but you should know that we are not talking about a system that covers everything. I mean, we will not say that the next day there will be no problem. We do not have a wall yet. Poland does not have a wall, nor do the Nordic countries. That drone wall, in which someone, as in a computer game, makes a curtain through which absolutely nothing passes, is a utopia. There is no such thing, but yes, we are watching very carefully and so far we have succeeded. We protect populated areas, we move ground devices depending on how we see what is happening on the other side of the Danube and what the Russian Federation's strategy is for attacking the Danube. There are permanent squadrons of fighter jets that for certain scenarios are lifted from the ground. We cover a good part of the situations", concluded the minister. Defense Minister Radu Miruță declared, live on Digi24, that Romania needs modern satellite communications capabilities and a revitalized defense industry, but decisions must be made pragmatically, with calculated risks. Regarding the military satellite that the Army would like, the minister emphasized that "we are analyzing whether to launch it. The launch costs around 700,000 euros and does not guarantee that the product, once in orbit, will work", adding that "700,000 euros just to see it go, I don't really sign". Miruță also discussed the SAFE program, military acquisitions and the stakes of strategic investments, specifying that Romania has already signed the acquisition contract for Mistral missiles. Defense Minister Radu Miruță claims that Romania needs satellite communications, but warns that such projects must be evaluated strictly from the point of view of efficiency and risks. He spoke about a research project in the field of low-orbit satellites, which is currently under analysis. "Romania needs satellite communications. Now I'll answer you, if you want, as a telecommunications engineer. The satellite is somewhere very high - this in low orbit, it's 400 kilometers above the Earth. It sees more than Romania. Maybe it's efficient to use the services of a satellite together with other countries, because I have my toy and you have my toy and we both do the same thing. The project is in a phase where the product exists and we are currently analyzing whether to launch it, to test what happened on the ground. The launch costs around 700,000 euros and does not guarantee that the product, once in orbit, will work. I asked for a clear analysis of the chances of success, because I don't really sign 700,000 euros just to see it take off," said Miruță. Regarding the European SAFE program, the Minister of Defense explained that Romania benefits from the advantages of joint procurement, both in terms of price and local production conditions. "The European Commission has just approved these projects for us. Contracts of approximately 600 million euros have already been signed for the Mistral missiles, in a joint purchase with seven other countries, which allowed us a much lower price than if we had bought them ourselves. I hear all sorts of things that we are giving money to the Germans or the French. It is nonsense and a fantastic intoxication. It is exactly the opposite: through the money from SAFE we are setting the condition that the Germans and the French come to produce here, in Romania. This happens through the contract", said the Minister. The Ministry of Economy must establish the percentage of production carried out on national territory for each product. "For some products, such as the assault rifle – the weapon at the foot of every Romanian soldier – it will be 100% produced in Romania. You can't buy from another country and expect the Romanian Army not to have a vulnerability," explained Miruță. In the case of Airbus's H225 helicopters, production will be partially carried out in Romania, and for the patrol ships, the condition is that they be built entirely locally, to support the Mangalia shipyard. "We have the H225 helicopters, which are a modern aircraft from Airbus. We had received approval for the 215 model, to come with a license in Romania for the 225, which is a high-performance model. We will only have a percentage - I don't know: 30%, 40%, 50%... that will be made in Romania. For the patrol ships - these must be 100% made in Romania, because it is the only way to decommission the Mangalia shipyard. There are also software products, there are radars that will be partially made in Romania. There are companies that produce radars and that have hundreds of employees in Romania. We will set conditions for a good part of the final product to be built in Romania. And the job is very strict here, but it is a very good opportunity. One argument is that being joint purchases, for the joint component, we get a lower price. Another argument is that it is an almost unique token, that by setting these conditions - to carry out production on Romanian territory - we can technology that we do not have in the factories where today, literally, trees grow inside the hall. And this discourages some who will manage to get on this boat”, the dignitary pointed out. The Minister of Defense drew attention to the fact that Romania has a limited time to sign contracts worth 9.5 billion euros. “If we do not sign, we lose the money. But we will not sign contracts at double or triple the price. We have a clear scale, with catalog prices, and we do not negotiate behind our backs. It is money that Romania will pay in 40 years, at a very low interest rate – this is the gain”, said Radu Miruță. The first major investment in this program is expected to be marked next week. "I understand that next week the factory where the self-propelled howitzer will be produced will be inaugurated, in Petrești, in Dâmbovița County. Not the final product, but the beginning of the construction of the hall - the laying of the foundation stone", the Minister of Defense specified. "He is resisting, he is resisting, without a doubt. And we see that he is resisting. And even if many things are behind schedule, he is resisting and moving forward. It is one of Mr. Bolojan's qualities. I think they were counting his days last summer, if I'm not mistaken, and at some point it was the day and the motion and the departure. Including yesterday they were trying to give sources, if I'm not mistaken, that he was resigning. The controversy over the contract to promote AUR in the US, during the presidential election campaign last year, continues. The firm that officially reported to the US authorities that it had concluded a lobbying contract with AUR, worth 1.5 million dollars, BGD Legal Consulting, has sued another company that allegedly promised, without keeping its word, to facilitate meetings between party leaders and several high-ranking officials of the Trump Administration, including the president himself. The complaint filed in the US courts also shows that BGD Legal Consulting facilitated George Simion's interview for NewsMax, in May 2025. AUR representatives, as well as Marius Lulea, deny, however, the information presented by BGD Legal Consulting in the US lawsuit. BGD Legal Consulting, the US firm with which AUR concluded a lobbying contract, and about which Digi24.ro wrote extensively here last year, had a lawsuit with another US lobbying company: Obsidian Advisory LLC. Court documents show that BGD Legal Consulting initially paid Obsidian Advisory LLC $100,000, out of a total of $500,000, to facilitate an interview with an AUR board member and NewsMax’s Chris Ruddy, as well as a photo with President Donald Trump at Mar-a-Lago, over Easter weekend 2025. However, in the week before Easter weekend 2025, Obsidian Advisory LLC informed BGD Legal Consulting that Donald Trump would not be in Florida that weekend and would not be able to hold any meetings. “By the time we were informed that no meetings would be held in Florida, the AUR delegation had already traveled to the United States, incurring significant costs in this regard,” according to BGD Legal Consulting’s complaint. On the Friday before Easter, when the Mar-a-Lago meetings were to take place, Obsidian Advisory LLC reportedly said it had managed to arrange a meeting between AUR members and Secretary of State Marco Rubio on that Friday, between 1 p.m. and 2 p.m., according to the BGD Legal Consulting complaint. "No meeting took place at the State Department. No meeting with the Secretary of State was confirmed," the complaint states. Later, Obsidian Advisory representatives allegedly promised another meeting between a U.S. official and AUR members, with an undersecretary of state for the Department of Homeland Security. At the same time, they allegedly promised that Politico would publish an article about the AUR members' visit to the U.S., the complaint states. "The promised article (..) was never published," according to the complaint cited. Because BGD Legal claims that Obsidian Advisory did not keep its word and did not facilitate any meeting, it ended up in a U.S. civil court. The same complaint, however, shows that BGD Legal Consulting facilitated an interview with NewsMax for AUR. According to the complaint cited, BGD Legal shows that this, the fact that Obsidian Advisory did not facilitate any meeting for AUR, led to a damage of 1.5 million dollars. This is the same amount that appeared in the contract that Digi24.ro wrote about extensively in April 2025. At the same time, the complaint cited also shows that, if Obsidian Advisory had kept its promise, it would have been another 3 million dollars in "other contracts". It is not clear whether these are also contracts signed with AUR. Contacted by Digi24.ro, Marius Lulea, whose signature appeared on the initial contract between AUR and BGD Legal Consulting, said that he "did not receive such things". "I have no knowledge of such a thing. I have not received such things. That is why it is better to contact the party. Maybe there are things that I do not know about. Before (no. In the spring of 2025) no payment was made, there is no contract", was the reaction of Marius Lulea. In turn, Ștefan Avrămescu, the spokesperson for the Alliance for the Unification of Romanians, claims that "no payment was made, not even 1 euro". "We did not make any payment, not even 1 euro. These false accusations were denied last year by us (...) We do not have any contract in force in this regard, it is part of the same disinformation campaign from 2025", Ștefan Avrămescu, the AUR spokesperson, told Digi24. And then, in 2025, AUR representatives defended themselves, initially claiming that the document did not exist, and later that it was just a draft and that the payment of 1.5 million dollars was not made. The representative of the American company BGD Legal Consulting, in a response provided in April 2025, did not deny the existence of the contract, but said that no payments were made. Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan said on Wednesday evening, regarding the UDMR's request to reduce taxes and duties by 50%, that the current legislation only allows for their increase, not their decrease. For this reason, the prime minister emphasized that in order to allow for a decrease in taxes, the law must be amended "as soon as possible, before the budget is approved", but he did not advance a percentage that could be reduced. Asked at the press conference, held on Wednesday evening at the Government, whether he would reduce taxes by 50% as proposed by the UDMR, Ilie Bolojan said that he had seen the proposal made by Kelemen Hunor and had discussed it with him during the day today. "The answer cannot be given very simply, because the issue of property taxes is quite complex and has a wide range of applications, but I would like to make a few clarifications. As you know, Romania has committed to bringing property taxes to a higher level, so that the benchmark is the market price of these homes. Of course, each locality has a margin to apply one percentage or another, which should apply from the end of this year. So, we still have to work on this scheme, we are in an intermediate formula. This means, for example, that the Government has established a minimum level for car taxation", stated Ilie Bolojan. "For example, some city halls, given the previous tax level, or by setting a higher increase, have ended up in a situation where the established level is higher than the minimum established by government law. Due to the discussions that have emerged in the public space, some city halls want to reduce the current level of car taxes, for example, to the minimum level established by law. The current legislation does not allow them to do this, so it allowed them to increase more than the minimum level, but does not allow them to decrease," the prime minister explained. "From my point of view, as a former public administrator, I believe that it is an attribute of local administration that above the minimum ceiling established by law, depending on the local policies that you can establish, you can increase it, but you can also decrease it, and, for example, from this point of view we can analyze to what extent we can bring this correction through legislation, so that where we have these situations, I emphasize, in which the established level is above the minimum, the city halls can return if they wish. Of course, we should do this as soon as possible, before the budget is approved, so that all these things are done before the local budgets are approved," Bolojan specified. "Anyway, as you know, this year was a special year - from the point of view of taxes - because they were adopted very late, due to the challenge at the Constitutional Court and, therefore, there was no time for explanations, clarifications. And do you remember what happened in the last, in the first months of the year, when some city halls communicated erroneous data because not all the databases were updated and it took two, three weeks for things to stabilize", the Prime Minister also said. The Head of the Executive also referred to the exceptions to property taxation that were eliminated by the Government. "One of these exceptions was the exemption from taxes, both on real estate and cars, for people with disabilities. Based on the discussions we had with local authorities, based on the analysis of the situation on the ground, we found that we were in a situation where, given that we have 957 thousand citizens who have certificates, in this sense, practically 10% of the real estate fund we have was not taxed. Also, a significant share of cars, out of the 11.5 million cars, again, was a number close to this percentage, and as a result, based on discussions at the government level and in the coalition, we made this decision to eliminate these exceptions," said the Prime Minister. The Prime Minister explained that these revenues are the contribution of each homeowner, car owner, to the local authority budget, to what the respective city hall does to ensure living conditions, to the asphalt it brings to your doorstep, to water and sewage networks and to better conditions in each locality. "Considering that, of course, nothing has been paid so far, and now suddenly the full amount is being paid, certainly for many of these citizens, and I have great understanding for this situation, because given personal knowledge, for example, I learned of such a measure in the case of a foundation that does some extraordinary things in Bihor County, and I discussed with the local administration to apply the legal provisions, that is, to grant an exemption considering their competence. Of course, we can see if we could supplement the competences of local authorities, to make certain additional reductions, but what we need to understand is that all the reductions, all the exceptions that we make, mean, in real terms, less money for the authorities and someone somewhere has to compensate for these resources and, in general, I am cautious to launch into statements", added Bolojan. The Head of the Executive also said that what they discussed was to do an analysis and see what such an impact is and they will make a decision. "We can't prolong the same thing for too long. In principle, of course, when you make a well-thought-out decision, you should avoid making corrections as much as possible immediately after making the decision, but, as you have seen, I was also put in the situation, due to the lack of correlation between two articles, to come up with a clarification, on the legislation regarding residents who are in the Danube Delta or in the Apuseni, because there were two articles that were not correlated, but, practically, nothing changed", Ilie Bolojan showed. The Mayor of the Capital, Ciprian Ciucu, announces that he will try to find out directly what is happening at STB and why public transport in Bucharest has ended up costing 1.8 billion lei per year. The Mayor states that he has asked the company's management to come up with a clear plan to reduce expenses by next Monday, and if the plan is viable, he will submit this plan to the General Council and the Government and will discuss it with the unions in advance. He also says that there will be no more discussions about fare increases until they have this plan clearly adopted. "You probably haven't heard in the last few years about a significant streamlining of the Bucharest Transport Company (STB). Neither have I. I asked the General Council to empower me to do an evaluation, a kind of audit, so that we all know what is happening in the "STB black box". Basically, I think we all need to know why public transport in Bucharest has come to cost us 1.8 billion lei per year. Let's know what this amount, equivalent to the entire budget of the city of Braşov for one year, is being spent on. Only PNL, USR and REPER voted for this to happen, the rest opposed it. We didn't have the votes, so the project failed", says the mayor of the capital, on Facebook, about the STB situation. Ciucu announces that he will try to find out for himself what is happening in STB. "I have nothing to do, I'm rolling up my sleeves and I'll try to find out firsthand what happened and what's happening at STB through meetings with the STB management, with ADI Public Transport Bucharest and with the PMB management. I've asked the STB and ADI TPBI management to come up with a clear plan by next Monday to reduce expenses and streamline the company's activity," announces the mayor of Bucharest. Ciprian Ciucu specifies that, "if the plan is viable, he will submit this plan to the General Council and the Government and will discuss it with the unions in advance." "TOGETHER we must avoid insolvency and improve public transport conditions for Bucharest residents! I will make STB's activity transparent. There will be no more discussions about fare increases until we have this plan clearly adopted. Discussions about eliminating cost-generating gratuities (such as VAT, which have accumulated and reached astronomical amounts, including from non-use of subscriptions) are pointless at this time. In a rare stance on the statements of a Romanian official, the Embassy of Ukraine in Bucharest harshly criticized a speech by PSD senator Titus Corlățean at the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe. At the end of January, Corlățean accused that from February 1, several schools teaching in Romanian in Ukraine are to be closed. The embassy provided clarifications and noted that the former minister's statements are untrue. The Romanian official, from the rostrum of the Council of Europe, declared: "We have reached a critical moment, when the restriction of education in the mother tongue for Romanians will reach an unacceptable threshold: on February 1, 2026, so in just 2 days, the Ukrainian authorities intend to close 28 of the 32 Romanian "academic high schools". A real drama for ethnic Romanians! We ask Ukraine to postpone and reconsider the implementation of this decision!" He also spoke about the situation of churches with ethnic Romanian parishioners: "Moreover, religious freedom is subject to increasing pressure: the threat to Romanian Orthodox priests by people from the Ukrainian security services and other authorities and their forcing to enter, with the Romanian churches, the Ukrainian National Church will mean their obligation to serve in Ukrainian, so practically the assimilation of the Romanian Orthodox Church and the disappearance of the Romanian religious identity in Ukraine. President Nicușor Dan said on Thursday evening, on Digi24, when asked if Romania should feel threatened by US President Donald Trump's violent speech against Europe, that there have been "shocks in the last year", but that they have not broken our country's relationship with the US. "We want the transatlantic relationship to be as harmonious as possible", the head of state stressed. Nicușor Dan declares himself optimistic about Romania's relationship with the US, which he says was built over a long period of time and is difficult to break. "We, Romania, have a strategic security relationship with the US and a predominantly economic relationship with the EU. We want the transatlantic relationship to be as harmonious as possible. There have been some shocks in the last year, but they have not broken this relationship and what we are trying to do in European debates, in different formats, is to discourage the escalation of tensions. For the moment we are fine and I am optimistic for the future, because this relationship was built over a long time, there are trade relations, there is technology transfer. It is difficult for this relationship to be truly broken. Until then, however, in an increasingly competitive world, it is very good what the European Union is doing and in internal debates we are of the opinion that we should open a trade agreement with South America, with India, so that our economies are much more competitive", declared the president. "Broadly speaking, I exclude this scenario of a transatlantic rupture", added Nicușor Dan, referring to the hypothesis in which Romania would have to choose between the relationship with the US and the one with the European Union. Asked about the blunt statements of NATO chief Mark Rutte, according to which there cannot be a European defense alliance without US support, Nicușor Dan said that he agrees "mostly" with him. "Until we get there, we have to compensate for the security deficit. Where Donald Trump is right is that, for decades, Europe has relied on the security provided by the United States and that the economic price paid for this has been unbalanced between the United States and European countries. And then what we have to do is - and, fortunately, we have started to do it and this war in Ukraine has spurred us on, I am talking about European countries - is to start investing in defense, to try to make the different military techniques that we have compatible, but this is a process that will take years, during which, and now Mark Rutte says, collaboration with the United States remains essential", the head of state also declared. In a speech in Brussels, Rutte said that “anyone who thinks that the European Union, or Europe as a whole, can defend itself without the United States is dreaming.” “You can’t. We can’t, we need each other,” he told MEPs. Rutte explained that if Europeans really wanted to build a new defensive alliance without the United States, it would cost them not 5% but 10% of their gross domestic product (GDP), and would also force them to build their own nuclear deterrent. “That costs billions and billions of euros. And in this scenario, you would lose the ultimate guarantor of our freedom, namely the American nuclear umbrella. So, good luck!” he told MEPs during a question-and-answer session. Nicușor Dan said that Romania is a “middle power” that has relations with both the United States and the European Union. The statement comes in the context of a stark warning issued by Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney at Davos. He said that the world order “is on the verge of extinction” and urged middle powers to act together in the face of Trump’s threats. “It seems like every day reminds us that we live in an era of great power rivalry. That the rules-based world order is on the verge of extinction, that the strongest can do whatever they can while the weak must suffer whatever they have to. Faced with such logic, there is a strong tendency for countries to go ahead like this, to comply, to avoid problems and to hope that if they comply they will be safe. That is not how it works,” said the Canadian prime minister. Carney declared that great powers should not bully their allies and force the international system too much. "Hegemons cannot continue to constantly monetize their relationships. Middle powers must act together, because if we are not at the table, we will be on the menu," he said, in a speech that went viral online. The Church and the Army remain the institutions in which Romanians have the most trust, reveals the Informat.ro – INSCOP Research Barometer, 7th edition. The Church and the Police are the institutions in which trust has increased compared to July 2025, all other institutions included in the survey - the Army (which still remains in second place in the top of trust), the Presidency, the Government, the Parliament - registering decreases. The Presidency is in fourth place, followed by the Justice, which was included in the January 2026 barometer, while the Parliament is in last place, with a trust share of 11.9%. The Church is the institution in which Romanians have the most trust, with 63.9% declaring that they have quite a lot and a lot of trust in this institution (compared to 57.7% in July 2025). The Army follows, with a trust capital of 61.8% (compared to 63% in July 2025) and the Police with 50% (compared to 43.2% in July 2025). The ranking is continued by the Presidency with 27.9% (compared to 34.8% in July 2025), Justice with 25.4% and Government with 18.4% (compared to 20.4% in July 2025). In last position is the Parliament with 11.9% quite a lot and a lot of trust (compared to 14.5% in July 2025). They trust the Church especially: PSD and AUR voters, people over 60 years old, those with primary education, rural residents. PSD and PNL voters, people over 60 years old, rural residents are the categories that have the most trust in the Army. They trust the Police especially: PSD and PNL voters, young people under 30, state employees. PNL and USR voters, young people under 30, people with higher education, residents of Bucharest and large urban areas, state employees are the categories that have the most trust in the Presidency. PSD and AUR voters, people between 18 and 44 years old, those with primary education have more trust in Justice than the rest of the population. They trust the Government especially: USR and PNL voters, young people under 30, people with higher education, residents of Bucharest. PSD, PNL and USR voters, young people under 30, residents of Bucharest have higher trust in Parliament than the rest of the population. "Institutions perceived as "non-political" dominate public trust. The Church and the Army remain symbolic landmarks of stability and identity, a sign that the population is looking for anchors of continuity outside the political game itself. It is a classic pattern in societies with structural distrust in the political class. Political institutions are trapped in a structural deficit of credibility. We are not just talking about conjunctural dissatisfaction, but a chronic distrust in representative institutions. This indicates a rupture between citizens and the classic mechanisms of representative democracy, which fuels populism, anti-system discourse and radical formulas of political representation”, states Remus Ştefureac, director of INSCOP Research. The data were collected between January 12-15, 2026, through the CATI method (telephone interviews). The research method was interviewing via questionnaire. The volume of the simple, stratified sample was 1100 people, representative of significant socio-demographic categories (gender, age, occupation) for the non-institutionalized population of Romania, aged 18 and over. The maximum allowed error of the data is ± 3%, at a confidence level of 95%. Editor: BE Follow Digi24.ro news and on Google News

Regarding Romania's position on the Peace Council, Goșu said that the country should not participate, emphasizing that the relationship with the United States "will survive" anyway. He also criticized a possible attitude of political submission. "If PSD wants to sit with its hand on its cap and behave like a Phanariot who quickly goes to the Porte, that's its business. It behaves the same when it's in power and when it's in opposition. You don't know whether to take it seriously," he said. The analyst warned that Romania must resist the pressures created by Donald Trump and his "accidental allies", who would aim to destabilize some European countries. "We need to keep our heads down, do serious analyses and use less internal political games. It is very easy to use Trump to attack the president or the governing partners," said Goșu. Regarding the invitation to the European Council, political sources told Digi24 that there is no pressure from the US. The main problem would be the lack of money, the sum of one billion dollars being difficult to find in Romania's budget. An analysis is to be made during a meeting of the European Council, and each state will make its decision at national level, after consultations. "We have the perfect pretext: we have no money and we shrug our shoulders nicely," concluded the analyst. Armand Goșu also commented on the absence of the President of Romania, Nicușor Dan, from the World Economic Forum, emphasizing that he chose to participate in the European Council meeting. "It's much better at the European Council. We are witnessing a spectacle that is not necessarily that of a superpower and is not worthy of America. What Trump is doing now is a cold shower that will mark future generations. Being surrounded by authoritarian political leaders and being rejected by Europeans is not a great image gain for Trump," said Goșu. According to him, Donald Trump is "desperately" looking for various solutions and is trying to replace the UN with an unclear structure, "an ostrich-camel", whose exact role is unknown. "I don't think anything serious will come of it," added the analyst. In Armand Goșu's opinion, many leaders from states that do not have direct access to Washington feel good at Davos, where they have the opportunity to socialize with Trump. George Simion's gesture of cutting a cake in the shape of a country is not unique. An older clip from 2019 has resurfaced on social media, when ultranationalist Russian politician Vladimir Zhirinovsky cut a cake in the shape and colors of Ukraine. George Simion's participation in an event in the United States, where he received an award from a radical Republican organization, made the rounds of the press after the AUR leader cut a cake in the shape of Greenland, frosted with the US flag. He later reacted, accusing disinformation and hypocrisy. However, his gesture attracted much criticism from the political environment, including from politicians with radical views. The cake-cutting episode at the US event brought back to the fore a similar incident that took place in 2019 in Russia: the ultranationalist Russian politician Vladimir Zhirinovsky cut a cake in the shape of Ukraine, glazed in the national colors - blue and yellow - and with a red portion, in the part where the Donbas region is located on the map, which Russia has not managed to fully occupy even after four years of war that began in February 2022. The images were posted at the time by Zhirinovsky himself on his social media account, where he said that he received "a wonderful birthday cake as a gift" from the hosts of the TV show "60 Minutes". "I cut it today," Zhirinovsky wrote on X in April 2019. Vladimir Zhirinovsky died on April 6, 2022, at the age of 75. Zhirinovsky was known for his anti-Western tirades and provocative outbursts that kept him in the public eye for over three decades. Vladimir Zhirinovsky predicted in December 2021 the evolution of tensions with Ukraine and announced when the war would start: February 22, 2022, at 4 am. His prediction was quite accurate: Russian President Vladimir Putin ordered the invasion of Ukraine on February 24, at 5 am, Moscow time. Editor: BP Follow the news on Digi24.ro and on Google News

Several dozen people filed a criminal complaint against 60 Romanian officials, former officials or associations on Thursday, January 22, accusing them, among other things, of crimes against humanity and demanding compensation of 1 million euros in the context of the cancellation of the 2024 presidential elections. Although the organizers claim that "the action is not political in nature", indications discovered by Digi24.ro point to a newly founded political party by people who held important positions in civil institutions in Romania or the army. Approximately 20 people were on January 22, around 10:20, in front of the General Prosecutor's Office to file a criminal complaint against 60 Romanian officials, former officials or associations. Generically, it is a criminal complaint focused on the cancellation of the second round of the 2024 presidential elections. People received a criminal complaint template and were advised by the organizers of this action to fill in their personal data and submit the same document to the General Prosecutor's Office on January 22, between 10 am and 12 pm. "The action is not a protest and is not political in nature, being initiated by unaffiliated citizens, from the country and the diaspora. The aim of the approach is to legally clarify responsibilities and restore trust in the democratic process, through the law," says a post by the Civic Movement "Valul Democrației". The organization of this action took place online, through a Facebook page that was created on January 10 and through a public Whatsapp group. The initiators call themselves "Civic Movement Valul Democrației", an organization promoted including by influential figures from the sovereignist area. Although the organizers of the action promoted by "Valul Democrației" claim that it is not political in nature, there are indications that point to a party founded by people who held important positions in the Romanian state or who worked within the Ministry of Defense. Specifically, in the "contact details" category there is the email address - valuldemocrației@asociatia-ales.ro. The domain "@asociatia-ales.ro" belongs to an association created in November 2025, namely the Association for Freedom and Social Equality (ALES). Another indication in this regard is the official email of the association: contact@asociatia-ales.ro. The official address of the association is found in Sector 3 of the Capital, in a building that appears in official documents as the headquarters of several companies, but also of a political party. This is the National Integrity Party (PIN), a party founded in the summer of 2025. In court, the representative of the ALES Association is Anton Gheorghe, who we find in the position of vice-president-treasurer of PIN. The building in which PIN and the ALES Association operate belongs to a former secretary of state from the PSD governments, Constantin Jenică Bucur. He is also the president of the political party. Constantin Jenică Bucur shows, in his personal description, that he is "a recognized leader in the fields of finance and banking, public administration and information technology". "He held leadership positions in fundamental institutions of the Romanian state, including the National Bank of Romania, CEC Bank, the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of Communications, where he contributed decisively to the modernization and digital transformation of Romania", according to his own description. Between 2021 and 2024, Constantin Jenică Bucur claims to have been Coordinator of the Cryptocurrencies and Digital Currencies Office within the National Bank of Romania. Among the positions held by Constantin Jenică Bucur in the Romanian state is the head of the Board of Directors of the National Radiocommunications Company SA. He was dismissed from this position in 2020. The leadership of the National Integrity Party (PIN) also includes Florin Stanciu (vice president - former head of the National Penitentiary Administration and the Ministry of Justice) or David Victor (vice president - among others, former officer of the Romanian Army, specialized in transmissions, communications and electronic warfare). Digi24.ro contacted Constantin Jenică Bucur, Gheorghe Anton, the National Integrity Party, but also an organizer who kept in touch with the people who participated in the action on WhatsApp. We will include their answers in the article as they come. Returning to the criminal complaint, it accuses, among other things, "a generalized and systematic attack against the candidate Călin Georgescu, but also against the 2.1 million Romanians who voted for or supported him". "This generalized and systematic attack launched against the 2.1 million Romanians who voted for or supported the candidate Călin Georgescu, through continuous public denigration committed through television, podcasts, press websites and posts on social networks, encouraged by the President of Romania, Government representatives, parliamentarians and other public authorities, an attack unsanctioned by state bodies", the criminal complaint states. The list of "perpetrators" includes, among others, the following: In addition to punishing the "perpetrators" for the crimes they are accused of, each person who filed the criminal complaint requests compensation of 1 million euros ("equivalent in lei") as moral and material damage. According to the organizers, approximately 60 criminal complaints were filed in the action of January 22. "The "wave" will continue in the coming period. So far, starting with December 22, over a hundred criminal complaints have been submitted to the authorities on the subject of the annulment of the elections. (...) The approach will continue with new requests to the Prosecutor's Office for the urgent start of the criminal investigation", the organizers sent to Digi24.ro. Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan states that, during this period, Government representatives are working on building the state budget for 2026, on "realistic grounds", with the objective of a "budget of recovery and investment". The Head of the Executive argues that reducing the budget deficit by over 1% of GDP, maintaining investments and increasing revenues have contributed to regaining Romania's credibility on the financial markets, even if fiscal adjustments have generated economic difficulties for the population. "The savings achieved in the second half of last year allowed us to reduce the budget deficit by over 1% of GDP, below the assumed target of 8.4%. We respected our commitments and regained credibility with investors and financial markets. In 2025, we reduced the deficit without reducing investments. These totaled 137.5 billion lei, representing over 7% of GDP. European funds, including those from the PNRR, recorded a high level of over-contracting, and projects were prioritized. We maintained financial discipline and went through a first stage of reducing state spending. We increased budget revenues, including by increasing some taxes. These adjustments generated an economic contraction and meant additional difficulties for many Romanians," Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan said on Wednesday evening in a post on his Facebook page. According to the head of the Executive, "without increasing taxes", there is "a solid basis for recovery this year". "We are working on building the budget for 2026 on realistic bases. The deficit target is just over 6% and will be finalized in the coming period. Inflation will decrease to 4%. Our objective is a budget of recovery and investments. Over 15 billion euros will come from European funds, through the PNRR and cohesion policy. This money will be found in infrastructure, economy and better public services", declared Bolojan. At the same time, he announced that at the beginning of February the Government is to take responsibility for the legislation that will restrict state spending in the administration and support economic recovery, with the state budget to be adopted later. "I know that, for now, the negative effects of deficit reduction are being felt in everyday life. From the following months, as a result of the recovery measures adopted and on a healthier economic basis, Romania's economy will enter a recovery path", pointed out Ilie Bolojan. Foreign Minister Oana Ţoiu declared on Wednesday that the law that came into force in Ukraine on Wednesday does not concern any restrictions on the right to citizenship of Romanian communities in Ukraine and this was false information, politically amplified. "I do not comment on the political statements of my coalition colleagues, but I still want to remind them that a good part of the officials in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, a good part of the good diplomats we have in the world, are the same diplomats and the same officials that you worked with during your terms as prime minister, for example. It is very easy to ask for clarification from any of them directly. The law that came into force today does not concern any restrictions on the right to citizenship of Romanian communities in Ukraine. This was false information, politically amplified," the Foreign Minister said, according to News.ro. Oana Ţoiu pointed out that "the law in question has an annex with a number of countries, which Romania is not actually a member of, but it talks about the right to acquire Ukrainian citizenship". "If there were to be a problem, then it would exclusively target Romanians who would like to keep their home citizenship and request Ukrainian citizenship. But these requests are not requests that are in significant numbers to the attention of either the Ukrainian state or Romania. So I want to say, again, it is false information that the law talks about dual citizenship, in the sense that those who now live in Ukraine and would have Ukrainian citizenship would also acquire other citizenships and then it would mean that it implies a disadvantage compared to the Romanian communities there. The law that came into force today talks about something completely different, namely citizens of countries whose citizens can also request Ukrainian citizenship without giving up their initial one", explained the minister. According to the minister, "a large part of the Romanian communities in Ukraine are Romanian-speaking communities that already have Ukrainian citizenship". "What I want to clarify is that we are not talking about the right of those Romanians to acquire Romanian citizenship. If a Romanian citizen wanted to obtain Ukrainian citizenship, indeed, they would face some obstacles in the legal process, but we do not know of any large number of requests. Think about it, this would mean that Romanian citizens would request Ukrainian citizenship and, in practice, would also put themselves under the constraints and obligations of Ukrainian laws, including that of conscription to war", the Foreign Minister also said. Oana Ţoiu mentioned that "this bilateral process between countries of legislative change and regarding citizenship, in all cases, is started there at times when there are a number of justified requests in that direction". "We are prepared, if there is this request in significant numbers. They have not reached us. But if there is, we will certainly include this in the diplomatic agenda. But, I repeat, the information that was in the public space, regarding the fact that the Romanian communities in Ukraine would not have, practically, through this law, other rights than other communities, is false information", stressed Ţoiu. PSD representatives requested, on Wednesday, the Romanian authorities to clarify "urgently" the reasons why Romania "was omitted" from the list of states for which Ukraine has regulated dual citizenship. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced on Wednesday, after PSD requested clarifications on why Romania was omitted from the list of states for which Ukraine has regulated dual citizenship, that the legislative amendment in question aims to obtain Ukrainian citizenship by foreign citizens who fight as volunteers in the Ukrainian armed forces or carry out humanitarian activities on the territory of Ukraine, their families, as well as to maintain and strengthen ties with the Ukrainian state of Ukrainian communities abroad. Tanczos Barna explained, exclusively for Digi24, why Ilie Bolojan doubled local taxes. The Deputy Prime Minister stated that some administrations kept taxes to a minimum, while others, on the contrary, increased them to the maximum level, so that inequalities emerged. At the same time, the UDMR politician emphasized that these collected taxes must remain in the local budget. "People ask you why "Ilie Sărăcie" doubled our taxes. Just because he wants to? What is the idea? Why did Ilie Bolojan need to double local taxes?", Tanczos Barna was asked by Cosmin Prelipceanu, on Jurnalul de Seară. "There are mayoralties and mayoralties. There is a range of taxation of real estate or cars. Some mayoralties have kept the maximum, other mayoralties have kept the taxes at the minimum level. Some have indexed with inflation, others have forgotten to index with inflation. And inequalities, incorrect approaches appear. Some, from a locality, pay 10 lei, others pay 5 lei or 100 lei. On the other hand, the contribution of the local community to the local budget must not necessarily be consistent, but there must also be a contribution from the local community through local taxes and fees," explained Tanczos Barna. The Deputy Prime Minister emphasized that he has always supported that these taxes remain in the local budget and that the money should never be taken by the government. "We have also been arguing for decades that income tax should remain 100% with the local authority, the city hall, the local council or the county. This scheme exists today," the UDMR senator said. At the same time, Tanczos Barna explained that it is important to have a "solidarity fund." "Mayors who cannot support themselves receive a balance. In 2025, we generalized this solidarity fund for the first time: that you cannot put an equal sign between a mayor's office of 1,500-2,000 inhabitants or an administration of 2,000 citizens and one of 200,000 citizens, where the tax per capita is three times, maybe 10 times higher than in a commune far from infrastructure, far from the highway, far from the national road. And then we need a national solidarity to which everyone contributes. And from that solidarity fund, let's keep the level high enough for those who were not born in the Capital, for those who were not born in Cluj-Napoca. On the other hand, where the peaks are very high, that is, 10 times, five times higher is the income tax per capita, from those peaks let's pinch a little and give to the communities that don't have a chance of a highways, an industrial park, a university center", said Barna. This would happen at the national level, not within the counties. "For example, the smallest county in the country, Covasna. You cannot say that Bucharest has enough to pay for everything and a commune must remain uninhabited. This solidarity fund must be continued", the deputy prime minister stressed. The crisis of trust in the Romanian judiciary is generated by visible dysfunctions and the lack of structural reforms, and the issue of special pensions has a major impact on the state budget, warns Valeriu Stoica, a legal specialist and former Minister of Justice. According to him, if this issue is not resolved, there is a risk that the entire pension system will reach the brink of collapse. "The issue of service pensions in the judiciary is a small part of a much larger problem, that of special pensions for all professional categories. Magistrates' pensions represent only a few percent of the budgetary dimension of this problem. Magistrates did not understand that, if this issue, which is the most flagrant for public opinion, is not resolved, it is very difficult for the Government to start solving the big problem. If this part, which has the greatest impact on public opinion, is not resolved, it is impossible to move forward. This is not just about magistrates, but about a problem with a major impact on Romania's budget, which will generate very serious complications in the coming period," Valeriu Stoica declared on the show "In Front of You". The former Minister of Justice warned that, otherwise, the pension system could even end up "cracking". "It could get to the point where the pension system completely collapses, because hundreds of thousands of beneficiaries of these service pensions mean a huge budgetary impact. The problem will not be solved if this part, the most visible of all, is not solved. In addition, structural problems must also be discussed, because there are other dysfunctions that are part of a larger problem," he explained. Valeriu Stoica argues that the issue of magistrates' pensions should not dominate all discussions about dysfunctions in the system. According to him, "the issue of premises, the issue of staff shortage and the issue of judicial management" should not be ignored. "Unfortunately, all these structural deficiencies generate two very damaging consequences: the long duration of trials, which rightly displeases litigants, and the emergence of a feeling of unfairness within the judiciary. These are real problems. I agree that the retirement age and service pensions are at the forefront, but if the other problems are not addressed, there will be no real improvement in the judicial system," Valeriu Stoica also said. The law on the reform of special pensions has been postponed, for the fourth time, by the judges of the Constitutional Court. The new deadline given is February 11, and the postponement blocked the entry into force of the reform from January 1, as provided for in the text adopted by Parliament. The last postponement, on January 16, was given "in view of the request to interrupt the deliberations for a better study of the issues that form the subject of the case, as well as the documents submitted by the author of the notification on January 15, 2026 (extrajudicial accounting expertise pro causa) and some incidental legal provisions". This is a document submitted by the High Court of Cassation and Justice, the institution that contested the draft law, which refers to the fact that the contested law "cancels the service pension". The law on the reform of magistrates' pensions was adopted last year for the second time, by assuming the responsibility of the Government in Parliament, after a first version had been declared unconstitutional due to the lack of the SCM's opinion. The Russian military intelligence service GRU was responsible for an attempted arson attack in 2024 on a factory in Lithuania that supplies radio wave scanners to the Ukrainian military, Lithuanian officials said on Friday. Six citizens from Spain, Colombia, Cuba, Russia and Belarus have been charged in connection with the incident, and the group has also attempted to carry out similar attacks in Poland, Romania and the Czech Republic, Vilnius police and prosecutors said, according to Sky News. Kremlin-linked intelligence officers are accused of trying to recruit people through messaging apps such as Telegram and gaming websites to turn them into “disposable agents” tasked with committing arson, vandalism and other hostile acts. Citizens of other nationalities are also being recruited. “The crimes were coordinated and the orders were given to the perpetrators by a group of individuals based in Russia and with ties to the Russian GRU,” Lithuania’s deputy chief of criminal police, Saulius Briginas, told reporters. The research report, published by the think tank Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), found that money was a key motivating factor, with teenagers, migrants and older people with Soviet military experience considered ideal candidates for recruitment. The payment – which ranges from hundreds to thousands of euros – is often promised in cryptocurrency, making the source of funding difficult for investigators to trace. “The methods used to recruit and assign saboteurs to tasks have shifted from the Cold War-era reliance on trained intelligence agents to a model characterised by remote, independent missions,” the report, titled “Responding to Russian Sabotage Financing,” said. “Hostile actors are now outsourcing low-cost tasks to ‘disposable agents’ recruited online.” The Kremlin has previously denied Western accusations of a growing campaign of sabotage and other hybrid hostilities. However, the number of serious acts of arson and sabotage linked to Russia across Europe is expected to rise to 34 in 2024, up from 12 the previous year and just two in 2022, Sky News reports. The authors of the RUSI report said this tactic of deliberately deniable activity, carried out below the threshold of conventional warfare, “has evolved into a systematic and geographically targeted threat.” They urged NATO and the EU to urgently improve their response to deter future acts of sabotage. This includes agreeing a definition of what constitutes sabotage and using counter-terrorism powers to track illicit funding channels. The report also says that governments should view individual incidents – no matter how minor – as part of a much more serious pattern of activity directed against Western allies. “While individual incidents may appear minor or opportunistic, taken together they suggest the emergence of a wider campaign designed to increase the cost of support for Ukraine, test NATO red lines and erode public confidence in Western national security arrangements,” the report says. Russia’s alleged sabotage covers a range of actions, from major operations such as damaging submarine cables to more modest attacks on military and civilian targets, including arson and vandalism, as well as reconnaissance. This low-level activity is the main focus of the report, which drew on the views of law enforcement, academics and journalists, as well as public policy experts, according to British media. Warning from the most famous Romanian commander: Russia could organize challenges to the Neptun Deep project Given that many Russian intelligence officers were expelled from Europe following Russia's large-scale invasion of Ukraine, the RUSI report found that Russian spies "are increasingly relying on intermediaries and 'disposable agents', many of them from Ukraine, to carry out sabotage missions." "If such incidents are treated simply as the actions of individual Ukrainians, this could fuel anti-Ukrainian sentiment and erode public support for Kiev - a strategic objective of the sabotage operations," the report says.
