The safety of dignitaries and the flight itself are the main elements taken into account for the purchase of an aircraft to be used by a country's president, according to Emil Dobrovolschi, a former pilot of aircraft that transported heads of state of Romania. He told Digi24 that these types of aircraft are configured with a work desk part, a rest part, even a shower, given the long duration of the flights. "Their configuration depends on the imagination of those who command the plane," the pilot also claims. At the same time, the existence of special communications on board such an aircraft, which are also encrypted, is vital. "First of all, I think about flight safety and I think about the safety of dignitaries. So it's not just about the president, it's about Romania's representatives on various trips. They need increased safety. In terms of costs, in that amount of time an airplane bought by the Romanian state for its dignitaries, for the president, for the prime minister, for ministerial delegations, NATO delegations would have been amortized. Flight safety is much higher, because you have people that you raise, train and supervise, who are yours, you have an airplane that has been prepared for the respective missions. By renting or by the fact that certain dignitaries fly on scheduled flights, it seems wrong to me from all points of view. At one point, we had something like that. I think in 2013, there were the last missions, in the United States of America, where the aircraft that we had at the time, which was intended for this type of mission, we were there in 8 hours. Or missions longer long. I once flew from Houston to Bucharest. I had the chance to be on board the plane that flew the longest flight in TAROM's history. I had a very strong tailwind and, without a stopover, I came from Houston to Bucharest, exceeding the plane's range by over 3,000 km", says Emil Dobrovolschi. He explained that they are aircraft intended for passenger flights, for which they are adapted inside to provide a certain comfort. "These types of aircraft are configured with an office part, for work, a part for rest. It also has a shower. Their configuration depends on the imagination of those who command the plane, but at a minimum it should have an office, a place to rest for the 10-12 hours that a long-haul flight can last, seats for advisors, seats for the press. Both Boeing and Airbus have the same offer for executive long-haul aircraft. These types of aircraft, not carrying many passengers on board and not needing so much luggage, the volume is reduced. Under the deck where the passengers step, they have some additional tanks that give this increased range. This type of aircraft can fly up to 13 hours, depending on the type of engine, depending on many other things. After a very long flight, the dignitary after 12-13h must look in a certain shape, represent Romania. But more than that, such an aircraft also has some means encrypted communication systems, which in themselves cost quite a lot. I don't know the prices, but they are vital to be able to communicate safely with the ground. It is vital to have special communications on board such an aircraft that are also encrypted, which can provide a live image of what is happening on the ground, because you are in this closed environment, in the air, in an aircraft at 12,000 meters for many, many hours and it is vital to have a connection with your team, with the ground", says Dobrovolschi. Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan declared on TVR 1 on Tuesday that the lack of money in the capital's budget is the result of an unbalanced distribution of revenues between the General City Hall and the district mayoralties, an old problem that has become more pronounced in recent years. "Bucharest has a special situation that differs from all other localities. Because it is the General City Hall with some responsibilities and the district mayoralties with other responsibilities. There has always been a dispute between the General City Hall and the district ones," the head of government explained on TVR 1. Ilie Bolojan showed that, over time, the balance of political forces has influenced the way in which tax revenues have been divided. "When the general mayor was strong, he was in a good relationship with the government, the shares distributed from the revenues were higher. When the district mayors were stronger, higher shares went to the districts," the prime minister said. According to him, the current situation has led to a sharp underfunding of the General City Hall. "Today, after 10 years, we have reached a situation in which the General City Hall is decapitalized, when you only have 40% of the amounts from taxes, and not 50%, as it was a few years ago," Bolojan said. He stressed that the impact is major on the functioning of the Capital, mentioning the accumulated debts. "That means 1 billion and that is just the STB debt to the Ministry of Finance," he added. In this context, Ilie Bolojan stated that a reform of the way financial resources are allocated in Bucharest is necessary. "Here, a reallocation of taxes in Bucharest must be made," said the prime minister. Referring to the referendum initiated by the general mayor Nicușor Dan, Bolojan showed that this was a justified approach. "The fact that Nicușor Dan held that referendum was a measure to respond, through a popular vote, to a need for underfinancing," he stressed. Putting the result of the referendum organized in Bucharest into practice will involve difficult decisions in the budget construction process and will generate dissatisfaction at the political level, warned Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan. The Head of Government stated that there is no simple solution that would satisfy all parties involved, given that the redistribution of funds will directly affect the budgets of local authorities. "It will be difficult to find a magic formula that would please everyone in the budget. There will be a decrease in amounts that will be transferred to local authorities, which will create transpolitical dissatisfaction," said Ilie Bolojan. The Prime Minister stressed that the Executive must take into account the vote expressed by Bucharest residents and correct the financial imbalances between the City Hall of the Capital and the district mayors. "We must proceed as correctly as possible, so as to balance things in Bucharest and respect the will of the Bucharest residents, so that the Bucharest City Hall is not a bankrupt entity without balancing the budgets", he specified. At the same time, Ilie Bolojan conveyed that local administrations also have the responsibility to adjust their expenses and identify savings. "They must come up with some proactive approaches in order to make the savings they can and come up with some formulas so that the administration, this year, functions better in Romania", the prime minister also declared. The referendum organized in the Capital aimed at reorganizing the financial relationship between the General City Hall and the sector city halls, and the Government is to include these adjustments in the budget construction, in a context marked by financial pressures and budgetary constraints at the national level. The Mayor of the Capital, Ciprian Ciucu, announced on Tuesday, after receiving only 317 million lei from the Government, until the PMB budget is voted on, most likely in March, that at the beginning of this year, the City Hall of the Capital "does not even have money to cross the street". The Mayor General said that restructuring, mergers, spending cuts will follow and that in March he will already come up with a first package of reforms. According to an AUR press release, Maia Sandu motivated her statement by saying that “we see what is happening around. Three AUR MEPs have officially notified the European Commission and the European Council of the lack of the legal mandate necessary for the signing of the EU-Mercosur agreement, announced for Saturday in Paraguay, according to News.ro. The three AUR MEPs are Georgiana Teodorescu, Adrian Axinia and Gheorghe Piperea. "According to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, the signing of an international agreement of such magnitude cannot take place without a formal decision of the Council of the European Union, adopted in a legally convened meeting or through a completed written procedure, in which the ministers of the member states express their vote and political mandate. A simple meeting of COREPER II cannot substitute this mandatory stage, as COREPER has an exclusively technical and preparatory role, without decision-making competence," an AUR press release states. According to AUR MEPs, in the absence of a decision by the EU Council, Ursula von der Leyen does not have the legal right to sign the Mercosur agreement, and such an action would represent a serious violation of European procedures and the treaties in force. The AUR MEPs mention that, "if an emergency meeting of the EU Council were to be convened before the announced trip to Paraguay, a minister with direct competence, namely the Minister of Economy or the Minister of Agriculture, could sign on behalf of Romania. Such a meeting would make visible, for the first time, how a USR minister or a PSD minister actually votes on an agreement that seriously affects Romanian farmers and the national economy. AUR believes that this is the moment of truth: Romanians must know with what mandate, on whose behalf and in whose interest the representatives of the Romanian government vote for an international agreement with a major economic, social and agricultural impact. The AUR MEPs warn that any circumvention of the EU Council and the ministers of the member states undermines democratic control, institutional legality and decision-making sovereignty of the states, and the signing of the Mercosur agreement under these conditions risks being legally challenged. The Alliance for the Unity of Romanians will continue all the political and institutional steps necessary to defend the interests of farmers Romanians, the national economy and strict compliance with European treaties", the statement also states. We recall that the President of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen, will sign the trade agreement with Mercosur on Saturday in Asuncion, the capital of Paraguay, Brussels announced on Sunday. The Commission's spokesman, Thomas Regnier, confirmed Von der Leyen's travel plans. She will be accompanied by the President of the European Council, Antonio Costa, his office confirmed. Deputy Prime Minister Oana Gheorghiu detailed, live on Digi24, the measures taken to reduce the losses recorded by state-owned companies in Romania. "It is a situation based on the financial data of 2024. There are many state-owned companies that are either operating at a loss, some are inactive, and others are bankrupt. What is different or what we are trying to do differently from now on, especially since we have a new law that allows us to make changes to the level at which state-owned companies are managed, is precisely the selection of these boards of directors according to OECD procedures and according to our assumptions in the PNRR. In fact and by law, the reform of a state-owned company consists of the quality of the board of directors. Deputy Prime Minister Oana Gheorghiu said on Sunday that what the Government intends to do is to clean up the state's property policy. She mentioned that there are around 185 companies that are completely inactive, they no longer have financial statements and the losses accumulated throughout the year and at the level of 2024, are somewhere around 14 billion lei. "This first list, which contains 22 companies that come from the energy, transport and Ministry of Economy sectors, represents a pilot project that we are doing in the new flow designed with members of the Government and together with AMEPIP. She mentioned that these 22 companies enter this flow in which we are doing a serious analysis of the figures. "It's not enough to look at a company and see that it has losses. We have to look at where they come from, why they come, what is their cause, is there an objective cause, it comes only from bad governance, it comes from reasons that are not necessarily related to the company," said Gheorghiu, adding that AMEPIP evaluates these companies. According to the deputy prime minister, several of these companies are already bankrupt or in some form of liquidation. "We have to see why they can't be closed down faster, because we have been left with corpses like these on the list for years and we are dragging them after us," she explained. "What we propose is to clean up, to look at companies as objectively as possible, to clean up the state's property policy. The state must decide what to do next. The state must not be an owner for the sake of having this quality, but must be an owner in the public interest, to be a shareholder where it is truly relevant, where it brings a long-term benefit to citizens", Oana Gheorghiu also explained. According to Oana Gheorghiu, from the global analysis of what she received from the Ministry of Finance, there are around 185 companies that are completely inactive, they no longer have financial statements, and they only exist because they have not been closed at the Trade Register, so they have not effectively closed. "That's what we need to do, clean them up, close them down. They no longer have assets, they no longer have employees, some of them are just some remaining buildings and we need to see what we do with these things", she said. Oana Gheorghiu mentioned that others are loss-making companies. "We need to look at where these losses come from, whether these companies are truly viable or not, whether they need to be closed or recapitalized. There are 230 central companies, these are the most important and the ones with the highest figures, they are the companies that also provide public services," Gheorghiu mentioned. She referred to Metrorex, which she said is a company that we need everywhere in the world, the metro runs on state subsidies, it cannot be self-financed, but, again, this subsidy must be thought of in a certain way and Metrorex's activity must be made more efficient. "We have the company Tarom on the list, with which the Romanian state must make a decision, what it will do. It is a company that has been struggling with losses for many years, which operates in a very competitive market, but which I believe must reach a level of recovery of activity, either independently, through good governance, by changing the way this company is governed, or, why not, through a partnership. But all these things will come out of the analysis", Gheorghiu pointed out. The Deputy Prime Minister also stated that over 1,200 companies are local companies, which belong to County Councils and city halls. "There are a lot of them. I looked a little at what is happening in other countries, similar to us. I think Poland has between 300 and 400 state-owned companies, as do other countries. Everyone has cleaned up in this area, because once a company has losses, it means a deficit in the state budget. In the long term, this means, in practice, that we all pay for these losses. And then we have to see what is worth keeping, what makes sense to keep, what is absolutely necessary, what are the strategic areas in which the Romanian state must remain", she said. Gheorghiu stressed that it is clear that in the energy sector the state has an important role and that in the defense industry the state must be the main actor. "There are probably other areas that will result from the long-term strategy. Yes, otherwise, there are things that the state must give up or work in a partnership that ensures the efficiency we need", she said. Asked about the privatization option for some companies like TAROM, Oana Gheorghiu said that "privatization can mean listing on the stock exchange or a public-private partnership that would bring you exactly this area of good governance and the area of efficiency and to better use the assets you have. "Privatization can also mean a sale, if this emerges from the analysis, that it would be the best solution. And I think we need to think about this privatization, not about that phrase that we are selling our country, that we are fighting with this and have fought over time, but we think about how we use what we have better. Because at this moment, as the figures show, we have things, but that we do not use for our benefit, but we keep creating losses that actually mean costs for every citizen. But it is difficult to pronounce before doing an analysis", the deputy prime minister pointed out. Asked what the state's losses are with these companies, Oana Gheorghiu said: "The losses accumulated throughout the year and at the level of 2024, we look at the figures, because we have them from the Ministry of Finance, they were somewhere around 14 billion lei. So they are not just the losses from 2024, but they are all the losses that the companies behind come with". According to Oana Gheorghiu, some companies have negative capital and this means that the losses they have accumulated are greater than the equity they hold. "These are very high-risk companies. The United States of America marks a quarter of a millennium of existence as a nation built on fundamental values such as freedom, sovereignty, faith, democracy and freedom of expression – values that have decisively influenced the evolution of the modern world and which remain essential for the future of Europe and Romania", AUR states in a statement. "Under the leadership of President Donald Trump, considered in 2026 the most important political leader at a global level, American influence has been felt both on the international stage and in the relationship with the European Union. The political, strategic and economic decisions of the American administration have had a direct impact on the geopolitical direction of Europe, on the security of the continent and on the defense of democratic values in an increasingly unstable international context", explain the representatives of AUR. In the opinion of AUR, America is the "guarantor of freedoms in Europe". "According to the National Security Strategy of the United States of America, the USA explicitly assumes the role of the main defender of political freedoms, democracy and freedom of expression in Europe, at a time when these fundamental rights are increasingly under pressure. In this context, Romania's relationship with the United States is not only strategic, but essential for maintaining political pluralism, freedom of opinion and national sovereignty", considers AUR. They believe that it is necessary to declare 2026 as the "Year of America in Romania", because Romania and the United States were linked by a solid strategic partnership, with vital political, military, economic and cultural dimensions, the US was the main guarantor of Romania's security within NATO and a key ally in the Black Sea region, and "America must once again become Romania's strategic partner in security matters, and any major decision adopted by Bucharest in this context - including regarding developments in Ukraine - must be consulted first with Washington". "Declaring 2026 as the 'Year of America in Romania' would allow: strengthening the Romanian-American strategic relationship; organizing cultural, educational and academic events dedicated to American history and values; promoting economic cooperation and American investments in Romania; reaffirming Romania's commitment to the free world, freedom of expression and authentic democracy; strengthening ties between Romanian and American societies", states AUR. AUR believes that "Romania must be an active part of this historic moment and send a clear message of respect and friendship towards the American nation and the American people." "At the same time, regardless of the decision of the Romanian state authorities, the Alliance for the Unification of Romanians publicly announces that: AUR will declare the year 2026 as the 'Year of the USA in Romania' and will act accordingly. AUR will organize, support and promote throughout 2026: conferences and public debates; cultural and commemorative events; educational initiatives dedicated to young people; public diplomacy actions and Romanian-American dialogue. For AUR, friendship with the United States of America is strategic and based on values, not on political conformism or external ideological directives. The year 2026 must be a year of freedom, sovereignty and alliances based on real values. AUR will remain consistent with this vision and will act firmly so that Romania's relationship with the United States of America is clear, honest and strong, in Romania's national interest", concludes AUR in the press release. The Head of the Executive registered several mentions on the day of the announcement regarding the drafting of the law on magistrates' pensions, of a press conference in which he spoke about reshuffles, about the cumulation of pension with state salary, limitation of early retirement, turnover tax. Minister of Energy Bogdan Ivan maintains his 4th place in the top of visibility of Government members, followed by Minister of Finance Alexandru Nazare, who moves up from 7th place, especially in the context of the statements regarding the budget rectification, but also those regarding the risks regarding the deficit, given that payments in the last two months of the year are traditionally high. Foreign Minister Oana Ţoiu, the 5th place holder in October, drops to 10th place. Special pensions have returned to public attention after some CCR judges did everything possible to prevent the law for which the Bologna Government assumed responsibility from being examined. The trial in which there should have been a verdict was still passed. Ultimately, four of the nine judges did not even show up for the hearing in which the subject should have been discussed. On this occasion, a new hearing was set for mid-January. Beyond the postponement of the postponement, Romania is facing a bigger problem due to the situation created. The elimination of special pensions is a milestone in the PNRR. Digi24.ro explains below the route of this milestone and how much money our country risks losing due to its failure to meet it. The National Recovery and Resilience Plan is a European Union mechanism designed to help countries in the community bloc overcome the crisis that has come to the continent due to the COVID pandemic. Our country has obtained among the largest sums at the community level, in a total amount of almost 30 billion euros, a good part of which is non-repayable. That is, our country receives "free money from the EU" that should be pumped into the economy. However, in order to take possession of this money, Bucharest has committed to initiating and implementing a series of reforms, including that of special pensions. The subject of the inequities created by these pensions has been extremely present on the public agenda in recent years. The subject of special pensions has been widely exploited as "political ammunition". Without wanting to, one of the most visible leaders of the National Liberal Party became the subject of memes on social networks because of a promise made in a press conference in which he was more than enthusiastic and committed to an approach that it was obvious he could not respect. "It is mandatory for the PNL that in the first 30 days since we came to power we eliminate special pensions. You cannot have a pension without having contributions. Special pensions cost us 1.7 billion euros every year. When someone has a pension of 300, 450 million and is also employed by the state, these 80% are employed in ministries, national companies and retired at 45, 46 years old and also have a salary from the public budget. This is one of the big issues that must be resolved", declared Rareş Bogdan back in 2019. The Orban government, which came to power after the dismissal of the one led by Viorica Dăncilă, set out to fulfill the promise made by Rareş Bogdan, only it was not to be. The law was "slammed at the CCR". In the meantime, the electoral promise has turned into a mandatory milestone within the PNRR. Simply put, in order to receive "free money", Romania must eliminate special pensions, which, beyond being a reason for social discontent, also represent an important source of expenditure within the Ministry of Labor budget. The politician explained at the time: "We cut them twice or three times. We cut them once on January 28, 64 days after Orban took over the government in Parliament, with an overwhelming vote. Mrs. Renate Weber, the People's Advocate, came and challenged the law at the Constitutional Court. COVID came in the meantime, but on May 10, the same year, the Constitutional Court ruled it unconstitutional and canceled the initiative. They never reached the president for promulgation. I came with a law initiated by my colleagues and taxed special pensions by 85%. The same Mrs. Renate Weber complained, filed a complaint with the Constitutional Court. The Court expressed its opinion immediately after the 2020 general elections, on December 14. It also canceled this initiative. We canceled the pensions of parliamentarians about twice. Each time they sued 840 former parliamentarians or 640. They won, this initiative was also canceled", said Rareş Bogdan. The troublesome milestone has the number 215 and it stipulates: "Entry into force of the legislative framework for reducing expenses with special pensions" (benefits and pensions established and paid on the basis of special laws). In order to meet the milestones and achieve the objectives of the proposed reforms and investments, the Ministry of Labor and Social Solidarity is in partnership with the National House of Public Pensions, and for the implementation of the milestones it benefits from the technical assistance provided by the World Bank. Within the National Recovery and Resilience Plan, as part of the "Reform of the Public Pension System", the issue of service allowances/pensions is also addressed. According to milestone 215, by the end of the fourth quarter of 2022, the necessary steps must be taken to finalize the "legislative framework for reducing expenses with special pensions". According to the PNRR, these will be reformed based on solutions aimed at correcting inequities between the beneficiaries of these pension categories and the beneficiaries of the public pension system from the point of view of contributory aspects, also taking into account the jurisprudence of the Constitutional Court. The new legislative framework will not allow the creation of new pension categories. Since service pensions regulated by professional statutes are considered contrary to the foundation of the retirement regime, the new regulation intends to introduce new criteria and concrete conditions for exercising the right to service pension, which have the effect of resizing their amount. The new resizing of the amount of service pensions will not be equivalent to the expropriation of service pension beneficiaries. The recalculation of service pensions does not amount to a restriction of a constitutional right, but is required to restrict budgetary expenditures, it was stated in an information note of the Ministry of Labor in 2021, led at the time by the social democrat Marius Budăi. Beyond resolving a situation that arouses animosity among society, failing to meet the milestone also comes with the risk of losing hundreds of millions of euros from the European Commission. After Romania kept asking for a "postponement of the postponement" from Brussels, European officials have come up with a new definitive deadline for implementing the long-awaited reform. Specifically, our country must adopt the legislation by the end of January so that the money that has now been "frozen" can still be delivered to Bucharest's accounts. In the difficult economic situation our country is in, it seems that any euro is welcome to keep things under control, especially when it comes to "free money". In this case, we are talking about 230 million euros that should have already been transferred to the accounts of the National Bank, which did not happen due to legal situations. Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan declared on October 9, after successive postponements of the decision of the Constitutional Court of Romania (CCR) on the reform of magistrates' pensions, that: "resolving magistrates' pensions is a milestone, therefore an obligation that Romania has assumed in the past years on which depends an amount of over 200 million euros that Romania has not received at the moment". The following day, the Superior Council of Magistracy (CSM) declared that the draft law on the reform of magistrates' pensions proposed by the Bolojan Government has no connection with Romania's obligations under the PNRR. In the press release sent at the time, the CSM makes a history of the adopted legislation: Thus, it is shown that with the adoption of Law no. 282/2023 – which we will call the 2023 pension reform – which substantially modified the retirement regime for magistrates, the European Commission considered milestone 215 to have been met, according to an assessment in October 2024. The 2023 law provided that magistrates can retire at the age of 60 and benefit from a service pension in the amount of 80% of the average gross salary and the bonuses received in the last 48 months of activity. In addition, it was established that the net amount of the service pension cannot be higher than 100% of the net income. It also established an additional tax of between 10% and 20% on magistrates' pensions, depending on their amount. Constitutional Court Decision no. 724/2024 derailed the 2023 magistrates' pension reform, considering it unconstitutional. Thus, the Law could no longer be applied. Taking note of this decision of the CCR, the European Commission decided, in March 2025, to consider milestone 215 as unfulfilled, so it was decided to block the 230 million euros from the PNRR. The point of view expressed by the CSM was harshly criticized by the Minister of Investments and European Projects, Dragoș Pîslaru, who claimed that "it is unacceptable for a state institution to mislead public opinion and directly contradict the reality confirmed by the European Commission". "From the Commission's perspective, the milestone regarding the pension system reform is not met, which is why the related European funds — 231 million euros — were suspended until the situation is clarified", Pîslaru emphasized. He also said that he had spoken with Céline Gauer, the coordinator of the implementation of the PNRR at the European level, who confirmed that milestone 215 will be met when the government finalizes the changes undertaken through the PNRR. "Therefore, the CSM's statements are not only unfounded, but also dangerous — they affect Romania's credibility in the relationship with the European Commission and fuel a false perception that the Romanian state does not respect the commitments undertaken," says Dragoș Pîslaru. CCR judge Dacian Dragoș claims that the PNL project regarding the sanctioning of Court judges who boycott plenary sessions would destroy the independence of the institution as it would put its members "at the mercy" of those who appointed them. In a show on Antena 3, Dacian Dragoș was invited to comment on the project initiated by MP Raluca Turcan and Senator Daniel Fenechiu, both from the PNL, which imposes sanctions on CCR judges who are absent from Court sessions, sanctions that can go as far as dismissal from office. "It seems to me that the law should not be amended because the regulation provides for disciplinary liability of judges. Other things can be done under existing laws. If they could be revoked, they would be at the mercy of those who appointed them. Only then would the Court be controlled. The independence of the Court be destroyed...", said Dacian Dragoș. Asked why the CCR has not managed to resolve the issue of special pensions for magistrates since October, Dacian Dragoș replied: "It is a law that is more difficult to analyze from many perspectives. It is still under analysis. And I have seen my colleagues act in good faith. Of course, there are different opinions. Society is also reflected in the CCR, but I am convinced that this impasse will be overcome soon. The Court is functional and can do its job. Some laws are easier to pass, others more difficult. There are exceptions of unconstitutionality that date back to 2021." Dragoș specified that "soon" there will also be a decision regarding the special pensions of magistrates. At the same time, he ruled out the possibility of a political order that influenced the positioning of some judges of the Court. Asked who is to blame for the fact that Romania will lose 230 million euros from the PNRR because the law was not promulgated, Dacian Dragoș said: "We are all to blame, Romania is to blame... From the political decision-makers... Of course, and the institutions. We cannot blame only the CCR. The pensions side has been discussed for a long time. The reforms have stagnated and it is difficult to detect who is to blame." The main measures included in the project submitted by the two liberal parliamentarians refer to: "None of the proposed measures affect the independence of the judges of the Constitutional Court in the exercise of their mandate, nor their irremovability during its term," said Turcan. The first hearing in this case took place on December 10, and the constitutional judges postponed making a decision. Later, at the meeting on 28 December, four judges, all proposed by the PSD – Gheorghe Stan, Bogdan Licu, Mihai Busuioc and Cristian Deliorga – left the meeting, so that no decision could be made. On 29 December, when the meeting resumed, the four judges who had left the room the day before did not appear at all. Subsequently, the four CCR judges sent a joint statement in which they claimed that their absence from today's meeting "did not mean a blockage of the Court's activity, but a decision related to compliance with the operating rules and the legal framework governing the activity" of the CCR. The Constitutional Court of Romania postponed again, on 16 January, for the fourth time, the ruling in the case of objections to the unconstitutionality of the Law on the service pensions of magistrates, setting a new deadline for 11 February. The judges made this decision following the request to interrupt the deliberations to study the issues forming the subject of the case and the accounting expertise submitted by the High Court of Cassation and Justice.

"Every time there are these surface-to-surface missiles within the governing coalition, the costs of Romania's loans increase. So, all these political missiles cost us in our pockets. We no longer have the time and we no longer have the economic or political space for such behaviors, so I would like there to be fewer missiles and more work," said Vlad Gheorghe, quoted by News.ro. He also commented on the presidential performance, showing that there is always room for improvement. "I believe that there is always room for improvement and I believe, again, that as far as the team is concerned, things can undoubtedly be improved, but that concerns me too. I am sure that there are always better people than me, who can do what I do better, but maybe not all the conditions were met. So yes, we can work, but this is also valid for the current team and the Victoria Palace. In general, if we were all that good, AUR would not have 46%. Asked if in 2028, Ilie Bolojan will make history or will be history, Vlad Gheorghe replied: "In 2028 we will all be history, if we don't understand that this isolationist trend, wrongly calling itself sovereignist, is growing with our own eyes. Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan signed, on January 30, a prime minister's decision designating former MEP Vlad Gheorghe as honorary advisor. "Starting with February 2, 2026, the quality of honorary advisor to the Prime Minister is granted to Mr. Vlad Dan Gheorghe.
