In the June 2024 MEP elections, he ran as an independent for a new mandate in Brussels, but without success. Vlad Gheorghe also announced his candidacy in the by-elections on December 7, 2025, for the position of general mayor of the Capital. Five days before the election, he announced his withdrawal from the race and his support for the PNL candidate, Ciprian Ciucu. Gheorghe then invoked the risk that the mayoralty would be won by Anca Alexandrescu, supported by AUR. "We all see that the extremist candidate with connections and history in the PSD has a chance to reach the Capital City Hall. The responsible thing to do is to support Mr. Ciprian Ciucu, so that Bucharest remains a bastion of democracy and does not fall into the hands of PSD extremists," Vlad Gheorghe said at the time.

The UDMR claims that "the anger and disappointment of the people are justified", referring to the increases in local taxes and fees that have taken place this year. The party led by Kelemen Hunor is now asking the coalition to reconsider the decision. "The UDMR is initiating the review of local taxes. The anger and disappointment of the people are justified. In recent weeks, we have taken advantage of every opportunity to listen to the grievances. We have been present at the protests, we have organized hearings and we want to help with all our strength", a UDMR press release states. The party led by Kelemen Hunor says that it is initiating today, "officially, alongside the prime minister, the possibility that local authorities, within the limits of the tax levels established by law, can reduce taxes until the budgets are adopted and to reintroduce tax facilities, especially for people with disabilities and for the most vulnerable families". "The government can do this through an emergency ordinance. At the same time, the UDMR has also initiated the provision, during the year, of targeted financial support for pensioners with small pensions, given the difficult period," according to the UDMR. The party claims to understand the people's requests, namely the need for predictability and fairness: "This is the role we assume both at the governmental level and in local administrations." In a meeting with citizens dissatisfied with the increase in local taxes and fees, which took place two weeks ago, after several people protested in Sfântu Gheorghe, the city's mayor, Antal Arpad, a prominent leader of the UDMR, a party close to Viktor Orban's Fidesz in Hungary, said that the protests organized on this issue were aimed at "dividing the community": "At least three forces have emerged that are trying to divide it: a political-puppet organization, an economic interest group and a political party in Hungary," the mayor said, at which point the image of Péter Magyar, the leader of the Hungarian opposition, appeared on the screen, according to hang.hu, an independent publication in Hungary. A few days later, the mayor and president of the UDMR Sfântu Gheorghe, Miklos Zoltan, announced in a press conference that they had decided, following the dissatisfaction of citizens, to reduce the level of local taxes and fees for cars and land (for legal entities) to the legal minimum. Protests regarding the increase in local taxes and fees were also held in Odorheiu Secuiesc or Miercurea Ciuc.

Senators voted, on the first day of the new parliamentary session, the law that defines “femicide” and aims to combat crimes against women. To enter into force, the bill must pass the Chamber of Deputies and be promulgated by President Nicușor Dan. The senators adopted with 97 votes “for”, one vote “against” and 7 abstentions the bill that introduces the term “femicide” into legislation for the first time. Now, the bill must also be voted on by the deputies, and then promulgated by President Nicușor Dan. The bill was submitted to Parliament on January 29 and had the largest number of supporters in the post-December history of the Romanian Parliament. It was signed by 273 senators and deputies from all parties. "We are talking about 5 femicide cases in January alone. Today, I believe that our society is very ready to have this debate for women's safety. Women do not die in Romania because we do not have laws, they die because these laws are not properly applied. 60 women were murdered in 2025. These are institutional failures," said Alina Gorghiu (PNL) from the Senate tribune on Monday. "Can a law stop femicide? I do not know. But I hope with all my heart that it will. Because for the first time Romania clearly says: 'Killing a woman because she is a woman has a name and has consequences'," said Cynthia Păun (USR) during the plenary debates. Cristina Dumitrescu, AUR senator, announced that the party will vote for the law that defines femicide "because we are a Christian party, because we value the family, because we do not want domestic violence." She said that the project also brings "overregulation" because qualified murder exists in Romanian legislation. "A crime remains a crime, regardless of whether it concerns a woman, a man or a child," added the AUR senator. Victoria Stoiciu, PSD, launched an appeal to the authorities to whom women in extreme situations have asked to apply the law: "Domestic violence is not a minor fact, it is not a simple quarrel between spouses. Domestic violence degenerates into crime." Unaffiliated senator Gheorghe Vela announced that he would abstain, although he wanted to vote "against". "I hate the hypocrisy and hypocrisy that can even encompass Parliament. In the last session, there were two bills by the Ionescus who came up with the "Woman First" law, which were rejected by the Senate. We have overregulation, we have the protection order law. What are we doing? Are we trivializing the Penal Code?" He also said that the value of life is the same, regardless of whether it is a woman or a man. Cosmina Cerva from the PACE group, Între România, repeated Gheorghe Vela's idea that acts committed against women are already regulated by the Criminal Code: "The Criminal Code regulates the aggravating factor when we are talking about acts committed against women as well. Why do we want to over-regulate when the Criminal Code is sufficient? Just to put difficulties and obstacles on those who apply these codes (…) If you think that you are making it easier for victims in criminal cases, you are mistaken, you are only making it more difficult for something that had quite good applicability in practice." In her intervention, Victoria Stoiciu explained that "the project is not limited to introducing higher penalties for crimes committed out of a desire for control, but tries to prevent them." The draft defines femicide as “the intentional killing of a woman or the death of a woman as a result of practices that cause harm to women, regardless of whether the killing or harmful practices are committed by a family member or a third party”. According to the draft, aggravating circumstances for qualified murder are introduced in the Criminal Code. Murder committed against a former spouse, cohabitant, partner or those motivated by gender, divorce, refusal of marriage or revenge are punished more harshly. Other measures included in the draft law are: The draft law also provides for obligations to protect victims of domestic violence or post-death measures for the children and heirs of the victim. In the event that there is a protection order or a provisional order that the aggressor violates, then the criminal prosecution will begin ex officio, without the need for a complaint from the victim or will continue even after the victim withdraws the complaint.

The PSD Bucharest organization announced on Saturday the proposals for the positions of president of the Social Democratic Party organizations in sectors 2, 4 and 6, following the resignations submitted by former presidents Rodica Nassar (Sector 2), Andrei Trocan (Sector 4) and Gabriel Mutu (Sector 6), Agerpres reports. Thus, the president of PSD Bucharest, Daniel Băluţă, formulated the following nominations, supported unanimously: Rareş Hopincă, the mayor of Sector 2, was nominated for the position of president of the PSD Sector 2 Organization, Alexandru Hazem Kansou, executive secretary of PSD Bucharest, was proposed to take over the leadership of PSD Sector 4 Organization and Adrian Vigheciu, deputy mayor of Bucharest Municipality, was designated to take over the presidency of PSD Sector 6 Organization. According to a press release sent by PSD Bucharest, the aforementioned proposals, in order to ensure the interim leadership of the three branches, until new elections are held in the immediate future, will be presented on Sunday, within the National Political Council, to be subject to statutory validation procedures. "The PSD Bucharest organization needs a new approach, which will allow us to put into practice the measures we want and that we must implement for the benefit of the people. We must restore Bucharest, identify the resources necessary to develop the city, but, at the same time, never forget that, beyond efficiency, cost reduction or infrastructure projects, our city is about people. Many of them, today, are having a very hard time, due to the high cost of daily living, and we have, first and foremost, a responsibility towards these people," declared Daniel Băluţă, president of PSD Bucharest, according to the aforementioned press release.

The government adopted an emergency ordinance on Friday that ensures the maintenance of the 50% reduction in local taxes and fees for the communities in the Apuseni Mountains and the Danube Delta this year, taking into account the status of disadvantaged areas. The decision comes after several mayors in the Apuseni Mountains area of Alba county announced the suspension of local tax payments, requesting the application of the fiscal facilities provided by Government Decision no. 323/1996, Alba 24.ro informs. The measure was announced on Facebook by the PNL deputy for Alba, Florin Roman, and also by Corneliu Mureșan, the president of the PSD Alba. "The Bolojan government adopted today the emergency ordinance that provides justice to the landowners in Alba, Cluj, Bihor, Hunedoara and Arad counties, which regulates the maintenance of the reduction in the level of fees for paying local taxes, taking into account the status of a disadvantaged area, along with the Danube Delta, something that has been enshrined since 1996. I promised this and I kept my word, along with the mayors in Apuseni, regardless of political color," wrote PNL deputy Florin Roman on Facebook on Friday. Contacted by HotNews.ro, deputy Florin Roman explained that "a decision given in 1996 by the Văcăroiu Government establishes a fiscal regime with 50% reductions for residents of disadvantaged areas in Apuseni and the Danube Delta that were in a sharp degree of depopulation and still are." "By introducing a 5% ceiling on local tax and fee reductions at the end of last year, these residents no longer fell within the ceiling and would have had to pay full and increased taxes. It was a double anomaly," said Florin Roman. The President of PSD Alba, Corneliu Mureșan, and Secretary of State within the General Secretariat of the Government, gave details on Facebook about the decision adopted by the Government. According to him, the new emergency ordinance provides the following: Contacted by HotNews, Corneliu Mureșan explained that the 50% reduction in local taxes and fees for residents of the Apuseni Mountains and the Danube Delta Biosphere is provided for in Government Ordinance 27/1996. "At the end of last year, package 2, which brought a series of amendments to the Fiscal Code through law 239/2025, introduces some provisions that say that local councils can still grant facilities and tax reductions. The problem arose when a few days later, GEO 78/2025 appeared, which in article 489 provides that Local Councils can grant reductions in the payment of local taxes and fees for a period of no more than 2 fiscal years and the total amount of exemptions or reductions cannot exceed more than 5% of the total revenue from local taxes collected until the day the decision was adopted, with most Councils adopting decisions by December 31, 2025," Corneliu Mureșan specified. "There are a few people who have paid the increased taxes and fees, although this legislative ambiguity has made some UATs encourage people not to pay taxes until the situation is clarified and they have filed memoranda with the Government", specified Corneliu Mureșan. "To see how much the tax has increased, if residents had a tax of 2 lei, with the reduction they paid 1 leu. This year they should have paid the 2 lei, indexed by over 70%, the minimum threshold by which local taxes have increased, plus 5.5% inflation. It is a much too steep increase for a disadvantaged area", specified Mureșan. According to him, the localities where these reductions are applied are mentioned in GD 323/1996 and 395/1996. The Government later announced on Friday that it had approved the legislative clarifications necessary for the uniform application of the 50% property tax reduction for residents of the Danube Delta Biosphere Reserve and the Apuseni Mountains. This facility applies to the payment of the tax for land related to the home, for buildings used as home (except for those used for economic activities) and for a single means of transport, at the taxpayer's choice. "For people from these localities who have already paid taxes for 2026, the amounts will be regularized as follows: either they are offset against other tax obligations or they are refunded according to the law," the Government statement said. According to the Government, the areas of the Apuseni Mountains and the Danube Delta Biosphere Reserve benefit from tax facilities because they are regions with natural and economic constraints, where the state has decided to intervene through support measures to support the population and economic activity.

Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan said on Tuesday, in an interview with RFI Romania, when asked about a possible minority government without the PSD, that he "does not rule out" such a scenario, but stressed that "it is not a working hypothesis" and that "it is desirable to have political stability". He also spoke about the attacks coming from the PSD leaders, which he said "go beyond a certain limit" and "do not help the Government's results". "It is not very comfortable to have four parties in a coalition, with complicated histories, with conflicts between them, some of which also want to play the role of the opposition within the government", said Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan, referring to the PSD. Bolojan also said that from a human point of view, it is not "very comfortable" to meet in coalition meetings with people "who behave absolutely rationally and then in statements on television stations behave completely differently". After saying that he did not want to intensify the conflicts in the coalition and that he did not want to respond in kind, Bolojan was asked if this attitude and the lack of counter-attacks did not give the impression of weakness. "You can give this feeling. Certainly, the attacks that come at a person who is in a public position can also weaken them. But if a Government does not have an authority, it cannot put its program into practice. This type of attacks that go beyond a certain limit do not help the perception of stability, nor the results of the Government", replied Prime Minister Bolojan. Asked directly if he could govern better without PSD, Ilie Bolojan explained that for political stability, for the stable majority necessary to adopt unpopular measures "you need the parties that can make this majority". "In a period of political crisis, we have already reached minority governments. I do not exclude that such things can happen, but I believe that for our country it is desirable to have political stability, to have predictable policies and responsible behavior of political parties," said the prime minister when asked about the option of a minority government. After the journalist asked him for clarification, Bolojan explained that the option of a minority government "is not a working hypothesis." "This is not desirable, it would be a borderline situation and I personally do not encourage this situation," added the prime minister. Then, he was asked about the PSD's delayed reforms: "Certainly, if we had respected the coalition protocol, the government program, we would be in a situation today where many measures that are not adopted today would have already been adopted. Many things that were adopted in a certain form would have been adopted in another form. It's not about making cuts, austerity policies, it's about responsibility policies. You can't spend what you don't have and you can't spend funds in areas that don't bring advantages to this country." Ilie Bolojan then said that regardless of whether the coalition protocol had been amended or not, "the main problem is the people who have to respect a contract. It's about responsibility and seriousness." On Monday, representatives of the ruling parties decided, in a meeting that lasted three hours, to postpone taking responsibility for the measures to reduce public administration spending, sources who participated in the discussions told HotNews. The Prime Minister was supposed to go to Parliament on January 29 to adopt measures aimed at reducing the expenses of city halls and county councils. The postponement comes in the context in which the PSD leaders who were present at the meeting did not agree that the assumption of responsibility for the administration reform and that for the economic recovery measures proposed by the Social Democrats should take place on different days. Basically, the Social Democrats want both projects to be assumed on the same day. According to HotNews information, the coalition leaders agreed on a draft of the economic recovery measures. "There are still details to be finalized and the procedural part to be completed," say HotNews sources who attended the meeting.

PSD President Sorin Grindeanu claims that even members of the PNL, the party led by Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan, do not agree with the austerity measures proposed by the Prime Minister and implemented by the Government. "It seems that around this type of austerity policy, there is still a part of the USR-ists, that they are not liberals, and that chorus of praisers from a politically unregistered area, more of an NGO area," says Grindeanu. The PSD leader was asked, Monday evening, on Romania TV, whether he agrees with his party colleagues who believe that Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan should resign, News.ro reports. Without giving a concrete answer, Grindeanu showed that not even the liberals support the measures proposed by the Prime Minister. "You know that I am a more settled person and not a fan of these, let's say, more abrupt exits (requests regarding resignation - no), but I would not look at my colleagues. Let's look at what the liberals mean and say. Because I see in the last week, at least, many liberals who have come out to contest... they are not contesting the person of Mr. Bolojan, but the measures, and there are more and more of them. It seems that around this type of austerity policy, of throwing people out, of imposing taxes and duties, of austerity, in short, there is still a part of the USR-ists left, that they are not liberals, and that chorus of praisers from a politically unregistered area, more of an NGO area. These are the ones who have remained in this area", said Sorin Grindeanu. He recalled that the PSD opposed the increase in the value added tax (VAT). "I want to tell you that today I am absolutely convinced that there was no need, and I agree with President Nicuşor Dan, that there was no need to increase VAT. (…) From the beginning, it was said that there was no need to increase VAT, but it went with the flow, if you remember. VAT does not increase, I do not go prime minister, something like that. But it is in the past, it is something that has already happened. State budget revenues were not much better than they were last year, all these things show that this increase was not justified, which many Romanians said," said Grindeanu. PSD President Sorin Grindeanu also declared on Romania TV that he would not accept that the Government assume responsibility separately for the package of measures regarding the administration and the one regarding economic recovery, and that the coalition tried to decouple the two packages of measures. "We met today in the coalition on an agenda discussed last week related to the budget, related to the discussions that took place at the Ministry of Finance on the recovery package and related to a certain calendar for simultaneously assuming the two packages, one for administration and the other for economic recovery and the calendar for approving the budget. (…) I want to tell you something very clear and I said it today in the coalition, and my point of view was also reinforced by Mr. Kelemen Hunor, I tell you that PSD is not giving up on this economic recovery package under any circumstances. (…) It is clear that Romania also needs something like this because for six or seven months we have been talking only about cuts, firing people, restructuring, VAT increases, tax increases. These things must stop and we must also deal with the other side. This economic recovery package is extremely important from our point of view and is essential if we want to "It continues with PSD within this coalition. (…) A kind of decoupling of the two packages was attempted today, but I think things were well understood – both packages must be approved at the same time," Grindeanu said, according to Agerpres.

The President of the Ilfov County Council, Hubert Thuma, is demanding "clarity" from the Government led by Ilie Bolojan when it comes to the money from the state budget that is to be transferred to local authorities for the investments that have been started. Hubert Thuma published on his Facebook account a video with Ilie Bolojan, from 2017, when he was mayor of Oradea, and said that the then Government "confiscated" the money of the City of Oradea. Hubert Thuma says that local elected officials do not want "the amounts produced in our communities" to be "confiscated" by the central budget and "we do not want less local autonomy": "As Mr. Bolojan said in 2017, when he was mayor of Oradea." Thuma published alongside this message a video with Ilie Bolojan, from 2017, when he declared: "We are forced to increase taxes for next year due to the confiscation of the money of the City of Oradea by the Romanian Government. The effect on the local budget is very large, and it is the biggest blow that has been practically dealt to local autonomy in the last 10 years". The President of the Ilfov County Council claims that in the case of the county he leads "the situation is even more complex". "The Bucharest-Ilfov region functions as a single economic and social organism, but is financed through an outdated fiscal mechanism, which has created a structural imbalance: Ilfov bears metropolitan costs (schools, nurseries, hospitals, roads, water-sewage, environment) for an accelerated population growth, confirmed even by Eurostat data at the European level, while a major part of the fiscal resource associated with the income of its residents reaches Bucharest, through the rule of collecting Income Tax at the employer's headquarters or at his workplace," Hubert Thuma wrote on Facebook. The PNL leader claims that "from our data, 127,284 Ilfov residents work in the Capital. According to the INS, the average gross salary in Bucharest is 11,928 lei, and the monthly income tax is 775 lei": "The result? An annual income tax of 1.18 billion lei is transferred to the Municipality of Bucharest by Ilfov residents working in Bucharest (tax 775 x 127,284 no. of employees x 12 months = 1,183,741,200 lei). In 2025, Ilfov should have received, according to the State Budget Law, 1.5% of the IVG allocated to the General City Hall, but in reality we received around 100 million RON", claims Thuma. He says that one solution would be the one proposed by the General Mayor of the Capital Cirpian Ciucu, namely a single metropolitan budget for the Bucharest-Ilfov region. "Until the administrative-territorial reorganization, it would be right to have a total Bucharest-Ilfov budget, and the distribution of IVG between the two entities to be done proportionally to the population. In such a model, Ilfov should receive at least 5 times more of the global income tax than in 2025", considers the elected PNL. Hubert Thuma concludes by saying that his duty to the citizens of Ilfov is "to defend their interests and that is what I am determined to do". "In addition, let it be known: Without a functional Ilfov, Bucharest will suffocate in traffic, waste and inefficiency. Maintaining the current financing framework is a political choice that favors a bankrupt administrative model in Bucharest, to the detriment of modern development in Ilfov", considers Thuma. Thuma's message comes in the context in which the PNL is trying to form a critical mass so that Ilie Bolojan loses the party's support. The leader of this anti-Bolojan group within the PNL is Hubert Thuma, Cotidianul wrote last week, citing political sources. In December, after Ciprian Ciucu won the elections for the capital's mayor, the PNL leadership replaced Thuma as coordinator of the PNL Bucharest-IIlfov with Ciucu.

few hours after Ciprian Ciucu said that Daniel Băluță "is directly responsible for the current situation of Bucharest's budget", the mayor of Sector 4 told him that "he made a reflexive gesture of blaming anyone else, only his administrative incapacity NOT". Daniel Băluță, the PSD mayor of Sector 4, responded to Ciprian Ciucu, after the mayor of the capital accused him of "knowing how to get money out of his pocket, through arbitrary political decisions, often for expensive and invented projects". "I tell the Mayor General that I prefer to finish a competition in last place, than not to tell people the TRUTH, as he does, from the position of winner", writes Daniel Băluță at the beginning of the Facebook post. He refers to the results he obtained in the elections for the Mayor of the Capital, when he finished in 3rd place, being surpassed by Anca Alexandrescu. Attached to the post is a photo of Pinocchio who has grown a nose. Daniel Băluță says that Ciprian Ciucu "made a reflex gesture of blaming anyone else, only his administrative incapacity NOT" and that "it was expected" that he would blame the heavy legacy and "accuse PSD of all possible problems". To the general mayor's accusations regarding expensive and invented projects, the mayor of Sector 4 responds by recommending him "to try to implement them and transfer them to his own portfolio, from which the results are missing". Băluță again recalls the general mayor's "laments", "reactions associated with the "cult of personality"" and "tears". "I want to specify that the heating agent circulates through the pipes of the district heating system in the Capital, not politics or the tears of the General Mayor", he writes at the end of Băluță's post. On Thursday evening, in an intervention on Euronews Romania, the general mayor of the capital, Ciprian Ciucu, declared that due to the lack of money from the City Hall of the Capital, he is considering "structural reforms, some of them difficult", such as merging or abolishing some institutions subordinate to the city hall and increasing the price of STB tickets. On Friday morning, through a press release, Daniel Băluță launched a new attack on him and "called" him "to stop complaining endlessly" and to come up with concrete solutions. The PSD mayor of Sector 4 said that he firmly condemns "the amateurism, administrative incapacity, the lack of vision that the general mayor demonstrates every day" and claimed that the increase in the price of public transport tickets and the merging or abolishing some institutions "are measures that betray despair, lack of solutions and a great injustice to the people". In response, Ciprian Ciucu said, also on Facebook, that "Daniel Băluță's populism was expected, not immediate, but it was completely predictable" and accused the PSD mayor of "being directly responsible for the current situation of Bucharest's budget."

President Nicușor Dan declared on Thursday night that he has more important battles to get involved in, listing justice and tax evasion here, than the issue related to the plagiarism accusations against PSD Justice Minister Radu Marinescu. "There are many battles to fight, that's my opinion. We had a period, the '90s-2000s, when it was a habit in universities in Romania, for some of the supervising professors, to instruct people to take from here, take from there... plagiarism. Some of these people are part of today's political elite in Romania. There is no political counterweight to this reality. I, to tell you very bluntly, there are more important battles such as justice, tax evasion, an economic project for Romania, in which I want to get involved," declared Nicușor Dan, in Brussels, in a press conference held on Thursday night, according to Agerpres. The head of state made these statements in Brussels, where he participated in the informal meeting of the European Council. On January 12, investigative journalist Emilia Șercan published an analysis in PressOne according to which at least 140 of the 247 pages of Radu Marinescu's doctoral thesis contain text copied from other authors. Radu Marinescu claimed that he had complied with all the rules that were in force at the time of writing his doctoral thesis, in 2009. Journalist Emilia Șercan, who published the evidence of plagiarism, responded and said that in reality plagiarism was also prohibited in 2009. Radu Marinescu rejected a resignation from the head of the Justice Department, and the PSD announced that they would continue to support the Minister of Justice "without reservations" and "condemn the despicable maneuver by which he was accused of plagiarism, immediately after he announced that the appointments of heads of high-ranking prosecutors' offices would not be of a political nature." The Ethics Commission of the University of Craiova has decided to analyze the doctoral thesis of the Minister of Justice, Radu Marinescu. It is not clear when the Commission will provide a final verdict. The decision can later be appealed to the National Commission for the Attestation of University Titles, Diplomas and Certificates (CNATDCU).

MEP Nicu Stefanuta sent AUR leader George Simion a message after he was filmed in Washington cutting a cake in the shape of Greenland, frosted with the flag of the United States. "Let it stick in your throat!" Stefanuta tells him, in a post viewed on social networks by over 500,000 people. In a statement to HotNews, George Simion claims Romania needs leaders who "understand it as it is, not moralizers on TV sets". "George Simion, I have a message for you. Let that cake stick in your throat! When you cut that cake, think that maybe it was Dobrogea instead of Greenland and someone was asking you for that territory", said Nicu Stefanuta in a video message in which he directly addresses George Simion. "We are part of a family and when you are part of a family, you take care of the needs of your family. If one of your family members is attacked, don't laugh at serious things. Because next time it might be your turn. So let that cake stick in your throat!", concluded Ștefănuță. The MEP's post quickly spread on social networks, reaching 305,000 views and 1,700 shares on Facebook and 230,000 views and over 1,000 shares on TikTok. In a statement to HotNews, George Simion claims that the partnership with the US is the only solid security guarantee for our country. "Sovereign, in my understanding, means a simple and clear thing: to put your country's interest first. No slogans, no hysteria, no absurd comparisons. For Romania, the strategic partnership with the United States of America represents the only real guarantee of security. This is a fact, not an opinion. The partnership with the European Union is, of course, natural and self-evident because we are part of Europe, historically, culturally and economically," said Simion. As Greenland represents a security issue for the United States, it is implicitly a subject that also concerns Romania's security, believes the AUR leader. "The whole story related to Greenland is a strategic security issue for the United States. And what concerns US security also concerns, implicitly, the security of NATO, the European Union and, therefore, Romania. Ignoring this means either naivety or bad faith. Comparing Greenland with Dobrogea is childish and denotes a total lack of understanding of geopolitical realities," argues George Simion. He argues that foreign policy should not be assimilated to image exercises, but only based on Romania's interests. "Romania needs leaders who understand the world as it is, not TV moralizers or politicians who confuse foreign policy with image exercises. Realpolitik is not done with slogans, but with lucidity, solid alliances and a clearly assumed national interest. And Romania's interest is simple: security, stability and respect. No hysteria. No propaganda. No double standards", concluded George Simion. George Simion was in the United States these days on a visit, accompanied by an AUR delegation. In a video published on X and distributed by an organization affiliated with conservatives in the US Republican Party, Simion can be seen cutting a cake in the shape of Greenland, the Danish territory that Donald Trump is trying to annex. "This is the atmosphere at a reception in Washington DC these days", says George Simion in a post on his blog. The George Simion video was originally posted by an X account named Mark Naughton, who poses as a journalist. The footage was later redistributed by the political advocacy group Republicans for National Renewal, which is affiliated with conservatives in the Republican Party and describes itself as supporting national and “America First” values.

The Mayor of Sfântu Gheorghe Municipality, Antal Arpad (UDMR) and the President of the UDMR Sfântu Gheorghe, Miklos Zoltan, announced on Thursday, in a press conference, that they decided, following the dissatisfaction of the citizens, to reduce to the legal minimum the level of local taxes and fees for cars and land (for legal entities). Initially, faced with the dissatisfaction of the people, the Mayor of Sfântu Gheorghe had blamed the situation on the leader of the opposition in Hungary, Peter Magyar. Mayor Antal Arpad said on Thursday that for the year 2026 “we had big plans”: “We considered that this could be the year with the greatest development of all time. But our duty, as community leaders, is to build the city and serve the citizens”. “There are times when the individual interest of the citizens does not coincide with the interests of the city. This is the situation with taxes. Because people pay their taxes and the advantage is with the one who receives the taxes”, explained the Mayor. Antal Arpad then referred to the protest in front of the Sfântu Gheorghe City Hall on Monday, where around 200 people gathered to protest against the increase in local taxes and fees. In addition to the protest, the mayor also organized a meeting with citizens on Tuesday. "In the last few days, as you may have noticed, we have had many meetings with citizens. We listened to them, we learned from them and their message was very clear. There are many citizens in this city for whom even the smallest additional expense represents a great burden. This year, in 2026, everyday life is more important for many citizens in this city than the development of the city. As mayor, I must understand and accept this," said Antal Arpad. The president of the UDMR Sfântu Gheorghe, deputy Miklos Zoltan, later explained that, given that the municipality's budget for 2026 has not been adopted, the Local Council decision of December 2025, by which local taxes and fees were increased, can be modified, which he proposed and will happen. "We are talking about a change in the sense of decrease, to the advantage of the taxpayer. It is legal," Miklos Zoltan specified. "In the case of hybrid cars, we should amend the CL decision in the sense that this tax should decrease to the minimum level established by the Fiscal Code. In the case of other cars, we should reduce the taxes to the maximum level, which they were at in 2025. This is also true for utility vehicles. The third proposal was that in the case of land taxes for legal entities, we should amend them in the sense of decreasing and set them at the minimum level established by the Fiscal Code. It is the lowest level among all municipalities in Transylvania," explained the deputy. "As for the building tax for legal entities, you know well that a de minimis scheme has been operating for 11-14 years, through which all taxpayers, individuals who pay building tax, benefit from the reimbursement of one third of the tax. It would be good for this scheme to operate in the future," he specified. Local authorities have appealed to people not to pay their taxes until February 2, when all the details of the changes will be clarified. Those who have paid in the meantime can request a refund, notes CovasnaMedia.ro. Since December in Sfântu Gheorghe, local taxes for individuals have not been increased by local decision, but only adjusted with the inflation rate, according to legal provisions. All local taxes, both those on housing and land, and those for means of transport, have been indexed in Sfântu Gheorghe only with last year's inflation rate, i.e. 10.4%, which is mandatory by law. "Thus, a family that has a 70 sq m apartment and a 1,400 cc car will pay a total tax of almost 400 lei next year, i.e. over 770 lei less than the maximum tax amount allowed by the Fiscal Code (1,170 lei)," the local authorities stated in a press release. In a meeting with disgruntled citizens on Tuesday, the mayor of Sfântu Gheorghe, who is from the UDMR, a party close to Viktor Orban's Fidesz in Hungary, said that the protests organized on this issue were aimed at "dividing the community": "At least three forces have emerged that are trying to divide it: a political-puppet organization, an economic interest group and a political party in Hungary," the mayor said, at which point the image of Péter Magyar, the leader of the Hungarian opposition, appeared on the screen, according to hang.hu, an independent publication in Hungary. Of the three "forces", the mayor "unmasked" one: the Tisza party, the quoted source writes. In the broadcast, participants can be clearly heard shouting that "this has nothing to do with the topic" and demanding that campaign politics be left in Hungary. However, Antal Arpád interrupted them, saying: "Yes, you have to listen to the end!" The mayor then showed people a name and a photo that he said belonged to a Tisza activist: "Do you think it's normal for a Tisza party activist, who has been living in Budapest for 22 years, to create a Facebook group in Sfântu Gheorghe in order to further inflame this mood until March 15?", Antal Arpad asked. Meanwhile, data from the Tisza database that had been hacked was displayed on the screen. Basically, the UDMR politician presented a list of supporters of an opposition party in Hungary. Approximately 200 people gathered on Monday, from 12:00, in front of the Sfântu Gheorghe City Hall, in Covasna County, to express their dissatisfaction with the increase in local taxes. The city's mayor, Antal Arpad (UDMR), came out and talked to the dissatisfied people. The protest was announced online by local activist Peter Fazakas, a former member of the County Council, according to CovasnaMedia.ro. The demonstration was peaceful, but there were also moments when the tone of the discussions became more tense, local media reports.

The former PSD Prime Minister launches an unprecedented attack on Ilie Bolojan, whom he accuses, on Facebook, of having "ordered an accounting scam" and of having "premeditated everything". Ciolacu is just one of the PSD leaders who in recent days have launched a series of attacks on the Government and the Prime Minister. On Wednesday evening, in an intervention on Antena3 CNN, Sorin Grindeanu was asked if Romanians were victims of a "scam", and the PSD President replied: "Yes, but more elaborate". In a post published on Thursday morning, former Prime Minister Marcel Ciolacu directly addresses Prime Minister Bolojan: "You cut the money of pregnant women and pensioners for nothing, you aberrantly increased taxes, destroying the private environment and when you saw that the effect was insignificant, you ordered an accounting scam to brag about how skilled you are in managing the country's money!". Ciolacu accuses that, in fact, there is no real reduction in the deficit following the fiscal measures adopted by the Bolojan Government of which the PSD is a part. "Investment expenses made including during my mandate, from the first part of 2025, were transferred from loans from the PNRR to grants and, thus, were recorded as income," claims Marcel Ciolacu, now president of the Buzău County Council. He accuses Ilie Bolojan of deceiving his governing partners, of lying to the press and the business community through "accounting tricks" and of lying when he said that the deficit was lower because of the savings made during the mandate that began in June 2025: "You premeditated everything and started this operation as early as September, while you were cynically lying to the Romanians, at all the press conferences, asking them to make sacrifices. You deceived your governing partners, you lied to the press and the business community, including on the budget adjustments based on these accounting tricks. And you continue to lie that the deficit was lower because of the "savings" made with you as prime minister. No, Bolojan's mandate only means a falling economy, inflation at 10% (double, in just a few months) and the most dramatic drop in the purchasing power of salaries and pensions in the last 25 years". Finally, the former PSD prime minister accuses Ilie Bolojan of everything he has done being "cruel and crude": "Ilie Bolojan, everything you have done is crude and cruel: you have sacrificed people, lied to institutions, manipulated figures and put the economy on the back burner just to polish your own legend. And under this veneer there is neither competence nor vision - you are just an austerity scoundrel, desperate to cover up your own failure". On Wednesday evening, in a Facebook post, Prime Minister Bolojan announced that the savings achieved in the second half of 2025 "have allowed us to reduce the budget deficit by over 1% of GDP, below the assumed target of 8.4%. He says that Romania has respected its commitments and regained credibility with investors and domestic markets. "In 2025, we reduced the deficit without reducing investments. These totaled 137.5 billion lei, representing over 7% of GDP. European funds, including those from the PNRR, recorded a high level of over-contracting, and projects were prioritized," explains Prime Minister Bolojan. "We increased budget revenues, including by increasing some taxes. These adjustments generated an economic contraction and meant additional difficulties for many Romanians," Bolojan continues. However, he says that in 2026 there is a "solid basis" for economic recovery without increasing taxes. "I know that, for now, the negative effects of the deficit reduction are being felt in everyday life. In the coming months, following the recovery measures adopted and on a healthier economic basis, Romania's economy will enter a recovery path," the prime minister added. Recently, several PSD leaders have launched a series of attacks on the Government and the prime minister. One of them is the party's president, Sorin Grindeanu. He was asked on Wednesday evening in an intervention on Antena3 CNN whether Romanians were victims of a scam. "Yes, but more elaborate. We said from the beginning, they must continue the investments. And they continued. Of course, with struggles like those that you conveyed. Sir, they must continue the investments, Anghel Saligny, for example. To give an example, where the strongest struggle was. Someone can't come with 11% and not take the PSD into account at all," Lia Olguța Vasilescu also declared. MEPs decided on Wednesday to refer the trade agreement between the EU and the Mercosur bloc (Argentina, Brazil, Uruguay and Paraguay) to the Court of Justice of the European Union. Romanian MEPs from PSD and AUR voted "for" this move, while those from PNL and UDMR voted "against". 334 MEPs voted today to send the agreement with Mercosur to the Court of Justice of the European Union for analysis. Of them, 16 are Romanians. Now, the entry into force of the agreement could be delayed by two years. All MEPs elected on the PSD and AUR lists voted "for" the legal review of the agreement, but they were joined by several elected representatives from other parties. These are: Șerban Dimitrie Sturdza and Claudiu Târziu (Conservative Action Party), Cristian Terheș (Romanian National Conservative Party), Georgiana Teodorescu (AUR), Dragoș Benea, Gheorghe Cârciu, Andi Cristea, Vasile Dîncu, Gabriela Firea, Claudiu Manda, Victor Negrescu, Ștefan Mușoiu, Dan Nica and Mihai Tudose (PSD). Nicu Ștefănuță also voted "for", as did Luis Lazarus, who entered the EP on the lists of Diana Șoșoacă's party. "The European Parliament's decision to request the CJEU to analyze whether the Mercosur Agreement complies with the European treaties was adopted with a majority of 334 votes in favor, compared to 324 votes against. The 10 votes of PSD MEPs made the difference!", PSD announced in a press release sent immediately after the vote in the European Parliament. PSD MEP Claudiu Manda wrote on Facebook that PSD does not dispute the benefits of Mercosur, "but we cannot accept that these are obtained at the expense of important sectors of activity for our country's economy". "We will continue to do everything possible to introduce firm and effective guarantees in the Agreement that ensure equal competition between European and Latin American farmers". MEP Nicu Ștefănuță, who won his mandate through an independent candidacy in Romania, is affiliated with the Green Group in the European Parliament. He explained, in a statement to HotNews, that he voted for the referral to the CJEU because the group he is part of "decided that the principle of honest cooperation was not respected, it is a legal matter, the agreement is divided into two parts, there was no legal analysis and the part of honest institutional cooperation was not respected either". "The effect of this vote is not to stop the Mercosur agreement. It applies from the moment it is signed and then it already creates effects. If the CJEU comes back and says that the agreement did not respect the steps, that the division into two types is not compliant, then it stops, which is perfectly normal if that is the case," explained Nicu Ștefănuță, who is also Vice-President of the European Parliament. He says, about the discussions in Romania about this agreement and about the vote given by the Romanian state, that "the public debate in Romania, in my opinion, was poorly prepared and hijacked by the far right." "We need trade treaties, but not so quickly, but with the participation of Parliament. Today's vote was with parliamentarians from all political groups on both sides, it cannot be said that the opinion is won by one side or the other. I hope that the legal analysis will come quickly," Nicu Ștefănuță also declared for HotNews. MEPs from PNL, USR, UDMR and PMP voted "against" the legal review by the CJEU. These are Rareș Bogdan, Daniel Buda, Gheorghe Falcă, Mircea Hava, Dan Motreanu, Siegfried Mureșan, Virgil Popescu, Adina Vălean (PNL), Lorant Vincze, Iuliu Winkler (UDMR), Dan Barna (USR), Eugen Tomac (PMP). Diana Șoșoacă, now unaffiliated, was the only Romanian MEP to abstain from the vote. In a Facebook post, PNL MEP Daniel Buda said it was "a black day for European farmers". "The decision adopted today leaves farmers in Romania and the European Union completely exposed, without any real and effective form of protection, in the event that the European Commission decides to implement the agreement with the Mercosur states", Buda added. The European Union and Mercosur signed a historic trade agreement in Asuncion, Paraguay, on Saturday, marking the end of 25 years of negotiations between the EU and the Mercosur states and the official creation of the world's largest free trade area, with over 700 million inhabitants, representing 30% of global GDP, according to AFP. The agreement was negotiated since 1999 between the European Union and the founding countries of Mercosur (Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay). Most European states recently supported it, despite the opposition of several countries, including France. This agreement eliminates customs tariffs for over 90% of trade and stimulates European exports of cars, machinery, chemicals, wines and spirits. In return, it facilitates access to the European market for meat, sugar, rice, honey and soybeans from South America. Major protests against this treaty have taken place in several EU countries, while large parts of civil society in Mercosur countries also oppose the agreement. The treaty has faced opposition from farmers and livestock breeders in several European countries, who have mobilized in strong demonstrations against its signing, in France, Poland, Ireland and Belgium. The text was approved within the EU with the support of 21 of the 27 member states. After the EU ambassadors had taken the preliminary decision on January 9 to approve the free trade agreement with the South American bloc Mercosur, the PSD announced that it did not agree with the decision for Romania to vote for the agreement. Previously, the Social Democratic Minister of Agriculture, Florin Barbu, had drawn attention several times to the fact that this agreement "will strongly affect Romanian agriculture". The PSD criticized the USR Minister of Foreign Affairs, Oana Țoiu, at the time. The Social Democrats condemned the Foreign Ministry's decision to mandate Romania's representative in COREPER to vote in favor of the EU-Mercosur trade agreement, "in the absence of clear clauses guaranteeing that Romanian farmers will be protected from imports from Latin America." Furthermore, they said that the decision to vote for the EU-Mercosur agreement "represents an act of betrayal of the interests of Romanian farmers."

Former President Traian Băsescu revealed, in a show broadcast on Sunday on Digi 24, what pension he has. Traian Băsescu was asked, on Digi 24, what pension he has, the former head of state answering that he has a pension of 11,000 lei, but that when he retired, in November 2014, he had 2,950 lei. "11,000 lei. I retired with 2,950 lei. But I retired in 2014, in November. So my pension was 2,950 lei. In the meantime, there were indexations, plus the big increase in the pension now, with the new law. I earned 6,000 lei in my pension with the new pension law. Something is in order, such a transfer of resources to the pension area", said Traian Băsescu, quoted by News.ro. He was also asked if he thought he had a large pension. "I don't think my pension is too large, it seems to me that it has suddenly increased. If there is anything ridiculous, it is that someone who was an employee, who was a ship commander, mayor of the capital, minister, president, after 44 years of service retires with 2,950 lei. That seems abnormal to me," Traian Băsescu said.

Several thousand people gathered in University Square on Thursday evening to protest against the “Vexler law” on combating extremism, in a demonstration organized by MEP Claudiu Târziu and supported by AUR, the party that Târziu was a member of until last year. The demonstrators then marched to the Government headquarters. “We need a state of Romanians, which represents Romanians, not foreign interests,” Târziu declared on stage at the demonstration. At one point, when the protesters were still in University Square, the message “March to Moscow” was projected onto one of the buildings. The demonstrators began to leave. The protesters are in front of the Government, with flags and vuvuzelas. The gendarmes confirmed to HotNews that the demonstration has authorization. In the meantime, some of the demonstrators went to the statue of Mihai Eminescu at the Athenaeum. The protesters began to arrive at Victory Square. The protesters continue their march towards the Government headquarters. At the moment they are on Magheru Boulevard. Several passers-by stopped to take pictures of them, while others were dissatisfied that they were disrupting traffic. The protesters started marching towards the Government, on Magheru Boulevard. During the demonstration in University Square, the message "March to Moscow" was projected on one of the buildings. The AUR leader announced that "a delegation will lay wreaths at the statue of Mihai Eminescu at the Athenaeum". "On the day of the great Mihai Eminescu, torn by some in the Romanian Parliament, our column will go on Magheru Boulevard and Lascăr Catargiu, but a delegation will lay wreaths at the statue of Mihai Eminescu at the Athenaeum and will join the march afterwards. Together, national unity!", declared George Simion from the stage of the demonstration in University Square. "We are going towards our main objective of this day, to the great poet Mihai Eminescu," said one of the organizers into the microphone. The crowd chanted again "Călin Georgescu president." The demonstrators are about to start the march. The leader of AUR, George Simion, is also present at the protest. In a post on Facebook, the deputy announced that the demonstrators will head towards the Government, on Magheru and Lascăr Catargiu boulevards. Actor Dan Puric is also participating in the demonstration. Claudiu Târziu claims that the Vexler law is an "anti-Romanian" law. "All the anti-Romanian laws were possible, just like this one, because of the lack of this state. What do we have to do today, noticing this? Let's take our state back, right?! Without our state, we no longer produce anything. Without our state, we no longer have sovereignty. Without our state, we can no longer hope for prosperity. We need a state of Romanians, which represents Romanians, not foreign interests," declared the MEP. MEP Claudiu Târziu, the organizer of the demonstration, also took the stage, giving a speech against the Vexler law. "The Romanian state has been replaced with an automatic robbery system," declared Claudiu Târziu. The protest in University Square has begun. Several thousand people gathered at the demonstration, with flags and vuvuzelas, including the flag of the United States. The demonstrators chant "Stop the Vexler law", but also "Călin Georgescu president", "National unity", "Freedom" and "Out, out with the thieves of the country". Around 10,000 people are expected to take part in the demonstration, says the main organizer, Claudiu Târziu, who said, in a dialogue with HotNews, that the only subject against which today's action is directed is the Vexler Law on combating extremism. "The Vexler Law, in our opinion, is a priority now from the point of view of the public reaction that we need to have. Of course, the other problems related to the way in which the PSD-PNL-USR-UDMR coalition governs also need to be combated, but we preferred to hold other events dedicated to those problems, of an economic and social nature, that the Bolojan government generates, not to mix our messages, because then no one will understand anything anymore", explained Claudiu Târziu. "There are other protests coming, but dedicated to other themes," he assured. In a Facebook post, Claudiu Târziu wrote that "there were times when poets were sentenced to heavy prison or even death for a poem. They seem to be returning." Asked what he was referring to specifically, he replied: "We know that, for example, Ioan Slavici served time in prison in the Austro-Hungarian Empire for his Romanian attitudes in the press. We also know that during communism there were poets, Christians, without any political involvement, like Traian Dorz, who were put in prison." He then spoke about the sentencing of Radu Gyr. "I saw that this association was also made. Yes, Radu Gyr was sentenced to death for a poem, not because he was a legionnaire. Be careful, because he was a legionnaire he had already been sentenced, he had served his sentence. But, in 1959, he wrote a poem: "Ridică-te, Gheorghe, Ridică-te, Ioane" (...) and he was accused of inciting legionnaire rebellion. I heard this phrase again in 1990, from Ion Iliescu, in University Square - and on this basis they sentenced him to death", declared Claudiu Târziu. "Sure, after that they commuted the sentence to 25 years in prison (ed. note: for Radu Gyr). But for a poem, yes? Which was not a legionnaire manifesto. It was not "Sfântă tinerețe legionnaire", which was a song of the legionnaires. It was a poem. It's as if Ana Blandiana had been convicted for "The Adventures of the Cat Arpagic", which, mind you, drew the wrath of the Securitate and the party and they put her on the index in the 1980s", said the leader of the Conservative Action party. He claims that the Vexler Law risks "censoring a literary work or a creator on ideological grounds". "It's a totalitarian reflex", he added. The idea expressed by Claudiu Târziu, according to which certain authors would be banned as a result of the Vexler Law, is not clearly provided for in the law adopted by Parliament in December. At the same time, last year, President Nicușor Dan attacked the law at the Constitutional Court and later sent it back to Parliament for re-examination, stating that "such a law must be very clear, so as not to leave room for interpretations and possible abuses". Bucharest Police announced that the declared purpose of today's protest is "the defense and promotion of Romanian cultural and identity values". The protest program will be as follows: "The Road Brigade will order measures to streamline traffic and prevent traffic accidents and requests drivers to drive with caution, to keep a sufficient distance to be able to brake safely, not to stop or park except in specially arranged places and to respect the signals and indications of traffic police officers", according to the Capital Police. The law adopted by Parliament for the second time in December of last year states that "distributing or making available to the public, in any way, fascist, legionary, racist and xenophobic materials constitutes a crime and is punishable by imprisonment from one to 5 years and the prohibition of certain rights", and if the act is committed through an information system, "the punishment limit is increased by half". The words "fascist and legionary" were also missing in the previous version. The law also introduces a penalty of 3 months to 3 years for people who publicly promote the cult of people "who were part of the leadership of fascist organizations." "The act of a person promoting, in public, the cult of people guilty of committing crimes of genocide, against humanity and war crimes of people who were part of the leadership of fascist, legionary, racist or xenophobic organizations, as well as the act of promoting, in public, fascist, legionary, racist or xenophobic ideas, conceptions or doctrines is punishable by imprisonment from 3 months to 3 years or a fine and the prohibition of certain rights," according to the adopted law. Previously, the law also sanctioned "the act of a person promoting, in public, the cult of persons guilty of committing crimes of genocide against humanity and war crimes, as well as the act of promoting, in public, fascist, legionary, racist or xenophobic ideas, conceptions or doctrines, within the meaning of art. 2 letter a), is punishable by imprisonment from 3 months to 3 years and the prohibition of certain rights". Another amendment is that "denying, contesting, approving, justifying or obviously minimizing, by any means, in public, the Holocaust on the territory of Romania or its effects is punishable by imprisonment from 6 months to 3 years and the prohibition of certain rights". Previously, the law also provided for the possibility of a fine, instead of a prison sentence.

Government spokesperson Ioana Dogioiu told HotNews on Wednesday that the Government "categorically" denies the Executive's intention to adopt measures such as reducing budgeted places for students or merging some universities. According to the cited sources, the measures were to target especially the university area. The information had also been previously reported by Antena 3 CNN and EduPedu.ro. Contacted by HotNews on Wednesday, Government spokesperson Ioana Dogioiu replied: "We categorically deny it." HotNews had asked Dogioiu if Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan plans for the Government to adopt a series of measures in 2026, in the field of education, the university area, in order to make more savings in the state budget and if the measures taken into account include reducing the number of budgeted positions for students and the possible merger of higher education institutions. Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan said on Tuesday on TVR 1 that almost all European countries have official planes, used to represent the state, and Romania can also have such a plane. Bolojan was asked if Romania can afford an official plane for state dignitaries, if it needs such a plane, considering the situation last week when President Nicuşor Dan was stuck in Paris for a whole day because the Spartan plane could not take off due to the weather. "Think that almost all European countries have planes that are used to represent the state. Romania can have such a plane too. All dignitaries can use it, nothing happens, it can be managed by the Ministry of Defense, by the Army, because they have to do their piloting lessons anyway, so it can have more destinations. Here it is always a decision that is related to a cost-benefit analysis. Think that if the planes that we have rented over the years for flights like this, the money had been used to take such a plane in a lease, we probably would not have come out very differently. So here, just like in a business analysis, an analysis must be made and decisions made, but coming out of an area of populism", said the prime minister, quoted by Agerpres. He mentioned that such an analysis can be made at this moment, although this is not the most important problem of the country. "Obviously, an analysis can be done. There are documents prepared, I understand, for about 10 years. When such decisions were made to buy, I don't know, one or two planes, you shouldn't buy these very large planes, but you should buy decent planes, in which you can solve both a decent cost and an aspect of representing Romania, because, indeed, that also matters in certain situations. But this is not the most important problem of our country. We have problems that concern our citizens. So, let's get through these months well, maintain stability, take care of serious things, more engine and less honking and, really, let's do what's right for our country. I think that's what Romanians expect from us," he concluded.

MP Ion Iordache, who is the president of the PNL Gorj, submitted to the Chamber of Deputies a bill "for the regulation of the authorization and control of sexual activities". The bill has the support of other colleagues from the PNL and a PSD parliamentarian and provides for the authorization of spaces where sexual services will be carried out and of the people who offer them. According to the bill, the purpose is to protect the physical and mental health and dignity of people who carry out sexual activities, prevent and combat sexual exploitation, abuse, coercion and human trafficking. Another purpose of the law is to "ensure the exercise of sexual activities under legal conditions" and "ensure a transparent fiscal framework for income obtained from activities regulated by this law". The operating agreement is to be given, if the law is voted and enters into force, by local authorities, based on several documents, the law states. "The spaces where the activities are carried out must respect minimum distances of at least 200 m from educational institutions, religious institutions or other institutions established by the decision of the local council, as a condition for issuing the operating agreement", according to the law. Sexual services will be legally offered by authorized individuals (in practice a PFA is required), and this type of activity will fall under the CAEN code 9699 - "Other activities of individuals providing personal services n.e.c.", according to the CAEN classification in force. The operating agreement for the provision of sexual services is issued by the city hall where the activity takes place and is valid for 12 months. To extend this term, a new application will have to be submitted. The documentation for issuing or extending the operating agreement must include: The law specifies that the authorized individual who provides sexual services "has the obligation to declare income and pay taxes and social contributions, according to the tax legislation in force". The suspension of the operating agreement may be decided by local authorities, if hygiene standards or other conditions imposed by law are not respected. "The authorities of the local public administration or of the sectors of the municipality of Bucharest within which the activity is carried out are obliged to carry out checks to verify compliance with the provisions of this law", according to the draft law. The checks may be periodic, with prior notice of at least 5 working days, or unannounced, in case of notifications, incidents or situations that endanger the health or safety of the beneficiaries. Authorized individuals who carry out activities "of a sexual nature" are obliged to carry out periodic medical examinations, in order to detect sexually transmitted diseases and other conditions that may endanger public health, the draft law states. "The medical examination is carried out at health units authorized by the county public health department or the municipality of Bucharest, based on a monthly schedule. The result of the examination is recorded in the medical record, which is a mandatory document for the extension or maintenance of the operating authorization. The costs related to the periodic medical examination are borne by the authorized individual", according to the previously cited source. Sex workers are required to participate, once a year, in a psychological counseling session for evaluation and support, according to the draft law. "Counseling has a preventive purpose and aims to maintain emotional balance and prevent forms of abuse or exploitation. Participation in the counseling provided for in paragraph (1) is attested by a psychological counseling certificate/certificate, attached to the medical record and is valid for 12 months", the draft law specifies. The confidentiality of the data of those who provide sexual services or those who benefit from them is also provided for in the draft law as being mandatory. “Authorized individuals are liable for contravention for failure to comply with the obligations established by this law and the methodological rules of application,” the draft law also states. The initiator of the law, PNL deputy Ion Iordache, wrote on his Facebook account that he knows that the subject of the draft law is a sensitive one, but he specifies that he chose “assumment”. “In Romania, these activities exist, but today they are carried out in the “black zone”: without sanitary control, without legal protection and under the domination of human trafficking networks. I chose regulation instead of hypocrisy,” he specifies. He says that “protecting public health and combating modern slavery can never be secondary priorities. The state has the obligation to regulate reality, not to pretend not to see it while the victims are exploited in the shadows.” "The law proposes rigorous control, not promotion of the activity: "States such as Germany, the Netherlands, Austria, Switzerland or Greece have understood that only through legality can you get people out of the hands of traffickers. In the absence of a law, the Romanian state remains a helpless spectator in the face of abuses. I thank my colleagues who understood the need for regulation and the importance of the approach by being initiators alongside me. Together we choose responsibility instead of chaos and control instead of indifference", the deputy also specified. Alongside him, the initiative is supported by PNL parliamentarians Alexandru-Ioan Andrei, Romică-Andrei Baciu, Ionel-Ovidiu Bogdan, Cristian Buican, Răzvan-Olimpiu Cadar, Adrian-Virgil Ciobanu, Dragoş-Fănică Ciobotaru, Ilie-Aurelian Cotinescu, Mihai Culeafă, Călin-Graţian Gal, Aneta Matei, Adrian Mocanu, Alexandru Popa, George Scarlat, Vetuţa Stănescu, Andrei-Ionuţ Teslariu, Călin-Petru Marian and PSD parliamentarian Augustin-Florin Hagiu.

The President of the Buzău County Council, Marcel Ciolacu, former Minister of Romania before Ilie Bolojan, is once again mocking the current Prime Minister, although they are part of two parties that form the governing coalition. Ciolacu published a message on Facebook on Friday in which he refers to a post by the current Prime Minister regarding the 2025 budget. In his Facebook message, Marcel Ciolacu attached a photo of a post made by Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan in which the Head of Government presents the conclusions of the 2025 budget. The post is titled: "The largest investments for development in the last 36 years". Ciolacu's post comes in the context in which he was Prime Minister at the time of the Parliament's adoption of the 2025 budget. And at that time, the governing coalition also included the PNL, the party led by Ilie Bolojan. "Congratulations to the Bolojan Government for the way it built the 2025 budget!
