Daniel David announced his resignation as Minister of Education on December 22, 2025. The surprise announcement coincided with the holidays. Since then, no interim leadership has been appointed at the Ministry of Education, and the Government has not made an official announcement regarding David's resignation. In this context, HotNews asked the Government, but also the Ministry of Education, who is currently leading the institution. The answer: still Daniel David. The law stipulates that after a minister submits his resignation, the Government sends the document to the president, and a decree signed by the head of state acknowledges the resignation. At the same time, until a new person is officially appointed to head the respective ministry, the prime minister proposes an interim minister to the president. For example, when Ionuț Moșteanu resigned as interim Minister of Defense, Radu Miruță was appointed, and then he was also chosen to lead the ministry with full powers. In the case of Daniel David, the Government did not make any official announcement regarding the registration of the resignation, and the President did not take note of the resignation of the Minister of Education by decree until Thursday, January 8, 2026, that is, 16 days after the announcement of the resignation. Daniel David is still Minister of Education, Government Spokesperson Ioana Dogioiu told HotNews, when asked who is currently leading the institution. Asked why an interim leadership was not appointed in the 16 days that have passed since the announcement of Daniel David's resignation, the Government Spokesperson also said that "Mr. Minister David was exercising his duties." Regarding the deadline by which the Prime Minister will make a new proposal for a minister, Ioana Dogioiu responded with a quote from Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan, who spoke on January 3, in a program on Digi24, about the situation in Education. "We are analyzing the options we have and, as I said, after a decision that the PNL, which supports this portfolio, will make, we will come up with a proposal in January," the prime minister said at the time. HotNews also contacted Daniel David. Asked if he still exercises his ministerial duties and goes to the ministry, he admitted that, at least from a legal point of view, he is still the Minister of Education. Daniel David explained that during all this time, no new projects are being started at the ministry and that "only processes related to the normal and usual functioning of the system or projects that have already started/are underway (before December 22)" are being carried out. Asked by HotNews when his mandate as Minister of Education will end, Daniel David said that this question "must be addressed to the prime minister." "I submitted my resignation on December 22 to his cabinet. Therefore, I am also waiting for the appointment of a new leadership," said Daniel David. The two people considered to replace Daniel David at the Ministry of Education are Marilen Pirtea or Luciana Antoci, as HotNews wrote, citing political sources, since the moment of Daniel David's resignation. Contacted by HotNews on Thursday, Marilen Pirtea did not give a concrete answer when asked if he had made a decision regarding taking over the position of Minister of Education. "I have not finalized the discussions," Pirtea replied. Previously, he had admitted that he had been offered the position of Minister of Education, but said that he was waiting for the holiday period to end to have a discussion with Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan. Luciana Antoci could not be contacted by HotNews for a point of view. Marilen Pirtea, a PNL deputy for the third term and honorary advisor to Prime Minister Bolojan, is the name currently being considered to take over the Ministry of Education, HotNews sources say in the context of Daniel David's resignation. Pirtea (52), rector of the West University of Timișoara since 2012, is also vice-president of the National Council of Rectors of Romania, also since 2012, and vice-president of the Danube Rectors' Conference, a network of almost 70 universities in the region, according to the description on the organization's official website. In 2016, investigative journalist Emilia Șercan wrote in PressOne that several scientific articles signed by Marilen Pirtea between 2008-2015 "present high suspicions of plagiarism". The liberal is also president of the "Universitaria" Consortium, as well as a member of the Council of the Doctoral School of Economic Sciences of the Romanian Academy, he also writes in his CV from the Chamber of Deputies. He is currently also an honorary advisor to Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan in the fields of education and research. Pirtea holds a PhD in economics and a master's and bachelor's degree in finance and banking, all from the Faculty of Economics and Business Administration of the West University of Timișoara. His CV shows that he has completed several advanced training courses at the Romanian Diplomatic Institute, including "International Security: Challenges of the 21st Century" and "Diplomacy & Intelligence". Pirtea also mentions in his CV that he is the author of several studies, including some "aiming at financial policy decisions of commercial companies, regarding investment selection, choice of financial structure, destination of profits and external financing". Another possible candidate for the post of Minister of Education is Luciana Antoci. In September, she was relieved of her position as prefect of Iași County to become a state advisor in the field of education in Prime Minister Bolojan's team. During the period 2021-2025, Antoci was the general school inspector in Iași during the period 2021-2025, according to her CV, published on the website of the Iași Prefecture. Previously, she was also the deputy general school inspector, for one year. Since 2003, she has been a teacher of Romanian Language and Literature at the "Grigore Moisil" Theoretical High School of Informatics in Iași. Luciana Antoci has a doctorate in educational sciences, obtained at the "AI Cuza" University in Iași.

Călin Georgescu, the former presidential candidate, declared on Monday that US President Donald Trump "is a man of action, who does not accept the theft of elections" and, after Venezuela, could also intervene in Europe, informs Agerpres. "I'll tell you something essential - the cancellation of the elections was not justice. There was a huge fear of the robbery committed over 36 years and the theft of minds not coming to light. And it will come to light. You see, six months ago, on a show (...) I said that the United States of America would return to the Monroe Doctrine. And today this is confirmed by the foreign policy document issued by the White House recently and by what happened in Venezuela. Because President Trump, perhaps this was not known, is a man of action and who does not accept the theft of elections and for a country to be seized by the mafia and the globalist network", Georgescu said on Monday, at a police station in Buftea, where he signed the judicial review. The former presidential candidate claims that the US intervention was not only determined by the drug problem, but also by political issues, such as election theft. "Of course, in addition, Caracas was the center of the drug mafia, but the main thesis is election theft and the globalist network that has taken over a country. Today in Venezuela, tomorrow, maybe in Western Europe, in Eastern Europe, before the sun rises," added Călin Georgescu. Georgescu's statement comes in the context in which US President Donald Trump reiterated on Sunday evening his desire for Greenland, an autonomous territory within Denmark, to come under US control. "We need Greenland from a national security point of view, and Denmark will not be able to take care of it. We will take care of Greenland in about two months (…) let's talk about Greenland in 20 days," the US president told reporters aboard Air Force One.

legislative proposal to eliminate the special pensions of mayors, deputy mayors, presidents and vice-presidents of county councils is under public consultation at the Chamber of Deputies until the end of January. The proposal, initiated by USR deputies Claudiu Năsui and Cristina Prună, provides for the repeal of the article in the ordinance on the Administrative Code that regulates these rights: "Article 210 of Emergency Ordinance no. 57/2019 on the Administrative Code, published in the Official Gazette of Romania, Part I, no. 555 of July 5, 2019, with subsequent amendments and completions, is repealed". Article 210 of OUG no. 57/2019 refers to the old-age allowance granted to mayors, deputy mayors, presidents and vice-presidents of county councils, informs Agerpres. According to it, "persons who, starting with 1992, have held the position of mayor, deputy mayor, president or vice-president of the county council and who meet the conditions of the standard retirement age, the reduced standard retirement age as provided for by the legislation on the public pension system or those provided for by other special laws are entitled, upon termination of their mandate, to a monthly old-age allowance". The old-age allowance represents the amount of money granted monthly to persons who have held the position of mayor, deputy mayor, president or vice-president of the county council. The amount of the old-age allowance is granted within the limit of three mandates, provided that the aforementioned persons have held at least one full mandate as mayor, deputy mayor, president or vice-president of the county council. Also, the amount of the old-age allowance is calculated as the product of the number of months of mandate with 0.40% of the gross monthly allowance in payment, the same article states. According to the explanatory memorandum, the legislative proposal for repeal represents "a necessary and urgent action, justified by the critical macro-financial context of Romania and the obligations assumed at European level". The initiators add that, for example, a former president of a county council would be entitled to a special pension ranging between a minimum of 6,260 lei per month and a maximum of 18,780 lei per month, almost seven times higher than the average pension in Romania, of only 2,816 lei. "The current economic situation requires the Government and Parliament to adopt immediate and decisive measures to limit public spending in order to ensure the sustainability of finances. We are faced with a budget deficit that has escalated to a level of approximately 9% of GDP, while public debt has reached over 50% of GDP. (…) Despite the fiscal emergency, so far, the political class and the governing coalition have preferred to balance the budget through austerity measures imposed on citizens, resorting to new increases in taxes and duties, instead of demonstrating a real restriction of the state's own spending. Although the repeal of the special pensions of local elected officials would not have an immediate impact in reducing current budget spending (since the right is suspended), this bill represents an essential and absolutely necessary political signal sent to the electorate. By cutting this privilege which, although not in force, is provided for by law, the political class finally demonstrates that it is indeed prepared to give up its own privileges and does not "only to place the burden of the deficit created solely on the shoulders of taxpayers. Given that this right is not active, it represents, from a technical and financial point of view, the easiest privilege to cut, thus becoming the credibility test of the commitment assumed to put the public interest above any form of sinecure", argue the initiators in the explanatory memorandum. The Senate is the decision-making chamber in the case of this project.

The Alliance for the Unity of Romanians (AUR) announced on Tuesday that only in February will the party have a clear picture of the number of MPs who will support the initiative to suspend President Nicușor Dan. AUR MP Ștefăniță Avrămescu announced that, at the moment, the initiative of the Pace – Romania First group is supported by 120 MPs. “At the moment, we are counting on 120 signatures, and we could reach approximately 140. By February, during the discussions we will have, we can collect the 155 signatures,” the MP said. He explained that meetings with the rest of the sovereigntist parties in Parliament will continue until February and that until then they will try to convince POT MPs and senators to sign the initiative. “In the coming period, we will also try to convince Mrs. Gavrilă to sign this initiative with us, as well as other MPs from the government,” Avrămescu added. Anamaria Gavrilă, the president of the POT, condemned the request to suspend President Nicușor Dan, initiated by a group of parliamentarians, for which signatures are being collected starting today. “A request from PACE is circulating for the suspension of Nicușor Dan. We will not sign it, as long as Mr. Georgescu is not allowed to run,” the deputy said on Sunday evening in a message published on Facebook. “They are trying to replace Nicușor Dan with Ilie Bolojan,” Gavrilă added. Senator Ninel Peia from the PACE – Romania First Group announced on December 21 that a group of parliamentarians intends to initiate the suspension of President Nicușor Dan, whom they accuse of interference in the functioning of the judiciary, following the head of state’s announcement regarding the organization of a referendum among magistrates. The suspension of the President of Romania is regulated by Article 95 of the Constitution, which stipulates that: "(1) In the event of committing serious acts that violate the provisions of the Constitution, the President of Romania may be suspended from office by the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate, in a joint session, with the vote of the majority of the deputies and senators, after consulting the Constitutional Court. The President may give explanations to Parliament regarding the acts imputed to him. (2) The proposal for suspension from office may be initiated by at least one third of the number of deputies and senators and shall be brought to the attention of the President without delay. (3) If the proposal for suspension from office is approved, a referendum shall be organized within 30 days at most for the dismissal of the President."

USR President Dominic Fritz submitted his application to obtain Romanian citizenship a year and six months ago. On Thursday, he will officially take the oath of Romanian citizenship. Dominic Fritz will take the oath on December 18, at 12:00, at the headquarters of the National Authority for Citizenship in Bucharest, the USR announced. Dominic Fritz, who is serving his second term as mayor of Timișoara, announced on July 4, 2024, that he had submitted his application to receive Romanian citizenship. "This is what the smile of a Romanian in the making looks like. Today I submitted my application to acquire Romanian citizenship," he wrote on Facebook at the time. Most recently, on November 13, Dominic Fritz announced that he had received a positive opinion to obtain Romanian citizenship after passing the interview test. On November 14, AUR asked the Minister of Justice, Radu Marinescu, and the leadership of the National Authority for Citizenship (ANC) for "clarifications regarding the accelerated procedure" through which the mayor of Timişoara, Dominic Fritz, obtained Romanian citizenship "in just one year, although the procedure usually takes at least two years for the average person." AUR claims, in a press release, that although the ANC says that the average duration for obtaining Romanian citizenship is over two years, Dominic Fritz "jumps the queue" and obtains it "in just one year."

Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan spoke on DigiFM on Wednesday about the justice system in Romania, a topic that has been intensely debated in society following the documentary Recorder. The Prime Minister said that from his point of view, acts of high corruption should not be subject to statute of limitations, being the first time that the Prime Minister has adopted a categorical position on this subject. "There are several problems that have been pointed out in recent days. We cannot deny that the statute of limitations on certain acts certainly generates dissatisfaction on the part of citizens and here we must certainly see how we can avoid such situations. I think that another important aspect is how the panels are formed, the way they are formed, delegations, detachments, having stable panels that issue sentences," said Ilie Bolojan. "I think it is also important to see why in identical cases at different courts you have different sentences, in order to avoid these situations and of course there are also problems related to the responsibility of magistrates, to promotion in the justice system. There are, I think, a few aspects that both as a citizen, but also institutionally, looking at what is happening, I think a perception can be drawn", continued the prime minister. Asked by journalist Florin Negruțiu if he agrees with the existence of a statute of limitations in corruption cases, Ilie Bolojan said that he does not agree in major corruption cases. "Without being a legal expert, I believe that at least in serious corruption cases there should be no statute of limitations. The fact that a trial takes a very long time, that a sentence, regardless of the sentence, is given at a very long distance from the date an act occurred, has no role from a social point of view, because the closer a sentence is given to the date it occurred, its educational role, of not doing something, the social memory retains the connection... When five years pass, seven years, you realize that people no longer know why a sentence was given," explained Bolojan. Asked whether he will make changes to the justice laws, the Prime Minister recalled that he created a working group at the Government, and in the end it will be decided whether the necessary changes will be passed procedurally, through Parliament, or by assuming the responsibility of the Government. Asked if he had considered dismissing Cătălin Predoiu from the Ministry of Internal Affairs, Ilie Bolojan said he could not criticize someone for another mandate he previously held in the government, Predoiu having previously held the position of Minister of Justice. "I encourage continuity," Bolojan said.

USR President Dominic Fritz stated, in an intervention on Digi24, that the simple motion initiated in the Senate against Environment Minister Diana Buzoianu is the result of coordination between AUR, the party initiating the motion, and PSD, despite the fact that the Social Democrats are part of the ruling coalition. "There is coordination between PSD and AUR, which disqualifies those from PSD, but also those from AUR who claim to be anti-system", declared the USR leader. In addition, Fritz believes that the motion is a way to try to divert public attention from a subject of broad interest. "It is also an attempt to distract attention from the most important issue of these days, that of justice", declared Dominic Fritz, specifying that his party demands that the Minister of Justice begin the procedure to dismiss the head of the DNA. Returning to Diana Buzoianu, Fritz claims that the Minister of the Environment acted correctly in the case of the Paltinu dam, based on the information received from the territory. On the other hand, the USR president invoked the report of the ministry's control body which showed that there was insufficient action at the local level. "Diana Buzoianu is struggling with one of the problems that caused this crisis, namely the politicization of deconcentrated areas", said Fritz, adding that the PSD has established "a system of nepotism" in local institutions. On Monday at 4:00 p.m., the Senate will debate the simple motion initiated by AUR entitled "Prahova under siege. Over 100,000 Romanians condemned to thirst and disease under the complicit gaze of the Minister of the Environment, Diana Buzoianu". According to some sources, the PSD senators will vote alongside the opposition against the USR Minister of the Environment. At the same time, in an intervention on Digi24, Senator Daniel Zamfir clearly stated that PSD "votes for the motion categorically". For the simple motion to be adopted by the Senate, the majority of senators present at the meeting must vote "for". PSD, AUR and the "PACE - Romania First" parliamentary group together have 76 of the 133 senators. Simple motions initiated by parliamentarians cannot dismiss a minister, even if they are voted for by the majority of parliamentarians. Only motions of censure, which are filed against the entire Executive, lead to the fall of the Government, once voted for by the majority of parliamentarians. The signatories of the simple motion demand the resignation of Environment Minister Diana Buzoianu, for interrupting the water supply to 13 localities in Prahova and Dâmbovița counties and 'ignoring' the situation of dams in Romania. They accuse Buzoianu of incompetence, "which led to the cessation of drinking water supply to over 100,000 inhabitants, the closure of hospitals in Prahova County, the Brazi power plant, educational institutions and public institutions."

The liberal mayor of Iași, Mihai Chirica, risks being expelled from the party after exchanging remarks with the head of the local organization, Alexandru Muraru, following controversial statements the mayor made about the documentary "Captured Justice" made by Recorder. Chirica had a nervous outburst on the WhatsApp group of PNL mayors in Iași county against the president of the county branch, according to the publication Reporter Iași, which published a series of screenshots of the discussions. On the WhatsApp group that brings together about 50 liberal mayors in Iași county, Chirica wrote several messages in which he insulted the deputy. "The beast Muraru comes out to attack me when they are forced to make peace in the homes of Romanians," wrote the mayor of Iași. He claimed that "we are starting over with all the political losers" and that "enmity divides, stupidity kills and disbelief breaks the relations between us." He continued with suburban language: "you sad paw, Muraru Alexandru (…) your right or left hand will hurt depending on the case". He claimed in messages that he knew that Muraru was in that group. "Why should we burn the country, Mr. Muraru? Shame on you, the vipers who intoxicate you and look at me, I fought hand to hand with Dragnea, Iliescu, I'm playing with you! (I know you're in the group!)". Aged 54, Mihai Chirica was elected PSD mayor in 2016, when he ran on the PSD lists. He was already interim mayor of the city, after the suspension of Gheorghe Nechita. In 2020, Chirica switched to the PNL, being re-elected mayor in 2024. According to his biography on Wikipedia, in 2017, Chirica declared his solidarity with the protesters against the Grindeanu Government, which had just issued the famous Ordinance 13 and then demanded the resignation of Justice Minister Florin Iordache. Chirica was expelled from the party in 2018. According to Libertatea, Chirica escaped two DNA files due to prescription. Alexandru Muraru is 43 years old and has been a PNL deputy for Iași since 2020, therefore, in his second term. He is the twin brother of Romania's ambassador to the US, Andrei Muraru. Both brothers were declared supporters of President Klaus Iohannis. In his messages to PNL mayors, Chirica claims that mayors are "elected by God", not just by citizens and seems to be referring to Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan, taking over an opposition narrative. "You are canceling presidential elections. You are invoking realities that I know, I know! And you are destroying other institutions! Why? There is no investment money, we know! Anyway, the party leader did nothing! But why should we kill the country?" Chirica wrote. "The messages are 100% true. They are sent on the PNL mayors' group in Iași," said party sources who wished to remain anonymous, due to the tense situation in the PNL Iași branch. Contacted by HotNews, Chirica confirmed that he wrote the messages on the group dedicated to communication between PNL mayors in Iași county. "In public, we are all very correct and modest. In private, however, mature people know that some things are said directly, manly, without detours. Yes, maybe some expressions were too strong. It happens. Anyone who served in the army knows that in politics there is no place for just ladies and sweet words. What is not said as strongly is that, for years, there has been pressure from some "hand-picked" leaders, completely disconnected from the reality of the people, to dynamite the branch from within. Equally harmful is the habit of doing laundry in public, behind other people's backs, instead of having a direct dialogue," the mayor of Iași told HotNews. "Do you have courage and dignity? Pick up the phone and talk face to face. Not with bluster, not with intrigue and whispers. Yes, words can hurt. But the reality of Romanians is much harsher and more painful," Chirica continued. Sources from the central leadership of the PNL told HotNews that Mihai Chirica must be expelled from the party: "Marginalization, total isolation and exclusion". As of this time, it is not clear when the proposal will be made in the party forums. The conflict between Muraru and Chirica, however, will most likely continue, in each trying to attract their colleagues to their side, HotNews sources claim. The mayor of Iași, Mihai Chirica, said on Friday that he did not like the documentary Recorder "Justice Captured". The liberal compared the film to the execution of the Ceaușescu wives. "I didn't even laugh, but I was so scared, because I think we have become a cursed people. Around Christmas, we always make a big fuss, from the shooting of a dictator and other misfortunes... But what is happening, it seems to me, below the national average, that is, shooting our judicial system in the head, considering it completely corrupt, seems to me the biggest stupidity that the Romanian people could do towards their own state," Chirica said, according to 7iasi.ro. Chirica claimed that after the release of the documentary Recorder, people who are truly guilty and who were convicted will come forward to say that in reality they are victims of the current justice system. In response, the leader of the party's Iași branch, Alexandru Muraru, published a long message in which he firmly distances himself from the mayor's statements, denouncing a "public offense" on Chirica's part. "They are incompatible with the values and principles of the National Liberal Party. In a moment of moral crisis for the Romanian state, we are not allowed to relativize the seriousness of the corruption phenomenon or the criminality of the communist dictatorship. Calling the 1989 Revolution and the execution of a criminal dictator a "bump" or a "misfortune" is not just a controversial opinion, it is a public offense. In a healthy public space, the mayor's statement is an alarm signal," Muraru wrote in a post on his Facebook page on Friday evening. In the opinion of the PNL Iași leader, equally serious is the idea that the investigation and critical questioning of possible abuses in the judiciary would represent a form of "suicide" for the state. Chirica responded to Muraru, also in a message published on Facebook: "I do not make personal assessments using the party logo, it is my point of view. My political and life experience teaches me that (social) peace is more valuable, sometimes, than the truth." The mayor claims that the "criminal, corrupt, finished, sold-out system" has "destroyed his peace," accusing him of being indicted by prosecutors for "facts that do not exist." "I did not steal, I did not have anyone steal for me, but I only did my duty, with sanctity, in the relationship between myself, the city, citizens and other institutions," Chirica declared. The mayor of Iași escaped in 2023 from a case in which he was accused of abuse of office, after the acts had become statute-barred. The case was sent to court by prosecutors in January 2021, for crimes committed in 2013. Chirica is currently facing another corruption trial at the Iași Court in which he is accused of intellectual forgery and complicity in abuse of office (the "Flux" case). The trial has concluded and the court is expected to rule in January 2026.

The motion of censure submitted by the PACE Group – Romania First and AUR was read in plenary on Monday, after 3:40 p.m., by Senator Ninel Peia. Except for an ironic speech by George Simion and a few outbursts, the session was mostly quiet. The text of the motion of censure, entitled “Romania is not for sale – without progressives in government,” runs for 7 pages. Through this motion, the signatories practically demand the removal of the USR from government and the removal of Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan from office. The text of the motion of censure can be read below: Not all parliamentarians were present in plenary when the motion of censure was read. The meeting started after 3:40 p.m., with 236 (some online) out of the 463 MPs present from all political parties: PNL, USR, AUR, UDMR, POT, PACE Group – Romania First. PSD MPs were late, because they had a group meeting scheduled for the same time, according to HotNews. “I’m sorry that the Prime Minister chose to read the motion alone, from home,” said George Simion, the leader of AUR, referring to the fact that no representative of the Government came to Parliament to witness the reading of the motion of censure. Not even opposition MPs listened to the reading of the motion of censure. Finally, Ninel Peia threw the “motion ball” to PSD MPs. The Parliament leadership decided in a meeting last Friday that today the motion of censure would be read in plenary. Next week, on Monday, the text of the motion of censure will be debated and then voted on. The opposition must collect 233 signatures for the motion of censure to pass, a number it does not have. In total, the four parties (PSD-PNL-USR-UDMR) that form the government have 293 MPs, to which are added 16 MPs from the group of national minorities, a group that supports the Government in Parliament. The motion of censure comes in the context in which the PSD is analyzing a possible exit from the government for next year, in the context of the results obtained by the party's candidate, Daniel Băluță, in the elections for the Capital City Hall.

After losing the race for the Capital City Hall, the Social Democrats are considering the possibility of leaving the government because "it is clear that people are voting for the opposition's messages," say sources from the party's leadership. After Sorin Grindeanu said on Sunday night that an internal analysis was needed to see why the mobilization in the sectors led by the PSD did not work, on Monday morning, sources from the PSD said that leaving the government is also being considered. According to HotNews information, the Social Democrats argue for their defeat by the fact that "it is clear that people are voting for the opposition, the opposition's message." So far, unlike other rounds of elections when a meeting of the party leadership was organized shortly after the elections, Sorin Grindeanu has not summoned the leaders for a meeting of the National Political Bureau. This analysis will most likely be done early next year, after the budget is adopted, say HotNews sources. The Social Democrats are also unhappy with the relationship with the USR, a party they would like to see removed from the governing coalition, political sources told Antena 3 CNN. On Monday morning, in a press conference, Dominic Fritz was asked about the scenario of the PSD trying to remove the USR from the government. "Yes, now the PSD is talking about this openly, including through voices like Mr. Ciolacu, and it is the PSD's right to want a different government, they must say it," replied the USR leader, Dominic Fritz. He says that the presence of the USR in the Government shows that the party leaders have the courage to make real changes, "which decouple private interests from state resources." "What is clear is that the PSD, these days, is using the USR as a kind of punching bag, it is not just to vent some negative emotions, but it is also a concrete result of the actions of our ministers, which have hit certain clientelistic interests, including those of the PSD", continued Fritz. The President of the Senate, Mircea Abrudean, close to Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan, declared, also on Monday, that "for now, I know that we are in a stable coalition, despite the results that have benefited or disadvantaged some or others at the City Hall of the Capital". Regarding the possibility that the Social Democrats will condition whether or not they remain in the coalition on the elimination of the USR, Abrudean says that Romania needs stability: "A Government supported by this strong coalition that does some good things for Romania, I believe, must continue to exist. The stronger the coalition, the more the Government will be able to restore Romania and things will end up on a normal path". He said that it would be very complicated for the Executive to complete the proposed reforms without PSD, the party with a majority in Parliament. "I don't think we want to get there at all. I repeat, I don't think it's good for Romania for any of the parties in the coalition to no longer be in this coalition. It's a signal of political instability and we don't want that," the PNL president of the Senate finally explained. The information regarding the possibility of PSD leaving the government comes in the context in which the Social Democrats' candidate, Daniel Băluță, ranked third in the race for the position of general mayor of the Capital. At a distance of over 8,000 votes compared to the candidate supported by AUR, who came in second place, Anca Alexandrescu. Sorin Grindeanu was asked on Sunday night by HotNews how he explains the fact that Daniel Băluță only won Sector 4, and the other two PSD district mayors and Vlad Popescu Piedone failed to mobilize the electorate. "It's an analysis that we will have to do in the Bucharest organization. You can say that even in Sector 4, approximately equal, he had 300 votes ahead of Ciprian. Obviously, we need to do an analysis, to see why it happened and what didn't work. In Sector 6, Ciprian in Sector 6 had about 42,000 more votes than Daniel (…) Obviously, analyses need to be done, obviously things cannot be extrapolated," the PSD leader replied.

Bucharest residents are expected to go to the polls on Sunday, December 7, to vote for the new mayor of the capital, who will have a mandate of approximately two and a half years. Polling stations will be open on Sunday, from 7:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. For local elections, citizens can vote at the polling station assigned to them according to their domicile or residence. Voting abroad is not allowed for these elections. In order to vote at their residence address, voters had to obtain proof of residence at least 60 days before the election date (until October 8). You can find out which polling station is yours on registrulelectoral.ro, after filling out the form with your CNP and last name. Afterwards, you will be directed to the page where your assigned polling station will be indicated. The site collects geolocation data so that it can provide directions to the polling station. Citizens who have reached the age of 18 can vote where they are assigned according to their domicile or residence address, if applicable: On the supplementary lists, voters with a floating visa who have not submitted an application for registration in the Electoral Register with their residence address can vote in their locality of residence on supplementary lists or in their locality of residence, on permanent lists. They can vote in their locality of residence only if they have established their residence six months before the election date.

The meeting, convened by PSD representatives, took place on Thursday in the Economic, Industries and Services Committee of the Romanian Senate and turned into a scandal between PSD and USR lawmakers. PSD Senator Daniel Zamfir said that USR's Environment Minister, Diana Buzoianu, is a "snitch". USR members accused the entire meeting, to which representatives of several institutions responsible for the situation in Prahova and Dâmbovița were invited, of being in fact a political move. The institutions involved in the crisis in Prahova, where approximately 100,000 people have been without water for a week, were attended by the director of the Exploatare Sistem Zonal (ESZ) Prahova company, the director of the Buzău-Ialomița Basin Administration, representatives from Apele Române and Hidroelectrica. Representatives from the Ministry of Environment, DSP Prahova and even the prefect of Prahova County were also invited, but they did not attend the meeting. A post shared by HotNews.ro (@hotnews.ro) The most vocal of those present was the leader of the PSD senators, Daniel Zamfir, who has been calling for the resignation of Diana Buzoianu since the beginning of the water crisis in Dâmbovița and Prahova. During the meeting, he repeatedly asked the representatives of the institutions if they would resign, as Buzoianu said they should. They said they would not resign, because, from their point of view, they had done nothing wrong. During the meeting, there were attacks between those from the PSD and the USR. USR senators Ștefan Pălărie, Violeta Alexandru, Simona Spătaru and Irinel Darău accused that the organization of the meeting was strictly political. "It's not a meeting, Mr. Zamfir, it's your sleight of hand," Simona Spătaru said at one point. "We will do this commission regardless of the noise you make and the way you try to cover them up...", PSD Senator Zamfir also said. "Without us you have no quorum", replied Darău from USR. Part of the dialogue: USR Senator Simona Spătaru: I'm not making a fuss. Wait. PSD Senator Daniel Zamfir: Who are you stopping? You have 3 members in the commission and you came 4. Spătaru: Can I explain? Zamfir: I want to clarify something. We will do this commission regardless of the noise you make and the way you want to cover up USR Senator Irineu Darău: Mr. Zamfir, without us there is no quorum. Let's have some common sense. Zamfir: Why doesn't a secretary of state show up? A secretary of state just because he's from USR refuses to show up. A company boss, because he is from the USR and does not have the necessary skills, does not show up. Darau: Let's respect the procedure. Let's end the statutory discussions and start the meeting. If we can, Zamfir: The minister said that some people here hid information from her. Don't you want to know what information? USR Senator Viorela Alexandru – I want to be allowed to finish the sentence to the end within two minutes. USR Senator Violeta Alexandru: Diana Buzoianu is something of a monster. You say that's how we start. Zamfir: She is an extremely nice person, but she is a gossip. Simona Spătaru: Mr. Zamfir, you are heated. Zamfir: I am not heated. (…) Call for help. Spătaru: This committee, which is led by the PSD majority, did not make a procedural call for the PNL colleagues to be present. You are preventing the senators who make up this committee from being present. It is your procedure how you frame today's fuss. The entire meeting, which lasted almost three hours, was marked by attacks and ironies between the PSD and the USR. Those theoretically called upon to explain how it came to be that 100,000 people from 12 localities were left without water witnessed the acidic exchanges of remarks between the senators who together form the governing coalition. At one point, at the insistence of USR senator Ștefan Pălărie, the director of the Buzău-Ialomița Basin Administration, Marilena Stoian, admitted that the documents sent to the Ministry of Environment did not specify the risks of emptying the dam - that is, the possibility of people being left without water was not taken into account. Only the risks were sent to the Ministry of Environment in case the works had not started, Stoian said. "At the moment the work has not been carried out, we have not managed to unblock the valve. The unpredictable event was the flood. Two days before, you have no other measures to take than to mitigate the flood", said the representative of Apel Române. The director of ESZ Prahova, the water supplier, Bogdan Chițescu, said during the meeting that the institution he heads was not called to the meetings preceding the start of the works: "We were called only once, when the meeting had already started, we do not know everything that was discussed, because we were not there from the beginning of the meeting", he explained. Chițescu also said that the reserve basin, the one that could be used in such situations, is also under the administration of Apel Române, but its use is not "viable", because it needs repairs, something he claims he previously conveyed to those from Apele Române. At the end of the meeting, Daniel Zamfir said that "PSD is no longer demanding the resignation of the minister": "From now on, the responsibility lies strictly with the prime minister, who has, at this moment, all the elements on the table". "If Mr. Bolojan continues to bail out a minister who is currently deprived of any authority, this minister can no longer manage the affairs of the Ministry of Environment in any way, just as President Ghiță (ed. note: the director of Apele Române, Florin Ghiță) can no longer manage them either. Therefore, urgently, the two I mentioned, Mrs. Buzoianu and the president of the National Authority Apele Române, must urgently leave office. And, I repeat, it is no longer just the decision of the minister to resign, it is the responsibility of Prime Minister Bolojan to urgently dismiss the minister", said Daniel Zamfir.

The Mayor of Sector 6, Ciprian Ciucu, the PNL candidate in the elections for the position of general mayor of the capital, proposed, on Saturday, the organization of an electoral debate in which the first five candidates ranked in the opinion polls would participate. "Today is the first day of the electoral campaign, a short campaign. I propose a first debate with the first five candidates, as presented by the opinion polls. Such a formula has several virtues: 1. Each of the candidates can significantly influence the outcome of the elections, the first five are perceived as the main actors. 2. It covers the entire ideological spectrum well and is balanced, allowing our messages to reach the people. Let's finally talk about visions and projects," declared the PNL candidate, in a message posted on Facebook. The electoral campaign for the appointment of the new mayor general of the Capital begins on Saturday, November 22, and ends on December 6, at 7:00, Agerpres reports. 18 candidates have registered in the electoral race for the seat at the Capital City Hall, vacated by Nicuşor Dan after winning the presidential elections. An AtlasIntel poll for HotNews between November 12-14 shows that the top five choices of Bucharesters for the position of mayor general are Ciprian Ciucu – 19.2%, Daniel Băluță – 18.6%, Cătălin Drulă – 18.1%, Anca Alexandrescu – 17.9% and Ana Ciceală – 7.1%. USR candidate Cătălin Drulă also challenged his campaign opponents to an electoral debate, but he explicitly invited only the PNL and USR candidates. "I once again call on my opponents Daniel Băluță and Ciprian Ciucu to come to the debates, to openly discuss projects and what we are doing for this city and its people," Drulă wrote on Friday evening in a Facebook post.

President Nicușor Dan sent, in a message on X, a message of support for Ukraine, in line with the one sent to Kiev by other European leaders. At the same time, the Romanian president supports the need for an intense dialogue between the US and the European Union and also invokes Moldova's interests in resolving the Russian-Ukrainian war. "I am following with the greatest attention the latest developments regarding the war of the Russian Federation against Ukraine. First of all, I welcome the renewed efforts of President Donald Trump to advance towards a lasting ceasefire and towards a negotiated and sustainable peace formula. It is also a good opportunity to reaffirm that the security of Romania and the whole of Europe depends on the conditions of the future peace in Ukraine and the subsequent agreements. I join the message of the other European leaders who today assured Ukraine of their constant support," the message posted on X in English says. At the same time, Nicușor Dan supports the intensification of the dialogue between the White House and the European chancelleries, based on their common interests. "We are going through an important moment that requires maturity, vision and courage from all of us. The circumstances show more than ever the importance of an intense and honest transatlantic dialogue, in the spirit of solidarity between allies and the complementarity of interests between the EU and NATO", believes the president. I am monitoring with the greatest attention the most recent developments concerning the Russian Federation's war against Ukraine. I welcome first and foremost President Donald J. Trump's renewed efforts to advance toward a sustainable ceasefire and toward the formula of a… "It is important for me to reaffirm that we evaluate current developments from the perspective of the interests of security, stability and prosperity of the Republic of Moldova, which are of paramount importance for Romania", Nicușor Dan's message also says. An agreement prepared by the US to end the war in Ukraine would force Kiev to make painful concessions in exchange for a guaranteed peace. Specifically, the proposed 28-point agreement mainly stipulates that Ukraine will completely cede to Russia the Donbas region (composed of the eastern provinces of Donetsk and Luhansk), which together with the Crimean peninsula would be recognized de facto as Russian, including by the United States. At the same time, the territories of Donbas ceded to Russia and not currently under its control would become demilitarized buffer zones, while the Kherson and Zaporozhye provinces in the south and southeast would be divided along the current front line. Ukraine is also required to limit its armed forces, reducing its strength to a maximum of 600,000 soldiers, to give up all long-range weapons, as well as the aspiration to join NATO, a commitment to military neutrality that it would enshrine in its Constitution. In return, Ukraine could receive Western security guarantees, but without the presence of foreign troops on its territory. This plan, whose existence was initially revealed by the American publication Axios, was developed following Russian-American consultations, in particular between US President Donald Trump's special envoy, Steve Witkoff, and Russian President Vladimir Putin's special economic envoy, Kirill Dmitriev, without informing Ukraine's European supporters, and some European politicians compare the proposals to a demand for Kiev's surrender.

The Electoral Office of the Municipality of Bucharest has sent the list of candidates admitted to the December 7 elections for the position of general mayor of the Capital. BEM admitted 18 candidacy files and rejected three others. According to a press release BEM sent on Tuesday evening, of the 18 candidates, 10 are running supported by the parties to which they belong: Cătălin Drulă (USR), Ciprian Ciucu (PNL), George Burcea (POT), Daniel Băluță (PSD), Mihai Lasca (PPR), Ana Ciceală (SENS), Oana Crețu (PSDU), Rareș Lazăr (Romania in Action), Liviu-Gheorghe Florea (PNȚ Maniu-Mihalache), Gheorghe Macovei (PRM). The list of independent candidates includes Virgil-Alexandru Zidaru (Makaveli), Dănuț-Angelo Trifu, Eugen Teodorovici, Gigi Nețoiu, Vlad Gheorghe, Angela Negrotă and Constantin Tițian Filip. They are joined by Anca Alexandrescu who, although running as an independent, is supported by the "Justice for Bucharest" Alliance, made up of AUR and PNȚCD. Three candidacies were rejected, namely Dumitrică Stan, Maria Marcu and Dan-Cristian Popescu.

The Minister of National Defense, Ionuţ Moşteanu, declared on Tuesday that he opposes the 10% cut in salary spending in the national defense system, noting that the coalition agreement two weeks ago was for this sector to be exempt, and on Tuesday "discussions went towards the idea of cutting everywhere", informs Agerpres. "I opposed this idea (to cut military salary spending - no). There are discussions related to the decrease in public sector salary spending. The agreement two or three weeks ago was that the national defense system would be exempt from these measures, taking into account the realities we are facing, we have a war on the border, drones rumble next to us every week, all the countries around us invest in defense, we have committed to investing more, up to 5% of GDP. And it seems totally inappropriate, to use a diplomatic term, to touch on the motivation of the military now," Moşteanu said in Parliament. Asked if he had guarantees from coalition leaders that defense salaries would not be reduced, Moşteanu replied: "There were no guarantees, but this was the agreement." "Cătălin Predoiu and I raised the issue of these possible exceptions, related to the discussion on salary cuts in the public system. Yesterday somehow the discussions went towards the idea of cutting salary expenses by 10% everywhere, and I do not agree with that in defense," Ionuţ Moşteanu stated. He added that the defense budget must increase, noting that this year it is 2.3% of GDP and must reach 5% of GDP in 2035. "We must have a gradual increase, the need for military equipment is great (…) We cannot talk about defense cuts at this time, when drones fall every week, you saw near Dobrogea, and we have very, very many challenges. That we can optimize expenses, I agree, we can optimize in certain places, but let's do it with a scalpel, not with an axe in this case," the minister said. According to him, the coalition only talked about personnel expenses, not investments. Asked what he would do if the coalition's decision was to cut personnel expenses by 10%, including in the army, Moşteanu said: "I don't want to discuss hypothetical scenarios now." "A lot has been discussed, a lot has been written, a lot has changed in these months of governance with a coalition that is going quite complicated, but with small steps we are going in the right direction, let's see how it goes, what decision will be made. I trust that all coalition colleagues understand the reality we are facing, as a country, and they also understand the priorities," he added. Moşteanu said that personnel expenses in the army cannot be cut at this time, taking into account that the Romanian army needs more soldiers than it does now. "We cannot cut personnel expenses in the army at this time; personnel expenses include salaries, equipment, and food allowance expenses. We need to have more people, to welcome more people into the army. Every year there is a promotion that needs to be filled, we need to recruit professional soldiers. This year, also for budgetary reasons, we were very late and only started training in November. Next year, 2,000 more professional soldiers should have entered, there is the volunteer army program that we are in Parliament with," the defense minister argued. In his opinion, expenses for endowment programs cannot be reduced either. "There are installments that need to be paid on ongoing programs, there are new programs that need to be started, the SAFE program is coming. Maybe some optimizations, for example, on the investment side and here maybe we don't renovate certain barracks next year, we renovate them in two or three years, we patch them up here and there (...) We need greater and faster endowment of the army, we need correct motivation, we need people to see a perspective and that things don't change as the wind blows", Moşteanu emphasized.

The AtlasIntel poll conducted for HotNews shows an extremely close moment, with an uncertain winner for the Capital City Hall. While four candidates (Ciucu, Băluță, Drulă and Alexandrescu) are fighting shoulder to shoulder, behind them another candidate, Ana Ciceală, from SENS, is gaining ground and is credited for the first time with 7.1%. Ana Ciceală is in 5th place in the voting preferences of Bucharest residents for the Capital City Hall, with 7.1% of the votes, according to the AtlasIntel poll. Ciceală was the first candidate to announce her intention to enter the race and is supported by the SENS party, but also by another party created by a former USR member, URS.PDF. Ana Ciceală has been credited so far in all polls, conducted by CURS or Avangarde, with 3-4%. A Novel Research poll, commissioned by the PNL, placed Ciceală at 4.9%. "We only have a few thousand euros, from donations, for this campaign. All the other candidates will fill the city with billboards for them, but from our money. From public money. We don't have this money," says Ana Ciceală in a video in which she urges her supporters to donate to her campaign at Bucharest City Hall. So how did a candidate with no money and exposure end up at 7.1%? The short answers: the campaign taken to the streets to collect signatures, the support received from influencers and the direct address to an audience ignored by the other candidates. The young people who encourage Ciceală are felt in Bucharest, they are visible on the subways, at intersections. They are also extremely active on the internet. "We are at 15,000 signatures. Come and sign," Ana Ciceală told her supporters on Friday. Her team has organized "campaign marathons" in recent weeks, through which they took Bucharest by foot to collect signatures and campaign. What other strategy can you adopt when you have no money, but you need to get to talk to as many voters as possible? Ciceală met with them on the subway, in the park, in front of the apartment building. Without TV cameras, without chants. The campaign now taken to the streets by Ana Ciceală and her team proved its efficiency in 2024, in other types of elections and in a different context. In the European Parliament elections that year, the independent Nicu Ștefănuță (who left USR) managed, together with several hundred volunteers, the impossible: he obtained, as an independent, a mandate as an MEP in the European Parliament. After that success, the hundreds of volunteers who practically sent Nicu Ștefănuță through their work to represent them in Brussels united in what is today the SENS party. Content creator Silviu Faiăr, physicist Cristian Presură, activist Bogdan Burdușel, content creator Alex Zlăvog or stylist Sabina Teodora are some of the public figures who walked the streets with Ana Ciceală to collect signatures. All of these people who joined the campaign for Ana Ciceală have hundreds of thousands of followers, especially people from Generation Z. It is all the more unusual since we very rarely see public figures who associate themselves so directly with the political sphere. The central theme of the campaigns for Bucharest City Hall in recent years has been trafficking. This year is no exception. All candidates indicate trafficking as the main "enemy". When you enter the website anaciceala.ro, you find another issue at the top of the list: “housing” – a theme that goes directly to her target audience, namely young people, many of whom have arrived in Bucharest from the provinces to create a better future for themselves, but have to pay hundreds of euros for rent with minimal conditions. The second point on Ana Ciceala’s list is “mobility”, meaning traffic. Ciceala’s proposed solution? “We need more buses, more trams and more pedestrian and cycling infrastructure. Together, we will turn them into reality”. She is not talking about even more parking lots, because another problem of Bucharest is, in Ciceala’s vision, the lack of green spaces. In the 2024 parliamentary elections, the SENS party ran for the first time as a political party. Then, in Bucharest, it obtained 48,506 votes, or 5.64%. Previously, the same movement had obtained 59,300 votes (7.71%) in Bucharest in the 2024 European Parliament elections, through Nicu Ștefănuță. However, those who resided in another locality were also able to vote in Bucharest in the European Parliament elections. In the elections for the General Mayor, these people can only vote if they have a floating visa. What does 50,000 votes mean in Bucharest? In 2016, Gabriela Firea won with over 246,000 votes. In 2020, Nicușor Dan won with almost 283,000 votes, and in 2024 he obtained over 326,000. However, if the 50,000 votes that Ana Ciceală could obtain went to another candidate (Ciprian Ciucu or Cătălin Drulă, for example), he would be greatly helped. However, Ana Ciceală remains difficult to convince - even impossible to convince - to withdraw from the race in favor of another candidate, according to political sources from SENS that HotNews spoke with.

The difference between the first four candidates in the December 7 elections for Bucharest City Hall is extremely small, 1.3%, shows the survey conducted for HotNews by AtlasIntel. Compared to other studies published during this period, the AtlasIntel survey indicates another leader. There is another big surprise: a political outsider is emerging, who has grown spectacularly, probably on the votes of young people who support SENS in Bucharest, and on whom the fate of the elections may depend, even if he cannot win them. Based on the data at this time, a historic, unprecedentedly close race is announced for the Capital City Hall, according to the AtlasIntel survey. No less than four candidates are grouped in a segment of 1.3%. The first of these candidates, the one in the lead, is the liberal Ciprian Ciucu. According to the research, Ciucu is credited with 19.2% and is followed by the PSD candidate, the mayor of sector 4, Daniel Băluță, with 18.6%. This is the lowest percentage that Băluță has in a poll – the other polling houses (Curs and Avangarde) credit him with scores between 24 and 27%. In third place is the userist Cătălin Drulă, with 18.1%, while in fourth place is the candidate supported by AUR, Anca Alexandrescu, with 17.9%. The producer from Realitatea PLUS, in whose shows Călin Georgescu was a constant presence throughout the presidential elections, is running independently, supported by AUR. Practically, between the first and fourth candidates there are only 1.3%, which means that the leading platoon is within the margin of error of +-2%. Regarding Ciucu, this is the third poll that indicates the liberal as the first in voting preference. If we analyze the polls made public between August 17 and November 17, Băluță leads in 5, Ciucu in 3, Drulă in one, and Ciucu and Băluță are tied in one. Leaving the USR, Ana Ciceală (SENS Party) and Vlad Gheorghe (Drept Party) also appear in the AtlasIntel poll – the first with 7.1%, the second with – 2.6%. Ciceală is one of the surprises of the poll, belonging to the progressive left. A former councilor in the CGMB and candidate for the District 3 City Hall several times, she is credited with scores of 3, maximum 4% in the polls conducted by the other polling houses (Avangarde and CURS). A fragmentation also takes place in the sovereignist camp, where Virgil Zidaru (Makaveli), the influencer who promoted Călin Georgescu on Tik-Tok, is rated with 2.8%, and George Burcea (POT) – 0.5%. 3.5% of those who answered the questionnaire say they would vote for another candidate, 4.6% would cancel their vote, and 5.1% do not know who they would vote for. The candidates' scores in the AtlasIntel survey also show the balance of power between the strong currents on the political scene at the moment. This, given that in the last five years the Capital City Hall was won twice by the independent who founded USR - Nicușor Dan -, while in the last local elections in 2024 the PSD won three sector mayoralties (2, 3, 4), and the PNL, two (1 and 6). According to an analysis published last year by AtlasIntel, in the elections for the position of general mayor of the Capital in 2024, the AtlasIntel polls were closest to the official election result. Basically, they were at most 0.7pp outside the margin of error. Nicușor Dan's result was underestimated by AtlasIntel by 2.4pp. All other polling companies underestimated Dan's result with errors between 4.6pp and 20.4pp. The results obtained by Gabriela Firea, Cristian Popescu Piedone and Diana Iovanovici- Șoșoacă were estimated by AtlasIntel with errors of less than one percentage point. However, the polls for the presidential elections were not as close to the result. Before the November 24, 2024, then canceled election, HotNews.ro presented several opinion polls conducted by AtlasIntel. On November 22, 2024, an AtlasIntel poll showed the continued rise of Călin Georgescu, but ranked him in 5th place. However, it gave Elena Lasconi in the 2nd round, as happened in fact. Later, the head of AtlasIntel, Andrei Roman, would explain why Georgescu did not emerge as the winner in the polls. what the polls showed in the presidential elections and how far they were from the official result. CLARIFICATION: In a previous version of this text, Ana Ciceală's score of 7% was incorrectly counted at the right-wing pole. In reality, SENS is a progressive left-wing party.

Bucharest is approaching its physical and administrative limit, and Daniel Băluță, the PSD candidate for Mayor of the Capital and mayor of Sector 4, claims that the city can no longer be managed efficiently in its current form. According to him, the solution lies in expanding the capital and integrating the neighboring localities into a metropolitan area. The mayor of Sector 4 stressed that expanding infrastructure, especially public transport, is essential to meet the needs of residents. At the same time, he draws attention to the problems generated by the real estate mafia. "We can't build anymore in this city, because there's no more room. From my point of view, this city must expand. (…) We need a metropolitan area, so that all the neighboring localities can integrate unitarily into everything that Bucharest means, precisely in order to be able to urbanize them properly. (…) Speaking of the real estate mafia, we in Sector 4 have the same problem. We have a continuous fight and attacks from pseudo-developers who contest building permits and demand tens of millions of euros in compensation. We can't build anymore in this city, because there's no more room. From my point of view, the city must expand," said the mayor of Sector 4. The PSD candidate also specified the priorities for urban intervention: supporting owners to renovate buildings at seismic risk and historic monument houses, with rapid authorization procedures, without changing the surface or height. At the same time, Daniel Băluță stressed the importance of the unitary management of the Bucharest-Ilfov region and a legislative amendment: "There are two aspects, one legislative and I rely on the fact that soon the governing coalition will deal with the administrative-territorial redistribution of Romania. This Bucharest-Ilfov area is an interesting area to explore for specialists and this legislative amendment can be ratified and approved with the amendment of the Constitution." The mayor also insisted on the need for a modernized General Urban Plan (PUG), which would replace the old PUZs and allow for the rapid authorization of constructions: "The PUG must be made urgently. This PUG must enshrine my vision regarding this aspect, a reality that exists in Bucharest. (…) It is not normal for a single person to make such decisions. The people have spoken out and all subsequent acts must be related to the cancellation of the PUZs and the existence of a PUG. The speed of this bureaucratic construction that issues building permits must be modified." Article supported by PSD
