The proposal was allegedly refused by Bolojan. "We were asked to give a blatch, but we refused. Not me, not Ilie Bolojan. Both, both PSD and USR, wanted anyone from PNL to run, but not Ciucu. And Mr. Bolojan, with the verticality that we all know, told them: this is what brought us here. The games at the green table and the fact that we do not enter the competition with what we have best. And he refused", stated Ciprian Ciucu, quoted by News.ro. He also said that USR president, Dominic Fritz, accused him of blatch with PSD. "Well, how do you make a fuss if you go into an electoral alliance with them? Where is the fuss? When you go into an electoral alliance with them, it is assumed. Is that a fuss? No, the fuss is what he proposed, that Ciucu should not run. That's the fuss. That's how I understand it in Romanian, I don't know, maybe Mr. Fritz understands it differently," commented the PNL candidate. In the same show, Ciprian Ciucu also accused his USR opponent, Cătălin Drulă, of starting a negative campaign against him. "What he says bothers me. It bothers me because he knows it's not true. He knows what the truth is. It bothers me because he started a negative campaign, he knows the truth, I stopped the negative campaign against him. He doesn't do it on his own, that is, he doesn't say it, on his own, but all sorts of things are said that are not true. It bothers me, but, in the end, I hope that together we can get over this campaign and that we can look each other in the eye," Ciucu also said. Asked if he was more bothered by Cătălin Drulă's accusations or Daniel Băluţă's attacks, Ciucu said: "Obviously I'm bothered by what Cătălin Drulă says, when he's negative, because he knows the truth. That bothers me, yes. What Daniel Băluţă says...and I had a completely decent relationship with Daniel Băluţă."

President Nicușor Dan, the leaders of the PSD, PNL, USR and UDMR met with representatives of magistrates on Wednesday evening to discuss the law that will increase their retirement age and reduce the value of their pensions, but no results were reached, according to HotNews sources among the participants. "I must say that it was a welcome initiative on the part of the president, the discussions were based on arguments from both sides. The materials submitted by us, the representatives of the magistrates, still need to be analyzed, and then we will see the next steps," a representative of one of the justice institutions told HotNews, on condition of anonymity, citing that it was agreed not to make statements at the end of the meeting at Cotroceni. The representative of the Ministry of Justice who participated in the discussions, State Secretary Roxana Momeu, told HotNews that the discussions were "constructive, applied, technical": "Following the meeting at Cotroceni, I can confirm that constructive, applied, technical discussions took place. In this context, the dialogue between the state powers was strengthened. The Ministry of Justice welcomes the openness to dialogue of all participants and, at the same time, the involvement of the highest institutional level in this dialogue." The discussions ended after three hours. Both sources among magistrates and political leaders told HotNews that no results were reached. The magistrates claimed that they wanted the pension to be 65% of gross income, compared to 70% of net income, as was provided for in the Bologna Government's project that was rejected by the Constitutional Court. The magistrates' proposal was, however, rejected by political leaders, according to HotNews sources among the magistrates who participated in the discussions: "They want us to be paid less than the politicians. We don't know what will happen, but we haven't even come close to an agreement." Political leaders would agree that under the new law the transition period would be 17 years, but the pension amount would remain at 70% of net income, say political sources. At this time, at the Cotroceni Palace, the meeting between the president, the coalition leaders and the magistrates' representatives is starting. The last such meeting, which took place on August 1, lasted approximately 3 hours. In an intervention on Digi 24, Claudiu Sandu, vice-president of the Supreme Judicial Council, stated that the magistrates want the transition period to increase from 10 years, as provided for in the project that was declared unconstitutional by the Constitutional Court, to 20 years. "What the prime minister doesn't understand is that this project of his takes magistrates below the percentages that apply to other categories. We would like a transition period of between 15 and 20 years, so that a real reform in the judiciary can be achieved, human resources can be redistributed," explained Claudiu Sandu. The judges also want a higher pension. The vice-president of the Supreme Judicial Council said that they do not agree with the option of a pension equivalent to 70% of the net salary and that 65% of the gross salary would be a reasonable percentage. "This 70% of the net is taxed with 10% - income tax, 10% - CASS and reaches somewhere around 50%, which is contributory. If the Government wants to pay pensions to magistrates on a contributory basis, there is no problem, provided that it pays pensions to all magistrates on a contributory basis and to all other special categories. I think that 65% of the gross would be a reasonable percentage. I am not an economist. Now it is 55% of the gross, I said that 65% of the gross, as the military and other social categories have, we reach a reasonable percentage", declared Sandu. Kelemen Hunor, the leader of the UDMR, who is part of the coalition, participated yesterday in the discussion at Cotroceni and who will participate today as well, declared that a compromise is needed on both sides, both from the coalition and from the magistrates. He also hinted that the magistrates' proposal cannot be accepted. "Compromise means everyone gives up something. So if someone thinks that they can permanently, in the years to come, put pressure on the political class, I think they are mistaken. Yes, there were times when the political class permanently gave in. The government has the obligation, beyond respecting the separation of powers in the state, to govern fairly and this issue of balancing things that were and are distorted, is the obligation of the Parliament and the Government through legislation, dialogue with the Supreme Court, with another court and so on, but one cannot accept what is not acceptable", declared the UDMR leader before the Cotroceni meeting. Kelemen Hunor also said that it is not acceptable to have a pension higher than the net salary and that "anything can be proposed, the paper resists any proposal". Asked what will happen if even after today's dialogue a consensus is not reached with the magistrates, the UDMR leader said that, in this case, the decision will be made in coalition: "We have no other way (ed. ed. than to come up with a project regardless of the magistrates' position). We have no other way, because there is injustice, plus there is an expectation. So everyone must understand this". Although until now Prime Minister Bolojan has been quite inflexible regarding the amendment of the provisions of the law that increases the retirement age of magistrates, he is now willing to negotiate the transition period. "From the discussions I had with the prime minister, I understood that there is flexibility during the transition period, to exceed the 10 years. Regarding the quantum, I understood that there is no", said Mircea Abrudean (PNL), one of the prime minister's close associates. According to HotNews, the prime minister is also considering increasing the transition period from 10 years, as provided for in the law rejected by the CCR, to 14 or 15 years. However, Bolojan would not like to increase the pension to more than 70% of the last net salary. In the summer, Nicușor Dan went to the Government to discuss with the coalition leaders. The subject was also the reform of magistrates' pensions. At that time, the president proposed the 15-year option for the transition period, but the prime minister did not agree. PSD, on the other hand, will wait today to see what the Government's proposals are, but according to HotNews, neither Sorin Grindeanu agrees with the CSM's demands, nor with the 20-year transition period, nor with the pension amount proposed by them. Nicușor Dan was asked today, in a press conference, whether, following the meeting he had with the coalition leaders, there is flexibility from the coalition regarding the revisions of the reform. He said that it is clear that all parties agree that the reform must be finalized: "I don't want to tell you because it is a negotiation process between several actors. I am a mediator, so I cannot tell you exactly what was discussed inside. But what I think I can tell you is that there is an understanding from all parties that this matter must be closed". Romania must close this reform by November 28, the deadline imposed by the European Commission. If the reform is not adopted by then, we lose 231 million euros from the PNRR. The adoption of this new reform attempt, however, depends on the opinion of the CSM, because the CCR declared the first law unconstitutional due to the fact that the Government did not wait 30 days for the opinion. Now, for the reform to be adopted by November 28, the SCM should give the Government its approval before the 30 days expire.

If there were a major earthquake in Bucharest, the scenario would be grim. Many buildings continue to present a high seismic risk, and consolidation programs have largely remained just promises. Daniel Băluță, candidate for Mayor of the Capital for the December 7 elections, says he has a clear plan for buildings at seismic risk and that solutions must be applied without hesitation. "We have to be very honest with ourselves, such an operation involves money. (…) There are two categories of buildings: some that are the property of the Romanian state, through AFI, others that are private properties. And at the level of these buildings, some are smaller – simple residential houses, single-family homes - and others are condominiums," said the PSD candidate for Mayor, Daniel Băluță. For smaller private buildings, the candidate proposes a quick solution that they have and that does not involve money, but only cooperation. "We need to create a rapid flow of issuing construction documents, so as to stimulate investments from this point of view. For those that are abandoned and belong to the state, they clearly need to be evaluated and sold, as long as the state has not had the opportunity to invest in them for so many years. And for those that are areas, they are private property and people do not understand this, from the money it gets even from the sale of unused, abandoned land, private property of the municipality, we use money for emergency housing," added the mayor of Sector 4. Asked if the City Hall has enough emergency housing, Băluță claims that yes: The City Hall of Bucharest has emergency housing, one hundred percent it does. Including AFI, it has a lot, I cannot quantify this because I have never had access to a list of the apartments it owns and which have never been used. Including RAAPPS, I am convinced, has in its patrimony many apartments of this kind, which are not used." However, the candidate acknowledges that the number of these homes should be expanded and says that there are legal instruments that allow intervention in urgent cases: "Today we have legislation that allows us to take measures similar to expropriation when it is imperatively necessary and people do not understand that they have to leave a building with an imminent risk of collapse. We must have, to assume the quality of leadership that we have, to assume the negative things that derive from this decision, but people's lives are above all. If they do not understand this very well, it is important for all of us, those who represent the Romanian state, to protect them!". Article supported by PSD

Deputy Prime Minister Oana Gheorghiu says that the fact that she remained a founding member of the "Give Life" association does not make her incompatible with the position in the government. She is responding to Carmen Uscatu, the co-founder of the NGO, who said in an interview for HotNews that, although she suspended herself from executive roles, Gheorghiu still retains the quality of a voting member in the General Assembly of the NGO, and this is "a very big vulnerability". In a point of view transmitted on Tuesday to HotNews, Oana Gheorghiu says that she fully complies with "the legislation regarding the incompatibilities regime applicable to members of the Government". "I suspended myself from the executive position and from the Board of Directors of the Dăruiește Viață Association before taking over the position of Deputy Prime Minister, in full compliance with the provisions of Law no. 161/2003. I communicated this within the Association, before the information regarding my appointment became public, and I submitted all the necessary documents to formalize the decision and to ensure the continuity of the projects that I coordinated", Oana Gheorghiu said. She says that everything she did was after consulting with lawyers, "precisely to ensure that I respect the law and the principles of public integrity". "Currently, I only remain a founding member of the Dăruiește Viață Association, which, according to the organization's statute, implies membership in the General Assembly, not in the executive management structure. The responsibilities regarding the management of the current activity fall to the Board of Directors, of which I am no longer a part", says Oana Gheorghiu. She says that, although she is still a founding member of the association, there is no incompatibility: "My status is 100% in accordance with the law": "Romanian legislation does not impose on members of the Government the obligation to renounce their status as founding members of a non-governmental organization, there are other people in the Romanian Government who are members of non-governmental organizations. I founded this association 13 years ago and I remain proud of everything we have built together - an independent organization, supported by over 350,000 people and 8,000 companies, which has demonstrated that solidarity can change the healthcare system in Romania". Oana Gheorghiu also says that there is "no interference" between her governmental duties and the activity of the Dăruiește Viață Association "and, even more so, regarding my status as a founding member, and any statement to the contrary is false and unfounded". "I am surprised by Carmen Uscatu's statements and I hope that it is a misunderstanding of the legal framework regarding the incompatibilities regime applicable to members of the Government, and not an intention to generate pressure or confusion in the public space or an intention to remove myself from the quality of founding member of the Association. I remain open to a direct discussion, between us, as I have always done," adds Oana Gheorghiu. "Sponsors ask us questions, some donors withdraw, others stay," said Carmen Uscatu, co-founder of the "Give Life" Association, about the effect of Oana Gheorghiu's appointment as Deputy Prime Minister of Romania, in an interview with the HotNews audience. "A very high vulnerability." This is how Carmen Uscatu, co-president and co-founder of the "Give Life" Association, described the appointment of her colleague, Oana Gheorghiu, to a leadership position in the Romanian Government. Oana Gheorghiu, co-founder of the "Give Life" Association, was sworn in as deputy prime minister on October 30. Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan proposed the "Give Life" co-founder for the position of deputy prime minister left vacant after the resignation of Dragoș Anastasiu, and President Nicușor Dan signed the decree appointing her. Carmen Uscatu and Oana Gheorghiu are the co-founders of "Give Life," an association that was created in 2012. Since 2015, they have been collecting donations for the construction of the first hospital built after the Revolution in Romania. The hospital opened in April 2024, as a section of the Marie Curie Hospital in Bucharest, built with donations from over 350,000 individuals and over 8,000 companies, according to the association's website.

Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan stated on Thursday, on Antena 1, that the announcement regarding the withdrawal of some American troops from the Mihail Kogălniceanu base was postponed for two days by the authorities in Bucharest because it was agreed with the American side to first make the announcement during a briefing in the Defense Committee of the House of Representatives. Ilie Bolojan stated that he had known since Monday that the United States would withdraw some of the military personnel stationed in Romania. "This decision was initially announced, without anyone knowing. On Monday, we were notified by the military attaché of our embassy who was summoned to the Pentagon," said Bolojan. Romania's ambassador to NATO also received a similar notification from his American counterpart. Thus, it was agreed that the official announcement by the Romanian authorities would not be made before Wednesday, the day on which the American government was to send a briefing to the House of Representatives. A press conference was already prepared at the Ministry of Defense in Bucharest, but the information "leaked" a day earlier, being published in the Ukrainian press. "It was considered that when the House of Representatives committees on defense were to be briefed on Wednesday, there was a possibility that this information would leak. And then, the Ministry of Defense prepared a press conference for Wednesday, in order to announce these things. But the data leaked, let's say, the night before," Bolojan reported. Ilie Bolojan said that the United States' intentions regarding the deployment of its troops abroad had been announced since the installation of the second Trump administration, when there was talk of changing the center of gravity to the Asia-Pacific region and of the assumption of more responsibilities by the European allies in NATO. "This was established in June at the NATO summit in The Hague. In recent days, the additional American troops brought to Europe after the invasion of Ukraine have been partially reduced," added the head of government. "We did not have stable bases, but a rotation. There have been practically no rotations, but the troops of our allies are in Romania, the military bases are active and all security guarantees are in place," continued Ilie Bolojan. He announced that negotiations with the European Commission on accessing the Defense funds provided for in the SAFE program are at an advanced stage and will be completed in the second half of November. "Then a CSAT will be convened in which our equipment plan will be approved, which will be presented to the European Commission," said Bolojan. Romania and the NATO allied countries have been informed of the United States' decision on the "resizing" of American troops in Europe, the Romanian Ministry of Defense announced on Wednesday. The MAPN confirmation came after the Ukrainian publication Kyiv Post wrote, citing American and European sources, that the Donald Trump Administration is about to withdraw “thousands of American soldiers” from Romania. Defense Minister Ionuț Moșteanu supported a press statement in which he said that troop rotations within a US brigade would be stopped. “We are not talking about a withdrawal of American forces, but about stopping the rotation of a brigade that had elements in several NATO states: Hungary, Slovakia, Bulgaria, Romania. Approximately 1,000 American soldiers will remain in Romania, contributing to deterring any threats and representing a continuation of the US commitment to regional security. Strategic capabilities remain unchanged in Romania,” Moșteanu declared in a press conference. According to HotNews.ro sources, the current decision practically means returning to the level of rotational American presence before the war in Ukraine, that is, before 2022. Thus, approximately 7-800 soldiers will remain at the Mihail Kogălniceanu Base, about 200 at Deveselu where the Aegis Ashore anti-missile shield operates, and over 100 at Câmpia Turzii. Compared to 2022, when it was decided to supplement the rotation with the US, a NATO Battle Group led by France has been established in Romania, comprising 1,100 people, with the possibility of raising it to brigade level if necessary, in a short time – that is, from 3,000 to 5,000 soldiers.

Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan presented, during Wednesday's meeting of the National Tripartite Council for Social Dialogue, the arguments for which he supports freezing the minimum wage in 2026. Bolojan claims that an increase in it would increase state expenses and would even have negative social effects. At the meeting with the leaders of major trade union organizations and representatives of employers, Ilie Bolojan said that the increase in the minimum wage would entail increases in a whole series of incomes whose amount is established according to this salary. "A possible increase in the gross minimum wage next year will generate cascading increases in many salaries, because over 40 normative acts and budgetary mechanisms are linked to the gross minimum wage, which, in turn, will lead to a cascading increase in collateral budgetary expenses: contributions, allowances, scales, bonuses, caps and allowances," a Government statement said. The Head of Government also recalled that labor productivity in Romania increased by 5% this year, below the level of wage growth, of 9%, a situation that is reflected in inflation, a phenomenon that affects those with low incomes. Thirdly, Bolojan invoked the existence of income disparities between regions and counties, which is why a uniform increase in the minimum wage would lead to the disappearance of jobs precisely in the environment where incomes are lower, that is, in rural areas and small towns. "Given the arguments of economic analyses, it is very likely that the gross minimum wage per country guaranteed in payment will remain at this year's level next year. Consultations will continue next month, with the Government due to make a decision by the end of November," the statement added. Trilateral discussions between the Government, employers' associations and unions on Wednesday did not lead to a solution agreed by the three parties. The major union confederations organized a large protest in Bucharest on Wednesday. Approximately 6,000 people protested in Victoriei Square on Wednesday afternoon. The trade unionists criticized the austerity measures taken by the government and demanded an increase in the minimum wage and pensions, fair taxation and job protection. Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan announced on October 23 that the parties in the governing coalition had reached “an agreement in principle” that the current minimum wage in the country (4,050 lei gross) would be maintained throughout next year. “I am not saying that the minimum wage in Romania is of a nature to ensure special comfort. But it has some effects. We discussed it in the coalition and by common agreement, I emphasize, we all agreed to try to keep the minimum wage at the same level, if wages are capped,” the head of government said in an interview with Antena 3 CNN.

In today's coalition meeting, the leaders of the PSD, PNL, USR and UDMR discussed, once again, the reform of magistrates' pensions that was rejected by the Constitutional Court. However, the four parties did not reach an agreement. At the same time, the Bolojan Government tried to negotiate with the European Commission to extend the November 28 deadline imposed for the reform of magistrates' pensions, but the response was negative, according to HotNews sources. The coalition meeting ended after approximately two hours. This time too, there is no agreement on the working group that would deal with the new law on magistrates' pensions proposed by Sorin Grindeanu. "Practically, nothing has been decided," a participant in the discussions told HotNews. PSD sources say that if the Government decides to come up with another bill to be adopted by engaging in liability, the November 28 deadline will be exceeded. On the other hand, the rest of the coalition parties believe that a working group would delay the adoption process and would not simplify its adoption. This deadline of November 28 is imposed by the European Commission. By then, the law must already be in force in order to meet the PNNR milestone of 231 million euros. According to HotNews, the Government representatives tried to negotiate with the European Commission to extend the deadline, but the answer was negative. On the other hand, the rest of the coalition parties believe that a working group would delay the adoption process and would not simplify its adoption. Asked on Tuesday, before the coalition meeting, what he would do if Prime Minister Bolojan again refuses to form a working group, Grindeanu said that he did not want to turn the discussion into a battle of egos. "I don't want to turn everything into a battle of egos. We, PSD and I, want to try to unblock things. We want to have a new law. It is unfair for this law to exist in its current form. We want to register for the November 28 deadline so that we don't lose European money," declared the PSD leader. He said that in waiting for the motivation from the CCR, the coalition is wasting time: "These days we are sitting, doing nothing, waiting for the motivation from the CCR. Our proposal is that in the coming days we should not sit, but work." In today's meeting, the leaders reached an agreement in principle on reducing the number of parliamentarians by 10%. The proposal came from the UDMR and will be discussed next week. The minimum wage was also on the agenda, but it was not discussed. The minimum wage is another topic that divides the coalition. PSD says that it must increase, otherwise Romania will enter the infringement procedure. On the other hand, Prime Minister Bolojan says that "in principle, it will not increase". After Sorin Grindeanu proposed the formation of a working group to draft the new law at the last meeting, was rejected by the other members of the coalition and left the meeting, today, the leaders of the ruling parties are meeting to discuss the same topic. Sorin Grindeanu said on Monday that he intends to bring the establishment of the working group back into discussion. "Our proposal is that until the motivation from the CCR comes to form this working group, we should finalize this draft law," Sorin Grindeanu said in Parliament on Monday. Asked what he would do if Prime Minister Bolojan rejects his proposal again, Grindeanu said that he sees no reason not to agree: "I don't see the reasons, the argument would be that it would be better for us to stay. In these days, let's work". Last week, on Tuesday, the leaders also discussed the reform of magistrates' pensions at the coalition meeting. At one point, those present began discussions on the subject of the law on amending magistrates' pensions, which failed at the Constitutional Court. PSD leader Sorin Grindeanu proposed to the coalition partners the establishment of a working group to draft the new law, according to HotNews sources. Ilie Bolojan, however, did not agree with Sorin Grindeanu's proposal, the same sources claim. The Prime Minister argued that the establishment of a working group would only delay the speedy adoption of the new law and categorically refused the idea, saying that he preferred to personally deal with the reform of magistrates' pensions. At the end of this discussion, the Social Democrats left the coalition meeting, which continued without PSD representatives. At the end of last week, Sorin Grindeanu met with magistrates' representatives in his office at the Chamber of Deputies, as president of the Chamber, he says, not as PSD president. He said that he informed Bolojan about the meeting. Grindeanu also said on Monday that the meeting was held to see if the magistrates are open to dialogue. "I believe that this coalition working group may or may not reach a common point of view. The coalition makes the political decision whether to accept or not," said the interim PSD leader.

Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan said in an interview with Digi24 that "people in the coalition" who have better solutions to Romania's problems should tell them and even initiate motions of censure to form another majority. Invited to comment on the criticisms directed at him from the PSD camp, Ilie Bolojan said that this criticism comes because of decisions that must be made regardless of who is in power. "This coalition was formed four months ago against the backdrop of very serious problems that Romania had: 1. the budget crisis, 2. an economy that must be put on healthier foundations 3. the crisis of confidence among the population. The protocol was assumed by all parties. I respected the protocol, I respected my partners and the agreements, but I did not try to pretend that things must be done, to say one thing and do another," the prime minister said. He added that the reduction in Romanian state spending must be done, regardless of who will be prime minister. "Any coalition will end up with its back against the wall if it does not make these decisions," said the head of government, who also said that tensions within the coalition are eroding the authority of the Executive in implementing the necessary reforms. Bolojan invited his critics within the coalition to come up with other solutions, which they believe are better, to Romania's problems, including the creation of a new government majority, following a motion of censure. "My stake is not to be prime minister under any conditions. If people in the coalition have better solutions, let them tell them. They can initiate motions of censure, they can create a majority as they want. If they had these ideas, they should have put them into practice years ago," the prime minister said. Asked how likely it is to form a new majority, consisting of PSD and AUR, Bolojan said: "If someone in the coalition has changed their mind and believes that the government can no longer function in this formula, they can file a motion of censure (…) The worst-case scenario is the situation in which you are in power, but you are also trying to be in opposition. That does not help us." He also said that the contradictory statements within the coalition only raise questions about the stability of the coalition. "The dialogue we are seeing gives the feeling of instability, and in the eyes of citizens, of lack of seriousness. You have not seen me intensifying conflicts...", Ilie Bolojan added.

Ilie Bolojan published on Thursday his engineering diploma and the one that certifies that he graduated from the Faculty of Mathematics at the University of Timisoara. The move comes after Libertatea wrote that the faculty from which the prime minister graduated was supposed to have a 5-year study period, but he only attended the courses for 3 years. Ilie Bolojan says that he completed his mandatory military service during that period before starting college, so this explains why his CV shows a one-year gap between the time he finished high school and the start of university. "Immediately after graduating from high school, according to the regulations of that time, young people admitted to college served 9 months in the army, and those who did not enter college did a military internship of 1 year and 4 months. In my case, I did my military service before starting university studies, which explains the "break" mentioned between finishing high school and starting college," Ilie Bolojan wrote on Facebook. He also explains that he had the opportunity to do a 5-year college if he had wanted to be able to teach at high school, but he preferred to study for a period of 3 years, as long as he needed to teach at the gymnasium. "Regarding the duration of university studies, the Mathematics specialization had, at that time, two distinct paths: a 3-year one for those who wanted to teach at the gymnasium and a 5-year one for those who aimed to teach at the gymnasium. I followed the 3-year form," Bolojan wrote. "Therefore, all the information regarding my educational background is clear, verifiable and in accordance with the legal framework of the respective period. I consider it important that these details be known, so as to avoid speculating on topics that can be easily clarified by facts and documents," the prime minister said. Libertatea published an article on Thursday stating that there are ambiguities in Prime Minister Bolojan's CV. In a response from the University of Timisoara published by Libertatea, it is stated that Ilie Bolojan received his graduation diploma from the faculty in June 1993, which is also confirmed by the documents published by the prime minister on Thursday.

"I have not seen the observations of the Ministry of Justice," said Ioana Dogioiu, the Government spokesperson, on Thursday, when asked if the Executive was warned by the Ministry of Justice that the CSM's opinion on the law on magistrates' pensions was necessary. "If my memory serves me right, I will ask to reread the transcript of the government meeting from that moment, when this bill was adopted in order to hold the government accountable, I do not remember anyone objecting in the government meeting," she added. The Government spokesperson was asked on Thursday at Victoria Palace whether the procedures regarding the necessary opinions on the law on magistrates' pensions were followed and whether the Ministry of Justice supported the Executive with observations in this regard. We recall that the law was declared unconstitutional by the CCR, the argument communicated being the lack of the opinion of the Superior Council of Magistracy (SCM). "I am only discussing what we all saw in the Constitutional Court's press release, namely that the reproach made, the reason why the notification was admitted, is the fact that 30 days were not waited for the SCM to rule. Personally, I understand from this that it is not the lack of the opinion itself that is a problem, but the fact that not enough time was waited, an issue that, of course, represents a somewhat new standard in the matter, compared to the jurisprudence of the Constitutional Court. I do not have other details," said Ioana Dogioiu. Asked if there were any observations from the Ministry of Justice that referred to substantive issues, not just formal ones, the Government spokesperson said that she had not seen any observations from the Ministry of Justice. "I am not commenting on political duels at this moment. I told you what we all read in the CCR press release and I can also tell you that, if my memory serves me correctly - but I will really check this aspect, I will ask to reread the transcript of the government meeting from that moment, when this draft law was adopted -, in order to hold the government accountable, I do not remember anyone opposing it in the government meeting", the Government spokesperson also said. The HotNews.ro reporter returned and asked why Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan did not wait 30 days for the CSM's opinion on the law on magistrates' pensions, given that the Ministry of Justice drew attention to the need for this advisory opinion. "Personally, I have not seen those observations, as I told you. From what my colleagues, the Prime Minister's advisors, have made available to me for my own documentation, this is the first time that the Constitutional Court has established the imperative of waiting for the 30-day period. There have been other such notifications on the Constitutional Court's docket, but only one was admitted, but then the matter was radical, so to speak, and namely the opinion was requested on the same day that the normative act was adopted by the government, which, of course, made it impossible to obtain an opinion," she declared. The clarifications come in the context in which PSD deputy Marius Budăi, former Minister of Labor, declared on Wednesday that Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan "knew that the law could not possibly pass the Constitutional Court", since "official documents from the Ministry of Justice and the Legislative Council informed him of both the absence of the CSM's opinion and the substantive flaws of the law". Also during Thursday's press conference at Victoria Palace, HotNews.ro reporter asked Ioana Dogioiu if the prime minister expects there to be substantive problems with the law on magistrates' pensions, given the statements of PSD leader Sorin Grindeanu, who claimed that he knows "from sources" that the CCR would have rejected the law on magistrates' pensions on the merits as well. "I don't know what the prime minister expects, I haven't discussed information from sources with him, we don't have information from sources from the CCR. I don't have any information about whether the prime minister expects substantive problems or not, but as long as he promoted this normative act, right, I assume he considers it entirely viable," she specified. The government spokeswoman said that she had no further details about the content of the future bill on magistrates' pensions, as long as "the coalition hasn't reached a common point of view either." "We are waiting for the Constitutional Court's reasoning, let's see what the judges of the Court had to say and, according to the rule in the case of CCR decisions, what is the way forward." She was also asked what Prime Minister Bolojan's opinion was regarding the statements of PSD leader Sorin Grindeanu, who said that the Government should leave if the future law on magistrates' pensions was considered unconstitutional. "It was not a rejection on the merits, it was a rejection on the procedure. At the limit, four judges considered that the procedure was fulfilled, five considered that it was not fulfilled. That is why it is very important to read the reasoning and also read the separate opinions, which in no way calls into question the decision itself. As for the statements of political leaders, especially the coalition leaders, I have no comment to make, and I have not discussed the subject with Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan," Ioana Dogioiu also specified.

USR candidate for Bucharest Mayor, Cătălin Drulă, submitted a bill to Parliament on Wednesday to make the result of last year's referendum in Bucharest law. Drulă says he discussed the bill with President Nicușor Dan and agreed with him on the final form. Nicușor Dan "wants" Drulă to become the new mayor general, claims the USR candidate. Cătălin Drulă said, in a press conference organized on Wednesday at Parliament, that the bill "exactly transposes the question addressed to Bucharest residents" in last year's referendum, regarding the capital's budget. At that time, Bucharest residents answered the following two questions: To the first question, 66% of those who voted answered affirmatively, and to the second 64%. "By adopting this bill, we return to normality. We have only one city. Not 7 slices. Let's continue the M5 metro, another 800 km of thermal networks, rehabilitations," said Drulă. The USR candidate, who is currently a deputy for Timiș, and therefore was able to submit the legislative project, said that he requested the adoption of the project in an emergency procedure: "This draft law does not introduce any new taxes. It is about our money, and the people of Bucharest." Cătălin Drulă said that "now you can see any form of hypocrisy" if some political parties do not vote for the project. "This project is formally signed in my name, but it does not belong to me. It belongs to this city and the people of Bucharest. I have not seen any party that says they do not want this," said Drulă. HotNews asked Cătălin Drulă why he decided to submit the project only now, a moment that coincides with the moment of setting the date for the elections for the Capital City Hall, considering that the referendum took place about a year ago. "As you saw last year, the political will was to follow the same path. I think it is opportune now. It is important to show the hypocrisy. I want this project to pass quickly through the committees, I want to see the positioning of my opponents", Drulă replied. The draft law can be read below: Asked by journalists if he relies on the support of President Nicușor Dan in the fight for the Capital City Hall, Drulă said that "I rely only on the support of Bucharest residents. The program, the team. What gives me strength in this campaign are the interactions on the street with Bucharest residents". "My relationship with Nicușor Dan is public", added the USR candidate when asked if the president conveyed his support for the electoral race. Asked if he feels Nicușor Dan's support, Cătălin Drulă said: "Yes, absolutely. I think he wants me to be mayor". "Two weeks ago, I discussed the details of the project submitted today with Nicușor Dan, at Cotroceni. I discussed it with him. He agrees with this form. It is a technical project that implements what is written in the referendum," he added. Cătălin Drulă was asked if he was willing to withdraw from the race for Bucharest in case the PSD candidate has an advantage and a collaboration of right-wing candidates will be needed to defeat the PSD candidate. Asked if he could withdraw in favor of the PNL candidate, who could be Ciprian Ciucu, Drulă said that he is not asking anyone to withdraw. "The only thing that would make me withdraw would be if when I go out on the streets, the people of Bucharest do not want my project," he said. Drulă also spoke about the most recent polls, which show Daniel Băluță, from the PSD, as the favorite for Bucharest, followed by the PNL and USR candidates. "There have been cases before. I haven't... Last year, the PNL told us that Mr. Burduja has 27%, and the next day Mr. Burduja got 7%. The discussion is excessive about quotas, polls. Bucharesters will decide who leads. And it's a beautiful thing, we see at the end of the day who Bucharesters voted for", said Drulă. The elections for the Capital City Hall will take place on December 7, the governing coalition decided on Tuesday, and each party will have its own candidate. The Government is yet to formalize the decision through a Government Decision.

The governing coalition decided, in a meeting at the Victoria Palace, that the elections for the Capital City Hall will take place on December 7, according to HotNews sources present at the meeting. PSD imposed its requirement regarding candidates, so the three parties (PSD, PNL, USR) will have separate candidates. The government led by Ilie Bolojan is to issue the Government Decision establishing that the elections for the Capital City Hall will take place on December 7. This will most likely happen in the government meeting on Thursday, given that an agreement was reached in the coalition today, according to political sources that HotNews discussed. The coalition agreement also stipulates that each party in the coalition will have a separate candidate in the race for Bucharest City Hall, according to the same sources. The agreement comes after the PNL and USR were considering having a joint candidate for the Capital City Hall, in order to increase their chances and not fragment the right-wing electorate. The PSD did not agree, even saying that it would end up isolating the Social Democrats in the governing coalition. "Politically, we have established a few conditions: we either want to have a joint candidate, or each party member of this coalition to have its own candidate. Otherwise, we find ourselves in a political coalition isolated from the others. Which could make us ask ourselves: 'What are we looking for in this coalition?' If things happen along these lines, we have no problem organizing the elections," PSD president Sorin Grindeanu declared on October 6. Organizing the elections in Bucharest was a hot topic of discussion within the governing coalition. USR called for them to be organized as soon as possible, and PSD demanded that each party have separate candidates. PSD claimed that if PNL and USR form an alliance for Bucharest City Hall, the governing coalition could break up. Daniel Băluță, the current PSD mayor of Sector 4, leads in voting intentions for the General City Hall of the Capital, with 25%, according to a CURS poll published on Sunday. In second place, are Cătălin Drulă (USR) and Ciprian Ciucu (PNL), each with 18%, according to a poll published on Sunday, October 19. The poll was conducted by the Center for Urban and Regional Sociology (CURS) between October 8–17, 2025, on a sample of 1,072 respondents from Bucharest, with a margin of error of ±3%, at a confidence level of 95%.

PSD will elect its new president on November 7, and Sorin Grindeanu is the only one registered in the race for the party leadership. Among the names that will be part of Sorin Grindeanu's team are MEP Claudiu Manda, Gabriela Firea or Daniel Băluță, the mayor of Sector 4. Sorin Grindeanu, the interim president of PSD, has decided who will be part of the new party leadership team, once it is validated by the congress. Sorin Grindeanu, who took over the interim leadership of the party on May 20, after the resignation of Marcel Ciolacu, is running for the position of president. The secretary general, practically the second most important person in the party, will be Claudiu Manda, an MEP. On the other hand, Lia Olguța Vasilescu, mayor of Craiova, who has held the position of vice-president of the party until now, will no longer be part of the leadership. She is president of the Association of Municipalities in Romania, so she automatically has a say in the internal meetings of the party. Alfred Simonis, president of the Timiș County Council, who is also president of the National Union of County Councils, is in the same situation. Now, PSD will have five first vice-presidents, instead of two. The positions will be held by Bogdan Ivan, Minister of Energy, MEP Victor Negrescu, Ionuț Pucheanu, mayor of Galați, Corneliu Ștefan, president of the Dâmbovița County Council. The fifth position of first vice-president will be held by Marius Oprescu, president of the Olt County Council. He is close to Paul Stănescu, who for 6 years held the position of secretary general of the party, but decided not to run. Until now, there were 16 positions of vice-presidents in the PSD leadership. Grindeanu proposes a team with 20 vice presidents: Five people will leave the PSD leadership. These are the current vice presidents: Florin Jianu, Victoria Stoiciu and Elisabeta Lipă, who joined the leadership team in the summer of 2024, when Marcel Ciolacu was re-elected party president. The congress in which the Social Democrats will elect their new leadership and, implicitly, the new president has been scheduled for November 7. Until today, October 20, PSD members can submit their candidacies to enter the race for party leadership. So far, the only announced candidate is Sorin Grindeanu, who became interim president of the PSD after Marcel Ciolacu's resignation on May 20 and hopes to become president with full powers of the party. Last week, Monday, on the day the congress was set, Titus Corlățean, who represents the more conservative voices in the PSD, announced that he was withdrawing from the race. In the message announcing his withdrawal, Corlățean criticized the party and said that the project proposed by him and the team supporting him "is not feasible." "I entered this competition with the conviction that we can change things, that we can build a serious, professional team, capable of restoring hope to this party. But the reality is different. PSD has become a space dominated by transactions, fears and personal calculations. There is no longer any courage, real debate or desire for reform. I met many colleagues who agreed with me, but too few were willing to get involved openly," Corlățean said on Facebook.

The acting mayor of the capital, Stelian Bujduveanu, announced on September 24 that “we are also renewing the uniforms of the STB controllers”. In a response to HotNews, the Bucharest Transport Company (STB) said that in reality the procurement procedure for the new uniforms has not started, and this will only happen “depending on budgetary resources”. Contacted by HotNews, Stelian Bujduveanu did not respond to offer a point of view. On September 24, the acting mayor of the capital, Stelian Bujduveanu (PNL), published on Facebook a series of photos of what he presented as the new uniforms of the STB controllers. “STB is changing for you, Bucharest residents! After renewing the STB fleet with new and modern means of transport, we are now taking the next step: we are also renewing the uniforms of the STB controllers. Why? Because you deserve civilized transport, in civilized conditions. We take care of Bucharest and all those who use public transport”, Bujduveanu wrote on Facebook. After the mayor's announcement, HotNews asked STB for details about the new uniforms for controllers, such as their cost and number. "They (ed. n.: their model) were presented to the public during the European Mobility Week, in a project phase, to also integrate the opinions of Bucharest residents. The project will be implemented according to budgetary resources and priorities, after the launch of the procurement procedure," reads the STB response, sent to HotNews at the end of last week, signed by the institution's general director, Andrei Dinculescu-Bighea. "After modernizing the fleet with green and environmentally friendly vehicles, STB is considering introducing uniforms for controllers. These are not just a piece of clothing, but a symbol of respect for travelers and the professionalism that we want to strengthen," STB sent. The institution also added that "the new models are designed in accordance with STB's visual identity, in order to convey a unitary, modern and coherent image."

UDMR President Kelemen Hunor gave a speech on Friday at the opening of the party's Congress, attended by representatives of the governing coalition, as well as Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban. In his speech, Kelemen Hunor also directly addressed his coalition colleagues. Kelemen Hunor spoke in Hungarian, but when he referred to his coalition colleagues he expressed himself in Romanian. Speaking about the PNL, the UDMR leader said that he wanted to encourage Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan to continue with "real, systemic reform". "We have a long history with the PNL, dating back to the 1990s. A few months ago we set off on a long and difficult path together. I want to congratulate you for your courage in starting the state reform, it is not an easy thing. I want to encourage you to see it through to the end, a real, systemic reform. You can count on us, we will be in solidarity with all the decisions we will take together", said Kelemen Hunor. Speaking about PSD, Kelemen Hunor referred to the congress that Sorin Grindeanu's party is going to have to establish the leadership. The UDMR leader made a joke and told Grindeanu that he shouldn't get emotional at this congress, but "there's another congress coming up where maybe it will be." "I greet Mr. Sorin Grindeanu. With PSD, we have a long collaboration again and starting with Adrian Năstase, everyone understood that our community, with our cultural baggage, is building this country together. Today you shouldn't get emotional, there's another congress coming up where maybe it will be. PSD is preparing for the elections and I hope that we will continue collaborating as we have always done. Good luck in the congress that you are going to organize," said Kelemen Hunor. When it came to USR, the UDMR president said that Minister Radu Miruță is "the representative of the Social Democratic Union," instead of the Save Romania Union. "I greet Mr. Radu Miruță, he is the representative of the Social Democratic Union (ed. n.: in reality, the Save Romania Union – USR). I am glad that you came with the message of Mr. President Dominic Fritz. We have started a collaboration that is based on mutual respect," said Kelemen Hunor. The 17th Congress of the UDMR takes place on Friday, October 10, in Cluj-Napoca. The event is also attended by the Prime Minister of Hungary, Viktor Orban.

Although the topic of cuts in public administration has been on the table of coalition leaders for two months, no final agreement was reached in Tuesday's meeting. This was expected to happen, after last week the leaders of PSD, PNL, USR and UDMR had taken a step forward. However, new reasons for disagreements and heated discussions have emerged. Even in Tuesday's meeting, the coalition leaders were unable to agree on how the public administration reform should be carried out. The discussion will be resumed on Monday, even though a final decision was expected in today's meeting, according to HotNews. The disagreements this time started from the fact that PSD wants to give mayors a free hand to choose between personnel cuts and salary cuts, coalition sources claim. However, there is a consensus, which they reached last week, regarding the percentage of reductions - 10% of the total number of employees in local administration. In addition to the administrative reform, the discussion on organizing the elections for the Capital City Hall was postponed to Monday, although this week is the last in which a Government Decision could be adopted so that the elections can be organized in November. Those present at the meeting also had a dispute on the topic of Emergency Ordinance 52/2025, which blocks several expenses of city halls and County Councils. Bolojan told those present at the coalition meeting that the Emergency Ordinance will be reviewed, sources from the coalition also told HotNews. The ordinance was adopted in the Executive meeting on October 1 and specifically, it stipulates that city halls and County Councils will no longer be able to give money, until December 2025, on: City halls will be able to continue spending money on salaries, bonuses, contributions, utilities, the functioning of educational institutions, dispensaries and city hall, for health, social assistance, for emergencies - such as ISU interventions and for auditing, banking services, mandatory IT, tax collection. The Association of Communes and Cities draws attention to the fact that in the period October-December 2025, payments for "Goods and Services" cannot exceed the monthly average of payments made from January to September 2025, to which 10% is added. Craiova Mayor Lia Olguța Vasilescu drew attention on Monday, after the PSD leadership meeting, to the Ordinance. "I requested that EGO 52/2025 be revised. It talks about the fact that by the end of the year we can no longer make repairs. We can no longer prepare the roads for winter," said Olguța Vasilescu. She also said on Monday that the Ordinance prohibits feasibility studies and expertise and that in the Government meeting on October 1, the project was read quickly and adopted. The option already discussed in the coalition involves differentiated cuts for the local administration: Therefore, at the local level, mayors and presidents of County Councils will have to choose between layoffs or salary cuts. While large cities and municipalities could opt for layoffs, town halls in communes, where there are few employees, would have the option of salary cuts. PSD also proposes a 20% limit for layoffs in each town hall. In the end, regardless of the option chosen, over 12,000 people, or 10%, must be laid off. The Social Democrats demanded that the local administration reform be carried out in conjunction with the central government layoffs. If last week's coalition meeting discussed the option of a 10% reduction in the salary envelope and the merger, abolition of some central institutions, in a meeting that took place yesterday, the PSD leadership established that it would demand a 10% reduction in employees in the coalition. In the meeting that will take place today at 2:00 p.m., the leaders are expected to decide what the public administration reform will look like. Then, it will be included in the third package of fiscal measures for which the Bolojan Government plans to adopt it all by engaging in liability, according to some sources. Initially, the local administration reform should have been part of the second package of measures aimed at bringing more money to the budget, but it was postponed because the PSD, PNL, USR and UDMR leaders failed to reach a consensus. Discussions about the cuts in city halls continued at Cotroceni Palace after the Government took responsibility for the second package. President Nicușor Dan summoned the leaders to discuss the administration reform and had set a deadline of September 15 to reach a consensus in the coalition, which did not happen. Then, asked at a press conference at the end of September about the state of the administration reform, the head of state said that "the problem is vast, with many aspects", but also that the system needs to be balanced. "If we look at the entire local and central administrative system, we see that there are areas where there need to be exits from the system, just as there are areas where more people are needed in the system, for example on the part of the police responsible for public security. We need to balance the system", Nicușor Dan declared at the time.

The President of the PNL and also the Prime Minister of Romania, Ilie Bolojan, has asked the PNL parliamentarians "clearly" not to vote for any project initiated by the PSD that modifies the measures taken by the government by assuming responsibility, according to HotNews sources in the party. The PSD has submitted to Parliament, for example, a project through which parents on parental leave are exempted from paying health insurance, a measure that would modify the decision of the Bolojan Government. Ilie Bolojan has asked the PNL parliamentarians since last week not to vote for such projects initiated by the PSD, in a party meeting. Ilie Bolojan asked the PNL senators the same thing on Tuesday morning, in a meeting at Parliament. "He clearly said that we do not vote for something like this. It is a flagrant violation of the coalition protocol if the PSD does something like this," PNL sources who wished to remain anonymous told HotNews. A bill initiated by the PSD, which exempts parents on parental leave from paying the health contribution (CASS), received a favorable opinion from the Labor Committee and the Health Committee of the Senate on Tuesday. PNL and USR abstained from voting, but the favorable opinion was possible with the votes of PSD, AUR and UDMR. The bill must also receive an opinion from the Budget and Finance Committee, and will later reach the plenary for a vote, where PNL parliamentarians are expected to vote against, as requested by Ilie Bolojan. PSD leaders announced in early September that they were submitting several bills to exempt mothers on parental leave, war veterans, political prisoners and monks from paying the health contribution. The bills come after the Government introduced the CASS payment for these categories in the first package of fiscal measures.

Following the rapid progress of the works to make the center of the Capital safe, by rebuilding the Unirii Plateau from the ground up, as well as as a natural consequence of a new opinion recently issued by the Technical Traffic Commission of the Capital City Hall, Sector 4 of Bucharest Municipality will extend the work area to the so-called "traverse adjacent to the Central Fountain", which also determines the establishment of new temporary road traffic diversions. Under these conditions, starting with the morning of Monday, October 6, it will no longer be possible to circulate in the area of the central fountain in Unirii Square, and drivers will have to use alternative routes established by the specialists of the Technical Traffic Commission of the Bucharest City Hall. Daniel Băluță, the mayor of Sector 4, spoke about these new routes to be followed in the next 6 months, during a press conference. "The rapid evolution of the works determines us to act in terms of efficiency, both in terms of costs and execution time. And precisely because we are in a central area of the city, it is mandatory to take advantage of this time advantage and to pull as much as possible, as long as the weather allows us to work", explained the mayor of Sector 4. Traffic participants will be able to use the alternative routes established by the specialists of the Technical Traffic Commission as follows: The mayor also presented the work plan that the builders will apply in the coming period, when drilling in the well area will begin. "We will move the equipment, which we had in the park so far, to the Fântânilor area and we will continue, at the same alert pace, the work that we have been carrying out for almost 4 months. So far, the builders have worked on 3 of the 4 stages of the project. Today, as we speak, we have already executed 161 bored piles out of the total of 254 such concrete columns, on which the new floor will be supported and which will become an integral part of the new construction. In total, the workers have so far integrated over 650 tons of reinforcement into the bored piles and over 4,000 cubic meters of poured concrete, which means that, in a short time, we will be able to pour the first section of the new floor. I am convinced that, if we manage to maintain this pace, we will manage to complete the work to make the center of the Capital safe earlier than initially established", Daniel Băluță also stated. The Mayor of Sector 4 also made public, for the first time, information related to another particularly important project for the capital's public transport. "For the first time at the Municipality level, we manage to bring together all the authorities with responsibilities related to public transport, so that Piața Unirii can be transformed into an intermodal transport hub that connects surface and underground public transport. More precisely, the tram with the metro, exactly as I showed that it can be done, at Eroii Revoluției. As you probably already know, the PUZ necessary to connect the tram line between Piața Unirii and Piața Sf. Gheorghe did not pass the General Council and will be remade, because in its current version, the PUZ did not fully regulate public transport in Piața Unirii. I confess that I, personally, did not agree with this PUZ either, because, for example, it did not take into account the need to build a new underground pedestrian passage that would connect the Piața Unirii 1 and Piața Unirii 2 metro stations, given that it is known that the current tunnel has difficulty handling the transfer of passengers from one station to another", revealed the mayor, thanking all the public actors involved in this project. Specifically, beyond the area of coordination of the works, Sector 4 will be the institution that will deal with both the design and the actual execution of them. "Sector 4 will carry out the feasibility study for this passage. This is very important for the new PUZ of the area which, once approved by the General Council, will be the starting point for the technical project that we, those of Sector 4, will also carry out. Basically, in addition to restoring the Unirii Plateau, Sector 4 assumes both the construction of the new underground pedestrian passage for the metro, meaning the feasibility study, technical project and actual execution, but also the interconnection of the tram line between the Piața Sf. Gheorghe station and Piața Unirii, consisting of the construction of the technical project and the actual execution. Once these investments are completed, the tram and the metro will be connected, following the model that already operates at Eroii Revoluției, through stairs, elevators and escalators, so that people who arrive by tram at Piața Unirii can reach the metro, underground, right from the tram station shelter and vice versa. It may seem difficult, but it is It is clear that such a facility will encourage the use of public transport, increase the safety of travelers in Piața Unirii and, last but not least, shorten travel times from one side of the city to another. We are not inventing hot water. The things I told you earlier, we, those of Sector 4, have already done at Eroii Revoluției, where we interconnected the tram on the surface with the metro underground, and people are very satisfied. That is why I am convinced that we will manage to do the same at Piața Unirii. For this, we still need the support of the people who live in this area and to whom I thank, once again, for the patience and understanding they show”, Daniel Băluță also declared. Article supported by the City Hall of Sector 4

Ramona Dinu was appointed on Monday, October 6, as state advisor for corporate governance and tourism within the Presidential Administration. Ramona Dinu was a USR senator from 2016 to 2020. She later became Nicușor Dan's personal advisor at the Capital City Hall and then executive director, having a role in the dissolution of municipal companies established by former mayor Gabriela Firea. Ramona Dinu's appointment was made by the President of Romania, Nicușor Dan, as part of a larger list of presidential advisors, state advisors and honorary advisors. Dinu was a USR senator from December 2016 to December 2020, vice-president of the Committee for Development and Economic Strategy (2-16-2018) and coordinator of the USR Tourism cluster from 2017 to 2020. Since April 2021, Ramona Dinu has become a personal advisor to Mayor General Nicușor Dan and then executive director of Bucharest City Hall, playing a role in the dissolution of municipal companies established by former mayor Gabriela Firea. This is despite the fact that Ramona Dinu is also an insolvency practitioner. Ramona Dinu is also a professor with a doctorate in the Department of General Economics, Faculty of Economic Sciences, Ovidius University of Constanta, according to a CV for the year 2022. Between September 2015 and January 2018, she was a researcher in the project "Cross-Border Maritime Spatial Plan for the Black Sea - Romania, Bulgaria" on behalf of this University. In her last wealth declaration, signed in June 2024, Ramona Dinu reported that in 2023 she received income of over 136,000 lei from teaching and research activity at Ovidius University of Constanta, plus income of 81,592 lei as executive director at the City Hall of the Capital. She has an apartment in Constanta and also owns shares (by inheritance) in an apartment in Bucharest and eight plots of land in Constanta and Bucharest. Ramona Dinu fully owns the company Ramona Fashion SRL and 50% of shares of Tomis Nautic Club SRL, whose value exceeds 300,000 lei. Regarding debts, she has three loans at ING Bank, one in euros - due in 2035 in the amount of 74,000 euros, and two others in lei due in 2025 and 2035 in the amount of 70,000 lei and over 327,000 lei, respectively.

PSD leaders are meeting at the party headquarters on Monday to discuss the version agreed in the coalition regarding the public administration reform. The latest form discussed in the coalition contains both spending cuts and job cuts at the local level. At the central level, mergers and closures of institutions are being taken into account, as well as reducing money for salaries. On Monday, from 1:00 p.m., the Social Democrats will have a meeting in which Sorin Grindeanu will consult the party regarding the new plan for cuts in the public administration. On Tuesday from 2:00 p.m., the coalition is expected to make a final decision. Last week, the coalition leaders came up with a new plan for the reform of the central and local administration. HotNews sources say that Prime Minister Bolojan also agrees with the PSD proposal, which also provides for spending cuts and job cuts, but maintains its condition that 10% of the jobs occupied in the local administration be reduced. 10% of the occupied positions would represent, say PSD sources, between 10,000 and 12,000 positions. More specifically, municipalities and large cities could opt for layoffs, while communes or small localities, which have few employees in the administrative apparatus, could opt for spending cuts. There was also a discussion about changing the rank of localities, based on the latest census data. Specifically, some municipalities could become cities, because they have fewer inhabitants. Because PSD requested that local administration be discussed together with the central one, the decision was postponed until Tuesday. "If we keep making layoffs, let's do them all," declared political sources, at the end of last week's coalition meeting. At the central level, a 10% reduction in the salary envelope is being considered, as well as mergers or abolitions of institutions. Administration reform was one of the main topics discussed in the coalition. Initially, it should have been part of the second package of measures aimed at bringing more money to the budget, but because the leaders of PSD, PNL, USR and UDMR did not reach a consensus, the discussion was postponed. The coalition leaders were also called to Cotroceni by President Nicușor Dan to discuss how the administration reform would be carried out. At that time, the conclusion was that the decision, at least in the coalition, had to be made by September 15, a deadline that was not met. While the coalition was discussing how the cuts in the administration could be made, the head of state said that there was a need for “balance in the system”. Last week, in a press conference held in Timișoara, President Nicușor Dan said that the administration reform is a “vast problem with many aspects”. "If we look at the entire local and central administrative system, we see that there are areas where there need to be exits from the system, just as there are areas where more people are needed in the system, for example on the part of the police responsible for public security. We need to balance the system." He stated that people need to leave certain institutions, but also that spending cuts are needed in other segments, such as goods and services, phasing of investments. He also said that Romania needs to return to a single salary law. "I am sure that a balance will be found in the coalition so that we have a common decision," added the head of state.

AUR President George Simion is once again the protagonist of a serious slip-up, being the third time this year that he uses the word "autistic" in a pejorative sense to insult a political rival. "I told you he's autistic and you didn't believe me. You believed those who told you that I'm bringing down the euro and the entire economy, that I'm taking Romania out of the EU and NATO. We could have been like Poland, now we're the laughing stock of the world," Simion wrote on Facebook on Saturday evening, without directly nominating President Nicușor Dan, to whom he lost the Cotroceni race in May. During the presidential campaign, while in Brussels, Simion got into an argument with a reporter from Pro TV, who asked him about his agenda that day. The AUR leader refused to answer, and after the journalist insisted, Simion replied: "You have a candidate you support, he's autistic, poor thing!". Later, he apologized during a meeting with Romanians settled in Belgium, but launched other harsh attacks on Nicușor Dan and spoke about "these mentally disturbed people" who "want to give drugs to our children", as they circulate here in Belgium and the Netherlands". "I'm sorry. ProTV was not scheduled, I wasn't paying attention, they interrupted me from the meetings I had today and I said that this opponent of mine is autistic. I don't think I used the correct term and I apologize to neurodivergent people. I meant to say that this candidate of mine is a security officer. And in this sense he has a proven diploma as a collaborator when he was going to the Olympics, about the only one he can boast of in life", claimed George Simion.
